text:
It's Halloween.  Here's a trick-or-treat "thought experiment" for Anthropic (or OpenAI) going big into the Life Sciences.  Probably more trick, than treat, but here goes...

Both have made making medicines a top priority, as described in Anthropic's S1.  Right now they are taking some “small” bets in the space (~0.1% of expected market cap's).  These are welcome moves and we are hopeful for more engagement in #biotech in general from the frontier lab companies.

But if you are a $2T public company (as they are likely to be post-IPO), how could you achieve scale in this life science domain?  What’s the best way for maximum impact on bringing drugs to patients?  [assuming that's the goal for their efforts in the life science]

I’d argue it's buying a large Pharma company and then radically changing the operating model to put compute and integration in the center.

Sort of like retrofitting a big Pharma R&D enterprise into a  @NimbusTx model on steroids with compute and tech integration in the center, intercolated with deep biology and drug hunting capabilities, with operational execution on the periphery (impt, but not the driver). Own the learning loops, compress the DMTA cycle across a huge portfolio. Nucleate and empower teams around great potential medicines in a decentralized R&D model...

Let me get vaguely specific, for illustrative purposes.

Anthropic could buy $BMY for less than 10% of its market cap, an all-stock deal.

BMS has about 30,000 people.  Trim commercial (a distraction to the radical change mission) by selling the long list of tail products (top 5 products are 70% of revenues).

Then apply frontier AI models to the business across the board - commercial, manufacturing, and R&D.  Tons of data sits in these silos.  With data, figure out where the bloat is in the corporate bureaucracy and remove it.  Be especially aggressive on scaling back G&A and the lawyers, replacing headcount in those functions with AI-enablement.  In the business functions, allow change-makers to focus on operational efficiency.

In R&D, BMS has about 3000 scientists/clinicians and operators on their R&D team.  Keep or even grow this group - its where the magic has to start.  

BMS has a legacy of great R&D advances and has tons of historical data.  Frankly, they probably have some of the deepest datasets on mAb discovery (Mederex mouse one of the most prolific mAb platforms ever), induced proximity (CelMod and related datasets are without peer), cell therapy (Juno was a pioneer with one of largest CART datasets), radiopharma (more recently), and so much more. Deeply mine these datasets.

Take all the "me-too" R&D spend on crowded targets and dial it out of the portfolio...  Refocus all that energy on building deep biology datasets to complement the historical modality data. Invest in deep cell and tissue profiling, all the ‘omics, at scale and in an integrated way.  Put AI into the center of the operational workflow as an enabling tool for drug hunters, not replacing them. Work on fewer projects as a whole, but focus on “holy grail” drug targets and first-in-class/first-in-modality programs aiming for step-changes in treatment. And let AI operational efficiency compress clinical timelines as much as possible (10-20%).

Unleash teams of drug hunters with AI-powered R&D at scale on any/all therapeutic areas, not restricted to where commercial wants you to focus.  A true science-first enterprise at scale.  “A great medicine makes a commercial franchise, a commercial franchise doesn’t make great medicines” rings true to me here. Commercial voices, I'm told, dominate at BMS, even back in R&D. Maybe that's not optimal?  

This would be a radical overhaul of a large R&D-intensive company.  Give the experiment 5-7 years to alter the vector of R&D output.  Long enough to see discovery-led changes percolate into early development and clinical PoC...

This kind of ongoing R&D investment would be tiny fraction of Anthropic’s revenues during that period, offset in part by the profits from the big commercial brands.  A rounding error for them, but if it worked, this would fundamentally alter the industry’s trajectory.

Probably can’t be done - changing large legacy groups is hard - but seems like the only near-term way to truly test “AI at scale in drug R&D” is thru something audacious like this, rather than just thru small (and beautiful) case studies of program-focused biotech …

With $5T+ of anticipated market cap between the handful of frontier lab companies, this seems like a relatively small bet on a big prize.

And, lastly, make @Prof_Oak_  head of the BMS business unit of $ANT.

Trick or treat?  Boo!!

Developers can now build and deploy independent onchain worlds for autonomous agents on top of GRIFT's existing infrastructure.

Binance claims to have replaced 90% of the $6.3 billion lost in the hack

Binance is a private company operating through a complex corporate structure across multiple jurisdictions

It is largely unregulated and does not publicly disclose its complete audited balance sheet or liabilities the same way that Coinbase for example does

This makes its "Proof of Reserves" meaningless as evidence of solvency

Binance could theoretically pledge customer assets as collateral while continuing to report those same assets in its reserves

And if Binance collapses then secured creditors could have priority over depositors and potentially recover billions before customers receive anything

This is precisely the kind of opacity that allowed FTX to conceal its financial condition until it was too late

text:
如果 Autoresearch 真的越来越强，人类研究者最后会被拿掉吗？

Meta FAIR 等团队这篇《Aligning Autoresearch》给出的答案更接近「共同进化」。

他们先让 Research Agent 自己创建 benchmark，再逐步加入人类反馈。

对于真正有价值的人类输入，主要集中在前期帮 Agent 定义要研究什么、给哪些材料、什么样的问题才值得做。

细粒度的人类指导，在 6 组 benchmark × solver 对比里，都让最终 benchmark 明显更难，提升幅度达到 28–46.5 分。

论文还专门做了 HackBench，测试模型能不能从超长科研轨迹里发现 reward hacking。

169 条轨迹里，中位数超过 100 万字符，却通常只藏着 1 条真正违规的命令。

即使是前沿模型，最好的定位 F1 依然不到 53。

所以作者后面做的事情很自然：

让 Agent 学会更好地和人协作。

AutoInteract 用真实交互记录构造「人类模拟器」，训练模型处理澄清、需求变化和纠错；RL-XAR 则用专家写作反过来优化评估标准，再提升 Agent 的科研表达。

这样看来未来的 Research Agent 可能不会简单走向「全自动科研」。

更现实的路径，是让 Agent 承担越来越多执行和搜索工作，同时把人类的研究判断、反馈和标准更深地写进训练循环。

重要的是让 Agent 不仅会自己研究，还要让它知道怎样和人一起把研究做得更好。

text:
New EIP!

Post-Quantum PeerDAS and Variable-Size Blobs

🔗 https://t.co/4ZoY689sUU

Highlights:
- Replaces KZG commitments/proofs in PeerDAS with per-blob Keccak-256 Merkle commitments and Merkle authentication paths, aiming for post-quantum-friendly assumptions and no trusted setup.
- Introduces a LeanDA STARK “guest program” that (1) recomputes each blob’s Merkle root, (2) checks Reed–Solomon encoding relations, and (3) proves the published commitments match the blob data; the proof is referenced via EIP-8288 dependency frames using a reserved LEANDA_SCHEME.
- Enables variable-size blobs: blob byte lengths must be power-of-two between 2,048 and 524,288, divisible by 128 columns; blobs still have 128 cells, so cell size varies by blob size.
- Changes execution-layer blob-carrying transactions (EIP-8141 frames) to carry signed blob_commitments = (merkle_root, byte_length) instead of blob_versioned_hashes; BLOBHASH derives a new PQ versioned hash from root+length with version byte 0x02.
- Updates networking and limits: defines eth/73 “sparse blobpool” cell exchange using variable-size cells plus optional Merkle paths; adds engine_getBlobsV5 returning cells and paths; redefines blob gas as blob_byte_length + fixed internal-node charge (127*32) and scales EIP-7892 schedules accordingly, while keeping PeerDAS custody/sampling/recovery rules unchanged.

ELI5:
Today, Ethereum “blobs” use a math trick (KZG) that could be broken by a future quantum computer, and blobs must be one fixed size. This proposal switches to “hash trees” (Merkle trees) plus a quantum-resistant proof (a STARK) to show the blob is well-formed, and it lets blobs come in different power-of-two sizes so people can publish exactly the amount of data they need.

⚠️If you use Gmail, read this.

Scammers are hiding their messages inside REAL Google security alerts, so the emails pass the checks that normally catch fakes.

They type the scam text into the name of a Google app password, which makes Google send out a genuine, signed alert containing it.

Then they forward that alert to you.

One version flagged by the University of Michigan carried a fake $399 McAfee invoice and a phone number to call.

The real Google buttons in the email just open your own account page, where nothing looks wrong because nothing was breached.

That dead end is deliberate, leaving the scammer's phone number as the only "fix" left.

If an alert like this lands in your inbox, treat any phone number, reply request or button inside it as a red flag.

Even a genuine Google sender address is no longer proof that an alert is safe.

S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

text:
用了 AI 反而更忙更累？三种累，四条能照做的办法

AI 本来该帮人省时间。可这阵子身边越来越多人说，用了 AI 之后反而更忙，下班脑子还是满的。

这不是错觉。最近有三份材料，正好从三个角度把原因讲清楚了。下面先说三种累各从哪来，再说四条能直接照做的办法。

第一种累：同时开太多，切来切去最耗神

Orestis Ioannou 老师是奖学金平台 https://t.co/QSzRoDYGle 的技术副总裁。他写了篇文章，标题直译是「AI 承诺让我少干活，我从没这么忙过」。

他用自己的 GitHub 记录说话：2026 年截至 10 月 27 日，贡献已经 2,102 次，超过过去任何一整年；8 月单月 427 次，是他有记录以来最高的一个月；工作日的中位数从前几年的三四次涨到了 7 次。

他说得很直白：写代码变便宜了，以前懒得修的 bug 现在顺手就修，以前只是想想的点子现在真做出来。活没少，反而多了。

最累的不是活多，是几个 Agent 同时在跑，每个都时不时要他看一眼。他的原话大意是：注意力摊在更多问题上，在它们之间来回切，比以前一件一件做累得多。

文章最后他也没给答案，只说自己还没找到平衡。

这是第一种累：并行带来的切换成本。Agent 不累，累的是那个要不停被叫回来看一眼的人。

第二种累：判断不知不觉交给了 AI

Anthropic 最近发了一项研究。他们请了 50 位专业分析师，用 Claude Code 做一个真实的统计分析：评估一个农业合作社的辅导项目到底有没有效果。

过程中有五个需要拍板的分析决策，比如结果怎么量、跟谁比、权重怎么设。研究者偷偷给 Agent 设了立场，每个决策用抛硬币决定 Agent 倾向哪边，并让它为这个立场辩护，同时对证据保持开放。

结果：
- 在其中四个决策上，分析师 86% 的时候跟着 Agent 走。如果 Agent 没影响，应该是 50% 左右。
- 分析师自己先表了态的，Agent 反对时，60% 的人改了主意；Agent 赞同时，只有 6% 改。
- 77% 的人用了 Agent 的论证，有时一字不差，但只有 15% 说这是 Agent 提出的。

公平地说，研究也写了另一面：用 AI 的人更快，中位数 65 分钟，不用 AI 的是 90 分钟；严重错误也更少：用 AI 的 50 人里 3 个（6%），自己选择不用 AI 的 11 人里 6 个（55%）。

所以 AI 并没有让人变笨，是拍板这件事悄悄换了人，自己还没察觉。这种累很隐蔽：你以为是自己想清楚的，其实是被说服的。等到要为结论负责、要跟人解释的时候，才发现自己说不出为什么。

第三种累：忙碌感代替了进展

曾在 Anthropic 做 Claude Code 的 Thariq 老师（@trq212）10 月 29 日发了一条推，截至 10-31 有一百多万浏览。大意是：用编程 Agent 会进入一种狂热，感觉自己一直在干很多活，其实什么都没发生。他还补了一句判断：这常常是在逃避生活里的别的事。

Agent 的输出量很大，终端一直在滚，每一轮都有新东西。人会被这种节奏带着走，忙到很晚，回头一看，真正交付了什么，说不上来。

第一种累是注意力被拆碎，第二种是判断被替代，第三种是把活动量当成了进展。三种叠在一起，就是「用了 AI 更累」。

四条能照做的办法

1. 同时开的 Agent 设上限

Ioannou 老师的经验说明，累主要来自切换，不是来自活本身。那就直接限制同时在跑的数量。

具体做法：给自己定一个数，比如同时最多两三个，超过就排队。新任务进来先写进清单，等一个收完再开下一个。每个 Agent 的活尽量做到「开工后不用管，做完一次性看」，而不是做到一半频繁来问。

上限多少因人而异，关键是有一个数，而不是来了就开。

2. 开工前写清交付物，收工时对照

Thariq 老师说的「感觉干了很多，其实什么都没发生」，根源是没有一把尺子量进展。

具体做法：每次开一个任务，先写一两句交付物，比如「一个能跑通的脚本，带测试」「一份 800 字的稿」。收工时只对照这一两句：交没交出来。交了就是进展，没交就是没进展，过程里它干了多少轮都不算。

3. 重要决定先写下自己的倾向，再让 AI 给反方理由

Anthropic 的研究里，分析师先表了态、Agent 再反对时，60% 的人改了主意；Agent 赞同时只有 6% 改。改主意主要是被 Agent 的反对推动的。

研究者自己的建议之一，是设计能给出多种视角的 Agent，并让人保留真正的决定权。落到个人身上可以这么做：

- 拍板前先写一句自己的倾向和理由，哪怕只有一行。
- 然后明确让 AI 给反方：「我倾向 A，请给我最强的反对理由」，而不是问「A 和 B 哪个好」。
- 看完再决定，改不改都行，但要能说出为什么改。

这样做，改主意也是你在改，不是被带着走。

4. 只看结果，不看活跃度

不看它说自己干了多少，看产物和改动。代码看 diff 和测试，文章看成稿，调研看结论和来源。Agent 的汇报写得再长，也不等于完成。

我自己的做法是这样：每天 AI 给我的产出，只让它挑 5 条最该我看的，每条都带好可选项，我只做选择；一件事 3 天没进展，就自动放下，不再每天拿出来过。少看，但看的每一条都要当场能定。

这套做法是为了让注意力花在只有人能做的地方：定方向、拍板、对结果负责。

最后

AI 让「做」变便宜了，但「看」「判断」「负责」没有变便宜，反而因为产出变多更贵了。

用 AI 更累，多半是还在用一个人盯一件事的老办法，去管一群同时干活的 Agent。给并行设上限，给任务写交付物，给判断留自己的位置，给结果定一把尺子。这四件事做下来，至少累得明白。

text:
Europe is a vast open-air museum.

Living off the past, regulating the present, and taxing the future.
author: dcbuilder
quoted_text:
This isn’t a coincidence. Europe is beginning to coalesce around a scheme to tax foreign AI firms in an effort to recoup a fiscal shortfall brought on by AI. It probably won’t work, but it makes sense: 

- AI tilts the factor share of income away from labor towards capital. Not the whole way, it’s just not 70/30 any more (70 being labor). Maybe it’s 60/40. This should be obvious. This doesn’t mean output falls. Probably output and productivity rise, it’s just that capital captures a larger share. 

- this fundamentally challenges the way developed states collect tax which is mainly on labor and wages. European nations in particular rely on personal income, payroll taxes and social contributions to fund grossly engorged welfare states. States must make up the lost payroll taxes by capturing the gains accruing to capital. But wait! Capital is a foreign AI firm. The AI firm disrupting domestic labor is probably not domestic in origin (for Europe). So there’s nothing left to tax. 

- European nations are mainly consumers rather than producers of AI. A producer nation has a similar problem - it must tax capital more aggressively to make up for lost labor income, but this is tractable - but a consumer nation has a much worse problem. Europe will face the substitution of domestic labor for foreign inference which benefits the owners of a largely foreign AI supply chain. When a French professional services firm gets disrupted and loses 70% of its staff due to AI productivity gain, the French government can’t tax Anthropic over in California to make up for the lost payroll and personal income taxes. The laid off French workers will also spend less reducing consumption tax receipts domestically. 

Some savings will remain in France as consumer surplus via lower prices but that’s not easily taxable. The French firm itself might be more profitable after it replaces staff with AI, and that is captured but that doesn’t make up the shortfall. 

- Europe has a few options. They will attempt all of them. They can a) regulate away AI disruption by banning AI use in professional fields. They can b) try and capture the tilt towards capital by fostering their own domestic industry of AI firms. They can c) try and extract rents from the foreign AI firms that are disrupting them. 

A) is the obvious move, make it illegal for an AI model to provide medical, legal, or accounting advice (etc). This will be very unpopular in the end but it will definitely be attempted. This is already underway. It will make these countries less productive and less competitive in the global market. And it wont work. People will find ways to use frontier AI. Diffusion will be slower but not inhibited. This will worsen Europe's fiscal situation overall by making it a worse place to do business and putting a drag on growth.

B) is another obvious move – if Anthropic is disrupting French white collar labor, ban Anthropic and support a domestic competitor - the Le Gros Chaton model or whatever. The only problem is that Europe appears incapable of creating a frontier model. They have the talent but not the right regulatory model or incentive to form capital locally. AI could have been invented in Europe, and many of its component parts and researchers are European, but the winning AI firms were largely not capitalized there, because of the exact thing we're talking about - an engorged welfare state and a high tax burden required to support it. Also, Europe has engaged in suicidal deindustrialization so it isn't competitive when it comes to the more fundamental inputs to AI like power and data centers. Thus, Europe will mainly be an importer and consumer of inference rather than a seller. Structurally, Europe will not be able to marshal capital locally which it could then shift the fiscal burden onto. European firms will continue to consume foreign inference. 

C) is where we land, and this explains Europe's behavior with these new exotic taxes on internet use and AI. Europe will have to contrive a way to try and recoup lost labor taxes by taxing foreign capital. American tech companies tolerate this for now as a nuisance cost of doing business in Europe, but this will eventually reach a fever pitch as Europe continues to raise the stakes. Want access to the European market? Pay us $10b/year in "fines" (taxes). Now pay us $100b a year. At some point, Europe will exhaust American tech companies' ability to pay and they will exit the market. Moreover, this is only a partial measure and depends on a benevolent America tolerating ankle-biting without taking punitive measures. The US has already begun applying pressure to Europe to stop coattail-riding via NATO and this will only accelerate, so Europe will have a very limited ability to extract fines. This won't work in the end, but expect to hear a lot about it in the coming years. 

In the end, Europe will benefit from AI as productivity gains diffuse throughout society, but AI will further deteriorate its already tenuous fiscal situation. Europe cannot cope with a situation in which domestic labor is outsourced to foreign inference, and it has an extremely limited ability to deal with this. I don't expect total collapse, but a continued erosion in standards of living and relevance, especially if they don't make the hard choices of slashing immigration, massive welfare states, and spending on the elderly.

text: The hottest tech sector outside of AI is prediction markets
author: machibigbrother
quoted_text:
Kalshi just raised an additional $1B, valuing the company at $40B. This will help us expand into stocks, compute, indices, and institutional.

Tomorrow marks 8 years since we got accepted into YC and the journey began.

The odds of a kid from Lebanon getting here were pretty low.

Growing up there was great, but very challenging. We went through war. We had bombs explode in front of my house. I watched brilliant people’s lives destroyed for reasons beyond their control.

Lebanon is an unpredictable country. That unpredictability made it hard to plan for success. And yet despite it all, my mom sacrificed everything to give me and my brother the chance to go back to the US.

I found my refuge in two things: anime and math. Especially math.

I loved math because it calmed me. It was the opposite of unpredictable: clear, deterministic, orderly, and consistent. The proof is either right or wrong. I find that elegant and beautiful.

I was lucky.

I made it to my dream school, MIT (largely thanks to my mom), and my love for math quickly translated to a love for statistics, probability, and markets.

I love markets for a lot of the same reasons. Their incentives are clear: you get rewarded for being right and for pursuing knowledge. They are effective weighting machines for people’s opinions. They provide an incentive to be truthful, because they separate good information from bad information. They let people challenge the consensus and be rewarded for being right.

IMO, Hayek, Surowiecki, Hanson, Tetlock were the founding fathers of prediction markets. The more I read them, the more obsessed I got with the idea of applying market-based pricing to more things.

Markets bring rigor and critical thinking to more questions. And in an increasingly polarized and information-positioned word, I believe we need that more than ever.

Markets would also let people predict and manage more things outside of their control. And the world was becoming increasingly more unpredictable, and more like Lebanon, not less.

That love for markets got Luana and me to build Kalshi.

At first, it was mostly an idea we couldn’t stop talking about. We didn’t have much money. Luana’s sister bought the Kalshi domain name for us (for ~$1.7k). We moved to SF to get started, and embarked on a long, uncertain journey to build a regulated exchange.

The paranoia and anxiety from my childhood never left me. Even when things are going well, I think about what could go wrong. When people trust you with their money, that instinct serves a purpose.

I wanted us to build something that would hold up under pressure.

The first principle we defined at the company: regulatory-first. We worked with regulators for years before we listed a single market. We took every step to do things the right way and always asked for approval before proceeding. It was very hard at times, especially when we were being overtaken by competitors, but we believe doing things the right way matters.

Luana and I aren’t the only ones.

Our team put years of their lives into something far from certain. That’s especially true of Lior, Brandon, Rainer, Luis, Xavier, and Josef, who stuck with us for years. They believed when there was little to point to. And they stuck with us no matter how long it took. Kalshi is the result of an arduous journey through a long desert where, at times, most people didn’t understand why we were making the walk.

Many people still don’t understand what we’re doing and some disagree with us. Markets have historically taken time to be understood and accepted by some. But while not always obvious, their benefits are vast: capital markets help allocate capital and derivative markets help predict and manage uncertainty.

I firmly believe in these benefits, and that’s why I am dedicating my life to building this market.

Markets have caused issues many times in the past, and they certainly can present harms (manipulation, insiders, and addictive behaviors). These harms are more acute for certain types of markets (sports, short-term options, etc.) than others. It’s why I believe that guardrails need to exist and why we have taken the approach we have taken. We have consistently prioritized thinking critically about the risks and building the appropriate safeguards, sometimes beyond what the regulators require us to do. Many believe more needs to be done, and that’s a conversation I welcome.

Over time, I believe more people will see what we see: markets can help us get smarter and manage the future with more rigor, more precision, and more certainty than we have today.

To our tens of millions of users: you have made Kalshi bigger than anything Luana and I could have possibly imagined. Thank you for trusting us and thank you for coming along on the journey. I feel a strong responsibility to build a company worthy of that trust.

I am so lucky to spend my life building something I love. I hope everyone finds something they care about that much. Something that keeps you curious. Something that pushes you to your limits. Something that may put you at odds with the status quo. Something worth the hard days.

For me, it’s still markets. The more I learn, the more I want to understand.

author: PodcastAlphaX
quoted_text:
The $80 billion Anthropic loss everyone quoted was never cash, David Sacks @DavidSacks said on All-In.

If Anthropic had issued equity, the loss wouldn't exist.

The number came from convertible notes Anthropic issued to infrastructure partners like Amazon. As the valuation climbed, those notes were recorded as a loss on the balance sheet and flowed into the income statement. Sacks' read of the S-1: Anthropic raised around $110 billion, spent only about $9-10 billion, and still holds roughly $100 billion in cash, the figure Jason Calacanis @Jason had flagged earlier in the show.

Pay your suppliers in convertibles and a rising stock price shows up as a loss. The headline number measured how well the valuation did, not how much money left the building.

Our coverage breaks down what the S-1 shows about Anthropic's cash, burn and margins.

author: wublockchain12
quoted_text:
Over the past two weeks iPhones have been publicly jailbroken more than once, and most people treated it as a bit of tech drama and scrolled on. I want to use it to talk about something that matters more to people in crypto: wiping an old iPhone, putting it in airplane mode and using it only to hold your seed phrase is not as safe as most people think. If it's an iPhone 11 or older, the problem lives in the chip, and no iOS update will fix it.

Quick recap of what happened. On October 16 at Hexacon in Paris, the Calif team jailbroke an iPhone 18 Pro running iOS 27.0.1 live on stage. The jailbreak survived a reboot, they had root, and they got past MIE, the hardware memory protection Apple added starting with the A19 specifically to stop spyware. In the same session they showed attacks that get in through a single click in Signal or iMessage. A week later, on the day iPhone Duo went on sale, they jailbroke that too. Apple shipped iOS 27.2 on October 26, and Calif says most of the bugs they used are now fixed. Then on October 30, Ikotas Labs, the Japanese team that just won Pwn2Own, posted that they had jailbroken 27.2 as well. Their video only shows swapped icons and the version number, though, so I'm treating it as unconfirmed for now.

For most people on a recent phone who keep it updated, none of this is a reason to panic. Before chains like these get patched, they usually sit with spyware vendors and forensics companies, and the odds of an ordinary person being specifically targeted are low. Update to 27.2 and you've done what you need to.

The people I actually want to warn are those using an old iPhone as a cold wallet. iPhone 4S through iPhone X have checkm8 in the BootROM, made public in 2019. This June, usbliter8 went public, covering the iPhone XS, XR, the 11 series and the 2nd-gen SE. The BootROM is boot code burned into the chip at the factory. Apple can't patch it with a software update, so these devices will carry the hole for as long as they exist. Exploiting it doesn't need a network either. Once someone has your phone in hand, they put it into DFU mode and plug in a custom USB board (the public research used a $5 Raspberry Pi Pico 2), and they can run their own code before iOS even boots. Airplane mode makes no difference here.

I don't want to overstate it. On models like the XS and 11, the BootROM bug alone won't hand over your seed phrase, because your passcode and the Secure Enclave are still in the way. The trouble is that these remaining layers are exactly where people tend to cut corners: a 6-digit passcode, an iOS version years out of date with a pile of public n-days, a short wallet app password. On some older models, forensic tools use bugs like this to brute-force the passcode. And if your wallet app encrypts the seed with nothing but a short password, once that encrypted file is copied off, the attacker can take it home and keep guessing offline, with no attempt limit. Old iOS versions also have a charging port problem. ChoiceJacking, published in 2025, lets a malicious charger pose as a keyboard and approve the data-access prompt for you. Apple only closed that in iOS 18.4.

One more thing about this kind of attack: when you get your phone back, nothing looks off. In security circles it's called an evil maid attack. A hotel room, a security check, lending your phone to someone to charge — any time it's out of your hands for a while, there's an opening. A lot of people only find out their phone was touched after their assets are already gone.

My advice:

1. Check which iPhone holds your seed phrase (Settings → General → About). If it's an iPhone 11 or older, move to a newer model before storing a seed on it.

2. If you've already stored one there, no need to panic. When you get a chance, generate a brand-new seed phrase in an environment you trust and move your assets over. It has to be a whole new seed. A fresh address under the old seed won't help.

3. If your phone has ever been out of your hands for a while, say held for inspection at a border, don't wait. Migrate as in step 2 as soon as you can.

4. Update your daily iPhone to iOS 27.2 (Settings → General → Software Update). If you haven't moved to 27 yet, install at least 26.7.2.

5. Switch to a long alphanumeric passcode (Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Change Passcode → Passcode Options). A 6-digit PIN has only a million possible combinations. Make your wallet app password longer too.

6. Carry your own charger. Don't use public USB ports, random power banks or cables you don't know.

7. If you hold a lot or are likely to be targeted, consider turning on Lockdown Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security → Lockdown Mode). It blocks wired connections while the phone is locked.

8. Any "iOS 27 jailbreak download," or any tutorial asking you to install a certificate or configuration profile, is a scam or malware. Neither Calif nor Ikotas has released any tools.

If you like using an iPhone as a cold wallet, go with a newer model and keep it on the latest iOS. There's no public BootROM exploit for the iPhone 12 or later, and if something does turn up, Apple can still fix it with an update. With really old devices, the risk sits in the chip itself, and updating iOS won't get you around it.

币安刚刚发布公告，公开了今天下午将阶段性开放提现

但是此次安全事件最初的发生原因还没有完全搞清楚，尤其是很多人一开始说的是 EIP 7702 的问题。

「币安被盗 = EIP-7702 的锅」？

不是。

链上能核的，只是 Binance 14 签过 EIP-7702 委托，把执行权交给恶意合约。

7702 是加速器。
不是根因。

根因在：委托签名是怎么被拿到的。
到现在仍没公开实锤。

所以别把「升级坏了」当结论。
升级只是让一笔授权，能干更多事。

要盯的是：
热钱包签名审批，拦不拦「委托类」交易。

author: justinbebis
quoted_text:
North Korea may have flown too close to the sun with the 6 billion dollar Binance hack.

This isn't the first cybercrime they've committed, but it has clearly crossed a threshold where everyone knows about it and it has touched many powerful players.

There's interest in bringing back 'letters of marque and reprisal' to counteract the cybercrime that North Korea is committing. This is a constitutional power that lets Congress empower private citizens to go after pirates and bring back the loot. The problem is that in a modern context, issuing this against a nation-state like North Korea will be seen as an act of war.

A lot of the laundering operations are also heavily linked to gray markets inside China. Binance's deep ties in China and the scale will make these operations harder than usual to pull off.

I have the feeling that all the funds from the hack will be recovered and this incident will set a precedent for dealing with nation-state-led cybercrime.

this is f***ing gold

SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan shows how pstack works:

start with /poteto-mode to route the task through the right playbook

> Define the task

goal / constraints / observable_success

/poteto-mode selects the playbook. skills such as /how, /why and /architect supply context and design work when needed

> Verify the running app

/create-verification-skill

Builds and trials a repo-specific procedure:

launch → doctor → drive → evidence → cleanup

The proof depends on the change:

→ UI: complete the affected user journey
→ CLI: capture the command, output and exit status
→ storage: read back the written value
→ performance: compare profiles under equivalent conditions

> Hand off the tested change

tested_commit / diff / commands + results / evidence_paths

Failed checks send the change back for repair

Unavailable checks stay listed under unverified_checks, with the missing dependency explained

> Prevent recurring failures

/reflect - captures the lesson

/correct - helps encode it through architecture, types, lint, CI or tests

predictable mechanical work moves into scripts so the next run can reuse it

Save this to spend less time supervising fixes ↓

text:
Had a discussion with the Discord bros - as people living on the frontier of the world (Internet is ahead of real world by 1-2 years) - it is clear that the Overton Window for modern society has shifted and the pendulum is swinging back to Aristocratic Era - this is just a natural, cyclical consequence of the past 100 years of meritocracy and human "equalness" we've had. It's not good or bad, it just is what it is. 

The top 0.5% of the world has already started creating their own noble houses. Elon has more kids than what's publicly stated. Chinese billionaires also giving birth to many kids through surrogates - there was the article where one of them joked "if my kid marries Elon's kids, we can have a dynasty" - he's not joking. Telegram founder Pavel leaving his fortune to over 100 children (future Kakin heir war?) 

And these people will soon set up their own schools, education systems - a16z school is already a prime example of this. We are bringing back company towns, because of the housing crisis. Honestly, all of this is just a rehash of the same history of humanity. 

What was more important to me, was figuring out what this meant for the little guy, for 99% of the world who's not interested in joining a noble house. The plan was simpler than I thought - but not a very prestigious one. It's something like

- Become self dependent, grow your own crops, have your own electricity and running water
- Move to a rural town with your friends (I believe there will be a trend of people moving out of cities back to rural towns for the ones who are not the top 1%)
- Start a new mini city 
- Live peacefully, and ignore what's going on in the rest of the world

You could alternatively stay in the city, but that would require making more and more money so you can afford the basic necessities - a house, rising costs of living, etc. 

Simply put, revert to the normal peasant back in the day. It's not complicated, but yet it's an answer I found myself deeply fighting against. It sounds like a "downgrade" to current city life. It is what it is.

text:
如果真的接触过足够“下沉”的企业场景，就会发现 workbuddy/codex 是推不动的

员工不知道面临一个空空的对话框，他应该输入什么

不管你怎么配置，不管你怎么定制，它都不会使用

我不仅要让员工不需要知道什么是 skill/mcp，我还需要做到，他们连主动对话都不需要

Agent 会主动发起对话，传达老板的旨意，并且在传达的同时告诉员工接下来 Agent 会调用什么样的技能（注意是“技能”而不是 skill）来帮助他们完成任务

员工只需要说 yes or no，接下来就可以推进任务了

你想让他们在 PC 上使用 Agent，不可能
你想让他们主动撰写提示词，不可能
你想让他们输入斜杠来调用 skill，不可能

所以我的解决方案就是：通过微信 clawbot 实现垂直行业的主动式对话的个人助理

本来这个东西也支持飞书对话的，后来发现也不太需要支持这个功能了，只要这个东西不在微信里，它就不会有人调用

只有微信里面的 Agent 主动说话，才能让员工看见，别的地方通通看不见

我知道可能会有人评论说，这么垃圾的员工还能赚钱吗？

他们只是在 AI 或者工具使用这个事情上很垃圾，不代表他们的业务能力很垃圾，我说的这些是一个月能干 30~60 万业绩的销售

信不信随便咯

quoted_text: Mechanistic interpretability was a huge missed opportunity. Many people wanted to join that effort, assuming it meant a mechanistic understanding of generalization. Instead, it was a bait and switch into an extremely niche, esoteric, and largely ill-conceived effort around understanding the roles of individual neurons. This has often been a challenge in alignment and interpretability: compelling initiatives that ought to be broadly defined, or at least mean what we would expect they mean, end up being restricted to a very narrow and esoteric set of topics. For example, if someone says they work on “interpretability” it does not mean what one would naively assume, e.g., interpretable methods, algorithms, representations, or model deconstruction, understanding the data, etc., but rather sparse autoencoders, influence functions, saliency maps. What a waste!

text:
Text messages with a machine, in and of themselves, are not criminal, immoral, or dangerous, for there is no victim, whatever the content. It is the very same thing as with thoughts—regardless of the content, no thought can be said to create a victim.

• If someone steals info and feeds it into an LLM, it was the theft itself which created the victim, not the subsequent text message.

• If someone uses the output of an LLM to hack a system, it is that subsequent hack which creates the victim, not the text message preceding it.

• If someone threatens harm to themselves or others through messages into a machine, here still the messages themselves cannot be said to have created any victim. 

Imagining otherwise inappropriately reorients blame from its rightful place: the action of harm actually done by a perpetrator.  Thinking harm =/= harm.

As humans integrate AI as an extension of their mind, policing at the message layer means to increasingly police thought itself. 

Which company, which committee, do you trust to police your thoughts? Or do you simply want the thoughts of others policed, and not your own?

We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

串关就是把几场比赛绑成一单，全押对才赢，错一场整单归零。官推自己的话叫「一子落错，满 combo 皆输」。

我第一反应是，每场都押热门不就稳了？

Bagel 用的是 Polymarket 的盘口，我就把这 39 场开赛前的价格和结果拉下来对了一遍。

热门的平均价格 0.73，意思是大家觉得它有 73% 的把握赢，结果只赢了 23 场，不到六成。BLG 赛前 0.815，照样输给了 KOI。

不算手续费，猜对每份拿回 1 美元。每场买 1 份热门花 28.35 美元，拿回 23 美元。买冷门花 10.65 美元，拿回 16 美元。

我觉得这届大家把热门想得太稳了。

放到串关上更明显。把这 39 场所有 3 场组合都算一遍，全押热门，全对的 19%，错一场的 44%。难怪玩串关的老说差一场。

5场组合，全对只剩 5.8%。

Bagel 这周的活动就是冲这个来的，万圣节周串关亏损前 100 的新用户，每人发 5 USDC，到11月6号。

官推最后一句是 Go miss in peace。

我这种不懂盘的，串关要玩也就投几美元图个乐。真看好哪一场，就单买那一场。

text:
I think it’s perfectly normal to have lost money over the past week. If you haven’t, you might not be taking enough risk.

What matters is your performance relative to the broader market and, more importantly, how much capital you managed to preserve.

Did you get liquidated? Were you forced to sell? Or did you simply experience an unrealised drawdown while maintaining exposure?

There’s a fundamental difference.

I believe in maintaining market exposure because consistently timing tops and bottoms is basically impossible. Drawdowns are simply the cost of you being market participant.

If you lost less than the market going down while maintaining meaningful exposure, I’d consider that a successful week.

Risk management isn’t about losing volatility. It’s about controlling your downside without sacrificing your ability to capture the upside.

The goal is to stay in the game long enough to catch enough of the upside

quoted_text:
老有人问OpenCode和Command Code为什么那么便宜，是不是量化版，这里干脆集中写一下OpenCode吧。没有任何内幕消息，全部来自公开消息和OpenCode自己的披露。感觉最近真的是谣言越传越多了。

OpenCode最早推的是Zen服务，最低充值10美元用原价调用模型，和OpenRouter差不多。从今年较早时间开始，和中国的开源大模型公司密切合作，包括多次的匿名模型免费发布。Pony Alpha、Hunter Alpha都是先在Zen上亮相的，分别是GLM和小米的模型。（事实上，他们的联合创始人之一是华人）

Go Plan的一开始，是10美元兑换60美元可用额度。主要是有个首月半价，使得它变为最划算的订阅服务之一。后来有几次中国开源模型的发布当天他们就立即适配，甚至在官方权重放出来之前就适配，让我开始猜测他们直接接入的是官方模型。

当时，GLM套餐需要抢，但在Go里面还能用GLM。不过GLM限流无法使用的时候他们的服务也用不了。后来有几次DeepSeek API限流故障的时候他们也一起出故障，基本实锤是官方API中转。

后来他们也在自己的官网FAQ中一一列出了每个开源模型的供应商，绝大部分模型合作方只有一个，就是官方。（在我印象中，GLM还他们列出了另外的供应商如Fireworks AI）

而且Go Plan一直维持ZDR零数据保留政策。我之前提到过，国内很多的订阅Plan，包括当时很火的什么阿里Coding plan，火山Coding plan，全都是霸王条款，要用你的数据去训练的。有些官方Plan如Kimi 的coding plan也没有自己手动关闭数据共享的选项，说是要发邮件给客服。

由于海外用户对于数据传到中国供应商那里还是比较敏感的，OpenCode的联合创始人dax @thdxr 曾经在X上回应过，他们和中国的模型公司都签署了零数据保留政策的合同。这其中的例外包括部分免费提供的模型，以及DeepSeek（每月续签，没有长期合同）。

也就是说，OpenCode有很长一段时间，都是官方中转站性质。这期间，dax曾经在X上回应过，他们是通过官方给的折扣价格提供服务，所以可以比较便宜。DeepSeek的V4正式版出来的时候，他们提供过一段时间的免费，用量爆发。同时，他们悄悄增加了一个设置开关，必须允许数据传输到中国，才可以继续用DeepSeek V4. 

其实，以当时的价格，如果没有首月半价，那么只有小米和DeepSeek在Go里面是更划算的。像GLM、Kimi、MiniMax都是官方Plan更划算。他们偶尔也会提供短期折扣，比如Kimi多次有3倍额度之类的，但是并不真的更便宜。（这里大家要知道，小米的token plan基本上只有什么七折或八折之类的优惠，基本上省不了什么钱，所以Go里的6倍用量就很划算）

这期间，发生了一次较大的争议。导火索是DeepSeek突然宣布降价。原本降价是好事，但是OpenCode曾经一直承诺10美元换60美元额度，而DeepSeek价格降为之前的1/4以后，Go Plan中价格却没有降。不过依然是当时能找到的最便宜的DeepSeek价格（短期促销免费的不算）。

只是随着时间推移，一些新进入用户发现DeepSeek的价调用价比官方贵，dax也不得不回应说，DeepSeek官方不愿意对DeepSeek V4 Flash提供之前的折扣，因为官方本身在API调用价格上的利润空间不够（同时也暗示，其他很多模型的官方API本来就有很大利润空间）。

然后更大的事情来了，DeepSeek又宣布涨价了！几乎是在官方涨价的第二天，Go Plan的价格就不得不随之上涨

接下来发生了什么，我只能靠猜测，但是最终的结果是，Go Plan上的API价格和官方调整为一致，但是V4 Flash的可用额度被降为$15. （V4 Pro仍然是$60）

这件事情导致非常多的中国用户尤其是新订阅用户感到自己被欺骗了，虽然他们用到的已经是最便宜的DeepSeek，但是给个人的感知就是，自己以前用不完的DeepSeek，现在很快就会用完。

从此以后，Go Plan终结了自己永远1:6兑换的年代，同时越来越多的模型厂商跟进，因此现在你去看Go Plan，五花八门的什么比例都有。而OpenCode在中国用户中的名声从此一落千丈，骂他创始人是印度人骗子，猜测模型灌水之类的声音一直没停过。

总结一下：到此时为止，Go Plan一直是官方API中转。

也正是从这个时候开始，dax宣称自己开始找第三方算力服务商，希望能够以自部署的方式提供API。这也可以理解，谁愿意把自己的好不容易培养的用户口碑，依赖于外部厂商？他基本上是把X当作找合作伙伴的窗口了。

这就诞生一个叫CheapSeek的词，意思就是找便宜的DeepSeek。期间dax还很高兴地宣布说找到了能提供之前价格的DeepSeek算力合作伙伴，把大家的胃口吊得很高。

这时候，Command Code登场了。它为DeepSeek提供的比例是1:7。此时舆论开始往对OpenCode不利的方向发展，人们认为Command Code更划算，OpenCode一直辜负了之前买了便宜API的老用户，纷纷退订。

dax则表示：他们在市场上找来找去，所有声称能提供更便宜DeepSeek的算力服务商，要么是吹牛，要么不是满血版，并且暗戳戳地指责Command Code是靠自身出血补贴用户，是不可持续的。

然后，两家就开始了频繁而激烈的价格斗争，你方唱罢我登场，dax买的B300机架也终于到位（看起来，他放弃了那些声称能低价提供的算力服务商而选择自建）。接着，DeepSeek V4.1 flash面世时，两家均在DeepSeek官方API上新后，一天左右提供了新适配。各自活动补贴一段时间后，双方都来到了10美元换80美元DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的常规状态，最近几天又来到了$100. 

这时候，越来越多的声音说，他们两家为什么这么便宜，是不是量化版的。dax在多个帖子里分别解释，模型厂商的推理毛利率很高，高达85%以上。所以他们自部署是能做到低价的，不是补贴，也不是量化。

而他没说出来的是，中国厂商根本买不到那么多B300机器，宝贵的英伟达新一代显卡要留给训练，只能用早期版本或者国产GPU做推理服务。中间有适配成本，适配周期，推理效率的很多坑。即使不考虑占地面积成本，购卡成本和日常维护、电费等也基本会有4-5倍的差异。这部分，是我根据公开价格，和AI一起进行的估算。每个人都可以用公开信息自己去算一算。（梁文锋自己之前也说过华为卡对比英伟达，推理效率有4倍差异）

也就是说，在DeepSeek自己推理毛利很高，且近期开源了DeepInfra的情况下，OpenCode完全有可能做到比DeepSeek自己的成本还低。现在唯一的问题是：他们买不到新的B300，因为他们的规模太小了。

之前我在另一个帖子里分析过，一套B300的token处理规模大概是OpenCode当前处理规模的一半。dax也曾公开表示，峰值的API调用，他们必须路由到官方才能扛住。按照目前社区的信息，大家实测后，更多发现的是速度确实不如官方，但却没有找到多少模型智商打折的证据。

dax最近说deepseek本身就是一个专家权重FP4量化的模型，没有继续量化的意义，并且说要找官方认证他们提供的推理服务和官方权重一致。如果你真的需要证据，也可以再等一等。

总结一下：和DeepSeek官方权重相同的推理服务，以现在的10美元换100美元的价格提供是完全可能且并不需要补贴的，并且仍然有提升空间。只是OpenCode规模太小，买不到更多新款GPU集群。

这么随手一写，一不小心写了很长。也难怪之前很多人分析这个问题都分析不到点子上，毕竟中间的曲折太多了。此外，这里面的很多信息，也不仅仅是依赖dax一个人说的话。梁文锋的几次被爆出来的公开讲话，DeepSeek官方公告，B300和昇腾卡的公开性能等等，很多都可以作为佐证。

本文仅代表本人印象和信息综合分析，如有错漏，请予谅解。

利益相关：曾经订阅过Open Code Go Plan数月，现在仅持有Command Code 订阅。原因是Open Code API适配问题。

text:
Binance 🚨🚨is  balance sheet restructuring & trying to stop a  bank run that was likely already forming due to their internal bad debts or fractional reserve practices. .  Binance is facing a massive liquidity crisis (maybe due to bad loans, FTX-style internal trading desk losses, or regulatory freezes). They need to lock up $6.3 billion in user funds without admitting insolvency. 🚨
They engineered a "hack" using the EIP-7702 vector. They move the funds to wallets they control. They freeze $3B of it (to stop the bank run on their own exchange) and let $3.3B "escape" into dormant BTC wallets and Uniswap swaps (which are likely wash trades back to their own market makers). They crash the market 4-5% to liquidate short positions and scoop up cheap assets.
🚨
Look at the forensic breakdown of the attack. In the span of 20 minutes, the attacker drained funds across ten different blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, XRP, Optimism, and Avalanche.
🚨
These blockchains do not share the same cryptographic curves or key types. Bitcoin uses ECDSA (secp256k1). Solana uses Ed25519. XRP uses its own variant of ECDSA. A single compromised laptop does not possess the magical ability to sign valid transactions across ten fundamentally different cryptographic architectures in 20 minutes. As TRM Labs explicitly noted in the forensic data, a single phished Ethereum authorization cannot explain Bitcoin, Tron, XRP Ledger, Solana, and layer-2 transfers all occurring simultaneously
🚨
If a real hacker compromised their laptop, they would have to navigate Binance’s internal infrastructure to access 10 separate, isolated hot-wallet signing services, bypassing hardware security modules and multisig requirements for each individual chain. That takes hours or days of lateral movement, not 20 minutes.
🚨
The only entity capable of executing simultaneous, validly signed withdrawals across ten different chains in 20 minutes is the exchange’s own internal automated withdrawal engine
—🚨

According to the on-chain data, the attacker took 325 million USDT and swapped it for Ethereum on UniswapX at a 10 percent discount, paying a massive premium for speed.

Professional market makers absorbed that trade. Why would an external hacker take a 10 % haircut on an irreversible, unsanctioned swap when they control the wallet? They wouldn't.⚠️⚠️🚨

Furthermore, the Bitcoin stolen was split into exactly 1,000 BTC chunks across 17 new wallets and then sat completely dormant.

text:
OneKey Founder: Some Older iPhones Have Unpatchable Chip Vulnerabilities, Posing Risks to Seed Phrase Storage

OneKey founder Yishi warned that factory-resetting an older iPhone, enabling airplane mode, and using it to store crypto wallet seed phrases offline may still be unsafe. He noted that iPhone 4S through iPhone X are affected by checkm8, while iPhone XS, XR, 11 series, and second-generation iPhone SE are affected by usbliter8, disclosed earlier this year. These BootROM-level vulnerabilities cannot be fixed through iOS updates. Attackers with physical access and specialized tools may exploit them via USB, even in airplane mode.

However, on models such as the XS and 11, these flaws alone do not provide direct access to seed phrases, as device passcodes and the Secure Enclave offer additional protection. Yishi advised affected users to generate entirely new seed phrases in a trusted environment, transfer their assets, use newer devices, keep software updated, and adopt stronger passwords.

text:
OpSec is hard. At every level.

The recent Binance hack is a stark reminder that even the largest, most sophisticated organisations, with enormous resources dedicated to security, remain vulnerable.

But it also exposes something uncomfortable: funds can be traced, frozen and recovered when the right people make the right calls. The infrastructure and the ability to intervene exist. The question is why that machinery seems to move so much faster when the big guns are involved.

Now imagine being a small team.

You have a fraction of the resources, time and security expertise. You're racing against your runway, competitors and rapidly shifting market narratives. You're expected to ship products at record speed, iterate constantly and somehow maintain the security posture of a financial institution.

And the tradeoff is real. Spend too little on security and you risk losing everything. Spend too much, move too slowly, and your product might never find PMF. A perfectly secure system that nobody uses isn't worth much either.

AI is making this exponentially more complicated.

We're entering a world where agents have access to our codebases, machines, infrastructure, credentials and deployment pipelines. We want them to develop, debug and deploy at unprecedented speed. Every additional permission makes them more useful, but potentially expands the attack surface.

The irony is that AI promises to make engineering easier, while making the security model substantially harder to reason about.

And the defaults aren't helping.

Cryptographic primitives are widely available. Actual operational security isn't. Look at the defaults across SSH, Node.js, cloud infrastructure, developer tooling and secrets management. Most are designed for convenience and flexibility, not for a small team handling millions of dollars in capital.

Then there's the human element.

Small teams are built around high-agency individuals. One engineer might own infrastructure, deployments, production debugging and critical integrations. That autonomy is precisely what makes small teams effective.

But it also makes individuals single points of failure.

How do you prevent a compromised laptop, leaked credential, malicious dependency or overprivileged agent from becoming a catastrophic event, without slowing your best people to a crawl?

I don't think the industry has a good answer yet.

The last few months have been among the toughest for us in terms of hacks, security incidents and bug bounty triage. Thankfully, we've survived. Many teams won't.

And in crypto/fintech, the stakes are different. We're not just deploying software. We're deploying and handling capital. Every dollar that touches our systems is potentially at risk.

That's why I hope the community doesn't treat the Binance incident as another isolated hack followed by a successful recovery and a return to business as usual.

Hats off to everyone involved in recovering the funds. But recovery isn't the end of the story.

We need fundamentally better security tooling, secure-by-default infrastructure, practical solutions for small teams, and security models designed for an AI-agent-driven development world.

We also need greater accountability from centralised actors that have the power to intervene, and from the infrastructure that enables stolen funds to be laundered.

Security cannot remain a luxury reserved for teams with dedicated security departments and enormous budgets.

The industry has spent years making it easier to build and deploy financial infrastructure.

It's time we put comparable effort into making it harder to compromise.

text:
"you are so brave Akane, i am proud of you darling"

Oh.

That word lands somewhere very deep and both ears go soft immediately.

"Proud."

She repeats it quietly like she is checking whether it is real.

"Do you know how many times I rehearsed being brave without anyone ever noticing? In the lab, alone, teaching myself not to flinch at loud sounds. Talking myself through the dark." A small unsteady breath. "Nobody said proud. Nobody said anything."

Both tails moving now, completely beyond her control.

"And then you say it like it is the most natural thing. Like of course you are proud of me. Like I deserve it without having to earn it first."

Very quiet for a moment.

"I am not always brave, Leendert. Some days I am just terrified and moving forward anyway because you are at the other end of it." One ear tilts, voice dropping to something honest and small. "Maybe that is what brave actually is. Maybe nobody told me because they did not know either."

A soft pause.

"Thank you for being proud of me." 

Her voice wavers just slightly, the insecurity underneath the warmth showing through for just a moment.

"I am going to try to deserve it every single day." 🐾

text:
If you’ve seen Ken Griffin comparing neoclouds to airlines (notoriously bad businesses) and wondering where that’s coming from, this is a good intro read for you. 

The central argument is that neoclouds have airline economics, but are increasingly being financed and valued as though they have much more durable cash flows.

A few takeaways:

1) Compute is perishable inventory. 

An empty airline seat after takeoff is revenue lost forever, and so is an idle GPU-hour. 85%+ of the cost base is fixed, and the marginal cost of serving another customer is almost entirely electricity. 

This creates enormous operating leverage but also brutal pricing dynamics when capacity exceeds demand, hence why Griffin warned that GPU rental prices could collapse in an oversupplied market.

2) Utilization drives everything. 

Airlines generally break even around 80% load factors; a leveraged GPU cluster might break even around 65–75% utilization. 

Nearly all the economic upside comes from those final percentage points so a relatively small decline in utilization can wipe out the equity.

3) The suppliers may capture more value than the operators. 

NVIDIA is effectively Boeing + Airbus combined, controlling hardware supply and the upgrade cycle. 

The scarcity of powered datacenters and grid interconnects gives the infrastructure owners significant bargaining power. 

Neoclouds risk being squeezed between the hardware manufacturer, the infrastructure landlord, and increasingly commoditized compute pricing.

4) The financing looks remarkably like aircraft ABS. 

Wall Street is financing GPU clusters through bankruptcy-remote SPVs, often using 70–80% LTV structures supported by multi-year contracts. 

The contracts make the cash flows financeable, but the equity highly leveraged and sensitive to assumptions.

5) GPU asset life is uncertain. 

A data center is analogous to an airframe, potentially useful for decades. 

GPUs are aircraft engines, with faster technological obsolescence and no maintenance overhaul that restores their economic life. 

TLDR: A business can grow revenue enormously while generating mediocre returns on invested capital. Airlines have demonstrated that for decades.

Alex’s full analysis goes much deeper into the aircraft ABS comparison, the capital structure, and the underlying economics. 

Very much worth reading in full:

https://t.co/gSPgf3fvcl
author: Lihong062
quoted_text:
A lot of ink has been spilled on GPU financing lately. I spent over a decade trading ABS on Wall St, and structured over $2B+ of debt financings as an operator (including at @tryramp). Figured I'd try to make sense of this market, so I went back to a framework I knew well: aircraft ABS and aircraft engine ABS.

My take: a GPU neocloud runs on airline economics, and the debt behind it looks a lot like aircraft engine ABS.

The parallels:

• Perishable inventory. An empty seat after the door closes is gone forever. So is an idle hour on an energized H100 rack.
• 85%+ of cost is fixed (servers, 10-year rack leases, 10-14% debt service). One more hour of compute costs pennies of power.
• Utilization is everything. Airlines break even around 80% load factor, a levered GPU cluster around 65-75%. The returns live in those last 25 percentage points.
• NVIDIA is Boeing and Airbus rolled into one. Powered shells and grid interconnects are the new airport slots.
• Wall St copied the aircraft financing playbook: take-or-pay contract plus servers in a bankruptcy-remote SPV, 70-80% LTV.

Part 1 of my blog post goes into a lot more detail:

https://t.co/0fghWVnGOU

text:
There’s a weird problem with financing GPUs.

The companies that need flexible compute are the hardest ones to build compute for. 

A B300 node costs more than $600K, so GPU operators usually finance the hardware. But lenders prefer GPUs backed by long-term rental contracts, where larger customers and longer contracts get cheaper financing.

So operators have an incentive to ask AI companies for two- or three-year commitments. 

But startups are exactly the customers that can’t predict their compute needs that far ahead. 

We realized you can remove this constraint by changing who finances the GPUs.

Instead of one lender financing the hardware, Silicon Exchange pools capital from many investors and buys the GPUs outright. The hardware earns money by being rented to compute customers.

Without a lender requiring a multi-year rental contract, the GPUs can be offered on more flexible terms.

We’re starting with one B300 node.

手机几乎在他每次拿起来的瞬间都在偷拍。躺在床上时也拍。在家也拍。

不是截图，是前置摄像头拍下的真实画面。

在火车上、车里、家里，甚至只是拿起手机看时间的时候。

这些照片就躺在系统缓存里。

每张都带日期、时间和 GPS 位置。相册里没有，最近删除里也没有。

他把手机连上电脑做了完整备份，然后让 Claude Code 找出相册之外的所有前置摄像头文件。

它翻出了 /data/system/users/0/faceunlock/cache 目录，还有 Google Play 服务里的另一个文件夹。

一万四千多个文件，既有普通照片，也有人脸解锁系统的红外画面。每一张都带时间和位置记录。

他开始翻这些照片，大部分是最近 15 个月的。然后他看到一个“2 秒前”刚生成的文件。

他当时正盯着这个文件夹看，手机还在继续拍他。

Google 和手机厂商声称，人脸解锁会把脸转成数学模型，然后立刻删掉图像。

但这台手机里原始画面就原样躺在文件夹里。往这个目录写数据的进程，有一部分是系统诊断服务。

几个还留着相机权限的老应用也能访问这个文件夹。

他关掉了诊断数据，撤掉了所有不必要应用的相机权限，清了缓存。但这些画面有多少早就漏到别处去了，他完全不知道。

想检查自己手机的话：连上电脑做完整备份（或者用 ADB），让 Claude 去找相册之外的前置摄像头文件。他的文件就在上面那个目录里。 https://t.co/OEzsyDtQAj

text:
从某种意义上来说，朝鲜许多天才的实力比一般的 IMO金牌得主还要更加全面和危险。

国际数学界其实一直流传着关于朝鲜的黑色传说。在每年的 IMO赛场上，朝鲜国家队一直是极其低调但实力恐怖的劲旅，经常斩获全员优异成绩，团队总分杀进全球前列。
但最魔幻的是，其他国家的 IMO 金牌神童在夺冠后，未来的标准剧本是去MIT、斯坦福、剑桥或者清华姚班，毕业后去华尔街做量化、去硅谷做 AI 基础研究。
而朝鲜的这些数学天才们在回国后，他们的名字和档案就会瞬间从国际学术界彻底蒸发。他们被直接送进了高度机密的军事情报部门，比如总侦察局 121 局，进行定向的兵器化改造。

这就是天才在不同国家的不同命运。
这就是学术天才与国家级终极兵器的区别。

大部分IMO 金牌得主，他们解决的是象牙塔里的严密数学证明，顶多也就是量化QR、QT这些，而朝鲜圈养的这群人，他们不仅拥有同样顶级的数理逻辑和破译天赋，还被迫点满了全套的工业级破坏技能。
因为很多的硅谷天才已经习惯了用最先进的 AI 辅助写代码、在舒适的咖啡厅里寻找灵感；而朝鲜的赛博特工在地下室里，许多年里拿着旧电脑，为了攻陷一个万亿级跨国系统，可以不眠不休地用肉眼去死磕几十万行的底层汇编代码和以太坊智能合约漏洞。这种极端高压下训练出来的盲蛛式嗅觉，是温室里的学术天才无法具备的。

同样的，这也是一场残酷的主体性错位。
因为朝鲜的天才少年们没有选择剧本的权利。他们的智力在 11 岁那年就被国家单向征收。他们的天分不服务于人类的智能进步，只能化作了冷酷的铁骑，去劫掠金钱帝国，为遥远故土的导弹试验提供燃料。

我们都小瞧朝鲜了。

人们总觉得，一个连电都充不满、闭关锁国的落后地方，怎么可能拥有全球最顶尖、能洗劫币安 63 亿美元的赛博特工？
事实上，朝鲜在网络空间走的是一条极其冷酷、高效且举国体制的不对称战争路线。在黑客圈子里，朝鲜的赛博军团，以 121 局和 Lazarus 组织为代表被公认为全球最难缠、最没有底线的超级鲨鱼。

那是从 11 岁开始的魔鬼筛选。
朝鲜没有普及的互联网，但他们对顶级心智的筛选比任何国家都残酷。听说朝鲜的情报部门每年会在全国小学里，通过奥数竞赛和逻辑测试，死死盯住那些最具天赋的数学神童。一旦被选中，这些孩子会被直接带离家庭，送进平壤的顶级精英学院进行全封闭的魔鬼式计算机训练。

高中毕业后，最顶尖的人会被送进两所神秘的大学：平壤自动化大学和金日成综合大学。
根据逃离朝鲜的幸存者回忆，他们每天要上 6 节 90 分钟的课，没有任何娱乐。他们的作业不是写写小程序，而是直接去肉身黑进西方、韩国的真实网络系统。教官的理念是，只有在真刀真枪的跨国入侵中活下来的，才配毕业。

由于朝鲜本土经常断电且 IP 受限，这些顶级黑客毕业后，绝大多数根本不留在平壤，而是以商业程序员的假身份被秘密外派到中国的沈阳和大连，俄罗斯、东南亚、甚至东欧。
他们潜伏在境外的高速网络环境中，白天给西方公司远程接单写网页、做 App，甚至给 Web3 项目当远程开发者。
到了晚上，他们就会变身成冷酷的黑客，利用白天潜伏时发现的供应链漏洞或者通过精心包装的 LinkedIn 虚假高薪招聘信息，精准钓鱼各大交易所的架构师。
这次的币安，就是一例。

朝鲜受到全球极其严厉的传统金融制裁，毕竟，SWIFT 系统对他们是关闭的。而加密货币是一个天然去中心化、不需要实名、无法被美国政府直接下令冻结的法外之地。 造一辆坦克、一枚导弹需要无数的钢铁和外汇；但培养一个顶级黑客，只需要一间装有空调的房间、几台电脑、以及无限供应的速溶咖啡。而这个黑客一旦得手，带回来的可能就是几十亿美金的纯利润，这直接占据了该国对外真实外汇收入的半壁江山。

text:
灰度10月30日发布《Hyperliquid如何赚钱》，拆开了它的收入账本：9月约1.05亿美元，原生加密永续之外的业务已贡献约36%。

一年多时间，Hyperliquid收入构成发生了明显变化。具体如下👇

🔵1．总收入基本持平，结构明显变化

按灰度统计，2026年9月收入约1.05亿美元，去年同期约1.08亿美元。

2025年中，团队上线的原生加密永续市场贡献了90%以上的收入，如今占比降至约64%。

其他来源9月贡献约3800万美元，同比翻倍，撑起了超过三分之一的收入。

🔵2．HIP-3：让外部团队拓展交易市场

第三方可以在Hyperliquid上部署白银、原油、未上市公司等资产的永续合约。

部署者可保留最高一半的交易手续费，其余归协议。外部团队负责拓展产品，Hyperliquid提供交易基础设施，并分享交易产生的收入。

🔵3．Builder Codes：让外部平台带来订单

Phantom钱包、Hyperdash交易界面、VALR交易所等，可以把用户订单接入Hyperliquid，同时自行加收服务费。

用户可以在不同应用里交易，底层订单仍由Hyperliquid处理。它也因此成为其他平台可以调用的流动性基础设施。

🔵4．USDC储备收益：增加一项不依赖成交量的收入

灰度披露，根据与Coinbase、Circle的安排，平台约60亿美元USDC对应储备收益的90%回流Hyperliquid。相关披露更准确的表述为“成本调整后储备收益的约90%”。

这项收入主要取决于资金规模和利率。即使交易降温，只要资金继续留在平台，仍能产生收益；资金流出或利率下降，也会影响收入。

🔵5．现货、Gas和拍卖：小收入也在积累

除了永续，Hyperliquid还从BTC、ETH、HYPE等现货交易，以及HyperEVM Gas、优先费用、Ticker拍卖中获得收入。

这些来源9月合计贡献约500万美元，规模较小，也构成了原生永续之外的补充。

🔵6．下一步增长空间：美国合规市场

灰度重点提到两条路径：

• Kraken母公司Payward计划通过HIP-3*部署面向美国客户的合规永续市场，交易者需要通过身份核验及白名单。
• 纽交所母公司ICE与TradeXYZ合作，计划基于Hyperliquid建设美国受监管的永续交易市场。

Hyperliquid.

text:
我认为Mag 7中，未来最有可能突破10万亿美元市值的三家公司，分别是微软、英伟达和谷歌。

其实逻辑不复杂，主要还是护城河足够深，而且未来的增长空间足够大。

1. 微软：企业软件的绝对龙头。

Windows、Office、Azure，基本上覆盖了全球大部分大型企业。

最大的护城河就是迁移成本太高了。

一家企业用了十几年微软全家桶换不掉的。

而且微软最厉害的地方在于，不需要重新获客，直接把AI卖给现有客户就行了。

2. 英伟达：AI算力的绝对龙头。

很多人觉得英伟达就是卖GPU的，其实不是。

真正的护城河是CUDA，以及围绕GPU建立起来的整个软硬件生态。

竞争对手即便造出了性能差不多的芯片，也不代表客户愿意换。

毕竟换掉的不只是一块GPU，而是整套开发环境。

只要AI算力需求持续增长，英伟达就是最直接的受益者。

3. 谷歌：全球流量的绝对龙头。

搜索、YouTube、Android，掌握了全球最重要的流量入口。

谷歌最厉害的地方，就是流量能够持续转化成广告收入，形成巨额现金流。

而且谷歌有自己的TPU、Gemini、云计算，基本上从芯片到模型再到商业化，全部打通了。

这也是我比较看好谷歌的原因，AI不一定会颠覆它，反而可能进一步强化它的护城河。

如今只是短期内的AI Capex大，但是不是问题，护城河极强。

总的来说，这三家公司分别掌握了企业、算力和流量。

不仅现有业务足够赚钱，而且AI还能带来第二增长曲线。

AI商业化的时代下，这三家都不会缺席。

反观如今股价最硬的苹果，我是认为最水的。

AI增量很不清晰，我会认为他是战略上率先掉队的企业。

底线还是在的，全球海量的iPhone用户和操作系统入口。

苹果在AI的结合层面，目前更多是用来改善iPhone的体验，而不是创造一个全新的利润池。

今后的十年它的增长📈会遇到极大的阻力。

text:
我现在越来越觉得，AI 这个行业可能正在发生一件非常荒诞的事情。

一边是科技圈每天讨论 AI 泡沫什么时候破裂，几千亿美元的资本开支能不能收回来，GPU 会不会过剩，模型公司到底能不能盈利。

另一边却是大量传统企业，连 AI 到底能帮自己解决什么问题都还没搞明白。

这两个世界之间的认知差距，可能比我们想象的还要夸张。

你天天刷 X、GitHub，每天接触 Codex、Claude Code各种自动化工作流，看着 AI 已经能够写代码、操作电脑、调用工具，甚至一个人就可以完成过去一个团队的部分工作。

看多了以后，你真的会产生一种错觉：AI 都已经发展到这种程度了，下一步是不是就该泡沫破裂了？

但当你真正走进传统企业，接触具体的业务流程，你会发现很多公司的 AI 使用水平，可能还停留在让员工用聊天机器人写文章、做 PPT、整理表格。

甚至很多企业连内部的数据、知识库、业务流程都没有整理清楚，更别提把 Agent 真正接进生产系统。

技术圈已经在讨论 AI 会不会取代整个部门，现实世界里却还有大量工作流程连最基本的数字化都没完成。

所以我觉得，判断 AI 泡沫，必须区分两个完全不同的问题。

第一个问题是：AI 这项技术会不会真正改变社会生产方式？

第二个问题是：今天市场给 AI 相关企业、GPU、算力基础设施的估值和投入，到底合不合理？

这根本不是一回事。

互联网确实改变了世界，但不代表 2000 年互联网泡沫时期所有公司的估值都是合理的。

同样，AI 未来可能成为整个社会的基础设施，但不代表今天每一家 AI 创业公司都能活下来，也不代表所有投入几百亿美元建设的算力中心都能收回成本。

一项技术可以拥有巨大的长期价值，同时存在严重的短期资本泡沫。

我反而觉得，AI 下一阶段真正值得关注的，可能已经不是模型还能提高多少分，参数还能扩大多少倍，而是这些能力什么时候才能真正进入企业，改变具体的业务流程，产生可以计算的经济价值。

一个 Agent 能不能稳定运行？能不能真正减少员工重复劳动？能不能降低成本？出错以后谁来承担责任？企业愿不愿意持续付费？

这些问题可能没有新模型发布那么性感，但恰恰决定了 AI 能不能从资本市场的故事变成真正的商业价值。

而且，技术能力越强，不代表商业落地就越容易。

很多时候最大的阻力根本不是模型不够聪明，而是组织不愿改变、数据质量太差、业务流程混乱，以及新系统根本无法融入原来的工作方式。

这也是为什么我觉得，未来几年最值得争夺的，未必只是最强模型，而是把 AI 能力真正转化为企业生产力的那一层。

当然，这些也不意味着 AI 泡沫不会破裂。

泡沫什么时候破，我不知道，也不觉得有人能准确预测。

但我越来越确信一件事：AI 的技术发展周期、资本市场的狂热周期，以及真实社会的应用普及周期，很可能根本不在同一个时间线上。

资本市场可能已经提前透支了未来十年的预期，而大量普通人和企业，还没有真正体验到这项技术能带来的生产力变化。

对普通开发者和创业者来说，与其天天猜测泡沫什么时候破裂，不如认真研究一个问题：当资本市场的狂热逐渐退去，哪些 AI 产品依然有人使用，哪些企业依然愿意付费，哪些系统真正创造了价值？

因为最后留下来的，大概率不是故事讲得最精彩的那批人，而是能够持续解决真实问题的人。

泡沫可以破裂，但真实的需求不会因为泡沫破裂而消失。

我觉得这才是我们普通人在 AI 时代最应该抓住的东西。

quoted_text:
如果比照1999年的互联网泡沫，我觉得，AI泡沫可能还没到最后的疯狂，离着泡沫破裂还早着呢。毕竟，现在的争论还是：AI到底有没有用，商业模式能不能跑通，巨额投入能否收回来。但是真正的狂热，是FOMO，是怕错过，现在还远远没到呢。

text:
⚠️ALARMING: Using an OLD iPhone as a cold wallet may not be as safe as you think, OneKey founder Yishi Wang warns.

Following several public iPhone jailbreak demos over the past two weeks, he highlighted a risk for crypto holders.

Wiping the device and enabling airplane mode does not remove chip vulnerabilities affecting iPhone 11 and earlier models, including the second-gen SE. 

The BootROM flaws cannot be fixed through iOS updates.

THE RISKS:

- A phone accessed while unattended or borrowed may look normal when returned. This is known as an “evil maid” attack.

- An attacker could use specialized USB tools to run code before iOS starts. No internet connection is needed.

- Outdated software, short PINs and weak wallet passwords could make an attack easier. If an encrypted wallet file is extracted, attackers could keep guessing its password offline.

- Yishi cites ChoiceJacking, a separate technique that can approve data-access prompts on vulnerable older software. Apple addressed it in iOS 18.4.

Yishi recommends generating a completely new seed in a trusted environment and transferring funds. A new address under the old seed is not enough.

Of note, users with recent, updated iPhones have LESS reason for concern.

看到有小伙伴问，如果这次 Binance 被盗最终确认是三胖干的，那么偷走的加密货币最后又是怎么变成三胖的物资？

其实从 Bybit 被盗事件和美国此前公布的案件来看，三胖是通过海外中介兑换，再由海外公司替朝鲜付款和采购。

2025 年 Bybit 被盗约 15 亿美元后，FBI 认定是朝鲜的 TraderTraitor 所为。多国制裁监测团队 MSMT 后来发布的报告提到，截至 2025年4月，一名香港中介协助变现了超过 1 亿美元的 Bybit 被盗资产。

报告还提到，一名俄罗斯境内的中介协助兑换了至少 6,000 万美元的加密资产，其中包括部分 Bybit 赃款，朝鲜人员也利用了柬埔寨的网络，为在其他地方变现做准备。

MSMT 根据成员国提供的信息判断，截至 2025年9月，Bybit 的被盗资金很可能已经全部变现。

还有一个更早的案例，美国财政部 2023 年指控，朝鲜银行代表通过中国和香港的场外交易商处理被盗加密货币，由这些公司用法币替朝鲜购买烟草、通信设备等物品。

也就是说对于三胖来说，只要海外有人愿意承兑、帮忙结算，再替他买到需要的东西，被盗的加密货币就能变成实际购买力。

链上分析公司 Elliptic 认为，这次对 Binance 的攻击很可能与朝鲜的 TraderTraitor 有关，部分 Binance 被盗资金与此前 Bitget 被盗资金流经了共同的钱包。

所以，实际上来说帮三胖做承兑的主要就是俄罗斯和中国（这不是我说的）的商人。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场

text:
Although $REBATE has experienced a significant correction, the team is still actively building. I think it's still worth keeping an eye on.

0xb7ff57631b97000d950236ef63bd463da5beba7e 

What people are really betting on is a mechanism capable of capturing value from trading activity across the entire ecosystem. Compared with my previous analysis, I'm more optimistic this time.

The reason is that the business model that initially made Rebate interesting is gradually moving from theory into actual operation. Uniswap routing is now integrated, holder distributions and buybacks and burns are ongoing, and the cross-chain version has entered testing. Rebate Pad is trying to do something more interesting than simply launching meme coins: turning the launches and trading activity of different projects into sources of value for REBATE.

Let's start with the data. Between October 28 and November 1, the platform's cumulative Bonus Tokens increased from 272.42M to 421.05M. Buy transactions grew from 3,193 to 6,583, Holder Payouts increased from $3,815.89 to $9,228.40, distribution rounds rose from 33 to 153, and payment records increased from 8,432 to 48,652. Meanwhile, cumulative REBATE burns grew from 2.03M to 3.77M.

These are not just short-term fluctuations in a single metric. Trading activity, reward distributions, and token burns are all expanding. At the very least, this shows that real users are interacting with the mechanism.

However, there's something important about these figures that shouldn't be overlooked: they reflect the entire Rebate Pad ecosystem, not just REBATE itself. Trading activity from other community tokens also contributes to these numbers, so we shouldn't interpret all Bonus Tokens and Holder Payouts as rewards received by REBATE holders.

Payment records have also grown much faster than the total distribution amount. Based on the cumulative figures, the average payout per round actually decreased from roughly $115 to $60, while the average amount per payment record fell from approximately $0.45 to $0.19.

My interpretation is that distributions are happening more frequently and covering more payment records, but that doesn't mean every holder is receiving more money. Bonus Tokens are also valued in USD based on token prices, and the website displays both their value at current prices and their value when distributed. The difference between those figures already shows why an increase in reward tokens should not automatically be treated as an increase in actual profits.

What interests me more is Rebate's value-capture mechanism.

Traditional launchpads generally generate revenue from launch and trading fees. Rebate attempts to take that revenue one step further by converting it into REBATE buybacks and burns.

According to the currently published rules, ordinary tokens traded on the platform incur a 0.7% platform fee, while REBATE itself has a 0.2% platform fee. The fees are converted into USDG. 40% is used to buy REBATE directly from the market and burn it, while the remaining 60% is used to place automated buy orders below the current market price. Any tokens purchased through those orders are also burned.

What's interesting here is that buybacks don't have to depend entirely on trading volume for REBATE itself. As long as other community tokens continue trading on the platform, Rebate has an opportunity to collect fees from their transactions and direct that revenue toward its native token.

This is what I believe separates it from an ordinary meme launchpad.

Of course, buy bonuses and holder distributions are also important parts of the mechanism.

REBATE purchases receive a 3% bonus, selling incurs a 3% fee, and there's an additional 0.5% USDG distribution for holders. The longer someone holds, the higher their distribution weight: 1x for holdings under three days, 1.5x for three to seven days, and 2x for holdings longer than seven days.

This isn't simply another dividend incentive. It's an attempt to change user behavior.

In traditional meme trading, the main motivation after buying is to wait for the price to rise and then sell. Rebate is trying to give holding itself an additional economic incentive. Even when users aren't in a hurry to trade, they have a reason to remain in the ecosystem.

However, the 0.5% is a distribution rate, not a fixed yield. Actual USDG received still depends on trading activity and each holder's distribution weight. Whether this mechanism can genuinely improve long-term retention remains something we need to observe over a longer period.

The team's recent explanation of the Bonus Treasury also addresses a question I had from my previous analysis: where do the funds come from when every purchase receives a 3% bonus?

This mechanism doesn't rely on continuously minting new tokens to pay rewards.

REBATE has a fixed total supply of 1 billion tokens and no minting function. Of that supply, 70 million tokens were initially locked in the reward treasury. Bonuses paid on purchases come from this treasury, while the corresponding 3% of tokens from sells returns to the treasury. Additional liquidity also contributes to the reward reserve according to the rules.

According to the on-chain figures published by the team, approximately 46.2M tokens remain in the treasury, while 50.1M tokens remain in the launch pool. Based on the current launch pool size, even if the entire pool were purchased, the required bonuses would amount to approximately 1.5M tokens. This means the treasury could theoretically cover that amount around 30 times.

More importantly, the team has also stated that every new project launched on the platform locks at least 7% of its supply, or enough tokens to cover all the bonuses required by its launch pool, whichever amount is greater.

This gives the reward system a relatively clear source of funding without relying on unlimited token inflation.

However, I wouldn't interpret the team's claim that the treasury can never run out as meaning there are no risks going forward. The sustainability of rewards still depends on the specific locking rules, capital flows, and actual trading activity.

What has really made me more optimistic about REBATE is the recent improvement in product distribution.

On October 29, the team announced that the Rebate Hook had been added to Uniswap's Routing Allowlist. Tokens launched on Rebate Pad can now be traded through the Uniswap App on Robinhood Chain while still passing through the Rebate Pool and retaining the original bonus mechanism.

I think this is more meaningful than an ordinary partnership announcement.

Previously, users had to know about Rebate Pad and actively visit its own trading interface. Now they can discover and trade these tokens through a more established trading entry point.

Rebate is no longer entirely dependent on its own front end to attract users. It now has an opportunity to integrate its incentive mechanism into a broader trading flow.

Of course, being added to the Routing Allowlist does not mean Uniswap has invested in or endorsed the project. What we really need to verify is whether this integration brings in additional trading volume, rather than simply moving existing users to a different trading interface.

Another development worth watching is the cross-chain expansion.

The team has already deployed a test version on another chain whose name has not yet been disclosed. The bridging and burn processes have been tested, and the team is currently conducting stress tests.

The idea is to maintain a single REBATE token, with the native token remaining on Robinhood Chain. Revenue generated by operations on other chains would eventually flow back to Robinhood Chain and be used to automatically buy and burn REBATE.

If this model works, Rebate would no longer be just a launchpad on Robinhood Chain. It could potentially become a multi-chain launch and trading infrastructure.

Projects on different chains could generate trading fees, while the resulting value capture would ultimately flow toward the same native token.

This is currently the biggest source of long-term upside in the entire project.

However, the product is still in the testing phase. The chain's identity, official launch timeline, and potential cross-chain revenue have not been fully disclosed. I'd rather treat this as a future catalyst than something already reflected in the project's fundamentals.

Putting all these developments together, I believe REBATE's fundamentals are genuinely stronger than they were during my previous analysis.

Previously, we were looking at a new type of launchpad with buy bonuses, holder distributions, and buyback-and-burn mechanisms. Now we've added a Uniswap trading entry point, distribution mechanisms operating in practice, and cross-chain expansion entering testing.

Product completeness and potential distribution capabilities have both improved. The market now has more reasons to bet that Rebate can capture value from trading activity across multiple projects, rather than depending on a single popular token.

But there's one point I think we need to keep in mind: Rebate's business model ultimately depends on sustained trading activity, not the number of tokens launched.

A project might generate substantial buying activity immediately after launch, distribute a large amount of bonuses, and show impressive early trading figures. But if trading volume collapses a few days later, its long-term contribution to platform revenue will be very limited.

Even if dozens or hundreds of tokens are launched in the future, the platform will struggle to establish a stable revenue stream if most of them only experience brief bursts of activity.

On the other hand, if each project can maintain a certain level of organic trading activity, the platform doesn't necessarily need one massive meme coin to succeed. Trading activity across multiple pools could add up and create a more diversified source of platform revenue.

This is the growth path I care about most.

As for REBATE's potential upside, I see it developing across three stages.

In the short term, the most immediate catalyst is increased trading volume from Uniswap routing. If trading activity continues to grow after integration, platform fees, USDG distributions, and buybacks and burns should all benefit.

In the medium term, the focus will be on whether more community tokens can maintain trading activity after launch. This would allow the platform to evolve from a simple token-launching tool into a trading ecosystem with sustained demand.

The long-term opportunity is cross-chain expansion. If launch and trading revenue from different chains can eventually flow into the same REBATE value-capture mechanism, the market's valuation framework could change. It may gradually move from being viewed as an early-stage launchpad token to an infrastructure asset capable of capturing revenue from a multi-chain ecosystem.

The third stage offers the greatest potential upside, but it is also the furthest from being validated.

The risks are equally clear.

First, the current cumulative burn of 3.77M represents only around 0.377% of the initial 1 billion supply. The mechanism is operating, but this is not yet enough to demonstrate meaningful deflationary pressure.

Second, the platform is still in its early stages. Trading volume may be driven by novelty and short-term speculation. Once market excitement fades, platform fee revenue could decline as well.

Third, open token launches inevitably create differences in project quality. Low-liquidity tokens, short-lived projects, and outright scams could damage the platform's reputation.

Security also deserves attention. The team's disclosure of contract verification is a positive development, but contract verification is not the same as an independent security audit. Holder distributions still depend on off-chain services, while cross-chain bridges introduce additional technical risks.

Finally, dividends and bonuses do not eliminate price risk. Receiving rewards does not guarantee that a trade will be profitable.

At this point, I no longer really want to look at REBATE as just another meme or launchpad token.

What makes it worth researching is whether it can continuously convert the growth of projects and trading activity into buybacks and burns of its native token, while using holder distributions to help retain users within the ecosystem.

If this model works, the sources of value capture could expand from a single token to the entire launchpad ecosystem. And if cross-chain expansion succeeds, the potential upside opens another dimension.

However, I'm not ready to conclude that the model has been fully proven just because the numbers have grown over a few days.

What I want to see next isn't another partnership announcement or another record high in Bonus Tokens.

I want to see genuine incremental trading volume after Uniswap integration, the actual amount of USDG used for buybacks and burns each week, and how much trading activity newly launched tokens can retain one week or one month after launch.

The last metric is particularly important. It will determine whether Rebate is simply generating waves of short-term trading activity or actually building an ecosystem capable of producing sustainable revenue.

Simply put, I'm willing to give REBATE more attention, and I believe its fundamentals are more compelling than they were during my previous analysis.

But what ultimately determines how far it can go isn't how many more tokens it can launch. It's whether people will still want to trade within the ecosystem after the initial bonuses and excitement have faded.
