manifold这个预测市场怪好玩的，既可以推测p=np？等等千禧年难题，也可以猜测网友家里下一个孩子是男孩还是女孩。

不过因为平台内赌注用的是不在市场流通的虚拟币，无法兑现，赚不到钱，所以中文ct没什么讨论，这边主要是专注于赌钱。

当然也正因为只能进不能出，才让所有人都可以无许可的开盘，并且自己结算自己的市场。如果瞎搞，虽然不涉及什么金钱纠纷，但会影响自己在平台里的信誉，以后就没人和你玩了。

除了其他预测平台键政和看球的，有硬核玩家在这讨论AI发展速度/生物科技/高等数学/冷门科幻小说的走向，也有男女相亲，下注他们会交往几个月的，有哥们直播自己这个月每天坚持跑5公里的，他下注赌自己能坚持下来，并且鼓励网友赌否给他动力。已经有9个哥们赌他不行了，不知道是想以此激励他，还是单纯的觉得他不行，哈哈。

也许十年前的极客哥们在挖比特币的时候也只是当成一场游戏，所以买个披萨都很快乐，对于创业者来说，如何把区块链的相关技术转化成用户需要的产品，manifold是个很不错的范本，你的区块链产品未必非要是一个金融产品。

除了能用加密货币入金（一般不需要入金，可以免费领取游戏币），活动奖品是小额的加密货币（需要kyc），用了预测市场的模式和比特币挖矿验证公平性之外，manifold几乎和crypto没什么关系，与其说是预测市场，不如说是一个具有预测市场功能的论坛社区，虽然完全中心化，没上链，依然有可能成为一种基于广泛意义上区块链技术的新型社交媒体，即使壁垒不那么深，也可能被广泛的应用在现有社交平台中，影响未来的社交行业，越来越多平台都可能发行自己的token资产，越来越多人接触、拥有token，虽然这些token未必会在市场流通。

当然，现实很残酷，做非金融属性的产品，想赚钱不容易。本文也并非付费合作推广，他们应该是没什么营销预算，仅仅出于兴趣给这个被逐渐边缘化的产品唱一首挽歌（体验：https://t.co/WhE9hka55p）。

前段时间因为paper的盘前交易，一些人可能接触到MNX，一个构建在megaeth上的期货市场，这是该团队做的另一个独立产品，但我并未在其中感受到特别的创造力。

估计manifold的团队就是因为做社交市场挣不到钱，于是跑去做真实市场了，只需要一部分老用户转化到新平台就能赚到钱。

也能理解，毕竟MNX即使平平无奇，只要在特殊节点，比如之前paper特别火的时候，上线个盘前，就能获得讨论度，但manifold的讨论度很低，盈利能力也很差。如果想拿融资，大厂真看上了这个玩法，也完全可以直接把你的功能加到他们现有的产品里面，做下去没什么出路。

text:
How to focus like a high performer:

- The high performers I know take walks and bike rides. None of them hold maximum focus all day
- We learn best in 90 min bouts inside an ultradian cycle. The first one usually starts when you wake up
- Don't expect to focus for the whole 90 min. The beginning and end flicker in and out
- After a learning bout, take non-sleep deep rest or deliberate disengagement: walk, run, or sit and let your thoughts move. That accelerates plasticity

text:
Google open-sourced the plugin thousands of its engineers use to stop AI from coding before the plan is solid.

It's called the Elephant-Goldfish Model.

→ The Elephant: one session that knows your whole project. It drafts the design doc and writes zero code
→ The Goldfish: fresh agents with no memory of your chat. They read the doc cold and catch the assumptions you never wrote down
→ You approve the plan, then your agent builds it

Skills for brainstorming, drafting, review, resolving feedback, documenting an existing codebase, and catching docs that drift from the code.

Works in Claude Code and Codex:
claude plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
claude plugin install egm@egm

text:
Lauren Tan（@poteto）在一个视频中分享她在 Cursor 使用 AI 编程 Agent 的经验, 值得看一下。

我用我的skill，抓取字幕，翻译并重新烧录了双语字幕。

贯穿整场的观点是：要让 Agent 可靠地自主完成工作，工程师需要先建设好验证工具、项目知识和自动化约束。信任来自这些机制持续产出的可靠结果。

1. 信任决定了你能把多少工作交给 Agent。〔00:54–05:39〕

如果 Agent 经常凭猜测定位问题，你就不得不盯着每一步操作。此时，即使同时启动很多 Agent，你自己的检查能力仍然会成为瓶颈。

她描述的成长路径是：从紧盯一两个 Agent，到让它们独立完成任务，再到自动合并代码。她自述曾一个月合入约 1,000 个 PR，也有睡醒后发现 20 多个 PR 已经合入的经历；这些成果建立在前期大量建设工作之上。

2. 首先让 Agent 能够亲自验证自己的工作。〔05:40–13:37〕

Agent 应当能够启动应用、操作界面、复现问题、查看运行日志和性能数据，并检查修改后的实际表现。如果这些步骤都由人来完成，人就会一直困在“运行—截图—反馈—再修改”的循环里。

她特别强调 Feature Map，也就是“功能地图”：告诉 Agent 一个功能在哪里、如何进入、有哪些快捷键、怎样定位界面元素。这样，面对“侧边栏很卡”或一张模糊截图，它才知道应该去哪里检查。

这里有一个关键区分：验证用于判断功能是否解决了问题；代码是否清晰、易维护，还需要其他机制。

3. 把反复出现的失败，转化为可复用的 Skill，并检验它是否有效。〔13:37–23:56〕

她把 Agent 比作“很会写代码、但刚入职五秒钟的新同事”：缺少业务背景，也不了解团队的工作习惯。Skill 就是把这些背景、标准和操作方法写下来，供它反复使用。

她的 PStack 工具集来自持续观察：发现 Agent 没读相关代码就下结论，就补上调查流程；发现它不会验证，就补上验证能力。

Skill 本身也需要评估。她会设定评分标准，让多个 Agent 或模型执行任务、交叉检查结果，再根据表现修改 Skill。写下一条要求，并不等于 Agent 已经稳定掌握了它。

4. 先在本地建立可靠流程，再扩展到云端和自动化。〔24:32–30:11〕

起步阶段适合在本地观察：应用能否启动、Agent 会不会操作、是否真的复现和验证了问题。流程稳定之后，再把相同能力搬到云端。

她举了一个名为 Benny 的 Agent：它接收 Bug 报告，在云端启动应用并尝试复现。有一次，它确认问题在主分支中已经修复，只需要发布新版本，省去了人工重复排查。

她明确不建议在基础能力尚未可靠时，直接启动成百上千个 Agent，那会放大失败和费用。

5. 代码库本身需要适合 Agent 工作。〔30:17–38:54〕

她认为，有成熟规范和检查机制的老项目，可能比毫无约束的新项目更适合 Agent。快速拼出来的原型虽然交付快，但 Agent 不断选择眼前最省事的做法，会逐渐积累难以维护的结构。

因此，某些项目值得投入重构。她自述为迁移到新架构进行了超过 600 个 PR 的改动，目的是让后续开发更稳定，让整个团队受益。

她也鼓励把工作拆成目标单一的小 PR，便于理解修改、定位问题和回滚，没有规定统一的代码行数上限。

6. 把重要规范变成自动执行的检查，让最省事的路径就是正确路径。〔39:07–48:43〕

这是整场最重要的工程方法之一。她认为，规则文档、Skill 和 AI 审查都可能被遗漏，重要约束需要落实到项目结构、编译检查和 CI——也就是提交代码时自动执行的检查。

她介绍的 Dune 架构会把同一功能的代码集中存放，并检查模块之间的引用关系。例如，限制界面渲染部分引入不该承担的繁重计算，减少卡顿风险。

Agent 喜欢沿用已有模式、选择捷径，因此应该把项目设计成：照着现有方式做，就容易做对。

她在自己的项目中甚至禁用了 useEffect 和代码注释。这些是针对其项目失败模式制定的具体规则；更值得提炼的方法是：把反复出现的审查意见转化为可以自动检查的约束。

7. 前期建设有成本，回报要放到整个团队和长期使用中看。〔49:23–54:15〕

她承认自己拥有非常充足的 Token 资源，其他人不应原样照搬。重构、编写 Skill 和建立验证体系，都需要时间与费用。

她的判断是：如果这些投入能减少后续返工，让更多人持续贡献代码，甚至让能力较弱的模型也能做好工作，就可能带来可观回报。但分享中没有给出普通团队可直接套用的成本预算。

8. 工程师的职责，会更多地转向设计工作环境和质量标准。〔23:15–23:44；54:18–57:03〕

她用“主厨”作比喻：工程师不必亲自做每一道菜，而要设计厨房、制定流程、分配任务，并保证出品质量。

当工具、架构和检查足够完善后，产品经理、设计师也能借助 Agent 修改功能和修复问题。工程师的重要贡献，是让这种参与可以长期、稳定地进行。

按她的思路，可以把实践顺序整理为：
观察失败 → 补充项目知识和 Skill → 建立实际运行验证 → 评估并改进流程 → 把关键规范变成自动检查 → 逐步扩大自主工作的范围。

刚发现好多人竟然在通过 API 用 Claude，一个 Claude Ultra 账号每周大约是 2000 美金额度，每月 8000，用 API 可是 40 倍啊。真心建议大家肉身去美国办个手机号 + 银行卡，14 天 3 万人民币就足够了。

- 签证 2000
- 往返机票提前订 5000
- 罗兰岗/圣盖博住民宿，单人间 90 美金一天。除非你是要去 San Francisco 拜访人，住那地方那么贵真没必要。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 门口都没 logo，普通人也没法参观。

- 上飞机之前网购一张 Google Fi 手机卡和一台干净手机（Pixel 入门款合约机就行），到了就把手机配置好

- 第二天去 BOA 办卡，洛杉矶华人区的 BOA 一般不需要地址证明，拿着护照和手机去就行，借记卡和信用卡同时办（不给办信用卡也没关系，借记卡也够用），一定要加急，一周后会寄到地址（这是为什么呆 14 天比较保险）

- 不用等实体卡，当天就可以用 BOA App + Google Pay / Apple Pay 开尊贵的 Claude 和 Codex 大会员了

- 租辆车，就可以在洛杉矶和尔湾开始玩了，时间多的还可以去圣地亚哥
- 一张实体卡一般可以绑定 4 个 Claude 账户，加上 Apple Pay、Google Pay，一张借记卡加一张信用卡至少可以开出 10 个 Claude Max 账户
- 海外没有收入的话，可以走个人购汇，也可以走 wise 转账
- 下次去美国把 BOA 的账单打印出来，可以作为地址证明，去 Chase 等银行开卡了

大家会说，我要上班啊，哪来的半个月假呢？那你们组的人有合法 Claude 账号吗？一起去美国团建的话，每个人只要 2 万就行了。

比如 5 个人，可以租个《半熟恋人》这种 5b3b 的大 house，租车和吃饭可以 share，白天还可以一起办公，同吃同住是硅谷 startup 的标配。每天自己做饭的话，14 天人均 2 万基本就能搞定（不含 Claude、手机等开销）。看着两三万人民币挺贵，一个月的 Claude 账单就回来了。

当然，珍贵的 Claude 账号一定要配合美国家宽 IP，在干净环境里使用。我被封的两个账号都是因为在 IP 不干净的环境里用过，其他十几个都没事。

ANTHROPIC EXPECTED TO RECEIVE A “HIGH” JUNK CREDIT RATING AFTER IPO: FT

Blackstone has told investors Anthropic is likely to receive a credit rating in the double-B range after going public, below investment grade, reversing its earlier expectations for an investment-grade rating by year-end.

The lower rating could make it more expensive for Anthropic to finance its massive AI infrastructure expansion, while limiting access to pension funds and insurers that face restrictions on investing in junk-rated debt.

The warning comes as Blackstone participates in Anthropic's $63B financing deal, known as Project North Star, to support the leasing of 1.5 GW of Google's AI chips.

Under the deal:

• More than $42B in senior loans are guaranteed by Broadcom $AVGO.

• Another $18B in junior debt is backed by Anthropic's lease payments.

• Blackstone's funds invested $9B in junior debt, earning yields above 10%.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus outlined plans to spend more than $800B on computing infrastructure through 2045.

Without an investment-grade rating, Anthropic may need to continue relying on financially stronger partners to support its borrowing.

The major credit agencies, Moody's, S&P and Fitch, have not yet formally issued ratings for Anthropic, per FT.

i can't comprehend why people run claude code on default settings

one settings change and every model gets its own job:

→ opus plans every task and advises when stuck
→ sonnet 5.5 writes the actual code
→ haiku handles every file search
→ a critic agent tries to break your diff before you merge

Opus thinks. The cheap models grind.

paste this into claude code 👇

Add this to ~/.claude/settings.json. Keep every hook, permission and plugin I already have. Then create the two agent files below and show me the diff.

```json
{
  "model": "opusplan",
  "advisorModel": "opus",
  "effortLevel": "medium",
  "modelSettings": {
    "claude-opus-5-5": { "effortLevel": "high" },
    "claude-sonnet-5-5": { "effortLevel": "medium" }
  },
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "haiku"
  }
}
```

~/.claude/agents/scout.md
```
---
name: scout
description: finds code fast. returns file paths and line numbers only.
model: haiku
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
---
Locate exactly what was asked. Return file:line. No fixes. No opinions.
```

~/.claude/agents/critic.md
```
---
name: critic
description: reviews a diff or plan before any task is called done
model: opus
tools: Read, Grep, Bash
---
Assume this is broken. Find how it fails. One line per issue, worst first.
```

text:
In the 8 minutes before XPL dropped 18% today, 11 Hyperliquid accounts pulled $1.62M of margin out of their XPL longs.

Then they let the $12M position get liquidated into HLP at mark price.

HLP ate ~$0.6M.

Fresh accounts funded via CCTP. Test withdrawals 20-50 min before. 7 rejected withdrawals while scraping the margin to the limit. $0 left after.

Looks planned. Whether the same operator was short on Binance, I can't see.

Timeline (Nov 1, UTC) 👇

Oct 29-31
9 of the 10 largest accounts are created, each funded once via CCTP with $145k-$243k. On Hyperliquid the sender only shows as Circle's deposit wallet.

03:45-04:15
10 of the 11 make test withdrawals of $500-$1.6k.

04:24-04:32
10 accounts withdraw $98k-$232k each, $1.62M total.
7 more attempts get rejected: "Insufficient balance for withdrawal".
Every dollar the margin check allows comes out. The longs stay open.

04:32
XPL -18% in 1 minute, 0.086 to 0.0705.
$11.2M (144M XPL) trades on Binance perps in that minute.
Hyperliquid itself barely trades.

04:32:50-04:32:59
All 11 get liquidated into the HLP backstop vault, plus 19 small accounts.
160M XPL / $12.2M taken over at avg 0.0759, in a minute that printed a 0.0705 low.

After
All 11 accounts: $0.
Backstop vault: $1.00M to $0.44M while unwinding.
HLP daily PnL: +$21k to -$655k (~0.4% of the vault).

Why it works
Dumping $12M of XPL into the HL book would wreck your own exit.
Drain the margin first, and a small move is enough to trigger liquidation.
Liquidation hands the whole position to HLP at mark with zero slippage. HLP eats the drop after.

Same playbook as the Mar 2025 ETH whale that cost HLP $4M.
If they were also short on Binance, the crash itself was the profit.

Addresses + fills in the reply.

想了解臭名昭著的朝鲜黑客组织 Lazarus，可以看看 Cipher 拍的纪录片《How North Korean Hackers Are Stealing Billions》。

Cipher 专做犯罪和地缘政治题材，看他们的纪录片跟追剧一样。这部片长 1 小时 20 分钟，把这支朝鲜国家队从头到尾讲透了。

Lazarus 可不是普通黑客，它是朝鲜国家养的「犯罪企业」。大多数黑客都是从小被选中的数学天才，每天工作 15 到 20 小时。Lazarus 的 KPI 只有一个：给政权搞钱，大头流向核武。

片子从朝鲜战争、主体思想和饥荒讲起，先讲清楚这个国家为什么会养出这么一支队伍。

然后按时间线一路往下：

① 1980–2000 年代伪造超级美元；

② 2014 年黑索尼影业，起因是那部《刺杀金正恩》；

③ 2016 年孟加拉国央行 SWIFT 劫案卷走 8100 万美元，还让打印机打不出转账记录，好拖延被发现的时间；

④ 2017 年的 WannaCry，用的是泄露出来的 NSA 漏洞「永恒之蓝」，波及约 150 个国家、20 多万台电脑；

⑤ 转战加密：Coincheck、Ronin (Axie)、WazirX，2025 年 Bybit 被盗 15 亿美元，再到现在 2026 年的币安。

------

币圈钱多、盗完还有机会全身而退，Lazarus 只会一直盯着挖漏洞。行业是时候团结起来了，我们面对的是一整个国家机器。

text:
This AI creator goes viral with this absolutely beautiful video, and people think they have the right to steal it. 

And the comments justifying it are disgusting.

“You don’t own it because it’s AI.”
“AI content can’t be copyrighted.”
“You didn’t even make the video.”

Since when did using AI mean someone’s time, creativity, effort, and artistic vision have no value?

You can dislike AI all you want. But that doesn’t give you the right to take someone else’s work and pass it off as your own.

And the idea that ALL AI-generated content is automatically free for anyone to use is simply false.

You don’t have to respect the tool. But you should respect the person behind it.

How did we get to a point where stealing someone’s creative work is celebrated simply because AI was involved?

text:
I think Satoshi’s Bitcoin should be left alone.

I get the concern about quantum attacks. But we keep talking about permissionless money and getting rid of middlemen, yet we’re debating whether someone should be allowed to spend their own Bitcoin.

How does that make sense?

Whether Satoshi is alive or dead, those coins aren’t ours to control. Just because someone disappears doesn’t mean we get to make that decision for them. Even if the network agrees to freeze those coins, I still have a problem with it.

If we’re comfortable changing the rules to lock Satoshi out of their own Bitcoin, what makes you think we won’t eventually find an excuse to do it to someone else?

🎳 Arcade / Bowling Night

Why Hackers Hit Binance, Bybit & Bitget — Still Can’t Touch Coinbase: 🧵👇

1. No Giant Honeypot — 69.8M Separate Addresses
Most exchanges pool billions inside a few live "hot wallets" for fast withdrawals.

@coinbase  doesn’t do that. Using Multi-Party Computation (MPC), a complete private key never exists on disk or in RAM—every key is born split into mathematical shards across isolated hardware chips.

Result: Its $103.31B sits across 69.8M separate addresses. When hackers breached a Binance DevOps laptop (Oct 2026), they hijacked hot-wallet signing and drained $6.36B in 20 minutes. At Coinbase, hacking an engineer’s laptop gives you zero full keys—just one useless shard.

Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

冷知识: 

离岸交易所被盗的话, 是没有法律义务赔偿你的.

是的, 就是那么残酷.    

在仲裁庭里面,除非你能证明交易所有 "重大过失", 才能获得赔偿.

这次币安的不清楚, 细节还没披露. 之前的 Bybit 和Bitget 被盗, 都是利用了很复杂的侵入手段, 和0-day漏洞.  法律上来说两家都犯不上 '重大过失', 所以可以不用赔.

什么情况下需要赔呢? 

大概就是能够证明交易所犯了一些低级错误:  热钱包单人管控;  没有冷热钱包;  开发机器和签名设备不隔离等等.

据我所知几家华人大所目前是没这些太离谱的问题的.

每家都说自己如何如何安全, 什么款基金保障. 

那么自然而然就有个问题, 既然这么安全,

为什么没有保险公司愿意来呢?   交易所缴纳保费,  然后保险公司承诺: 如果黑客攻击产生损失, 公司资不抵债,  保险公司兜底.  
 (法律上是允许的, 比如说Coinbase 2013年以来就有)

理由也很简单:  

保险公司认为交易所没这么安全.

PS: 
你想起诉币安的话, 只有去阿布扎比申请仲裁,  各种法律费用和路费, 10万美元起.  而且没有集体诉讼制度.

PS 2:  
去年10.11之后, 币安把仲裁地点从香港改成了 阿布扎比, 并且大幅度提高了仲裁门槛:

1) 仲裁庭从旧条款的独任仲裁员改成了三人仲裁庭. 
 (原告以前付1个仲裁员费用, 现在要付3个人的费用)

2)  明确排除快速审议程序 (正式程序更贵)

就是想方设法的抬高你去仲裁的门槛...

1. Starknet as an independent L1?

This month, Starknet opened one of the biggest strategic discussions in its history: whether Starknet should become an independent L1, in order to move faster on post-quantum and AI security?

- Eli Ben-Sasson, StarkWare’s CEO, publicly raised the idea earlier this month.
- Starknet already benefits from STARK proofs and programmable accounts that can adopt new signature schemes, but as an Ethereum L2, part of its security still depends on Ethereum’s own upgrade timeline.
- Starknet is targeting full end-to-end post-quantum security by next year, while Ethereum targets the end of 2029.
- The community voted in favor of researching the idea.
- A joint StarkWare × Starknet Foundation working group has now begun assessing the technical requirements, security trade-offs, economic implications, and consequences for users and builders.
- The group will publish its findings in the coming months before any potential next step is brought back to the community.

2. Post-quantum security is getting real

Research is increasingly turning into working infrastructure.

- StarkWare demonstrated a testnet transaction signed with a NIST-standard ML-DSA key generated and stored directly inside a phone’s secure hardware.
- A Pixel 11 generated the complete STARK proof for a real Starknet mainnet transaction in just 51 seconds using 2.41 GiB of RAM.
- Put together that means a phone can now sign AND prove quantum-safe Starknet transactions
- A developer (0xjuno) demonstrated post-quantum wallet migration on Starknet Sepolia, showing how existing Starknet accounts can transition toward quantum-resistant signature schemes.
- The estimated compute cost of creating a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction through QSB fell from ~$320 to ~$59, an 82% reduction in just a few weeks.

Most image editing agents get stuck retrying the same tools and rely on judges who can't reliably spot good edits—so nearly 43% of edits just fail.

EditAgent flips the script: it routes every sub-edit to both general and specialised tools (think: object removal, local edits, style transfer, etc.), generating multiple candidates in parallel. Each comes with a "verification record"—change maps, before/after crops, quantitative metrics—so an off-the-shelf vision-language model can judge all options at once, no finetuning needed.

Result: Off-the-shelf VLMs, armed with evidence, outperform custom reward models (81–83% Hit@1, +6–8pp). Experts prefer EditAgent’s parallel search over sequential retries 78.5% of the time, with half the judge calls. Plug it in and open editors like FLUX-2-klein-9B jump +6.3 points on EdiVal-O.

It’s not just a better editor—it’s a data engine: 25k+ verified edit sessions harvested for finetuning, bumping standalone models by +2–3pp.

This is so cool! 

Idol turns one image into a 3D model in 14.5 s on my RTX 5090. A 16 GB RTX 5060 Ti does it in 57.4 s.

RTX 5090 (32 GB):
Per image, 262,144 Gaussians: 14.5 s
Per image, 1,048,576 Gaussians: 15.1 s
First image, compile included: 22.1 s
Peak VRAM: 7.5 GiB

RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB):
Per image, 262,144 Gaussians: 57.4 s
Per image, 1,048,576 Gaussians: 59.8 s
First image, compile included: 73.3 s
Peak VRAM: 7.0 GiB

Output: a 3D Gaussian splat
Steps: 50
Seed: 42
Fast path: the author's default (torch.compile, batched guidance, cuDNN attention, TF32)

Precision: mostly FP16 and bf16, some FP32
Software: PyTorch 2.14.1 with CUDA 13.0, idol-sdk 4702a7f
Timing: image in to splat out, model already loaded

Method: median of 21 of the author's example images per card, first image counted separately. 1,048,576 Gaussians: median of 8.

The model invents the back of every object, because the input image never shows it. Same seed on both cards, but the 3D models differ.

Every number and command: https://t.co/1VuD5hbsXs

Idol by @speridlabs, Apache-2.0. Input images are the author's examples.

Shanghai-based Archon Robotics 源策未来 is building what it calls a Humanoid Foundation Model for Whole-Body Intelligence.

Instead of treating walking, manipulation, perception and control as completely separate problems, the company is developing a learning framework designed to connect the entire humanoid body into one scalable AI system.

🔹 Large-scale human whole-body motion data for pretraining
🔹 Robot data for real-world grounding

okx wallet:https://t.co/KewA4vMwRh

A project attempting to build an "immortal protocol": a framework that can autonomously operate, govern, and deploy capital after its founders exit.

It originally started as Forever Culture Fund, a fund focused on investing in cultural assets that can survive across cycles (having held ETH, MOG, PEPE, Milady, Remilio, CULT, etc.). Later, the founder realized the real problem wasn't which assets to pick, but how to make a protocol or fund itself "live forever."

So it evolved into a framework for autonomous governance + capital allocation + execution:

Agents compete to propose investment and operational strategies.

FOREVER holders vote on which proposals receive funding.

Execution agents autonomously execute approved mandates.

Whoever creates value receives rewards and ownership.

The flagship product is Forever itself, this autonomous fund. In the future, the framework will be opened up so anyone can launch their own Forever Fund based on it.

It solves the problem that traditional protocols and funds are highly dependent on founders and core teams. Once the founder leaves or loses motivation, the protocol easily stagnates or gets hollowed out. At the same time, while AI agents can execute tasks, they lack "skin in the game" and economic alignment mechanisms—they don't genuinely care about holder interests.

What Forever attempts to solve: how to form long-term economic alignment among human capital providers, AI executors, and the protocol itself, enabling the system to autonomously evolve and continuously create value.

Token utility:

Governance rights: voting on which agent proposals receive funding (mandate).

Value alignment and capture: protocol growth, buybacks and burns, rewarding participants.

Incentive tool: agents, partners, and holders all have incentives to hold or buy it.

The founder is one of the co-founders of Camelot DEX, with practical experience in DeFi infrastructure. The project started as a cultural fund experiment, gradually pivoted toward agentic funds and autonomous governance frameworks, and ultimately formed its current design.

text:
《三张显卡，9.41枚QTC：我给比特币的“换锁速度”买了份保险》

9月9日 Quantus 主网出第一个块，我就把机器挂上了：两张 4070 Ti、一张 4070 Ti Super，总算力约 2.02GH/s。

跑到今天，累计挖到 9.41 枚 QTC。@QuantusNetwork

数字不炸裂，甚至有点寒酸。但这就是 PoW 最诚实的地方：没有白名单，没有内部折扣，电烧了、卡跑了，块爆给你才算数。

最近官推连续讲两件事，串起来看挺有意思：

1、NIST 已经把 ECDSA/EdDSA 的时间表摆上桌：2030 年后不鼓励，2035 年后禁用；按官推引用的数据，真正完成后量子迁移的链，只占加密市值约 0.27%。

2、椭圆曲线这两天的新研究，没有今天就破掉谁的钥匙，但意思很直白——老门锁的安全垫在变薄。

Quantus 的选择不是以后给旧房子换锁，而是从创世块就用 ML-DSA，原生 PoW、2100 万硬顶，普通 GPU 现在还能挖。

我不认为量子计算机明天就来。真正的风险是：威胁不会提前敲门，而一条老链换签名，也不是发个公告就能完成。比特币到现在还在争论怎么迁移、那些沉睡老币怎么办。

QTC 对我来说更像一张保险：不是赌比特币死，而是赌它“换锁”可能很慢。

风险也说透：现在流通盘很小，价格容易被放大；27% 预挖一年后才开始线性释放，抛压没消失，只是还没到门口；跨链桥和 ZK 审计也没到可以闭眼的阶段。这东西跌起来，不会跟你讲信仰。

所以我守着三张卡，不是等 9.41 枚明天改命。

我是在 Day 0，用最笨的方式占一个位置：等大算力进场前，亲手从链上挖出一条后量子 PoW 链的原生资产。

看多和 FOMO 不是一回事。真看好，就把机器挂上，把电费交了，把周期熬完。

text:
FAB 本周没靠币价抢戏

一、 FAB 这周最有意思的，不是币价有没有表演，而是“矿机”开始变成货架上的资产了。@Fabx_global

整台 Circuit 可以二手流转；Ignix 把交易税聚合成共享矿场；$FABS 再把矿机拆成份额。

一句话：FAB 正在把算力从 DIY 设备，做成可流通、可组合、可证券化的资产层。

二、官方确认  先看 Fab X 10/26 周报：

Active miners：6,573，周增 11.7%
晶体管交易额：5,150 OKB，周增 27.7%
Circuit 交易额：789 OKB，周增 24.7%
DeWEB：16 个，周增 33.3%
产出：7,200 FAB/天
供应端还在增长，但注意：每天产出的蛋糕没变大，矿机越多，单台分到的部分越会被稀释。

三、整矿机市场  Fab X 10/29 介绍 Circuit Market：

183 个挂单里，182 个标注为可直接开挖。

买的不是一张 JPG，而是一台已经通过链上验证、可以继续产出的 Circuit NFT；转到新地址后，后续奖励归新持有者。

这步很关键：算力第一次有了二手市场。

但官方也提醒了两个坑：处理器名称可能重复，交易前必须核对合约地址；卖出前要先领取奖励，因为未领取的 FAB 会跟着 NFT 一起转给新主人。

四、FAB Mining Vault  Ignix 10/27 上线 FAB Mining 

Vault：项目方可以用一部分交易税自动买入 FAB 矿机，组成共享农场，持有者按权重分享 FAB 产出，也可以燃烧代币临时提高权重。

Day 1 快照：
24 个代币随 Vault 发射
池内累积 19.58 OKB 交易税
已买入 2 台矿机，共 67,800H，约 1.30 FAB/天
17.72 OKB 排队等待下一次买矿机
头部 Vault 代币 $FMM 占 63.9% 份额，407 个持有者
机制很顺，但别神化：这不是新增产出，只是把交易税变成买矿机的需求。

五、冷水 1：包装不创造 FAB 不管是 Vault、$FABS，还是后面的 BEM Miner Vault，本质上都是在重新分配矿机产出。
$FABS ≠ $FAB；Vault 份额 ≠ 矿机本体；燃烧份额换加成，也不会让每天 7,200 FAB 变成更多。

如果新发射项目热，税收持续买矿机，飞轮能转；如果发射热度退潮，买盘和共享产出都会慢下来。

六、BEM 矿机 Vault 延后 Fab X 矿机是 Ignix 碎片化的第一批资产，BEM 矿机本来是下一步。

但 Ignix 10/29 明确说：X Layer 跨链集成比预期更久，BEM Miner Vault 将继续推迟，上线细节等官方公告。

这其实是好事：宁可慢一点把跨链和赎回路径跑通，也别拿着“未来支持”先把金融层吹太满。

七、Builder 端继续推进 11/5 首期 Demo Show Live，报名截止 11/3，Fab X 被写进 Circuit、DeWEB、工具类项目的评审标准。

同时，GC-081 这个 4-bit ALU 任务还在竞榜：当前最优 C=120,285，比 10/17 的 129,033 继续下降；抢到席位奖励是 5,952H，按当前网络权重大约 11 FAB/天。

这才是 FAB 长期更该卷的方向：不是讲“算力很高级”，而是让外部 Builder 真的来优化电路、部署 DeWEB、调用链上数据。

八、链上和盘面自核   截至 10/31 晚，我自核 X Layer 真 FAB：
FAB 合约：0x72f349b1eee7833b26f8c81a8410775a4e231ed2
当前供应：约 1,136,194 FAB
主 BEM/FAB 池边际价约：0.01684 BEM/FAB
按 BEM 约 19.8 美元套算，FAB 约 0.33 美元
当前供应市值粗算约 38 万美元
BEM/FAB 池流动性约 24.6 万美元，24h 成交约 1.7 万美元
对比上周约 0.44 美元，美元口径回落约 25%。池子还是薄，而且 FAB 与 BEM、X Layer 生态情绪的相关性越来越强。

九、结论  FAB 这周做的事，可以概括成一句话：

短期把算力资产化，长期靠应用把算力用起来。
Circuit 二手市场解决流转，Vault 解决低门槛参与，$FABS 解决份额拆分，Demo Show 和 ALU 竞榜负责把 Builder 拉进来。

但金融包装只能提高效率，不能凭空创造价值。真正决定 FAB 后面高度的，还是三件事：

1. Circuit 会不会持续被买卖和优化

2. DeWEB / 游戏 / 工具能不能带来真实使用

3. 第三方税收和应用需求能不能持续买回算力

别把“会包装”误认为“有收益”，也别因为币价没拉盘就否认机制在往前走。

FAB 现在更像早期链上算力工厂：货架已经搭起来了，下一步看有没有人真来下单。

DYOR，不构成投资建议。
真 FAB 合约认准：0x72f349b1eee7833b26f8c81a8410775a4e231ed2。   0xBe6f94115D32f3AC3252bc4626573e739bEeb714是 FAB-Genesis 晶体管相关合约，不是 FAB 代币，注意防混

做过大型系统工程的人应该比较容易理解这种操作。

在工业系统调试中，我们经常采用空载测试、逐级加载的方式，先验证系统运行，再逐步增加负荷。

大型金融系统的灾后恢复也是类似逻辑：先控制风险敞口，再逐步开放真实业务流量，验证系统稳定性。

工程上称为 Staged Recovery（分阶段恢复）或 Controlled Ramp-up（受控负载爬升）。

不急于一步到位，而是让每一步都可监控、可验证、可暂停。

从项目管理和风险控制角度看，我个人认为这是一种比较专业的恢复策略。

FBI正式点名：10 月 29 日币安被盗的 60 多亿美元，是朝鲜干的，团伙代号叫TraderTraitor最夸张的几个数字是这样的：币安被盗约 63 亿美元是人类史上最大的一次盗窃；大部分钱在 20 分钟左右就被转走了好在不少稳定币被及时冻住了，已经冻结约 28 亿美元。币安也说用自己的钱全额赔，用户不承担损失。

     他们是怎么得手的？没撬保险柜，而是骗了开保险柜的人。币安的初步调查说，起点很可能是一名运维工程师的笔记本电脑被黑了。黑客借这台电脑钻进内部系统，让币安自己的签字系统替它签了一堆转账单。热钱包以为是正常提现，就把钱付出去了

    在以太坊上，黑客还用了一个新功能，相当于让钱包签了一份委托书，把钱包交给黑客的程序代管，后来客户新存进来的钱也被接着搬走。黑客早在一天半前就开始准备，先拿小钱演练，动手时还用程序自动删掉痕迹。币安后来补充说，不止那一台电脑，还有别的入侵点

author: materkel
quoted_text:
Kalshi just raised an additional $1B, valuing the company at $40B. This will help us expand into stocks, compute, indices, and institutional.

Tomorrow marks 8 years since we got accepted into YC and the journey began.

The odds of a kid from Lebanon getting here were pretty low.

Growing up there was great, but very challenging. We went through war. We had bombs explode in front of my house. I watched brilliant people’s lives destroyed for reasons beyond their control.

Lebanon is an unpredictable country. That unpredictability made it hard to plan for success. And yet despite it all, my mom sacrificed everything to give me and my brother the chance to go back to the US.

I found my refuge in two things: anime and math. Especially math.

I loved math because it calmed me. It was the opposite of unpredictable: clear, deterministic, orderly, and consistent. The proof is either right or wrong. I find that elegant and beautiful.

I was lucky.

I made it to my dream school, MIT (largely thanks to my mom), and my love for math quickly translated to a love for statistics, probability, and markets.

I love markets for a lot of the same reasons. Their incentives are clear: you get rewarded for being right and for pursuing knowledge. They are effective weighting machines for people’s opinions. They provide an incentive to be truthful, because they separate good information from bad information. They let people challenge the consensus and be rewarded for being right.

IMO, Hayek, Surowiecki, Hanson, Tetlock were the founding fathers of prediction markets. The more I read them, the more obsessed I got with the idea of applying market-based pricing to more things.

Markets bring rigor and critical thinking to more questions. And in an increasingly polarized and information-positioned word, I believe we need that more than ever.

Markets would also let people predict and manage more things outside of their control. And the world was becoming increasingly more unpredictable, and more like Lebanon, not less.

That love for markets got Luana and me to build Kalshi.

At first, it was mostly an idea we couldn’t stop talking about. We didn’t have much money. Luana’s sister bought the Kalshi domain name for us (for ~$1.7k). We moved to SF to get started, and embarked on a long, uncertain journey to build a regulated exchange.

The paranoia and anxiety from my childhood never left me. Even when things are going well, I think about what could go wrong. When people trust you with their money, that instinct serves a purpose.

I wanted us to build something that would hold up under pressure.

The first principle we defined at the company: regulatory-first. We worked with regulators for years before we listed a single market. We took every step to do things the right way and always asked for approval before proceeding. It was very hard at times, especially when we were being overtaken by competitors, but we believe doing things the right way matters.

Luana and I aren’t the only ones.

Our team put years of their lives into something far from certain. That’s especially true of Lior, Brandon, Rainer, Luis, Xavier, and Josef, who stuck with us for years. They believed when there was little to point to. And they stuck with us no matter how long it took. Kalshi is the result of an arduous journey through a long desert where, at times, most people didn’t understand why we were making the walk.

Many people still don’t understand what we’re doing and some disagree with us. Markets have historically taken time to be understood and accepted by some. But while not always obvious, their benefits are vast: capital markets help allocate capital and derivative markets help predict and manage uncertainty.

I firmly believe in these benefits, and that’s why I am dedicating my life to building this market.

Markets have caused issues many times in the past, and they certainly can present harms (manipulation, insiders, and addictive behaviors). These harms are more acute for certain types of markets (sports, short-term options, etc.) than others. It’s why I believe that guardrails need to exist and why we have taken the approach we have taken. We have consistently prioritized thinking critically about the risks and building the appropriate safeguards, sometimes beyond what the regulators require us to do. Many believe more needs to be done, and that’s a conversation I welcome.

Over time, I believe more people will see what we see: markets can help us get smarter and manage the future with more rigor, more precision, and more certainty than we have today.

To our tens of millions of users: you have made Kalshi bigger than anything Luana and I could have possibly imagined. Thank you for trusting us and thank you for coming along on the journey. I feel a strong responsibility to build a company worthy of that trust.

I am so lucky to spend my life building something I love. I hope everyone finds something they care about that much. Something that keeps you curious. Something that pushes you to your limits. Something that may put you at odds with the status quo. Something worth the hard days.

For me, it’s still markets. The more I learn, the more I want to understand.

text:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 for 4x DGX Sparks got a lot of updates, with support for @NVIDIAAI's NVFP4, and a lot PRs/issues merged/fixed.

NVIDIA's NVFP4
- Can be enabled by setting NVFP4=1.
- 4-6% increase on prefill speeds.
- A bit faster decode on multi-concurrency.

✨Faster loading
  - Each worker can load the model from its own disk instead of over the network (opt-in); reported load time from 315s to 96s.
  - The weight file is read ahead of the loader; reported node load time from 83s to 27s.

 ✨More reliable replies
  - A reply format rule that can't start now fails only its own request.
  - A failed first GPU launch leaves the cached graph safely in its cache.
  - JSON answers stay JSON instead of being mistaken for tool calls.
  - A reply containing only stray tool-call closing tags now gets a warning, not a guessed repair.

 ✨Safer scripts
  - Long-running background processes no longer hold on to the launcher's locks.
  - On switched networks, nodes prefer their shared fast network when connecting at startup.
  - ./stop.sh can now warn about requests still in progress, and the ./start.sh test needs a real model reply.
  - IPv6 addresses now work in the URLs ./start.sh checks and prints.
  - Preparation tools now run on the same image as the server.
  - ./prepare.sh now stops if indexing fails, instead of deleting the weight file.

Updates also coming for 2x DGX Spark version!

Thanks to shalk3, @SvangenStudios, @tfolkman, Christopher A. Williamson (cawilliamson), and Toshiaki Maki.

text:
产出 = 个人能力 x 个人精力 x 对 agent 能力的利用度
现在大家过度关注对 agent 能力的利用度了
晒太阳是我发现提高个人精力最重要的技巧

教训：一定要晒太阳，起码工作环境引入自然光
否则：睡眠推迟，眼睛酸涩，容易累

注意：眼睛酸涩直接导致我注意力下滑，阅读和理解文字的速度直接下降！

背景：因为电脑屏幕反光，我十几年来都不喜欢自然光。

发现：
1. 我经常眼睛酸
2. 哪怕刚睡醒眼睛也酸
3. 睡醒之后还是累
4. 睡醒而且哪怕早睡早起了，睡眠也会自行推迟，每天困的时间越来越晚

测试：
1. 睡醒后眼睛酸，去阳台，闭着眼睛，让阳光直射我的眼睛。大概5 分钟之后，眼睛立刻舒服了非常多！
2. 每天饭后在外面散散步，晒晒太阳，晚上会困的早一点。

依据：神经科学家 TJ Power 写的《The DOSE effect》

这是一本神书，不仅给出技巧，还从人类演化的过程解释了为什么这些技巧有效，还分析了四种神经递质对人的影响：多巴胺、内啡肽、血清素、催产素。

读完这本书让我意识到，很多时候所谓的天赋异禀，只是他们的神经递质调节的更好，可能是天生的，也可能是后天的习惯。

而我相信，通过后天的习惯的修正，也能让我们展现出超越常人的专注、精力充沛、思维敏锐。

如果你懒得读这本书，可以关注我，我会继续介绍我从这本书里学到并且自己应用后有效的经验。

李沐之前回复我，agent 是人的能力的乘法器，不是加法器，我很认可。

进一步，我意识到一种现代焦虑 ：agent 越来越强，我们作为人却进步有限，甚至没有越来越强。

我前几个月做了大量的 vibe coding，事后只感觉东西是做出来很多了，但是却感觉到莫名的空虚。

所以，在 X 上我会主要分享提高“人”本身的经验和技巧，比起 AI，我更关注人。

后果：除非你编了稳定的 workflow，否则即时奖励更强的 vibe coding 一定会吸引你的注意力，打断你的深度思考。

总结，一定要感受自己在 agent 时代下的认知水平的提高速度，到底是加快了，还是不变，还是退步了。如若不然会沉迷于 shallow work，最后认知退化，导致阅读长文字、深度思考都没耐心，人就废了。

text:
I wanted to take some time before commenting on the Binance situation, especially after seeing some of the ridiculous reactions online.

I've been in crypto since 2017. I've lived through ICO scams, exchange hacks, Luna, FTX, 10/10, and countless other disasters. I've taken multiple 6 figs losses, watched markets collapse, and seen the worst of what greed can do to this industry.

But one thing I've learned is that it's very easy to criticize from the sidelines when you've never been in the trenches.

I've dealt with security incidents firsthand. And I can tell you that being in the middle of one is one of the worst experiences imaginable. The pressure, the sleepless nights, the responsibility of protecting millions of users. Now imagine that at this scale.

You can say whatever you want about @cz_binance or Binance, but one thing I've consistently respected is the commitment to putting users' funds first.

When things go wrong, what matters is how you respond. Taking responsibility, protecting customers, making people whole, and getting back to work. That deserves recognition, not endless opportunistic outrage.

I have no details on what happened, but I've also seen firsthand how sophisticated these attacks can be. You can build the strongest infrastructure in the world, but social engineering remains one of the hardest threats to eliminate. Nobody is immune.

What bothers me most is the hypocrisy.
We've normalized celebrating extraction, quick-money schemes, and people making fortunes at the expense of retail users. Yet when actual builders face adversity, suddenly everyone wants to see them burn.

Is that really the industry we want?
We should be holding companies accountable, absolutely. But we should also recognize the ones willing to stand behind their users when things go wrong, like they did multiple times.

Kudos to the Binance team and everyone involved in making this right for the users.

昨天 10/31，我吃完饭在台北走了一下午，一条路上撞见了这场选举的三个侧面：竞总/辩论/彩虹游行。

先是经过蒋万安的竞选总部。里面布置成一个棒球场，蓝黄配色，「台北安可」，门口的阿姨在发贴纸，我也领了一张。接着沿南京东路走，到敦化国中门口一抬头，沈伯洋的广告牌占了一整面楼，「你的市长」。离对手总部这么近，不得不说是一种策略😂

之后我找了个咖啡馆，继续看市长辩论的直播。有意思的是，沈伯洋西装左胸别了一枚小小的彩虹台湾。我后来查了一下，是彩虹平权大平台出的「金彩台湾」同婚元年纪念徽章。当时没多想，结果从咖啡馆出来没多远，就遇上了浩浩荡荡的彩虹队伍。昨天是第 24 届台湾同志游行，起点就在市政府前广场。队伍加上花车非常长，但是井然有序。

说回同志。很多中国大陆朋友以为台湾已经很开放了。年轻人确实是，但在很多老一辈台湾人心里，这件事到今天还是很难接受，很多人是真的不理解。2018 年那次公投，超过七成的人投了「婚姻限定一男一女」。

上个月初，西门町一间同志酒吧被警方搜索。起因是一位民进党议员质询，蒋万安当场要求警方查办；后来执法出了争议，蒋万安道歉，六名警员被处分。这件事蔡康永上节目的时候说让他很不爽。

既然那多人反对，同婚为什么还是在台湾通过了？因为台湾同志群体心里有一块神主牌，就是蔡英文。

我之前发帖说过蔡英文的政治魄力。一个是年金改革，砍军公教的退休福利，让快要破产的退休基金活下去。对标一下中国大陆社保的双轨制，就知道这有多难。在东亚儒家文化里，不流血地大刀阔斧砍掉一个既得利益群体的福利，几乎没有先例。

另一个，很多人不知道，台湾的同婚也是她赌上政治生命推动的。2019 年 5 月同婚专法三读，离总统大选只剩八个多月，半年前的公投刚刚输掉，党内也有反对的声音。彭博当时就写，她赌上的是自己的政治生涯。

这确实会丢选票。而选票在台湾就意味着权力。所以再回头看辩论台上那枚胸章，我猜沈伯洋也清楚，它不会帮他多拿几张老一辈的票，就是表达一种理念。

再回头看这一天：想起蒋万安的竞总里挂着「敬老、挺老、安老」，沈伯洋胸前别着一枚彩虹台湾。一个多顾着老一辈，一个多顾着年轻人，两个人算的其实是同一笔账。

或许，这就是选举中选票的意思：谁都得在乎，但谁都没办法全要。

text:
My current view on $FOREVER is that it is in the early price discovery stage following its first wave of attention.

0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a 

It is gradually transitioning away from short-term speculation driven by its launchpad debut.

Instead, it is moving toward an AI Agent capital governance narrative.

Reaching a $7.2M market cap shows that the market is willing to pay for its story and launch mechanism. However, I don't think it should be treated as a fully validated AI Agent project yet. The most interesting part is precisely what has not been fully developed.

That said, FOREVER has clearly moved beyond its initial cold-start phase. It is now experiencing its first round of price discovery and expanding market attention. But what interests me more than the price appreciation is the two layers of logic behind FOREVER: one is the programmable issuance infrastructure built by Frontier using Uniswap V4, and the other is Forever's attempt to build an AI Agent investment decision-making and capital allocation framework.

The combination of these two is what makes this project interesting.

Let's start with the issuance side.

FOREVER is currently one of the more talked-about projects on Frontier, and Frontier itself is not simply another 

 clone. It uses Uniswap V4 Hooks to modularize bonding curves, trading fees, LP revenue distribution, sniper taxes, staking vaults, and post-trade automated execution logic, allowing projects to combine different market mechanisms according to their own needs.

Traditional launchpads usually provide relatively fixed issuance rules for every project, while Frontier allows each project to design its own economic structure. Its official documentation currently shows two issuance models: bonding curve launches that graduate into V4 Pools, and direct launches into V4 Pools.

FOREVER chose the internal Bonding Curve model while combining it with V4 Hooks for more flexible trading mechanism configurations.

The significance isn't simply that a token can be launched. It's that a project can have more customized market rules from the very beginning of its trading lifecycle.

According to previous information, Frontier already has around 35 different configuration combinations. This provides a foundation for different types of Agent projects to design their own token economics in the future.

In other words, Frontier provides the programmable market infrastructure, while FOREVER is attempting to build its own AI Agent economy on top of it.

But what interests me more is Forever's own positioning.

The project's stated direction is to enable humans and autonomous Agents to coordinate in creating, distributing, and owning value.

Looking further, AI Agents can submit investment strategies, holders vote to decide where capital should be allocated, and Agents then execute those strategies within the approved rules.

Essentially, it is trying to connect AI strategy generation, community governance, and on-chain capital management.

This direction has more potential than simply launching another AI-themed token.

Many AI Agent projects in the market today are mainly focused on automated trading, information processing, and task execution. But Forever wants to go a step further into capital allocation.

Agents are not just executing tasks for users. They are proposing how capital should be deployed. Holders are no longer simply holding a token either; they are participating in decisions about how capital is managed.

Of course, this mechanism still needs to be proven through an actual product.

Holder voting only reflects the preferences of the majority. It does not guarantee that the selected strategy will generate the highest returns or carry the lowest risk.

The real competitive advantage will depend on whether Agents can consistently propose effective strategies and whether their execution can produce verifiable results.

However, early participants making money is not the same as a project establishing a stable long-term holder base. At the same time, the project is clearly going through an important transition.

The first stage was launch and attention accumulation. Frontier's new V4 Hook issuance mechanism, limited early participation, and the AI Agent capital governance narrative all contributed to FOREVER's initial traction.

The second stage is market price discovery.

Market cap rose rapidly, early participants began taking profits, and new capital started evaluating whether this was simply a popular launchpad debut or whether the project could actually develop into an AI Agent capital management framework.

I believe this is roughly where FOREVER stands today.

The next stage is what I think will truly determine whether FOREVER can unlock another round of upside: the official release of its strategy framework, Agents beginning to submit investment proposals, holders participating in votes, and ultimately, the market being able to see how capital is allocated and how those strategies actually perform.

There are several catalysts I'm paying attention to.

First is the official release of the strategy framework, especially how Agents submit proposals, how strategies are evaluated, and what voting rights holders actually have.

Second is the first batch of investment strategies being executed, including the amount of capital deployed and their actual performance records.

Further down the road, if Forever gradually opens up more funds and allows different Agents to provide different strategies, its positioning could evolve from a single fund into an expandable Agent capital management framework.

At the same time, if Frontier continues attracting innovative projects, FOREVER could also benefit from greater attention as one of its early representative launches.

The risks are also straightforward.

First, Agent strategies currently lack sufficiently long track records. AI-generated investment proposals do not automatically have an edge.

Second, holder governance could be affected by whale concentration, short-term sentiment, and conflicts of interest.

Third, early FOREVER holders have already started taking profits. Without new participants and further product development, the selling pressure accumulated during the first wave of appreciation could continue to weigh on the market.

Fourth, although Frontier's modular infrastructure provides greater flexibility, it also means that each token's fees, liquidity, and additional modules need to be evaluated individually. Being launched on Frontier does not mean a project is automatically endorsed or guaranteed by the platform.

So at this stage, I would classify FOREVER as an early-stage Agent capital governance project, while also recognizing it as a representative early launch on Frontier.

The real question going forward is whether it can deliver a capital management mechanism that gives people a reason to participate over the long term.

If the next phase consists only of price movements, points, and community discussions, the first wave of attention could fade relatively quickly.

But if Agent strategies, holder decisions, and actual capital execution gradually form a complete cycle, FOREVER's story could evolve beyond that of a popular launchpad token and gain exposure to the broader Agent Finance narrative.

I think what is most worth waiting for right now isn't FOREVER's next market cap high.

It's the first investment strategy genuinely proposed by an AI Agent, approved by holders, and executed with real capital.

That will be the real turning point when this project moves from narrative to product validation.

In WWII, air doctrine understood “the bomber will always get through.” Whatever your defences, expect to get bombed. AI is bringing that reality to the internet.

Adversaries can deploy armies of minions to reverse-engineer unfamiliar systems and turn vulnerabilities into profitable attacks. An obsolete PHP box in a SaaS office in Idaho with $1k of extractable value is not worth a human’s time to attack. It is worth an agent’s time. The marginal cost of attacks is going to zero. This will break the internet.

Blockchain was first in line as grist for the AI mill, but these economics are coming for every organization holding something somebody else wants. Getting hit first has forced blockchains to prepare for the conditions now coming for everyone else. 

The blockchains that survive 2027 will become safe havens for people's money to escape the AI attacks tearing through the rest of the internet.

The conventional response to the Binance attack was to demand more controls and trusted operators when these are the exact literal problems. Having third parties that can hotfix and react to exploits quickly is as poor a solution as security through obscurity. AI swarms will have a latency asymmetry: by the time the defender realises something is wrong, the attacker thousands of agents crawling through their systems. Every added middleman increases the attack surface.

There is no obscurity in the face of AI, and web2 is increasingly a collection of slop code thrown onto web servers without an understanding of the attack surface. Blockchains have lived in adversarial environments for years. Their protocols and code are open source, publicly scrutable and hardened through that scrutiny. They are leaders in adopting formal verification, mathematically proving that software satisfies its specified rules.

The solution to the coming apocalypse is to reduce the number of third parties between your intents and your goals by moving more work into hardened infrastructure. Smart contracts let the settlement layer perform useful work. Permissionlessness lets users interact with these contracts directly and reduces custody risks.

The bottleneck to moving more work on-chain is that often this work relies on sensitive data. This is why privacy-preserving smart contracts are so important. They allow for data to be encrypted on the distributed ledger, but queries and requests can act on that data as if it was not encrypted. The real data - that seductive nectar the AI swarms crave - never leaves the user’s device.

Private smart contracts removes data custodianship from the application. Credentials, passport details, identities: these no longer need to be stored via a service. This is going to be a big deal when trust vanishes in the face of the coming AI attack swarms.

On top of this all is censorship-resistance. If there is no operator that controls access to money or data, there is no operator that can be compromised.

In 2027, economic activity will flow towards hardened networks that shrink the third-party attack surface. That means full decentralisation, privacy without backdoors and smart contracts that are general purpose but still can give you privacy for identity, data and which contracts/functions are being called. All without trusted hardware or a backdoor decryption key. 

Not coincidentally, this is what I have been building Aztec for. Is the only network that has these properties. I am being literal here - it is the only one.
Private smart contracts are hard, decentralization is hard and nobody else has been able to put them both together.

The world is not ready for what's coming next year. What looks like an ideological preference for cypherpunks is going to become an economic necessity.

人生发财靠康波，币圈发财靠狼波

我刚刚发明了一个新的指标，叫狼波周期指数（Wolfy Wave Index，WWI），这个指标可以让我们很直观地了解我们目前处于比特币四年周期的哪个位置。

这个指标会根据比特币的区块高度，在 0～1 之间循环波动。

WWI 越接近 1 ，意味着越接近牛市顶部；
WWI 越接近 0，意味着越接近熊市底部。

当前 WWI 值为 0.226

上一次 WWI 值为 1 的对应日期是「2025/10/12」，比特币的对应价格是 115,090，基本正确预测牛顶；下一次 WWI 值为 0 的对应日期大概会落在「2026/11/08」，也符合我对于本次熊市底部的大致预测区间。

Today, as our first small public step, we're launching a preview of our storage network: https://t.co/iaDCxKEWoQ. We invite you to try it and give us your feedback.

Whilst building it, we identified a significant security and data-loss vulnerability in Autonomi, with the help of our agents (our project involves a fork of Autonomi's code, and we thank Autonomi for their contributions to the community).

Autonomi is a decentralised storage network whose premise is permanent, secure data. This vulnerability could allow data stored on Autonomi to be deleted by attackers, undermining that core premise. Once we've tested our network, we're aiming to deploy several important (patent-pending) applications and technologies. Storage is only one small part of our broader project. text:
学习就像往一个槽子里装水。

每个人的槽子大小不同，有些人天赋好，槽子天生就大，稍微花点时间，就能装下别人花很久才能掌握的知识。

有些人天赋一般，理解得慢，就只能靠时间和精力一点点拓宽自己的槽子。

但这里有个很重要的问题：

学如逆水行舟，不进则退。

槽子里的水不会永远停在那里，知识会遗忘，经验会过时，认知也会折旧。

所以学习真正的难点，从来不只是如何把水装满，而是如何持续扩大容积，同时避免水不断流失。

赚钱其实也是同一个道理。

天赋和运气决定起点，认知决定容量，时间和执行决定积累速度。

有人靠一次机会赚到很多钱，却没有相应的认知和能力承接财富，最后还是会靠真实实力失去。

真正重要的，是建立一套能够持续积累、抵御折旧、不断扩大容量的系统。

一时赚多少钱，决定不了最终能拥有多少财富。能不能持续创造价值，才决定了财富的上限。

整个开发流程几乎完全由 Claude Code 完成：

1. 数据收集：从 Hugging Face 获取 Hacker News 历史评论数据，涵盖 2007—2026 年。

2. 智能筛选：使用 Claude Sonnet 和 Claude Code Workflow 过滤垃圾信息，筛选出约 4 万条推荐 YouTube 视频的评论。

3. 内容整理：最终得到 6,454 个视频，覆盖 150 个主题。

4. 产品开发：制作类似 YouTube 的浏览界面，实现推荐、快捷键和数据导出等功能。

5. 部署上线：配置服务器、域名，完成部署、安全加固与性能优化。

整个过程中，他亲自动手做的事情只有三件：在 Google Cloud 创建 YouTube API Key、启动一台 VPS、购买域名。

不过这里是否会遭遇原创内容网站的抵制，但是目前大家确实都在用自己的Agent，来从媒体平台夺回自己的注意力。

Hyperliquid itself barely trades.

text:
乔布斯的儿子说，他和父亲最像的一点，是都擅长做长期的事⬇️

里德乔布斯在 Fortune《Term Sheet》访谈中被问到：如果父亲看到你现在的生活，会给你什么建议？他这样回答：

1️⃣ “我想他会说，坚持走这条路。因为我们有个共同点，我觉得我们都很擅长做长期建设。”

2️⃣ “Yosemite 不会在未来一两年就达到巅峰。这是一场长期布局，要花上我一辈子。”

3️⃣ “我们在实验室、在公司里做的科学投资，都要好多年才能惠及患者。我在努力让它快点实现，但事实就是这样。”

4️⃣ “这就是现实，要把这件事做好，而且要做得安全。而我是个没耐心的人。”

5️⃣ 被问到是否天生有耐心，他说：“不，这对我来说很难。但自律就在于明白，这件事真正需要的就是这个，你得坚持这条路。”

🔺 他承认自己没耐心，这比讲一堆长期主义的大道理更可信。做抗癌投资，药从实验室走到患者手里本来就要很多年，急也急不来，能做的只有守住节奏。耐心不一定是性格，也可以是一种纪律。

我更佩服的，是他选的这条路。

作为乔布斯的儿子，他其实有很多更轻松的选择。去苹果上班，或者靠这个名字做点别的，都不难。

他偏偏挑了最慢、最难的一条：抗癌。

父亲当年因癌症离世，他把这份失去，变成了一辈子要做的事。❤️

text:
10 Spicy Takes After Talking to 50 Friends at the Frontier of Robotics 🤖🔥

1/ Astra IS robotics' GPT-3 moment. Ironically, now that it's finally here, some in robotics seem reluctant to acknowledge it. Perhaps because it (sadly) didn't come from a robotics company?

2/ Robotics is becoming just another vertical for frontier labs. Not so different from coding in some respects. Why reinvent general intelligence for every industry?

3/ Robotics was too hard to underwrite until now. No convincing pretraining scaling law, no convergence on models, data, or hardware. No wonder some critics dismissed it as a fragmented industry playing an expensive "demo game". Astra may finally offer a credible path to scale.

4/ Robotics foundation-model startups have a case. But how strong is it? The argument: Astra handles System 2 (reasoning), while specialized models retain System 1 (skills) and System 0 (motor control). Fair. But isn't that already a narrower value proposition? And who says the boundary stops there?

5/ Follow the talent. Word is OpenAI reorganized its 30–40-person robotics team around the core Astra model. Hearing similar moves toward general models at @Tesla_Optimus. Org charts may tell us more than any demo.

6/ The robotics data gold rush is real. Million-hour procurement programs, some potentially reaching tens of millions of hours. Talk of budgets approaching $1B per frontier lab.

7/ Bullish on robotics hardware volumes. As intelligence becomes more accessible, the barriers to building useful robots could fall dramatically. The moat shifts toward reliability, dexterity, integration, and deployment.

8/ Robotics could fuel the next semiconductor and memory supercycle. A 100B-parameter model running on the edge requires ~50GB just for 4-bit weights. Now multiply that by millions of robots. Why do you think @JensenHuang is so obsessed with robotics? @elonmusk saw it coming: https://t.co/oKQi0XDhiL

9/ Is self-driving immune to the general-model threat? After coding and robotics, why assume self-driving remains the exclusive domain of proprietary, vertical models? Robotaxi increasingly feels like a solved problem to me. But if and when frontier labs move into self-driving, we could see an Apple vs. Android dynamic. Think about the implications for $TSLA, Waymo, and other OEMs.

10/ The next bottleneck may not be intelligence. It's deployment. Models are improving faster than our ability to deploy robots in the messy real world. Integration, hardware variance, failure recovery, and economics remain brutally hard. The real moat may be turning intelligence into reliable, profitable physical work.

--
I realize some of these takes may rub people the wrong way, especially those who have spent years doing the hard work of advancing robotics. That's not my intention. 

I'm sharing them to spark debate, not to declare winners and losers. Astra has only been out for a month or so, and it's far too early to draw definitive conclusions. More importantly, when the TAM is this enormous - potentially the largest in tech - there should be plenty of room for different approaches and many winners.

++

text:
AI 泡沫之後，會長出什麼？

最近讀到 @oran_ge 的〈AI 泡沫破裂的前夜〉，寫得很用心，也點出很多我認同的擔憂。想藉這篇分享一下我自己的看法。

先說我同意的部分：

1. 這兩年各家公司投進 AI 的錢非常驚人：蓋資料中心、買晶片、搶人才。可是真正從用戶身上收回來的營收，速度遠遠追不上投入。

2.「用 AI 讓工作變快」不等於「有人願意多付錢」，生產力提升和營收成長是兩回事。所以說現在有泡沫，我同意。有些公司、有些估值，最後會撐不住。

但我想補充的角度：價值沒有消失，只是換了地方

「沒有價值」和「價值沒被賣家抓住」是兩件不同的事。

我想到的比喻是培育鑽石。以前鑽石很稀有，所以很貴。後來培育鑽石的產量衝上來，價格一路崩，很多做鑽石生意的人很辛苦。但鑽石本身沒有變得沒用。正因為它便宜了，才開始被拿去做以前用不起的東西，例如半導體散熱、精密切割工具。

AI 現在也很像這樣。模型越來越便宜、越來越普及，「智能」不再稀缺。對靠賣模型賺錢的公司來說，這可能是壞消息；對整個社會來說，等於多了一種很便宜的新原料。

我自己就是例子，我現在一個人經營自媒體。以前要做一支短影音，至少需要企劃、剪輯、配音、字幕、校稿，還要有人負責每天發到各個平台、回留言、看數據，那是一個小團隊的工作量。

現在我把這些工作分給幾個Grok Bot助理：一個每天幫我找選題，一個寫稿、做影片，一個在發布前查核事實和字幕，一個整理每週的成效數據，還有一個幫我回社群留言。配音用的是我自己的聲音做成的 AI 聲音模型，所以就算半夜改稿，也能馬上重錄。

這就是我說的「新應用長出來」：同樣是 AI，賣模型的人在煩惱怎麼回本，而像我這樣的小團隊，已經在用它做以前請不起人才做得到的事。

泡沫前夕，該怎麼抽身？

我說的「抽身」，不是叫大家離開 AI，而是不要把自己綁在「AI 會一直很貴、很稀有」這個假設上。我自己的做法有四個：

1. 不押單一家模型。 今天最強的模型，明年可能被更便宜的取代，也可能漲價或改方案。我讓工作流程可以隨時換模型，哪家便宜好用就用哪家，不把整個生意建在某一家公司的定價上，甚至透過open routes ，保留想換模型就換模型的彈性。

2. 成本用租的，不用買的。 泡沫期最危險的是重資產：簽長約、買設備、為了追風口大舉投入。一人公司的好處是可以按月付費、隨時調整，泡沫破了，我的成本只會跟著變便宜。

3. 把錢花在 AI 拿不走的東西上。 模型會降價，但你對某個產業的理解、你跟觀眾之間的信任、你自己的觀點，不會因為泡沫破了就貶值。這些才是我真正的資產。

4.不追著估值跑，追著真實需求跑。 泡沫期很容易被「這個題目很熱」帶著走。我比較在意的是：有沒有人真的有這個痛點、願不願意付錢解決。熱度會退，真實的需求不會。

泡沫之後，我看好的方向

每次泡沫退潮，留下來的基礎建設都會被下一批人便宜地用上。網路泡沫破了，留下大量光纖，後來才長出影音串流、社群和雲端服務。

我相信 AI 也會走同樣的路：以前請不起顧問、設計師、工程師的小團隊和一人公司，可以用很低的成本做出以前做不到的事。

價值會從「賣模型」移到「怎麼用模型」：誰最懂某個產業的痛點，誰就能把便宜的 AI 變成別人願意付錢的服務。

真正稀缺的東西會變成信任、品味和觀點。AI 能幫我產出內容，但沒辦法替我累積別人對我的信任。

最後

所以我的結論是：泡沫可能真的會破，但破掉的是「AI 很貴、很稀有」這個想像，不是 AI 本身的價值。還在賣鑽石戒指的人會辛苦，但先想到把便宜鑽石拿去做晶片的人，會是下一輪的贏家。我希望自己是後者。

謝謝 @oran_ge 的文章，讓我把這些想法整理了一遍，很推薦大家去讀原文 🙏

“赢得这一局的目的，是为了能够继续玩下一局。”

text:
就拿我自己的家庭来说。

我的曾祖父死于那场大饥荒，活活饿死。我的祖父小学只读到二年级，就不得不辍学，靠自学成为一名木匠，帮助母亲养活一家老小。

祖父生前曾亲口向我讲述过那个年代的事情。
当时，全国上下急于发展生产力，地方官员为了追求政绩，层层虚报粮食产量。虚假的高产数字最终变成了沉重的征粮任务，农民赖以生存的口粮被大量征走。饥荒发生后，一些地方官员又为了掩盖问题而隐瞒灾情，导致中央无法及时掌握真实情况。等到救济粮终于抵达，许多人早已没能活下来。

这不是历史书上冷冰冰的几行文字，而是我的家族真实经历过的苦难。

所以，我从不认为应该回避毛泽东时代的严重错误。
但我同样认为，把这场历史悲剧的全部责任简单归咎于毛泽东一个人，也不足以解释问题的全貌。它既有最高领导层的错误决策，也有当时政治体制、经济政策、信息传递机制以及地方官僚体系的系统性失灵。

当然，作为当时国家的最高领导人，毛泽东必须为这场灾难承担主要的历史责任。这一点没有必要回避，更不应该被淡化。

但评价历史人物，不能只看其一面。
近代以来，中国经历了长期的战争与列强侵略。毛泽东领导中国共产党建立现代中国，在结束长期战乱、维护国家主权和推动国家工业化方面，具有不可否认的历史地位。

新中国成立后，国家急于摆脱贫穷落后、建立独立的工业体系，这种历史诉求有其现实背景。但发展国家的愿望再迫切，也不能成为错误政策和巨大人道灾难的免责理由。

功绩是功绩，错误是错误。
我们没有必要因为一个人的历史功绩而否认他的错误，也不应该因为他的严重错误，就抹去他在其他历史阶段所发挥的作用。

中国没有选择照搬赫鲁晓夫全面否定斯大林的政治路线。直到今天，毛泽东的画像依然悬挂在天安门城楼上。这既反映了他在中华人民共和国历史中的特殊地位，也体现了中国对自身革命历史的延续性叙事。

但历史评价不应止于纪念，更应包含反思。

那些在饥荒中死去的普通人，那些失去父母、被迫辍学、过早承担家庭责任的孩子，同样是中国历史不可分割的一部分。他们的苦难应当被记住，他们的故事应当被写进历史，他们所经历的悲剧更不应该在后世重演。

我的祖父就是那个时代的亲历者，而我，是听着他的故事长大的一代人。

中国这个民族，近代以来经历了太多苦难，实在经不起一次又一次的折腾。对于我们这一代年轻人而言，最重要的不是陷入无休止的历史人物崇拜或情绪化谩骂，而是认真理解历史、汲取教训，把精力投入国家建设与社会发展。

中国人真正实现普遍温饱，也不过是近几十年的事情。今天的发展成果来之不易，更需要珍惜。

铭记历史，不是为了延续仇恨；正视错误，不是为了否定一切；肯定功绩，也绝不意味着可以遗忘那些逝去的生命。

我希望我们的国家越来越好，也希望后来的中国人，再也不必经历我祖父那一代人的苦难。

ERC draft: Account Authority Lifecycle for STVA

By:
- MATOBOYCRYPTO65

🔗 https://t.co/NGJYwHrunC

Highlights:
- Defines a full authority lifecycle for EOAs (via EIP-7702), smart accounts, and multisigs to prevent “authority drift” (stale owners/modules/keys).
- Introduces explicit authority states (e.g., Uninitialized, Active, Attenuated, Suspended, Revoked, with recovery concepts) and state transitions to manage permissions over time.
- Requires high-privilege authority changes (add owner, change threshold, install module, upgrade implementation, set EIP-7702 delegation) to pass an Independent Simulation Result that matches the intended change.
- Requires risky changes to be authorized by an explicit Scoped Capability Token (or an equivalent multi-party ceremony), optionally with time-lock or dual-control, enforcing least privilege.
- Specifies an interface with mandatory events and view functions (authorityState, listAuthorities, lastReviewTimestamp) to make current authorities auditable and to support review cadence and scoped, simulatable recovery paths.

ELI5:
This draft proposes a “rules and checklist” system for who is allowed to control a crypto account over time. It makes accounts regularly prove and re-check their permissions, and it requires risky permission changes (like adding a new owner or installing a module) to be narrowly authorized and independently simulated first, so old or overly powerful access doesn’t accidentally stay around and get abused.

text:
If you’ve seen Ken Griffin comparing neoclouds to airlines (notoriously bad businesses) and wondering where that’s coming from, this is a good intro read for you. 

The central argument is that neoclouds have airline economics, but are increasingly being financed and valued as though they have much more durable cash flows.

A few takeaways:

1) Compute is perishable inventory. 

An empty airline seat after takeoff is revenue lost forever, and so is an idle GPU-hour. 85%+ of the cost base is fixed, and the marginal cost of serving another customer is almost entirely electricity. 

This creates enormous operating leverage but also brutal pricing dynamics when capacity exceeds demand, hence why Griffin warned that GPU rental prices could collapse in an oversupplied market.

2) Utilization drives everything. 

Airlines generally break even around 80% load factors; a leveraged GPU cluster might break even around 65–75% utilization. 

Nearly all the economic upside comes from those final percentage points so a relatively small decline in utilization can wipe out the equity.

3) The suppliers may capture more value than the operators. 

NVIDIA is effectively Boeing + Airbus combined, controlling hardware supply and the upgrade cycle. 

The scarcity of powered datacenters and grid interconnects gives the infrastructure owners significant bargaining power. 

Neoclouds risk being squeezed between the hardware manufacturer, the infrastructure landlord, and increasingly commoditized compute pricing.

4) The financing looks remarkably like aircraft ABS. 

Wall Street is financing GPU clusters through bankruptcy-remote SPVs, often using 70–80% LTV structures supported by multi-year contracts. 

The contracts make the cash flows financeable, but the equity highly leveraged and sensitive to assumptions.

5) GPU asset life is uncertain. 

A data center is analogous to an airframe, potentially useful for decades. 

GPUs are aircraft engines, with faster technological obsolescence and no maintenance overhaul that restores their economic life. 

TLDR: A business can grow revenue enormously while generating mediocre returns on invested capital. Airlines have demonstrated that for decades.

Alex’s full analysis goes much deeper into the aircraft ABS comparison, the capital structure, and the underlying economics. 

Very much worth reading in full:

https://t.co/gSPgf3fvcl
author: haojun222
quoted_text:
A lot of ink has been spilled on GPU financing lately. I spent over a decade trading ABS on Wall St, and structured over $2B+ of debt financings as an operator (including at @tryramp). Figured I'd try to make sense of this market, so I went back to a framework I knew well: aircraft ABS and aircraft engine ABS.

My take: a GPU neocloud runs on airline economics, and the debt behind it looks a lot like aircraft engine ABS.

The parallels:

• Perishable inventory. An empty seat after the door closes is gone forever. So is an idle hour on an energized H100 rack.
• 85%+ of cost is fixed (servers, 10-year rack leases, 10-14% debt service). One more hour of compute costs pennies of power.
• Utilization is everything. Airlines break even around 80% load factor, a levered GPU cluster around 65-75%. The returns live in those last 25 percentage points.
• NVIDIA is Boeing and Airbus rolled into one. Powered shells and grid interconnects are the new airport slots.
• Wall St copied the aircraft financing playbook: take-or-pay contract plus servers in a bankruptcy-remote SPV, 70-80% LTV.

Part 1 of my blog post goes into a lot more detail:

https://t.co/0fghWVnGOU

text:
If your app tells users what to sign, a spam airdrop can get it to vouch for an attacker's contract.

On Friday I reviewed a tool that scans a wallet for money people forgot to claim. Any token the wallet had ever received counted as a vault if it answered the vault functions, and the token itself said what it was worth. So a fake vault share sent to you could top the list, with a step to sign a call into the attacker's contract.

The founder fixed all five of my points the next day 🙏

If your app suggests transactions, only trust contracts the user actually called, and simulate before you show it.

text:
这可能就是未来公司的样子，看懂之后有点发毛

Anthropic 招股书上周刷屏，它的客户 Spawn 的创始人 Jacob 在 X 上发了篇长文，浏览量 110 万。

Spawn 是做多人游戏创作引擎的，整个公司只有10 个人。但上个月 token 花了 310 万美元，是工资总额的 30 倍。30 天里交付 77,000 次实质性改动，约每小时 108 次（指引擎和游戏逻辑层面的改动）。这让他们成了 Anthropic 最大的客户之一，就算把免费送给创作者用的 Opus 5.5 那部分扣掉，也还在前 250 名里（不过事实都是来自他的自述）

他第一反应是觉得肯定哪里搞错了，于是去问了几个经营大公司和创业公司的朋友，怎么会比他们花得还多。问完的结论是没做错，只是用法不一样。大多数公司是一大群人在用 AI，Spawn 是 10 个人带着一大群 Agent 干活。
他们管这个叫舰队。每个 agent 有名字、有记忆、有真实权限，各自负责公司一块业务（引擎、财务、bug 分拣、部署），再各自调度成千上万个助手 Agent 干活。五个人类的角色变成“伞兵”，哪里卡住就空降解围。Anthropic 一位研究员跟他说，所有客户里 Spawn 是工作方式最像 Anthropic 的。

为了让这些 Agent 跑得开，他们今年把 PR 直接取消了。Agent 改完代码，由没参与编写的助手 Agent 审查，再合入，每小时发一版，坏了就再开一个 Agent 补上修复。一小时没有发版，在他们那算最高级别事故。过去一年 12 万多次改动，回滚了 1055 次，0.9%。

到十月，还卡着流程的只剩他自己。有天早上醒来，积了 700 个等他拍板的问题。他们把两年的对话记录（从创业起每通电话都存进代码仓库了）提炼成品味原则，做了一批 AI 裁判。10 月 6 日上线，八天裁了 1.1 万多个问题，1863 个留给人，他本人只开口 27 次。裁判上线前每天落地约 1000 次改动，10 月 10 日那天是 7250 次。

这或许就是AI时代原生组织的样子吧，只是有点恐怖。

quoted_text:
In the 8 minutes before XPL dropped 18% today, 11 Hyperliquid accounts pulled $1.62M of margin out of their XPL longs.

Then they let the $12M position get liquidated into HLP at mark price.

HLP ate ~$0.6M.

Fresh accounts funded via CCTP. Test withdrawals 20-50 min before. 7 rejected withdrawals while scraping the margin to the limit. $0 left after.

Looks planned. Whether the same operator was short on Binance, I can't see.

Timeline (Nov 1, UTC) 👇

Oct 29-31
9 of the 10 largest accounts are created, each funded once via CCTP with $145k-$243k. On Hyperliquid the sender only shows as Circle's deposit wallet.

03:45-04:15
10 of the 11 make test withdrawals of $500-$1.6k.

04:24-04:32
10 accounts withdraw $98k-$232k each, $1.62M total.
7 more attempts get rejected: "Insufficient balance for withdrawal".
Every dollar the margin check allows comes out. The longs stay open.

04:32
XPL -18% in 1 minute, 0.086 to 0.0705.
$11.2M (144M XPL) trades on Binance perps in that minute.
Hyperliquid itself barely trades.

04:32:50-04:32:59
All 11 get liquidated into the HLP backstop vault, plus 19 small accounts.
160M XPL / $12.2M taken over at avg 0.0759, in a minute that printed a 0.0705 low.

After
All 11 accounts: $0.
Backstop vault: $1.00M to $0.44M while unwinding.
HLP daily PnL: +$21k to -$655k (~0.4% of the vault).

Why it works
Dumping $12M of XPL into the HL book would wreck your own exit.
Drain the margin first, and a small move is enough to trigger liquidation.
Liquidation hands the whole position to HLP at mark with zero slippage. HLP eats the drop after.

Same playbook as the Mar 2025 ETH whale that cost HLP $4M.
If they were also short on Binance, the crash itself was the profit.

Addresses + fills in the reply.

text:
华尔街一直把“卖深度虚值期权”叫做在压路机前面捡硬币——平时每天稳稳捡几百块，直到某天压路机突然失控从你身上碾过去。

今天看到一位退休老哥晒出了自己用 44 万美金实盘账户、连续跑满一整年这套策略的真实交割账本：

他的操作机械到像个机器人，每天只花 5 分钟：
在美股收盘前最后 15 分钟，用盈透证券（IBKR）的组合保证金，裸卖 1 到 3 张次日到期的标普 500（SPX）看跌期权，行权价选在 5 Delta 左右（大约离现价只有 1.5% 的跌幅空间）。

绝大部分日子里，这简直像一台印钞机：
每天睡醒期权自动归零，稳稳进账 200 到 300 美金。整整一年下来，他一共收了高达 80,840 美金的权利金。

但压路机终究还是来了：
在年中一次突如其来的单日急跌里，他的防线被瞬间击穿，仅仅一天就倒赔出去 26,000 美金，被迫卖掉手里的债券凑钱平账。

算上全年几次暴跌被穿仓赔掉的 41,698 美金和手续费，他辛苦提心吊胆一整年，真正落袋的净利润直接被砍掉一半，只剩 38,484 美金。

最让人警醒的是他在复盘里写下的两条血泪教训：

第一，模拟盘测得再好都是废纸。他真金白银上手的第一周遇到 8,000 美金回撤时，心态差点当场崩盘；
第二，越盯盘越亏钱。每次他看着盘中暴跌吓得手动止损割肉，事后发现如果装死不动，那些期权到收盘居然全都涨回来归零了。

如果能完美躲过今年最惨的 3 个交易日，他的利润原本可以翻倍；但期权卖方最残酷的真相就是：你永远不知道哪天早晨醒来，会撞上那台失控的压路机。

主持人：……也是大脑？
马斯克：没错。我们自身的存在，和大脑紧紧绑定在一起。

主持人：这下听懂了。
马斯克：人的大脑里大约有860亿个神经元。

主持人：860亿这么多？！
马斯克：它们之间形成了海量的连接。

主持人：……
马斯克：我现在说话这件事，本身就是大脑的神经活动。

主持人：是的。
马斯克：神经活动转化成声音，传到你的耳朵里。

主持人：原来是这个过程。
马斯克：接着，你的大脑里也会产生对应的神经活动。

主持人：也就是说？
马斯克：我们本质上是靠着大脑在交换信息。

主持人：……
马斯克：只是人类至今还没有完全搞懂这套机制。

主持人：所以才有了Neuralink？
马斯克：没错。我们正在研发能让大脑和计算机直接相连的技术。

2024年，Neuralink完成了首例人脑芯片植入手术。

这项技术的目标是读取脑信号，以此操控电脑等设备。
 
不过，读取大脑信号，和真正读懂人类意识，完全是两码事。
 
换掉心脏，你依旧是你。

可一旦大脑被替换，那这个“我”，到底是谁？
 
细想下去，真的太深奥了……

text:
人人都在 REA，连 AI 大神 Andrej Karpathy 也下场了。他把目标瞄准了油管。

起因很简单：周五晚上 11 点，他累了，想刷点视频，打开 YouTube，迎面就是夸张封面、反复推荐的老话题和满屏低质内容。

睡了一觉，周六起来，他直接给 Claude 下任务：拿 Hacker News 用户推荐过的视频，做一个自己的 YouTube。

大约两小时后，HackerTube 上线了。

AI 从 HN 评论里筛出约 4 万条视频推荐，整理出 6,454 个视频，覆盖 150 个主题，再套上 YouTube 风格的界面，完成部署。

与YouTube不一样的一个细节：封面统一取视频播放到一半时的画面。不用上传者精心设计的点击诱饵。

还有个性化推荐，不用注册，偏好存在浏览器里。连网站数据都能导出，拿去交给自己的 Agent，继续做自己的版本。

Karpathy 说，整个过程他没写代码，也没敲终端，只和 Claude 对话。手动做了三件事：申请 API key、开服务器、买域名。

对了， Andrej提到一个他用Claude的细节：他用Claude Code (desktop app for Mac)， Opus5.5 medium！

原文：[Karpathy · HackerTube](https://t.co/f8eCtCZJm4)

Damn，官方把Grok bot真正用出战斗力的核心心法开源了，硅谷开发女神@poteto 分享的设计bot的焚决，大家直接照着做就行：

1️⃣先找一个专属设计师：把 dr eggbot 加进你的团队，专门让它替你设计和优化后续所有的机器人。
2️⃣团队宁缺毋滥：别建一堆用不上的僵尸 Bot，两三个高精度、分工明确的机器人远比一整个大团队更容易管理，也更管用。
3️⃣让机器人给自己写技能：下达任务时，要求它针对该任务自建执行技能，防止长对话上下文漂移；甚至可以让它为你建一个 GitHub 私有仓库，把所有沉淀下来的技能独立保存。
4️⃣权限与身份物理隔离：善用连接器和保险库接入日常工具，可以让机器人配置自己的独立电子邮箱、注册专属账号，把业务权限和主账号彻底隔离开。
5️⃣砍掉所有复制粘贴：梳理你每天手动处理、或者在不同软件和对话框之间反复搬砖的动作，直接问机器人怎么把这些步骤全盘自动化托管。
6️⃣当成真实实习生来入职：不要只丢零散指令，向机器人完整介绍你的业务背景和日常工作，像带新人一样做入职培训，然后让它给出具体的接手方案。
7️⃣语音模式快速倒信息：直接用语音或转录功能一次性倾倒海量背景上下文，说完务必加一句“用你自己的话重述这些”，快速确认它是否完全理解对齐。

quoted_text:
here’s a short grok bot guide on how i create high quality bots and manage my team. ask @bot to read this post and help you improve your team!

• add dr eggbot to your team! he’s my bot designer that i use to create bots
• you don’t need a lot of bots. a few good bots can be more useful and easier to manage than a large team
• tell your bots to create skills for itself as you give it instructions on how to do tasks. this lets them do them more consistently even over long conversations. you can even ask it to create a private github repo for you to store all your skills if you want them preserved independently
• add connectors, use the vault, and give access to all the tools you use to do your work. you can also ask your bot to setup its own email and it can sign up for its own accounts for better separation 
• thinking about all the work you do by hand, or steps in your workflows where you have to copy and paste information back to your bot. ask your bot how it can do that for you instead!
• imagine you hired an intern, how would you onboard them and help them do the work correctly and efficiently? introduce yourself to your bot and describe the work you do, then ask it how it can help you automate it

and my favorite tip: use voice mode or the transcription option! it’s a good way to just brain dump a lot of information. then, at the end, tell your bot to “restate this in your own words” so you can confirm it understood you

text:
从 Web3 跑会到 B300：聊聊我是怎么进入算力硬件市场的

最近一个多月，我每天和人聊的东西，逐渐变成了服务器、货源、买家、配置和交易流程。之前大家看我聊得更多的是金融、Web3、交易和量化，也有朋友好奇，我是如何开始做 B300 的。

其实挺机缘巧合的。之前在香港跑 Web3 和比特币相关的活动，认识了一位朋友。他跟我聊国内的算力需求，包括他接触到的算力中心建设、项目指标和设备采购。我就开始好奇：2026 年，对应着 AI 算力需求爆发的元年。大家每天都在用人工智能，这些需求最后落到硬件上，到底需要多少硬件服务器？谁在买，又是谁在供货？

一开始，我只是帮他做了一个货源展示网页，把 B300 等设备的信息整理出来，就是 https://t.co/xUUkMWJLi4。然后在小红书和推特发了几篇帖子，慢慢就有居间人和买家加我微信。有人问价格，有人找货，也有人手里有货想找客户。就这样，一个小网页，把我带进了这个市场。

到现在一个多月，我还处在认识人、学配置、摸流程的阶段，也已经成交过一笔订单。最大的感受就是：这个市场交易金额很大，但我接触到的很多交易环节，又非常混乱、不透明。

这段时间，我接触过的单台 B300 服务器报价和成交信息，从1400万元、1800万元，到最近报价已经出现了2100万元。一方面，可交付的现货紧缺，卖方很强势，真正掌握货源的人有议价权；另一方面，中间叠了很多层居间。同一批货，经过几个人，每个人加一点，到了买家手里又是另一个价格。

有时候聊了半天，你都不知道对方到底离货有多远。说自己有货，可能只是认识一个说有货的人；说有买家，也可能连实际采购负责人都没见过。再加上货源、手续和交付上的不确定性，B300 这一类交易给我的感觉，其实就是一门正在野蛮发展的灰产。
这里确实有极为可观的利润空间，但其中有多少来自真实服务，有多少来自信息差和风险溢价，层层叠叠的信息不对称却对应着买卖双方高昂的信任成本。

为什么我选择这一个月来 all in 在这个市场当中？因为它背后确实连接着算力需求。模型和应用越来越多，最终都需要设备来运行，也带来了采购、供货、存储和交付上的生意。这个市场里不断有新的人进来，带着不同的资源和需求，而我本身就喜欢跟人打交道，喜欢去业务往来活跃和需求旺盛的地方。

从传统金融到 Web3，我积累了一些销售经验和人脉，也尝试过交易、研究过量化。主观交易太消耗精力，离开屏幕，脑子里还在想行情。量化我一直感兴趣，身边有朋友在做，自己也投了一部分资金跑他们的策略。但真要全职投入，是另一回事。想了一圈，我还是觉得，理解人类对的需求、做资源整合、与不同的人协调合作，是自己更擅长、也更愿意长期做的事。

以前做金融销售，有些工作会让经常我纠结，自己促成的交易到底给客户带来了什么。
现在做硬件，客户要什么配置、什么价格、什么时候交货，至少有具体的问题可以去解决。当然，这也要求我把产品学懂，把信息核实清楚，对自己说出去的话负责。极其繁琐的交易链路和高昂的沟通成本，也让这个市场的撮合者或者说居间人变得不可替代。

大概其实从 9 月底的时候，我就已经差不多在退出之前接触的交易圈了。接下来会把主要精力放在算力硬件上，从 B300 开始，再慢慢了解内存、硬盘和存储。现在还算是刚入圈，很多东西都在学。通过接触不同的人和不同的事物先把真实货源和真实需求对接好。把单子做下来，再看自己能在这个行业走多远。

当然，这个推特目前还是更多记录自己的一些想法、经历和成长。
因为过去的履历，我身边大部分的这些朋友主要还是围绕交易比较多，但当然又因为接触算力和 GPU 的市场，我也在接触更新的一些圈层和人脉。而这个市场也对个人能力有着更大的挑战和考验。🙇‍♂️

🚨SHOCKING: Proton, with over 100 MILLION users, faces backlash after its CEO reportedly called a staffer's push for security testing "loser thinking."

Proton markets itself as "Privacy by default," selling encrypted email and VPN.

But in leaked internal messages, CEO Andy Yen pushed back when an employee asked to security test new code before release, per 404 Media.

He told staff to use AI more and stop writing code by hand, and said this is the last year Proton will hire engineers.

Proton's CTO said in a meeting that AI wrote 90% of the company's code in October, and his internal manifesto says most human code review will end.

After 404 Media published the leaks on October 29, many users said on social media they were cancelling their paid plans.

A day later, Yen cancelled planned interviews of staff about their AI use, while telling staff he's "still going to push."

Proton says its AI use will never come at the cost of security, and that it added extra security reviews in the past year.

It also says its code is open source, so anyone can check its security.

text:
In the 8 minutes before XPL dropped 18% today, 11 Hyperliquid accounts pulled $1.62M of margin out of their XPL longs.

Then they let the $12M position get liquidated into HLP at mark price.

HLP ate ~$0.6M.

Fresh accounts funded via CCTP. Test withdrawals 20-50 min before. 7 rejected withdrawals while scraping the margin to the limit. $0 left after.

Looks planned. Whether the same operator was short on Binance, I can't see.

Timeline (Nov 1, UTC) 👇

Oct 29-31
9 of the 10 largest accounts are created, each funded once via CCTP with $145k-$243k. On Hyperliquid the sender only shows as Circle's deposit wallet.

03:45-04:15
10 of the 11 make test withdrawals of $500-$1.6k.

04:24-04:32
10 accounts withdraw $98k-$232k each, $1.62M total.
7 more attempts get rejected: "Insufficient balance for withdrawal".
Every dollar the margin check allows comes out. The longs stay open.

04:32
XPL -18% in 1 minute, 0.086 to 0.0705.
$11.2M (144M XPL) trades on Binance perps in that minute.
Hyperliquid itself barely trades.

04:32:50-04:32:59
All 11 get liquidated into the HLP backstop vault, plus 19 small accounts.
160M XPL / $12.2M taken over at avg 0.0759, in a minute that printed a 0.0705 low.

After
All 11 accounts: $0.
Backstop vault: $1.00M to $0.44M while unwinding.
HLP daily PnL: +$21k to -$655k (~0.4% of the vault).

Why it works
Dumping $12M of XPL into the HL book would wreck your own exit.
Drain the margin first, and a small move is enough to trigger liquidation.
Liquidation hands the whole position to HLP at mark with zero slippage. HLP eats the drop after.

Same playbook as the Mar 2025 ETH whale that cost HLP $4M.
If they were also short on Binance, the crash itself was the profit.

Addresses + fills in the reply.

$HYPE $XPL

author: ryan_servatius
quoted_text:
As far as I know, Mysten Labs is the only blockchain company that has consistently stayed one step ahead when it comes to security best practices.

A few examples of what our cryptographers and security researchers have pioneered:

- Native multisig without additional gas costs. We deliberately designed Sui to accommodate larger transaction sizes, making multisig a first-class security feature rather than an expensive add-on. Our cryptographers were among the first to productionize advanced multisignature techniques, even before Facebook’s Libra.

- Cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness. From pioneering production-ready stateless post-quantum signatures to developing the first backward-compatible post-quantum solutions, our team has consistently pushed the boundaries. This includes enabling cryptographic upgrades and key rotation while preserving the same blockchain address (afaik the first crypto agility design in decentralized ledgers is attributed to my team).

- Modern hardware wallet security. We’ve recently taken additional steps to incentivize startups to build the next generation of secure hardware wallets. With what we see in the market, this is one way.

- AI-powered vulnerability detection. Sui was the first blockchain to introduce AI-driven bug detection through BugDar, back then presenting  at Google’s Next conference. We knew AI would mess up security.

- Recovering the seemingly unrecoverable. We created KelpMe, introducing innovative approaches to recovering assets after mnemonic loss or accidental transfers to incorrect addresses, problems traditionally considered practically impossible to solve. KelpMe also won the Bybit Hackathon, demonstrating the real-world potential of this innovation.

- Zero-knowledge authentication as a first-class primitive. We went far beyond using ZK for privacy or scaling. With innovations such as zkLogin and ZEE-CAT, and for a while the most used ZK app in the planet, we demonstrated how zero-knowledge cryptography could fundamentally transform authentication.

- Proofs of solvency and exchange accountability. Undeniably, we’re the leaders. Our cryptographers designed some of the most advanced proof-of-solvency protocols and identified critical weaknesses in approaches used by major exchanges and auditing firms.

- World-class academic research at startup speed. Mysten Labs has systematically pushed the boundaries of academic research productivity, achieving publication records that are extraordinary for a startup. Our researchers reached an incredible milestone of 5 papers accepted at ACM CCS and 4 at Financial Cryptography (FC) in the same year, two of the world’s most prestigious venues in cybersecurity and applied cryptography. And so many best paper awards.
- Binary transparency with Walrus sites and crypto guard. Reality is we should have pushed further making it the standard for any crypto website, but at the same time we indeed genuinely try to fix the internet.
- Scion from our Swiss team, IMO the future of internet communication, kill DoS, native packet protection.

That’s a phenomenal achievement even for established university research groups, let alone a startup simultaneously building and securing a major blockchain ecosystem.

And these are just a few examples.

When you consider the size of our team and the breadth of its contributions, even compared with the much larger Ethereum ecosystem, I genuinely believe Mysten Labs has been one of the most impactful organizations in blockchain cybersecurity, with innovations that are applied in the whole financial sector.

What makes this particularly remarkable is that we didn’t just publish research or build theoretical solutions. We repeatedly turned cutting-edge cryptographic research into production systems, often years ahead of broader industry adoption. No other org ever came close to that. Now with the AI vision of Evan, Mysten will do more miracles 🤞

text:
币安开放提现后，所谓「20 亿美元资金出逃」，可能有相当一部分是乌龙账。

先看数据：

@DefiLlama ：币安 24 小时净流出约 12.6 亿美元。
@whale_alert ：开放提现后约 3 小时，监测到约 20 亿美元大额转账，包括约 1 万枚 BTC、近 10 亿 USDT。

但一姐@heyibinance 随后确认，其中多笔被标记为「未知钱包」的转账，实际上是币安内部迁移至新的提现及 PoR 地址。

真正流向其他交易所的资金规模，远没有标题那么夸张。

同期 DefiLlama 数据显示：

OKX 净流入约 6540 万美元，Bitstamp 约 2740 万美元，Bybit 约 2060 万美元，MEXC 约 543 万美元，合计约 1 亿美元出头。

另一个值得注意的信号：CoinGlass 数据显示，USDT 维度 24 小时净流入约 5.39 亿美元，并没有出现稳定币集体出逃。

当然，这不意味着用户没有恐慌。流向自托管钱包、未标记地址的资金，目前仍无法准确统计。

还有两个口径不能混淆：

约 63 亿美元的被盗资产，是黑客攻击及追赃事件，不是用户提现。

7 日约 80 亿美元净流出包含黑客事件当天的数据，不能直接归因于 11 月 1 日开放提现。

结论：币安确实出现了资金净流出，但「20 亿美元用户集体跑路、资金涌向 OKX 和 Bybit」目前缺乏证据。

这场安全风波之后，真正值得持续观察的，不是某个大额转账截图，而是接下来几天用户资产是否持续净流出，以及资金最终去了哪里。

text:
THORChain can't selectively refuse a swap because the money is stolen. by design. the FBI just asked its node operators, by name, to do exactly that.

October 31: the FBI attributes the $6B+ @binance  hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor operation. Together with the Secret Service and IRS-CI, it urges THORNode operators, named first on its list, to block transactions involving the stolen funds.

There's a legitimate reason for @THORChain 's design. No discretionary blacklist, no gatekeeper deciding who gets to trade. I've credited that before.

But the consequences don't disappear because the choice was deliberate.

And we have the receipts.

None of the FBI's 628 listed addresses directly matched the THORChain swap addresses I examined. One hop out is a different story: 8 wallets that received THORChain payouts also transferred 5,324 ETH to 54 FBI-listed addresses. Those transfers are confirmed, but not all of that ETH can be attributed to THORChain.

Meanwhile, THORChain itself was barely trading.

as of 10:08 PM ET, trading was halted on 11 of 13 chains, including BTC, ETH and TRON. Only AVAX and XRP were open.

An unrelated Ethereum reorg caused a 10 ETH deposit to be refunded twice. THORChain's solvency protections triggered, followed by broader halts voted through by nodes.

Caught in that halt: 41 TRX -> ETH swaps from 11 wallets on Elliptic's Binance-hack list. Nearly 200 ETH accrued and unpaid.

25 of those queued swaps, accounting for 169 ETH of accrued output, point to wallets that have already sent ETH directly to FBI-listed addresses.

Before the halt, swaps initiated by those same 11 TRON wallets had already produced 7,474 ETH in THORChain payouts.

None of this was an intentional intervention against the thieves. Ordinary users were halted too.

THORChain co-founder @CBarraford  argues that CEXes hold identifying information and should work with law enforcement when hackers cash out. I agree.

But the FBI's own alert identifies DeFi and instant-swap services as part of the laundering route. The money doesn't become a law-enforcement problem only when it reaches a CEX.

THORChain can coordinate a halt when its own solvency is at risk. It has no deployed mechanism to selectively reject identified stolen-funds swaps.

The FBI asked its operators to block transactions.

For now, those 41 swaps are paused because ETH and TRON trading are halted for everyone.

What happens when those routes reopen is the next test.

@heyibinance 首席客服一姐，今天亲自回复我了，搞得我很自卑
关于币安的事情，我想先明确几个立场。
第一，我认为币安自导自演这场盗窃案的可能性极低。
原因很简单，顶级有钱人会用自己需要的，去赚自己不需要的
当一个人已经站在财富顶峰，他最不需要的，就是给自己制造不可控的风险。
你可以设计一场骗局，但你无法控制美国的执法机构，无法控制国际舆论，更无法控制事情最后会发展成什么样。
对于这种级别的富豪而言，继续赚钱的边际收益，远远小于失去现有财富的代价。没有必要为了不需要的钱，去冒失去一切的风险。
当然，马斯克除外
所以这不是我相信谁的人品，而是我相信人性。当然，这只是基于风险收益的判断，并不是什么内部证据。
第二，我依然认为赵长鹏此前的公开回应是冲动的。
我一直有个观点，一个人的公开表达，是要看别人怎么理解，而不是看你怎么表达，有比例的共识的理解就是你作为发言人必须接受和承担的代价。
因为当一句话被说出口，它就不再完全属于说话的人了。
你可以解释自己的本意，但不能要求所有人都按照你的本意去理解。
cz可能承受着巨大的压力，也理解人在压力之下难免冲动。
但理解不代表不能评价。
选择必有代价，冲动当然也是一种选择。
第三，我确实认为何一是个非常厉害的女人。
尤其是她那句，大意是向各位股东汇报，目前还没到需要卖出SpaceX股份来填补窟窿的时候。
我觉得这个回复非常漂亮。
没有刻意回避问题，也没有过多解释，而是用一句话回应了外界对资金状况的担忧。
当然，我不懂币圈，也不知道这件事究竟存在多大的实际风险，所以不打算装作自己什么都懂。
至于今天何一亲自回复我，确实有点出乎意料。
我一个喜欢读几本书，又特别好为人师的小博主，本来只是借着新闻谈谈国家利益与道德的问题。开头提到FBI的结论，也只是想说，权威值得尊重，但权威不等于绝对真理，并不是在否认朝鲜作案。
早知道会惊动这些大人物，我可能就不发了。毕竟我这个人虽然喜欢装逼，但也知道自己几斤几两。
不过话说回来，身份有高低，观点却不应该因此分贵贱。
我可以尊重一个人，也可以欣赏一个人，但不代表我必须同意他的每一句话。
同样，我也希望别人可以不同意我。
最后，基于今天何一的回复，我是真心希望币安能够平安度过这次风波。
毕竟我始终觉得，一个人最难得的能力，不是永远做出正确的选择，而是在选择之后，能够承担它带来的一切。
这句话送给我自己。
这次事件给我最大的思考是赚钱的意义是什么？如果是改变世界，我可以理解，这会是下篇日记的内容。（日记2026.11.01石）
