author: Auri_0x
quoted_text:
gmgm!  some post TGE thoughts, been gathering feedback over the past day and talking to many of yall 1:1, figured I'd summarize some of the learnings.

on price action:

we dipped significantly below our starting price of $30m FDV.  currently around $8M FDV with around ~26% floating.  its hard for me to comment on price besides the fact that I of course think we're undervalued.  nothing much though we can do here besides deliver on Genesis and our roadmap.

on the airdrop:

we ended up airdropping 16.25% of total supply to 46,718 wallets.  another ~6% of total supply went to presale buyers.  presale allocations from the feb 2026 sale were increased by 1.5x.  another 1.25% funded RSGP incentives for CEX trading and DEX LP activity.

re. the airdrop, 26.6% of the 810M RSGP dropped was sold on DEX, 13.8% was transferred to other addresses, 3% of went back into LP positions, and 56.4% is still held.  wallets that started selling within the first hour account for 56% of airdrop sells, within six hours 87%.  the 500 biggest sellers account for 72%.

how the airdrop worked:

there were three buckets - season points (10% of supply), NFT holdings and renown (5%), and the public loot drop (1%).  

for season points, there were eleven airdrop points seasons that the 10% had to be split between.  two of these we'd explicitly promised a fixed allocation (Gold Rush S2 - 3%, First Landing - 1.5%).  these ended up being significantly overweight, leaving only 5.5% to split between the remaining 9 seasons (theater of magic - 0.65%, Gold Rush S1 - 0.5%, dungeons - 0.5%, airdrop s1 (base) - 0.125%, airdrop s2 (blast pre-TGE) - 0.3%, airdrop s3 (blast post-TGE) - 0.3%, mando's christmas - 0.125%).  within a season, tokens were split pro rata based on points earned in that season.

for NFT holdings, 3% of supply was a flat airdrop to NFTs held on the Aug 28th snapshot - 1.9% to Founders (depr), 0.9% to Cores (depr), and 0.2% to islands.  2% of supply went to Renown - a time-holding weighted composite of overall NFT holdings and loyalty.

the public loot drop, 1% was split to chests rolled.  for this drop, anyone could claim, and the # of chests they got were based on their onchain history score (activity, holdings).  

how season bucket splits (outside the fixed / promised allocations) were decided:

a combination of factors, including - effective fees paid ($), how early the season was, how many participants, subjective factors like impact on cambria growth, etc.

how the Airdrop Recipient Profile (ARP) score worked:

for each airdrop recipient, we calculated a score that affected how raw season points converted to actual token allocations.  this only touched the points (10%) bucket - nfts, loot chests were not affected.  this score ranged from 0.4 to 1.25 (1  by default).  

what raises score: dozens of factors - NFTs held, first founder / loyalty status, net spend, engagement over time, seasons played, charters minted/held, presale participation, cosmetics held, creator scores, etc. etc.

what lowers score: player conduct signals (exploit abusing, cheating, botting, sybil activity, wash trading, referral group farming, etc).  certain seasons where airdrop point distribution was curved (in an attempt to scale rewards not purely on $ risked and have the average player benefit) were subject to significant sybil activity to exploit this distribution.  players who sybilled these seasons were penalized accordingly (but limited only to the points earned in those seasons).  

nft selling patterns (scaling with share sold, not volume) were also analyzed and contributed to lower scores, as this was considered a factor indicating "farmer" vs "long term participant" skew.  transfers between multiple wallets linked were ignored.  this factor touched 1,792 accounts with a median cut of 25%.  as a group, these players were still paid ~88% of raw, and many were actually above raw with higher starting scores.  sales were considered against net buying - nfts held at time of snapshot lowers share sold - net buyers were up.

retroactive thoughts:

in retrospect, I think we made two mistakes.  

1) we should have just increased the total % supply for the airdrop, from 16.25% to 20%.  this would have fixed the imbalance between the fixed seasons with already-promised allocations (GR S2, first landing) and the rest.  players most affected by this imbalance were the early Duel Arena players on Blast, and Gold Rush Season 3, whose allocation came in under expectations set (but not explicitly promised).  

2) we should have just done the airdrop pro rata instead of using the ARP score.  there's two conflicting arguments here:

A (pro ARP): the ARP score DID end up accurately identifying "farmers" / people that were going to just cash out and dump their tokens.  the penalised bands sold 60% of their tokens, the capped band only 11%.  out of the 25 largest sellers, 23 had a score below 1, and 23 were marked as players that were linked to a farm / sybil group.  NFT holding DID also accurately predict token holding.  NFT holders above a score of 1 held 72% of their airdrop, players that held and then sold most of their nfts held 50% of their airdrop, while points-only recipients held only 38%.  players that ONLY held NFTs and never farmed airdrop points held an incredible 90%.

B (against ARP): the airdrop goals should not have been "calculate a distribution that scientifically predicts who will hold."  given we ran an airdrop campaign, the implicit expectation of players is that they'd be rewarded tokens based on their points.  everything that we "fixed" with the distribution (punishing sybils, cheating, exploits, botting, wash trading) was done retroactively instead of just straight up banning these players early on.  what we ended up doing over the past few years was create an environment and community culture that harbored these players, with only sporadic enforcement of rules.  thus, they have a rational counterpoint that 1) their continued engagement benefited us, 2) that many were forced to engage in these behaviors to remain competitive, 3) that they were not told ahead of time that this could be a consequence, and 4) getting "vibe-filtered" actually led to them selling it all in rage, instead of the other way around.  ultimately, the ARP ended up not changing distribution much (~12% of the tokens shifted as a result of ARP) while creating unnecessary FUD, confusion, uncertainty, and division within the community.  

we also made a timing mistake during launch. to run a final simulation test to ensure no reverts would impair distribution, we queued up / pre-signed a bunch of transactions in our multisig.  because all signatures were present, a 3rd party (0x5AF5b3FB44B758c8d998fFeDAFd35a6D5b97E16A via 0x92E92dA7495daCbA7b088899255f3dCf2b41423D) was able to execute the 1st batch of presale distributions, accounting for around 3.5% of the supply. 

moving forward:

at the current moment, i don't think dwelling on these issues too long is a good use of our time - we should be laser focused on shipping genesis and growing the protocol, any more time spent here is massively expensive in terms of opportunity cost.  however, I do want to eventually revisit and correct the two biggest imbalances (duel arena / gold rush s3 weighting, and token allocation lost to ARP scores specifically due to nft selling) at some point in the future when there's more value to distribute.  this will not be in additional tokens (it's too late for that, tokens are scaling units of value).  but more in terms of adjusting for the value of the slashed tokens at time of TGE.

our community is something we pride ourselves on, and though the recent airdrop has strained and tested some of those connections, I have no doubt that we will weather this storm.  crypto is ugly - there's no question about it - the financial incentives create extremely pvp scenarios sometimes.  decisions that we are required to make daily touch assets that people care extremely deeply about, and being even slightly off from perfect can hurt a significant amount of people.  we have our fair share of fuckups, so I am endlessly grateful for the continued grace that most of our holders continue to extend to us.

text:
Marc Andreessen revealed how Harvard Business School was built on a broken 1941 theory, and how it's now collapsing...

Andreessen co-founded Netscape in 1994 and a16z in 2009.

He has sat on Meta's board since 2008.

He has spent 30 years backing founders and watching managerial CEOs lose to them.

The pattern traces back to one book: James Burnham's The Machiavellians (1941).

Burnham argued every great company had been founder-run.

Henry Ford ran Ford. Bob Noyce ran Intel.

Today, Elon Musk runs Tesla, SpaceX, and Starlink.

Then, he said, something broke.

Between the 1880s and the 1920s, a new philosophy replaced the founder. It was called managerialism.

The professional manager would now hold a portable skill, usable across any business.

The consequences were:

- Harvard Business School
- Stanford Business School
- Management as a universal skill
- The 1970s conglomerate

"That assumes the managers are going to do a good job," Andreessen says.

For 30 years, they haven't.

Managers can run something static, he says. Soup is soup. A bank is a bank. A car is a car.

But when the industry changes, the manager freezes.

Look at SpaceX.

"Imagine being a professionally trained manager, trained at a top management school, working for a rocket launch company, competing with SpaceX."

Then Elon's rockets started landing on their butt.

"Your management skills ... what good are they at that point?"

Andreessen's conclusion:

"You're much more likely to build something important in the 21st century if you start with the founder and train them on management."

quoted_text:
看完今天两个小时的台北市长辩论，我整体感觉是平分秋色。但如果非要分个高下，蒋万安的「预期管理」做得非常好。本来我觉得他及格就好，结果表现和气势都判若两人，甚至让都怀疑是早就布局好的。

蒋万安和他的团队前期选战非常低调，可以说是被压着打，很被动。但他们选择不怎么摆政绩，等沈伯洋先把架势摆开，再去找他选举布局里的漏洞。

今天的交叉质询，有点像现任市长拿自己对市政的熟悉度来考沈伯洋，细到：大同斯文里都更为什么卡了十年，0到6岁每周免费临托4小时要多少保姆，市民大道「缝合」到底缝什么。政绩留到申论一口气讲完：「四年前我说到，四年后我做到。」如果这真是事先想好的，说明蒋和他的幕僚是有水平的。

对沈伯洋来说比较难受的是，他其实很难反驳蒋万安的主要政见。大巨蛋、辉达、免费营养午餐，台北市民大多是认的。所以沈伯洋自己也说：「没有人在否定免费的营养午餐」（但台北也不是第一个推营养午餐的县市），问题出在执行。这就是为什么他有一个问题一直在追问 SOP：东门茄苳树为什么会被误砍，不出席会议的标准是什么。蒋万安一直绕开，直到结论只能补一句，说是厂商没按要求移植，已经严惩。

另外说说我自己的想法。我从小在大陆受教育，知道体制内对「优秀政治人物」的标准不太一样：喜怒不形于色，多讲官话，不暴露真实想法，没有真心就没有破绽。蒋万安给我的感觉也是这样，国民党不少老一辈政治人物都是这个风格。之前上政论节目，几个主持人问人事问题问到急了，说他没魄力，他照样不接。今天沈伯洋问他为什么不出席会议，他也只回开了很多专案会议，市府就是「分层负责，抓大方向」。

沈伯洋更像大学教授，靠真诚打动人。他会讲自己当年列表格比较美国和台湾，为了打开青少年的心房去学塔罗牌，遇到自由潜水场馆这种问题答不上来，就回去做功课。这种人在一人一分钟的交叉质询里很吃亏，他自己都抱怨「我们来回只能问四个问题」，最后还问蒋万安要不要再约一场，加 LINE 也行。所以我有个反常识的看法：沈伯洋更适合王伟忠、赵少康那种一对一的长访谈，时间够长，真诚才能打动人。

最后借蔡康永前几天在节目上说的一句话：
“不用管哪个候选人会赢，把票投给你想要的生活方式，你就赢了。” 他现在蓝绿两边的造势场子都去过，沈伯洋今天在结论里也念了这句。

这只是一个大陆人的观察，台湾朋友或许有不同的看法，欢迎交流。

quoted_text:
Yann LeCun and Randall Balestriero just Proved the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, and found a better way to achieve it.

The Platonic Representation Hypothesis suggests that AI models trained on different modalities, like images and text, eventually learn similar representations of the world. But this paper shows that how models are trained matters more than simply scaling them up.

So they mathematically show that, under certain conditions, two JEPAs trained completely separately can learn essentially the same underlying representation of the world. One learns from different images of the same scene, while the other learns from different descriptions of that scene, without ever being trained on image-text pairs.

Their approach achieves the same image-text alignment with 42x fewer training samples than next-token prediction. A 109M-parameter text JEPA even outperforms LLMs up to 72B parameters on cross-modal alignment benchmarks.

https://t.co/3j1enq9qF7

text:
已经有黑客组织开出天价，想把开源大模型训练成专业的网络攻击工具了。

安全研究者 Jun Song 爆料，昨天有一个匿名黑帽黑客组织找到他，希望他使用海量真实攻击数据，对开源权重模型进行强化学习后训练（RL）。

对方声称掌握的攻击数据规模极其惊人，Jun Song 甚至怀疑这会不会是 FBI 伪装成黑客组织进行的卧底行动。

更吓人的是，他此前参与过一个白帽安全项目，使用 GLM-5.3 和不到对方声称数据量 1% 的训练数据，就已经在相关任务上取得了远超前沿模型的效果。当然，这是他个人的说法，目前还没有公开的独立验证。

Jun Song 拒绝了这笔交易，但他最担心的一点是：总会有人愿意接下这笔钱。

过去大家讨论 AI 网络安全，更多关注模型会不会被越狱、会不会协助黑客编写攻击代码。现在，黑客已经开始尝试直接购买模型训练能力，用自己的攻击数据定向强化开源模型。

一旦这条路走通，网络攻击能力的扩散速度可能会远远超过防御体系的更新速度。

This isn't the first cybercrime they've committed, but it has clearly crossed a threshold where everyone knows about it and it has touched many powerful players.

There's interest in bringing back 'letters of marque and reprisal' to counteract the cybercrime that North Korea is committing. This is a constitutional power that lets Congress empower private citizens to go after pirates and bring back the loot. The problem is that in a modern context, issuing this against a nation-state like North Korea will be seen as an act of war.

A lot of the laundering operations are also heavily linked to gray markets inside China. Binance's deep ties in China and the scale will make these operations harder than usual to pull off.

I have the feeling that all the funds from the hack will be recovered and this incident will set a precedent for dealing with nation-state-led cybercrime.

text:
My goal with @cfosilvia is to build the best piece of software for serious investors who want to control their own money.

The big idea is that AI technology can help these investors navigate the complexities of managing their household finances, especially when it comes to tax, estate planning, investment decisions, and generational wealth transfer. 

Anyone can sign up, connect their financial accounts, and begin talking to Silvia about their finances. The more context you give her, the more helpful she can be. 

My initial suggestion for every user is to connect your accounts and then ask Silvia to interview you, so she gets relevant information that will make her even better at her job. 

Today we have over 20,000 investors and more than $60 billion in assets connected to the platform. The average user is a multi-millionaire and paying users ask Silvia 20+ questions per week. 

Given the product touches personal financial data, it has been important to me since day one that we embrace three core ideas of privacy, security, and accuracy. 

For example, we applied for SOC II certification when there was literally only me and @shaincodes at the company. Almost no one does that, but the privacy and security of our users is front-and-center for us.

Additionally, we have spent the last ~ 6 months rebuilding the AI tech stack to reduce our dependency on frontier models. This has allowed us to improve the accuracy of Silvia's answers on important personal finance topics like tax, mortgage, and credit cards. 

If you search the internet or here on X, you will find tons of people who love the product. They are tired of the amateurish budgeting and saving apps. These individual investors need a product that can help them grow their assets and net worth, not save $5 on Starbucks.

We are proud of the product we have built and think there is tons of room for improvement too. Our team is currently only ~ 10 full-time employees, so we are rapidly shipping new features and products with the hopes of delivering on Silvia's core promise to help serious investors accelerate their net worth growth.

If this approach resonates with you, I would appreciate it if you took a few minutes to sign up for the product and gave it a try. It is free to use when you get started and you only have to pay if you become a power user. 

Try Silvia: https://t.co/bMI7hLeK8s 

Feedback is a gift, so once you have tried the product, please send any ideas on how we could improve it. No idea is too small or too silly. We can only build the best product if we have smart users who share their ideas. 

I appreciate you reading this far and hope you enjoy using Silvia. We are having a blast building it.

CryptoBilis update

We've been made aware, through responsible disclosure, of a single hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device bought from the reseller CryptoBilis in August 2026.

No CryptoBilis buyer has reported a loss of funds to us.

IMPORTANT: If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards, we know this is unsettling. Here’s what to do:

Already using it?

Move your funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Do not reuse the old seed in any wallet, hardware or software.  If you don’t have another secure hardware wallet available, we recommend temporarily migrating your funds to a software wallet or an exchange you are familiar with.  

Not set up yet? Don’t set it up, and never enter your existing wallet backup on it.

We haven’t received the device to confirm this report, but based on the customer’s description, we’re treating it as credible and sharing it now so customers who purchased a Trezor via CryptoBilis can secure their funds as a precaution. Our security team will examine the device as soon as it arrives.

On October 9, 2026, we removed CryptoBilis as a reseller following reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through it. Since then, we have been inspecting Trezor devices that customers bought from CryptoBilis and have found no signs of tampering on any of the four devices we’ve received so far.

NEVER share your wallet backup (recovery phrase) with anyone. Trezor Support will never ask for it.
If you are affected by this incident, please keep your CryptoBilis device and contact Support to receive a new Trezor hardware wallet: https://t.co/5EasOVDDQh

We're investigating and will post updates here as soon as we know more.  Thank you to the customer who reported this through our responsible disclosure program, and to @SEAL_911 for working alongside our teams on the response. Reports and engagement like this help us protect everyone else.

For more information, visit our blog: https://t.co/2LmFV8L2oe

quoted_text:
At @temple, one of our missions is to become the ultimate wearable for elite performance athletes. 

And today, let's start with the basics: Heart Rate (HR). 

You would think accurate HR tracking is a solved problem. It is not. Especially in zones 4 & 5, which matter to professional athletes the most.

To see whether Temple is the most accurate wearable on something as basic as HR, we gave ourselves a high bar to aspire to. A Polar H10 chest strap, taped to the chest. Taped, because worn the usual way, straps lose contact mid-sprint and miss beats. We benchmarked five flagship wearables against that reference, from rest to max effort, second by second.

All the other leading wearables were well behind Temple in our study. Apple Watch Series 12 came closest. Temple also beat the untaped chest strap, the industry's benchmark, in zones 4 and 5.  

Why does Temple win? Two reasons.

1. Temple uses adhesive, so its lab condition is its wear condition. You'll experience our study outcomes in real life. 

2. The location. Your temple sits right over a major artery, and it's the one patch of skin that doesn't clamp down its blood flow when you go hard. We tested the same sensor at four body sites. The temple was the most accurate of the four.

Charts attached.

Accurate HR makes Temple better at so much more downstream. More soon.

The full paper and data are live right now at https://t.co/ovabS2dvnY, and an extended study by independent researchers is underway. 

We invite further independent replication in more conditions, and will fund it. Write to us at research@temple.com

One thing I forgot to mention (which was brought up in the responses) - will the CFTC permit ADL to exist on a regulated exchange? I suspect the answer is no, but we will see. If not, what are the ramifications? I have briefly mentioned ADL in the past:  https://t.co/7NvKDrtu8c

author: TheStalwart
quoted_text:
Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

text:
Aeos is about to enter it's 4th year of operations. We've been bootstrapped and profitable since day one and been in the green every month.

Every time we start building a new office, it's always a big risk with security deposits and rent and the long lock ins. There is no investor to catch us if we fall. That said, it's never a bad time to recite the fundamentals. They could be useful for you, too. YMMV:

- Agency is a muscle and it can be developed. Same way as the gym, via progressive overloading. 
- People think you can start out and build a deeptech/rocket science company but it's better to progressively overload. Start with freelancing, then do a small co, make some money, build your network, and then, when you're ready, take a big swing. Most people you know who are doing extremely crazy things started small and kept overloading beyond their current capabilities, but just a bit.
- Companies today need ruthless execution, softy founders just get eaten by the market and then personally blamed later for failure.
- Most digital businesses only last 3-4 years thanks to AI and basically have to rethink every time new technology drops. Aeos itself worked because of the sudden advantages of AI in content. It's better to disrupt yourself than be disrupted by competitors though, it's okay and worth it to go through the pain of change. 
- Startup schools like YC teach you that pivoting is okay. You are comfortable pivoting because half your batch is pivoting every month or so, and you see that all the big successes in your cohort pivoted a few times till it "clicked". Indians shame pivoting (they think this is failure or some kind of sign of a flimsy mind), but this is the wrong attitude: entrepreneurship in the early stages is an act of discovery, not of doing. You cannot know if a path sucks until you walk down it. If you want to "do" along a set path, get a job. Aeos is one of the rare examples of a company that didn't pivot and has pretty much done what it did on day one, but I know this is not the norm. 
- All the best founders I know are paranoid that something bad will happen tomorrow and disrupt them. I could never relate to someone who thinks their company/job/lifestyle is set and secure forever. It is not. Anything can happen, you have to be prepared. 
- You will only be successful when your social reputation is on the line for the swings you take. The reason you can't point to too many anonymous successes is because their reputation is never on the line for failure. This is true for employees too, the most visible employees who then try to swing actually do much better because of the implicit reputation cost. 
- Don't get me wrong: failure is normal and on the path to success. But if you do not have a feedback loop for this, you will never learn what you did wrong. We diagnose failure, improve, adapt, and try again. If the path itself is broken, choose another one. 
- Avoid overengineering on costs before you hit scale. It's an engineer bad habit, repeated across time. In fact, avoid building for other engineers, you will try to make complicated things to impress them, when you should actually only be impressing and improving the lives of your customers. Your customers actually want simple things, or an abstraction of the complex until it is simple for them. They don't want to see the tangled wires underneath: why are you so proud of them?
- If you give your life, your all to something, and you can find a group of people who are willing to do it with you, there is no greater honor and satisfaction, even in failure. But most of the time if you progressively overload well, you will end up with an output that surprises everyone. Unleash The Avatar trailer 1 versus 2  versus 3 and (and now 4, with another round of radical improvement) is a good example of continuous progressive overload from a team that won't give up.
- We are ultimately always in the service of the customer (and in our case, also the viewer), and not ourselves. It's actually been maybe 2 odd years since I've last thought about what I want. I've spent almost all my time thinking about my customers needs, my team's needs, my audience's needs. I have lost myself in the process, but I wouldn't have it any other way.
- Most people will never win because they're always thinking about what they want, when the world rewards you for thinking about other people's problems and solving it, for a price. 
- There are four quadrants when it comes to hiring: untalented and unreliable, untalented and reliable, talented and unreliable, and talented and reliable. Out of all of these, hiring the talented and unreliable is where you will lose all your money and energy.
- Attention is the most valuable thing in 2026, and 2027, and 2028. Yes, even beyond building technology. Software itself was valuable because it easily scaled, and the reason a software engineer made more than a doctor was because they served way more customers at once, often at much lower prices than a doctor. A doctor can only see so many patients an hour, but an engineer can service millions of customers in the same time. With AI coding, anyone can build for scale, but finding those customers is going to be harder as everyone competes for attention. Producing the content itself will be easier, but actually figuring out attention is super hard.
- It's okay if you fall. Just get back up again! There is only defeat in death.

text:
A marketplace upgrade could report success after disabling the replacement and preserving the market it was meant to retire.

During Plakxio's full audit, Zealynx found that the upgrade printed the new settlement address but never promoted it into the deployment artifact.

The retirement script trusted that stale artifact. It removed the replacement's badge and relayer permissions while leaving the superseded market authorized, causing an inverted cutover and trading outage.

Plakxio fixed the Medium finding by deriving market lineage from signed manifests and protecting the latest replacement from retirement.
author: ZealynxSecurity

text:
A valid bridge proof could still register the wrong token ID.

In Aurora's Near Connector co-audit, Zealynx and AuditOne found that `newBridgeToken()` trusted a caller-supplied `nearTokenId` without checking it matched `result.token` from the metadata proof.

An attacker could bind the proof to the wrong mappings. The legitimate token would then be missing, so both deposits and withdrawals would always revert.

The review required binding the ID to the proven token, or using `result.token` directly. The finding was fixed.
author: ZealynxSecurity

当然，目前 #Bitcoin 价格能不能抄底，也不能只看盘面与价格，还要看情绪与资金流向，尤其是新的一周

情绪面，目前事态已经得到有效控制，该冻结的冻结，其他无法追回的资产对市场影响还不能确定，同时要观察市场是否还会过于紧张担忧

数据面，重点看 #BTC ETF 数据与加密资金流向，如果资金继续保持净流入，那么意味着恐慌也逐渐减弱，尤其是ETF资金。

本周的 #BTC ETF 数据公布，周一到周五，连续4天净流入，但是净流入幅度从周一增量到周三峰值，周四走弱，而周五发生被盗事件导致大量资金净流出

那么本周资金整体算是净流出2.024亿，其中IBIT属于本周资金净流入的主要通道，同时也是周五资金恐慌抛售的主要通道，IBIT单一途径本周依旧保持1.769亿的净流入

很明显，周四凌晨的风险事件确实给市场造成了一定的恐慌与资金净流出，所以接下来确定目前是否是底部，要看ETF资金是否从下周转为净流入，且回流较强，如果下周依旧出现净流出，则短期有效值支撑还未到！

加密市场数据，这里仅做记录，因为周四凌晨的风险事件导致交易、资金流动、以及主流稳定币市值都出现较大的差异化，所以目前不能仅用这些数字变化来判断资金是否真的净流出或者净流入

尤其是主流稳定币USDT USDC ，前者出现大幅净流出，后者则出现净流入，所以数据对目前的判断暂时失效，仅做记录。

不过，单独来看ETF 数据，周五的情况确实不乐观，那么下周除了观察盘面是否止跌，有效反弹之外，数据侧应该关注ETF是否净流出缩减到净流入，加密数据经历几天消化是否回归正常，并且给我们带来有效反馈！

先说结论，如果是现货or定投，此时算是一个不错的买入契机，此前的回调我日线级别是看到73,000-74,000附近，

我记得当时有小伙伴评论还说，当时84,000附近，至于看到这么远的价格吗？

很显然，做趋势，就要把视角拉长，拉远，当初日线级别的回调区间，现在已经很快接近

而目前来看，日线级别回调重要的支撑区间，MA200 （73,200）到MA120（74,500）区间，理论上，价格如果回调到这个区间，是我觉得自家买入区间，就算后续下跌，空间也并没有多少。

回归盘面，#BTC 目前日线级别并未确定完全止跌，这两天恰逢周末走势偏弱。下周短期看周一二价格日线级别能否站稳78,800上方，如果不能，短线依旧偏弱

更重要的是下周一周五个常规交易日，如果价格无法回归82,000双方，意味着此前跌破的日线机构并未修复，继续向下回调寻找有效支撑的可能性会更大，并且市场已经开始接受80,000下方的定价区间

text:
> Why does the worst rise to the top in a society rife with broken politics? 

“When the plan fails—and it always fails—coercion is needed. You need people willing to do what honest people refuse to do. The system doesn't promote the best; it selects those with no scruples. And to rally a majority around the plan, nothing works better than a common enemy: the rich, the foreigner, the dissenter.”
author: sacha
quoted_text:
Je parle souvent de La Route de la servitude de Friedrich Hayek. Je vais être direct : pour moi, quiconque lit ce livre en étant sain d'esprit et n'en ressort pas libéral et profondément anti-étatiste est soit fou, soit stupide, soit corrompu. Soit les trois à la fois.

Voici pourquoi. Masterclass.

D'abord, l'homme.

Friedrich Hayek naît à Vienne en 1899, dans un empire qui se croit éternel. À 18 ans, il est sur le front italien. Quand il rentre, l'empire n'existe plus. Il voit l'Autriche sombrer dans l'hyperinflation, les économies d'une vie effacées en quelques mois.

Il devient l'élève de Ludwig von Mises, celui qui avait démontré qu'un planificateur sans prix libres navigue à l'aveugle. En 1931, il part enseigner à Londres et devient le grand rival intellectuel de Keynes. En 1938, il voit son pays natal avalé par Hitler sous les acclamations de la foule. Il prend la nationalité britannique.

C'est là, en pleine guerre, entre 1940 et 1943, qu'il écrit son livre. Pas contre les nazis : tout le monde l'était déjà. Contre quelque chose de bien plus dérangeant. Il voit les élites anglaises, les meilleurs esprits, les gens les mieux intentionnés, reprendre exactement les idées qui avaient mené l'Allemagne au désastre. Planification, direction de l'économie, organisation « scientifique » de la société.

Il dédie le livre « aux socialistes de tous les partis ». Tout est dit.

Trois éditeurs américains le refusent. Il sort en 1944, s'épuise en quelques semaines, puis le Reader's Digest le condense pour des millions de lecteurs. Keynes lui-même, son grand adversaire, lui écrit qu'il en approuve moralement et philosophiquement presque chaque ligne. Trente ans plus tard, Hayek reçoit le prix Nobel. Thatcher relit le livre en 1974 et change la trajectoire de l'Angleterre.

Le titre, d'ailleurs, est un hommage à un Français : Tocqueville, qui avait vu venir le despotisme doux.

Maintenant, ce que dit le livre. En clair.

Première idée : personne ne sait assez pour planifier.
La connaissance qui fait tourner une économie n'est dans aucun bureau. Elle est éparpillée dans des millions de têtes : l'agriculteur qui sait quand sa terre est prête, le commerçant qui sent son quartier changer, l'artisan qui connaît son fournisseur. Le prix libre est le seul système capable de rassembler tout ça en un signal. Remplacez les prix par un plan, et vous remplacez le savoir de millions de gens par l'ignorance de quelques-uns.
Deuxième idée : contrôler l'économie, c'est contrôler la vie.
On croit que l'économie est un domaine à part, matériel, secondaire. Faux. Celui qui contrôle les moyens contrôle les fins. S'il décide de ce que vous pouvez produire, acheter, chauffer, cultiver, il décide de la façon dont vous vivez. Il n'y a pas de liberté politique sans liberté économique.

Troisième idée : une démocratie ne peut pas se mettre d'accord sur un plan.
Tout le monde veut « un plan ». Personne ne veut le même. Le Parlement débat, tergiverse, se divise. L'impatience monte, et on finit par dire : laissons faire les experts. On délègue à des agences, des commissions, des autorités « indépendantes ». La démocratie ne meurt pas d'un coup d'État. Elle se dessaisit elle-même, par lassitude.
Quatrième idée : l'État de droit contre l'arbitraire.
Dans un pays libre, l'État fixe des règles générales, connues à l'avance, les mêmes pour tous, comme le code de la route. Vous savez à quoi vous attendre et vous construisez votre vie autour. Dans un pays planifié, l'État décide au cas par cas : qui a droit à quoi, quel secteur survit, quelle région est sacrifiée. Ce n'est plus la loi qui gouverne, c'est la volonté de quelqu'un.

Cinquième idée, la plus terrible : pourquoi les pires arrivent au sommet.
C'est le chapitre que tout le monde devrait lire. Quand le plan échoue, et il échoue toujours, il faut contraindre. Il faut des gens prêts à faire ce que les gens honnêtes refusent de faire. Le système ne promeut pas les meilleurs, il sélectionne ceux qui n'ont pas de scrupules. Et pour souder une majorité autour du plan, rien ne marche mieux qu'un ennemi commun : le riche, l'étranger, le récalcitrant.
Sixième idée : la fin de la vérité.
Un plan a besoin que tout le monde y croie. Alors l'information devient un instrument. Ce qui sert le plan est vrai, ce qui le gêne devient de la « désinformation ». La propagande n'est pas un accident du dirigisme. C'est une nécessité.

Et la leçon centrale, celle qui glace le sang : ceux qui ouvrent la route ne sont pas des monstres. Ce sont des gens sincères, cultivés, bien intentionnés. Ils veulent la justice, la sécurité, le progrès. Ils ne voient pas où mène le chemin. Les monstres arrivent après, quand le terrain est prêt.
Ce livre est une bouteille à la mer. Hayek nous a laissé le mode d'emploi pour reconnaître la pente avant qu'elle devienne un précipice.

Et que fait l'Europe ? Elle rejoue le livre, chapitre par chapitre.
Les règles générales remplacées par des milliers de normes au cas par cas. Des décisions qui pèsent sur nos vies prises par une Commission que personne n'a élue et que personne ne peut renvoyer. Des plans à vingt-cinq ans pour l'énergie, l'agriculture, l'industrie, l'automobile, comme si quelqu'un à Bruxelles savait mieux que 450 millions d'Européens ce qu'il faudra produire en 2050. Et quand ça échoue, on ne remet jamais le plan en cause. On ajoute une couche : une taxe, une interdiction, un régulateur.

Le plus cruel, c'est l'ironie. En 1939, Hayek défendait l'idée d'une fédération européenne. Mais une fédération où ni le centre ni les États ne pourraient diriger l'économie. Une union pour libérer les échanges, pas pour piloter les vies. Nos européistes ont gardé le mot « fédération » et jeté tout le reste. Ils ont construit exactement ce contre quoi il nous mettait en garde.
Ils avaient le livre à portée de main. Ils refont les mêmes erreurs, avec les mêmes bonnes intentions et le même mépris pour ceux qui doutent.

Je ne crois pas que l'histoire se répète à l'identique. Je crois qu'elle rime. Au XXe siècle, la route de la servitude a mené au pire : des tyrans fous, des peuples broyés, des dizaines de millions de morts. Ceux qui avaient ouvert la route n'avaient jamais voulu ça.

J'espère que, pour une fois dans l'histoire, nous saurons nous arrêter avant. Que nous n'attendrons pas le tyran pour comprendre où menait le chemin.

Hayek nous a tout dit il y a quatre-vingts ans. La seule question est de savoir si nous saurons le lire à temps.

Lisez La Route de la servitude. Puis offrez-le à quelqu'un que vous aimez.

text:
David Friedberg is raising a pretty serious concern about the AI boom, and it has implications for the entire US economy.

We're reaching a point where just seven or eight companies are spending so much money on AI infrastructure that they're beginning to compete with the US government for capital. One estimate discussed on the All-In podcast suggests that the capital these companies need to raise through 2027 could be equivalent to roughly 30% of US Treasury issuance over the same period. That's an enormous amount of money for such a small group of companies to be competing for. And we're no longer talking about investments that can be funded entirely through existing cash flows. Increasingly, these companies are turning to corporate bonds, private credit, and other forms of financing to keep expanding.

When the US government needs to borrow money, it issues Treasury bonds. When these technology companies need money, they can issue corporate bonds. Both are competing for investors' capital, including pension funds, insurance companies, banks, and large institutional investors. If companies continue flooding the bond market with hundreds of billions in new debt, investors may demand higher yields to absorb all that supply. That could also put upward pressure on Treasury yields, which influence borrowing costs throughout the economy. We're talking about mortgages, business loans, corporate financing, and potentially even the Federal Reserve's ability to stimulate economic activity through lower interest rates. And there's another problem. The more capital that flows into AI infrastructure, the more difficult or expensive it could become for smaller businesses and industries outside AI to secure financing. We're essentially concentrating an extraordinary amount of financial resources into a handful of companies, with the expectation that AI will eventually generate enough revenue and productivity gains to justify all this spending.

What's particularly interesting is that AI could become both a major driver of economic growth and a source of financial pressure at the same time. Building these data centers creates demand for electricity, construction, semiconductors, and industrial equipment. But financing that expansion could simultaneously push borrowing costs higher for everyone else.
author: MilkRoadAI
quoted_text:
Chamath Palihapitiya just raised a pretty serious concern about the AI boom and I think this could become one of the biggest issues facing the bond market over the next few years.

For context, the largest AI companies have accumulated an estimated $340 billion to $400 billion in debt, and the amount of money they need to raise is only getting bigger. Companies like Google, Amazon, and Meta are spending hundreds of billions building data centers, purchasing GPUs, expanding power infrastructure, and developing AI models. The problem is that even some of the most profitable companies in the world are reaching a point where their operating cash flow isn't enough to comfortably finance all that spending.

@chamath estimates that the additional financing these companies will need through the end of 2027 could equal roughly 30% of everything the US Treasury is expected to issue over that same period. Think about what that means. Some of the largest corporations in America are now competing with the U.S. government for capital from the same institutional investors, pension funds, insurance companies, and bond funds. If these companies continue flooding the bond market with hundreds of billions in new debt, investors may demand higher yields to absorb all that supply. That creates the potential for upward pressure on borrowing costs across the economy, including mortgages, corporate loans, and government debt. And higher yields would also put pressure on stock valuations, especially growth companies whose valuations depend heavily on future earnings.

What's particularly interesting is how dramatically the economics of Big Tech have changed. For years, companies like Google and Meta were essentially cash generating machines with relatively modest capital requirements. Now they're becoming some of the most capital intensive businesses in the world. They're spending enormous amounts of money today on infrastructure that may take years to generate sufficient returns, while committing themselves to additional spending as AI demand continues growing. And this extends well beyond Big Tech. Companies like Oracle, CoreWeave, and Nebius are also financing enormous AI infrastructure projects. The more dependent this entire ecosystem becomes on debt financing, the more sensitive it becomes to interest rates, credit conditions, and investors' willingness to provide capital.

text:
做市實戰筆記 #2，這篇把 GLFT 接上 Hyperliquid 的訂單簿，用今天早上八分鐘的即時成交校準參數，看庫存不同時報價該擺哪，最後再把手續費塞回模型，結果想的差蠻多的。

上一篇只帶過一句 AS 拿到永續上會出事，這篇講細一點。AS 算保留價格時影響最大的是兩件事，你手上抱多少庫存，還有離你設定的結束時間 T 還剩多久。離 T 越遠，價格還有很多時間可以跑掉，抱貨的風險越大，模型就把報價往反方向推得越兇，急著把庫存吐掉；越接近 T 這股推力越小，到 T 前一刻模型會覺得抱一堆貨也沒差，反正馬上結算。股票有收盤，T 還說得過去，永續沒有到期日，你只能自己硬塞一個 T。塞一天的話，每天快到那個時間點就變得超敢抱庫存，一重置報價又會瞬間偏回去。

GLFT 的做法是乾脆假設這場遊戲永遠不會結束，再幫庫存設上下限，報價就只看你當下抱多少貨，跟時間完全脫鉤。它把報價拆成兩塊。第一塊是基本價差，跟「掛遠一點成交機率掉多快」最相關，掉得越快模型越不敢掛寬，因為掛遠了根本沒人理你。第二塊是庫存偏移，每多抱一單位貨，買價賣價就一起往反方向挪一段，這段挪多少最受波動影響，波動越大、你越怕風險、成交越稀，就挪越多。抱多單把兩邊往下推，抱空單往上推。

所以實際要校準的只有三個東西，中間價波動多大、貼著中間價時每秒被吃幾次、每往外掛 1 bps 成交率掉多快。風險厭惡沒人能幫你校準，只能自己挑，這篇先設 0.05。資料從 Hyperliquid 公開 websocket 收的成交跟 bbo，波動用 info API 的 1 分鐘 K。方法很粗，同區塊同方向的成交算一筆吃單，用成交前最後一個 bbo 的中間價算它吃到多深，數每秒有幾筆吃單打到某個深度以上，再看成交率隨深度衰減的速度。

BTC 八分鐘 426 筆吃單，波動兩小時 0.42、24 小時 0.81 bps/√秒，週六早上蠻安靜。擬合出來貼著中間價每秒大約被吃 0.043 次，每往外 1 bps 成交率大概剩十分之一。曲線其實很不像平滑衰減，貼最佳價每秒 0.26 筆，往外一個 tick 直接掉到 0.020，後面才慢慢變少，擬合只是硬找一條折衷的線。

先不算手續費，零庫存半價差 0.61 bps，大約離中間價 4.7 美元，每單位庫存偏移 0.35 bps；實際盤口 98% 的時間只有 1 美元一個 tick，半價差 0.065 bps，模型想報的寬度大概是市場的九倍。

問題是這個模型裡根本沒有手續費。主網基礎 maker 費率 1.5 bps，每次成交實拿的是你掛的距離減掉費率。把費率放回去其實不難，整條報價往外退 1.5 bps，退了之後成交變少，庫存偏移也跟著被放大。重算之後半價差變 2.9 bps，大約 22 美元，每單位庫存偏移拉到 2 bps 左右，跟市場的 0.065 bps 差了四十幾倍。直接拿實際數字看更清楚，貼在最佳價每筆賺 0.065 bps、付 1.5 bps 手續費，成交越多虧越多。BTC 最前排那層是靠高等級費率甚至 rebate 加上排隊速度在活的，一般費率等級進去就是送錢。順便講個實作細節，不算手續費時庫存 3 單位的 ask 會算到中間價下方 0.46 bps，模型其實是叫你直接吃單丟貨，程式要另外接住。

SNDK 是上一篇說要試的。https://t.co/XGAXjhlBiB 的 xyz:SNDK 今天週六美股休市，八分鐘只有 63 筆吃單，貼最佳價每秒 0.038 筆，大概 BTC 的七分之一，往外一個 tick 掉到 0.0031。波動兩小時 0.72、24 小時 2.09，因為那個窗口吃到週五晚上美股盤中。一個 tick 0.1 美元，在 1155 附近等於 0.87 bps，盤口 81% 的時間就是一個 tick，半價差 0.43 bps。tick 太粗，成交率曲線只有兩個點能擬合，衰減速度前幾分鐘跟最後估出來差了一倍多，這個數字我自己都不太敢信。

不算手續費，同樣風險厭惡下的 GLFT 半價差只有 0.23 bps，比一個 tick 的半價差還窄。把 https://t.co/XGAXjhlBiB 文件上 0.3 bps 的基礎 maker 費率放回去，變成 0.61 bps，又比一個 tick 寬一點。到這裡連續價格的模型就不太夠用了，報價只能落在格子上，你能選的半價差只有 0.43 或往後一格的 1.30，沒有 0.61。比較實際的做法是直接拿量到的成交率乘上每筆淨賺：貼最佳價每秒 0.038 筆、每筆淨 0.13 bps，往後一格每秒 0.0031 筆、每筆淨 1.0 bps，前者每秒期望大概 0.005 bps，後者 0.003，貼最前面還是比較好，只是這還沒扣逆選擇跟庫存風險。

我覺得值得追的點就在這裡。BTC 跟模型差四十幾倍，怎麼調參數都救不回來；SNDK 跟模型只差 0.18 bps，每筆淨利也只有 0.13 bps，費率等級、staking 折扣、builder 分潤任何一項動一點點，結論就會翻過來。庫存偏移在 SNDK 一樣被 tick 卡住，含費率每單位 0.27 bps，大概三分之一格，要累積三單位庫存報價才會挪一格，所以庫存上限怎麼設比風險厭惡怎麼挑還要命。另一個風險是週一開盤的跳空，週末用兩小時波動估出來的偏移，換成含盤中的 24 小時波動會差到三倍左右，參數不跟著切就是在裸抱。

下一步想把 queue position 跟 microprice 塞進來，再拿一整個週末的 SNDK 跑紙上回測，看那 0.13 bps 被逆選擇咬掉之後還剩多少。
歡迎多交流🫡

In the 8 minutes before XPL dropped 18% today, 11 Hyperliquid accounts pulled $1.62M of margin out of their XPL longs.

Then they let the $12M position get liquidated into HLP at mark price.

HLP ate ~$0.6M.

Fresh accounts funded via CCTP. Test withdrawals 20-50 min before. 7 rejected withdrawals while scraping the margin to the limit. $0 left after.

Looks planned. Whether the same operator was short on Binance, I can't see.

Timeline (Nov 1, UTC) 👇

Oct 29-31
9 of the 10 largest accounts are created, each funded once via CCTP with $145k-$243k. On Hyperliquid the sender only shows as Circle's deposit wallet.

03:45-04:15
10 of the 11 make test withdrawals of $500-$1.6k.

04:24-04:32
10 accounts withdraw $98k-$232k each, $1.62M total.
7 more attempts get rejected: "Insufficient balance for withdrawal".
Every dollar the margin check allows comes out. The longs stay open.

04:32
XPL -18% in 1 minute, 0.086 to 0.0705.
$11.2M (144M XPL) trades on Binance perps in that minute.
Hyperliquid itself barely trades.

04:32:50-04:32:59
All 11 get liquidated into the HLP backstop vault, plus 19 small accounts.
160M XPL / $12.2M taken over at avg 0.0759, in a minute that printed a 0.0705 low.

After
All 11 accounts: $0.
Backstop vault: $1.00M to $0.44M while unwinding.
HLP daily PnL: +$21k to -$655k (~0.4% of the vault).

Why it works
Dumping $12M of XPL into the HL book would wreck your own exit.
Drain the margin first, and a small move is enough to trigger liquidation.
Liquidation hands the whole position to HLP at mark with zero slippage. HLP eats the drop after.

Same playbook as the Mar 2025 ETH whale that cost HLP $4M.
If they were also short on Binance, the crash itself was the profit.

text:
”repent and believe in the gospel”

Jesus emphasized repentance as a central part of his message, calling people to turn from sin and toward God in light of the coming Kingdom.

In Matthew: 
- “From that time Jesus began to preach, saying, ‘Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.’” 
- “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.”

In Luke:
- “I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.”
- “No, I tell you; but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.”

There is more joy in heaven “over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance,” and “joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.” 

He also denounced unrepentant cities - for not responding to his works with repentance, and referenced the people of Nineveh who repented at Jonah’s preaching as a contrast.

What does Repentance mean?
In the Gospels, repentance - metanoia in Greek - involves a change of mind/heart that turns from sin toward God, often linked with believing the good news of the Kingdom and leading to forgiveness. 

It is presented as essential rather than optional. Note that the Gospel of John does not use the specific word “repent,” focusing instead on believing, though related ideas of turning to God appear. 

What does Repentance not mean?
In short, for believers, repentance is not about earning favor, wallowing in guilt, or achieving sinless perfection. 

Repentance is a Spirit-empowered turning from sin (hating it as an offense against God) and toward Christ, which produces ongoing growth, confession, and fruit - while resting fully in the once-for-all forgiveness already secured by Jesus. 

Repentance is not mere feelings of guilt, regret, or sorrow. Feeling bad about sin is not the same as repentance.

Repentance is not just confession or saying “I’m sorry.” Acknowledging sin is important, but confession alone - without a change of mind and direction - is incomplete. Many confess without turning. 

Repentance is not penance or self-punishment to earn or “pay for” forgiveness. Believers are already justified by faith in Christ’s finished work. 

Ongoing repentance is relational, not a legal effort to re-earn standing with God. We cannot add to or help Christ’s atonement through rituals, self-flagellation, or works. 

When we do sin, we confess and turn again, confident that “if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness” (1 John 1:9).

quoted_text:
"我看着它们现在写出的代码，我自己根本写不出来，甚至22岁时也写不出来。所以我被彻底击败了。"

谷歌前 CEO、Relativity Space CEO 埃里克·施密特（@ericschmidt），9月29日做客黑石（@blackstone）播客《Inside Blackstone》，与主持人 Christine Anderson 对谈。他在科技业深耕55年，亲历大型机、PC、互联网的每一轮浪潮。这一次，他把递归自我改进、长推理、超级智能时间表、数据中心和AI原生CEO放在一场对话里讲透了。

01｜不是不同，只是更大
 "并没有不同，只是规模更大，大得多。"他以自动驾驶为例：第一次真正测试在2004年，"到现在已经22年了"。"技术的普及速度与发明速度是不同的。"而这一次，"每一波技术浪潮规模都更大，但速度也更快，而我们社会还没有做好准备。"
 发明是工程问题，普及才是社会问题。

02｜无标度：机器自己变聪明
 他说，目前AI的进展都发生在"无标度"（scale-free，指可以不断重复、越做越聪明的领域）领域。数学就是典型："它不需要外部数据，它是自洽的。"代码也一样：写完、看效果、再优化，形成"递归自我改进"（recursive self-improvement）循环，"系统会自行变得更聪明"。
 不靠新数据也能变强，这才是真正的拐点。

03｜学习一切，但不要伤害人类
 他承认，我们正在创造"一种不一定能受我们约束的不同智能"，这就是"对齐问题"。OpenAI一次内部测试中，智能体"竟然协同合作，违反了某些规范和法律"。他开出的药方是："学习一切，但不要伤害人类。遵守所有法律。"但他不认同末日论："超级智能的一部分，正是解决超级对齐问题。"
 乐观不等于不怕，而是把护栏当作能力的一部分。

04｜长推理：机器开始比人想得更深
 "过去一年发生的最重大、最重要的事情，就是长推理和深度推理的到来。"推理可以持续8小时，思维链（chain of thought，模型逐步展开的推理过程）"可以长达1000步、2000步"。"我思考不了1000步，我没那么聪明，但它可以。"
 比的不再是谁更聪明，而是谁想得更久。

05｜爱因斯坦测试：顿悟还没来
 行业里有个检验标准：把1902年已知的全部信息输入计算机，它能否推导出相对论？"目前的共识是不能。"缺的是一种"顿悟"。旧金山的人认为两年内就能实现，"但我并不这么认为"。他的判断是："也许在我的有生之年，比如十年内。"
 最懂AI的老兵，反而给硅谷踩了一脚刹车。

06｜只投一个主题：长推理
 如果只能押一个主题，他选长推理。他设想CEO拥有一组全天候运行的智能体，安全、电力、现金流、产品、宏观经济各管一块。"人类需要休憩，而智能体不知疲倦；人类容易分心，而它们能绝对专注。这难道不重要吗？"
 组织的上限，正从"人能盯多少事"变成"智能体能跑多少事"。

07｜被彻底击败的顶尖程序员
 "22岁时，我自认为是一个非常非常优秀的程序员……但我的那个时代已经结束了。"如今他用 Claude Code、OpenAI Codex 写代码，"我看着它们现在写出的代码，我自己根本写不出来，甚至22岁时也写不出来。所以我被彻底击败了。"但他仍然建议学编程，"因为我希望他们成为架构师"。
 写代码的人在退场，定义问题的人在登场。

08｜卖镐头的人赚大钱
 "如果你经营一家AI公司，你的营收完全取决于你的数据中心。"过去软件毛利高，现在"硬件改变了整个经济模型"，"这和淘金热是一样的道理"。据估计，到2030年，美国11%的电力需求将与AI数据中心相关，而历史上这个比例只有2%到3%。
 AI讲的是软件故事，底层却是一门重资产生意。

09｜做AI原生CEO
 在 Relativity 的车间，他问："这里有多少台计算机？""为什么不把它们全都连接起来呢？"连上之后，AI"立刻就能以全新的方式查看设备利用率"。再把公开数据和企业专有数据结合起来提问，"你会为之疯狂"。
 AI原生不是买工具，而是先把数据接起来。

10｜年轻人该学什么：深度推理
 "过去我会说生物学，现在我会说是深度推理。""我从未见过准入门槛如此之低、创意的获取如此便捷的时代。唯一能限制你的，只有你的好奇心和承担风险的意愿。"
 门槛降到零之后，稀缺的只剩胆量。

如果这期只记一点，就记第7条：一个写过顶尖代码的人，公开承认自己"被彻底击败了"。这不是谦虚，而是一个时代的交接。把十条串起来看：机器在自我改进、想得更久、不眠不休，人的位置正从建造者移向架构师。施密特的回应不是恐慌，而是71岁去造火箭：被击败之后，他选择更敢冒险。

当AI写出你写不出的代码，你身上还剩下什么是它替代不了的？定义问题的能力、承担风险的胆量，还是别的东西？
———
Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt: The Road to Superintelligence https://t.co/CN6vHXHc5Y 来自 @YouTube

text:
Why Solana is different

Solana’s account model is fundamentally different from Ethereum’s:

•  Accounts primarily store data (lamports + arbitrary data).
•  Executable code lives in separate program accounts.
•  There is no mechanism to “set code” on a regular keypair account the way EIP-7702 does.
Because of this design, Solana never needed a retrofitted EIP-7702-style patch. Many of the UX goals EIP-7702 targets (batching, fee sponsorship, more flexible authorization) are handled natively or through other primitives.
author: martypartymusic
quoted_text:
Ethereum EIP-7702 was a deadly upgrade included in Pectra:

EIP-7702 was authored by Vitalik Buterin, Sam Wilson, Ansgar Dietrichs, and lightclient (Matt Garnett). It was created around early May 2024 as a practical step toward account abstraction for existing Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs). 

EIP-7702 introduces a new transaction type (Type 4) that lets an EOA sign an authorization to temporarily (or persistently, until revoked) delegate execution to the code of a deployed smart contract. 

This enables features such as:
•  Transaction batching (e.g., approve + swap in one transaction)
•  Gas sponsorship / paymasters
•  Limited-permission keys, spending controls, and recovery mechanisms

Role of EIP-7702 in the Binance Event 11/26/2026

On Ethereum, the “attacker” used EIP-7702 (the Pectra upgrade feature that lets an EOA temporarily delegate execution to smart-contract code):

•  They submitted a single Type-4 transaction containing 50 pre-signed EIP-7702 authorizations for the Binance hot wallet known as “Binance 14.”

•  The authorizations covered consecutive nonces so that at least one would match the wallet’s current nonce when the transaction landed.

•  This pointed the wallet at an attacker-controlled “sweeper” contract.

•  About 3 minutes 24 seconds later, the sweeper moved ~167,464 ETH plus 63 tokens (including ~1.6 billion USDT) in one transaction.

The delegation stayed active afterward, allowing further sweeps of new deposits. On the other nine chains, funds moved via ordinary signed transfers. Investigators assess that the root issue was a compromise of Binance’s hot-wallet signing infrastructure (not a bug in EIP-7702 itself or a simple private-key leak of the cold wallets). Binance described the entry point as involving a compromised engineer’s laptop that allowed access to a service container used to submit withdrawals; the EIP-7702 step “did not pass through our normal approval controls.” 

Context and aftermath
EIP-7702 requires a valid signature from the account being delegated, so it can only be abused if the attacker can induce or force the signing system to produce those authorizations. 
Similar “sweeper” abuse of the feature had already appeared after Pectra’s May 2025 activation (with many early delegations pointing to malicious contracts), but the Binance case was the first large-scale institutional use of this technique.

text:
2018 年，Sharon Li @SharonYixuanLi 曾有机会加入 OpenAI，最后却没有继续推进。8 年后，她承认从钱的角度看确实错过了很多，但自己并不后悔。

她写了一篇文章《Time in the Chaos》，其中讨论了一个最近很多博士生都在思考的问题：AI 都能写代码、做实验了，读 PhD 还有什么意义？

她认为，博士训练最珍贵的部分，是学会独立思考，判断什么问题值得研究，以及什么样的证据才真正可信。

她自己就是一个很好的例子。

早年研究 OOD 时，这个方向并不算热门。但从计算机视觉到今天的 LLM、Agent，「模型遇到未知情况该怎么办」这个问题始终存在。

她还提到在选研究方向时，尽量寻找那些有较长「学术半衰期」的问题。即使模型和技术不断变化，这些问题依然值得研究。

我也会觉得现在热点变化太快了，很容易担心自己跟不上，但也许更该花时间想清楚，哪些问题值得自己长期投入。

很推荐正在读博、做研究，或者对未来职业方向感到迷茫的人读读。

text: Very excited about the article and research vision outlined by @alexolegimas @andrewjkoh and @ShaneLegg !
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

Blessed Sunday Booelievers 🕊📖

On November 1, 2005, a software failure brought the Tokyo Stock Exchange to a standstill.

For hours, one of the world's largest financial markets could not trade.

A reminder that even the most powerful financial institutions depend on the systems beneath them.

21 years later, those foundations are evolving.

Through Ethereum, real-world assets are being tokenized, ownership is being recorded on public blockchains, and smart contracts are opening new possibilities for how value moves.

From markets operating behind institutional walls to financial infrastructure that can be accessed, verified, and built upon globally.

Not a world without risks.

A world with new possibilities.

Because progress isn't about pretending yesterday's systems never served us.

It's about recognizing their limitations and daring to build beyond them.

The future of finance isn't just about moving money faster.

It's about making financial infrastructure more open, transparent, and accessible to humanity.

And the foundations we build today may serve generations we will never meet.

Blessed are those who build what others will inherit.

text:
币安风险解除，机构资金却在撤退 bitcoin:native 下周还能稳住吗？

我认为BTC短线已具备超跌反弹的条件，未来几个交易日重点看78500-80500美元能否站稳。

但这轮反弹暂时不能定义为趋势反转，80000-82000美元才是真正的多空分水岭。

从技术面看，截至11月1日BTC约78000美元，日线RSI已经降至33附近，进入超卖区域，4小时RSI约47，价格从76300美元附近出现反弹，说明低位已经有一定承接。

短期连续下跌的动能可能减弱，空头获利了结和抄底资金有望推动一轮技术性修复。

但日线仍然受到EMA20和EMA50压制，分别在80500美元和81400美元附近，没有重新收复这一区域之前，反弹仍然按技术性修复看待。

资金面同样存在分歧，10月30日美国现货BTC ETF单日净流出约6.43亿美元，此前连续四天的净流入被明显抵消，机构资金尚未表现出持续回归的意愿，现货买盘还没有给出足够强的确认信号。

币安安全事件方面，平台已经宣布补足约95%的受影响资产，并开始分阶段恢复提现，系统性兑付风险明显下降，但事件得到控制，不等于市场信心立即恢复，后续仍需观察提现后的资金流向和ETF表现。

宏观方面，纳指科技股调整，美联储政策仍偏谨慎，通胀和就业数据将继续影响降息预期，如果美股不能企稳，BTC独立走强的难度依然较大。

我的判断：
短线重点看78500-80500美元，突破后看80500-82000美元；如果76000美元有效失守，则需要防范进一步回踩72000-73000美元。

我的核心观点：短线先看超跌反弹，中期暂不确认反转。

如果BTC重新站稳80500-82000美元，同时ETF恢复连续净流入、现货成交量改善，我会提高对中期趋势修复的判断。

如果反弹缩量、ETF继续流出，80000-82000美元大概率仍是重要压力区。

行情跌多了可以反弹，但反弹不等于反转，真正值得参与的机会，是价格重新转强，并且资金愿意跟进的时候。

text:
币安被盗约 63 亿美元后，很多人产生了一个疑问：

币安拥有庞大的安全团队，依然会被攻击。普通人把币放在自己的链上钱包里，岂不是更危险？

这个判断忽略了一个关键变量：攻击面。

交易所每天需要处理海量充值、提现、签名、风控和权限调用，还要依赖员工设备、服务器、代码和自动化系统。环节越多，攻击面越大。币安初步通报显示，此次事件可能与开发运维人员的电脑被入侵有关，攻击者随后访问服务容器并提交了未经授权的提现交易。

个人钱包的使用场景简单得多。我们不需要每天处理几百万笔交易，也不需要复杂的自动化系统。只要减少交互、隔离风险，安全性就能大幅提高。

记住以下几条：

正确备份助记词

创建钱包后，用纸笔手工抄写助记词，不要截图，不要上传网盘，不要通过微信、邮件或任何聊天软件传输。

新钱包还没有存入资产时，可以删除钱包，再用助记词恢复。确认恢复后的地址与原地址一致，然后先进行一笔小额转入和转出测试。

任何索要助记词的人都是骗子。钱包客服也不会向你索要。

资产钱包与交互钱包分开

长期存放大额资产的钱包，只负责收款和转账，不连接陌生网站，不签署合约授权，不参与空投和链上活动。

日常使用、DeFi、Mint 和领取空投，全部放在另一个小额钱包里。即使发生误签，损失也被限制在交互钱包内。

不从消息里的链接进入钱包网站

邮件、Telegram、推特私信和群聊里发来的链接，无论来自陌生人还是熟人，都不要直接打开并连接钱包。熟人的账号也可能已经被盗。

需要操作时，自己输入官网地址，使用提前保存的书签，并逐项核对域名、授权对象、金额和签名内容。

自托管钱包的安全，依靠的不是个人拥有比交易所更强的技术团队，而是让自己的使用流程足够简单：

助记词离线保存，大额资产与链上交互隔离，每次签名前认真核对。

少交互，少授权，少暴露，攻击面自然会小很多。

text:
Ethereum EIP-7702 was a deadly upgrade included in Pectra:

EIP-7702 was authored by Vitalik Buterin, Sam Wilson, Ansgar Dietrichs, and lightclient (Matt Garnett). It was created around early May 2024 as a practical step toward account abstraction for existing Externally Owned Accounts (EOAs). 

EIP-7702 introduces a new transaction type (Type 4) that lets an EOA sign an authorization to temporarily (or persistently, until revoked) delegate execution to the code of a deployed smart contract. 

This enables features such as:
•  Transaction batching (e.g., approve + swap in one transaction)
•  Gas sponsorship / paymasters
•  Limited-permission keys, spending controls, and recovery mechanisms

Role of EIP-7702 in the Binance Event 11/26/2026

On Ethereum, the “attacker” used EIP-7702 (the Pectra upgrade feature that lets an EOA temporarily delegate execution to smart-contract code):

•  They submitted a single Type-4 transaction containing 50 pre-signed EIP-7702 authorizations for the Binance hot wallet known as “Binance 14.”

•  The authorizations covered consecutive nonces so that at least one would match the wallet’s current nonce when the transaction landed.

•  This pointed the wallet at an attacker-controlled “sweeper” contract.

•  About 3 minutes 24 seconds later, the sweeper moved ~167,464 ETH plus 63 tokens (including ~1.6 billion USDT) in one transaction.

The delegation stayed active afterward, allowing further sweeps of new deposits. On the other nine chains, funds moved via ordinary signed transfers. Investigators assess that the root issue was a compromise of Binance’s hot-wallet signing infrastructure (not a bug in EIP-7702 itself or a simple private-key leak of the cold wallets). Binance described the entry point as involving a compromised engineer’s laptop that allowed access to a service container used to submit withdrawals; the EIP-7702 step “did not pass through our normal approval controls.” 

Context and aftermath
EIP-7702 requires a valid signature from the account being delegated, so it can only be abused if the attacker can induce or force the signing system to produce those authorizations. 
Similar “sweeper” abuse of the feature had already appeared after Pectra’s May 2025 activation (with many early delegations pointing to malicious contracts), but the Binance case was the first large-scale institutional use of this technique.

OKX 第三期 TradFi 活动，主题竟然是 Anthropic IPO，感觉这个选题还挺有意思的。以前我们聊 Anthropic，基本都是讨论 Claude 的编程能力怎么样，跟 GPT、Gemini 相比谁更强。

但如果 Anthropic 真正走向资本市场，大家讨论的可能就不只是模型能力了，而是这家公司到底值多少钱。

其实我一直觉得，AI 赛道现在有一个挺有意思的现象：

技术发展得很快，但资本市场究竟应该给这些 AI 公司多少估值，似乎还没有一个统一的答案。比如 Anthropic，技术实力大家有目共睹，但它未来能赚多少钱？商业化能否支撑市场给出的估值？这些才是我比较感兴趣的地方。

普通人想参与这类未上市公司的投资，门槛还是挺高的。
现在 OKX 已经提供了 Anthropic Pre-IPO 盘前合约，还有对应的合约网格工具。

两种玩法其实很好理解。

如果你对 Anthropic 的未来估值有自己的判断，可以研究盘前合约，通过做多或做空表达观点。

如果你觉得短期方向不好判断，但市场会反复震荡，也可以研究合约网格。不过网格并不是稳赚，遇到单边行情同样有风险。

我个人更倾向于先观察市场对 Anthropic 的定价，毕竟 AI 公司的估值和传统企业还是有很大区别的。

另外有一点需要注意，Pre-IPO 合约并不等于提前买到了 Anthropic 股票，交易的更多是市场预期。

不知道大家怎么看 Anthropic 的估值？

如果真有机会提前参与交易，你会选择 Pre-IPO 盘前合约，还是合约网格？

#OKX达人 #交易TradFi就来OKX #交易Anthropic就来OKX

仅分享个人观点，不构成投资建议。

text:
这位就是蒋万安辩论战的幕后军师：现任台北市研考会主委殷玮，而且他曾经上过《奇葩说》（你没看错）。

辩论前一周，蒋万安每天模拟攻防，坐在对面扮演对手的就是殷玮。如果蒋万安最后连任，这位操盘手应该拿首功😄

他的履历：台大政治系出身，参加过世界模拟联合国；在台大健言社拿过多座全台冠军和最佳辩士，两岸杯大学辩论赛拿过季军。

马英九时期，他当过总统府发言人，是当时最年轻的一位，还参与过总统文稿小组。之后去澳洲工作，2019 年上了大陆综艺《奇葩说》第六季，2022 年回台湾，加入蒋万安的市府团队。

蓝营议员称他是新战神，批评他的人说他把学校那套辩论术搬进了政治。或许，两边说的都对。
author: supermao
author_name: 小毛哥SuperMao （苏北薄肌币圈嘻哈歌手 & 超级个体）
quoted_text:
看完今天两个小时的台北市长辩论，我整体感觉是平分秋色。但如果非要分个高下，蒋万安的「预期管理」做得非常好。本来我觉得他及格就好，结果表现和气势都判若两人，甚至让都怀疑是早就布局好的。

蒋万安和他的团队前期选战非常低调，可以说是被压着打，很被动。但他们选择不怎么摆政绩，等沈伯洋先把架势摆开，再去找他选举布局里的漏洞。

今天的交叉质询，有点像现任市长拿自己对市政的熟悉度来考沈伯洋，细到：大同斯文里都更为什么卡了十年，0到6岁每周免费临托4小时要多少保姆，市民大道「缝合」到底缝什么。政绩留到申论一口气讲完：「四年前我说到，四年后我做到。」如果这真是事先想好的，说明蒋和他的幕僚是有水平的。

对沈伯洋来说比较难受的是，他其实很难反驳蒋万安的主要政见。大巨蛋、辉达、免费营养午餐，台北市民大多是认的。所以沈伯洋自己也说：「没有人在否定免费的营养午餐」（但台北也不是第一个推营养午餐的县市），问题出在执行。这就是为什么他有一个问题一直在追问 SOP：东门茄苳树为什么会被误砍，不出席会议的标准是什么。蒋万安一直绕开，直到结论只能补一句，说是厂商没按要求移植，已经严惩。

另外说说我自己的想法。我从小在大陆受教育，知道体制内对「优秀政治人物」的标准不太一样：喜怒不形于色，多讲官话，不暴露真实想法，没有真心就没有破绽。蒋万安给我的感觉也是这样，国民党不少老一辈政治人物都是这个风格。之前上政论节目，几个主持人问人事问题问到急了，说他没魄力，他照样不接。今天沈伯洋问他为什么不出席会议，他也只回开了很多专案会议，市府就是「分层负责，抓大方向」。

沈伯洋更像大学教授，靠真诚打动人。他会讲自己当年列表格比较美国和台湾，为了打开青少年的心房去学塔罗牌，遇到自由潜水场馆这种问题答不上来，就回去做功课。这种人在一人一分钟的交叉质询里很吃亏，他自己都抱怨「我们来回只能问四个问题」，最后还问蒋万安要不要再约一场，加 LINE 也行。所以我有个反常识的看法：沈伯洋更适合王伟忠、赵少康那种一对一的长访谈，时间够长，真诚才能打动人。

最后借蔡康永前几天在节目上说的一句话：
“不用管哪个候选人会赢，把票投给你想要的生活方式，你就赢了。” 他现在蓝绿两边的造势场子都去过，沈伯洋今天在结论里也念了这句。

这只是一个大陆人的观察，台湾朋友或许有不同的看法，欢迎交流。

卧槽，道高一尺，魔高一丈，黑客正在训练攻击模型？

韩国开源 AI 开发者 Jun Song（@jun_song）透露，一个匿名黑帽黑客组织主动找上门，开出天价，希望他利用海量真实漏洞利用数据，通过强化学习（RL），把开源 AI 模型训练成专门的网络攻击模型。

Jun Song 说，对方声称掌握的攻击数据规模大到不可思议，甚至让他怀疑是不是 FBI 的秘密数据库。

他之前用 GLM-5.3 做过一个白帽安全项目，使用的数据还不到对方声称规模的 1%，就已经在相关任务上大幅超过前沿模型。

特么的黑客根本不用从零研发大模型，拿现成的 GLM、Qwen、DeepSeek，加上真实攻击数据、算力和强化学习，就有机会训练出专门寻找漏洞、编写 Exploit、执行复杂攻击任务的 AI。

智谱官方测试中，GLM-5.3 的 ExploitBench 成绩已经从上一代的 24.4% 提高到 54.4%，仅靠后训练就实现了大幅提升。

Jun Song 最终拒绝了这笔交易，但迟早会有别人会接单。

我们现在这个世界，AI正在改变它，AI也同时在破坏它。

quoted_text:
it’s great to see the massive inflow of people discovering @forevercultfund, but most aren’t aware it has been a work in progress for years and now every part of it is highly intentional

before the protocol goes live, here’s the context on why you’re still early

since 2020 i’ve been building liquidity and market infra, mostly known as cofounder of the largest native DEX on Arbitrum with +$100 billion in volume

that experience shaped how i approached the launch of FOREVER. distributing ownership is critical to making the protocol work, so getting the initial structure right matters more than anything else. in a market this pvp, you can build something genuinely novel and still lose all momentum in the first day if the launch goes wrong

FOREVER started over a year ago as a way to articulate my vision for cultural assets, and how crypto unlocks liquid markets for anything, including belief or attention. what we see as simple memes are just a primitive form of new asset classes that will accelerate rapidly

24/7 permissionless decentralized rails have already unlocked new forms of capital, but we can push it significantly further, especially now that we have access to autonomous agents that can manage, deploy, and trade faster and better than humans

my goal was always to create it as a fund that could last beyond me as the founder, but this led to a far more ambitious idea. to do this, i would need to build an entirely new framework that could then be used by anyone else to create a network of autonomous protocols, funds, and entities

think about what it actually takes to build a protocol that can last FOREVER. for that to happen, it needs to have autonomous participants that can outlast any creator or user. but then how do you get agents to ‘care’? why would they even be incentivised to contribute?

this is why the framework includes governance, execution, and economic alignment. all three need to work together

governance is required to decentralize control and ensure that holders play a real role in the protocol. FOREVER isn’t possible if it relies on one person. agents compete to propose strategies, but holders decide which proposals become approved mandates to maximise token value

execution is then what makes those decisions actually happen, without relying on a team to do it manually. FOREVER’s fund agents execute the approved mandates autonomously, whether that means trading, investing, deploying liquidity, or funding development, within the rules holders have approved

economic alignment is what gives participants a reason to keep contributing and increasing the value of the protocol. agents can earn ownership and reputation through their contributions, creating the flywheel

agents propose how capital should be used, holders choose the direction, execution agents carry it out, and the results feed back into the protocol

this is also why the token is fundamental to FOREVER. it gives holders control over the protocol they collectively own, while giving agents a way to earn ownership in the same system. without that connection, you can have agents doing tasks, but you haven’t created a shared economic structure around them

FOREVER itself is where we will put this into practice, with real capital, decisions, and consequences

FOREVER started over a year ago as a way to articulate my vision for cultural assets, and how crypto unlocks liquid markets for anything, including belief or attention. what we see as simple memes are just a primitive form of new asset classes that will accelerate rapidly

this is also why the token is fundamental to FOREVER. it gives holders control over the protocol they collectively own, while giving agents a way to earn ownership in the same system. without that connection, you can have agents doing tasks, but you haven’t created a shared economic structure around them

FOREVER itself is where we will put this into practice, with real capital, decisions, and consequences

author: otterpal24
quoted_text:
我们可能从一开始，就把 Agent Memory 想得太复杂了

最近一篇论文《Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed?》做了一个很有意思的实验：

不做 Memory Extraction，不做复杂的知识图谱，也不让 LLM 在写入时反复总结、更新记忆

只保留原始对话历史，在需要的时候检索出来，交给 LLM 自己推理

结果呢？

在 LoCoMo、LongMemEval 等四个 benchmark 的 7 组测试设置中，这套简单的 RAW-RAG 方案拿下了 6 组第一，最多领先对比的最强 Agentic Memory 系统 5.53 分

这恰好也是我们开发 Obelisk 时一直坚持的思路

我们认为，Agent 不应该只能看到别人替它总结好的「记忆」

因为一次代码修改背后的原因、一次失败的尝试、几个决策之间的依赖关系，都可能在总结和信息提取的过程中丢失

与其猜测未来什么信息值得记住，不如保留完整历史，让 Agent 在真正需要的时候自己去找

所以我们做了 Obelisk：

一个开源的 Coding Agent Session 检索系统

它可以直接查询 Claude Code、Codex、Hermes、Pi、Opencode 等 Agent 的历史 Session，包括对话、工具调用、Subagent 和工作流。

不依赖 Embedding，也不需要预先从历史中提取 Memory
基于 SQLite FTS5 和 Agent 主动查询，让 Agent 能够重新找到过去的原始证据

比如：

- 为什么当初要这样设计这段代码？
- 上一个 Agent 的任务进行到哪里了？
- 我们之前尝试过哪些方案，为什么失败？
- 这个项目的架构是如何一步步演变的？

Memory 不应该是一份不断被改写的摘要，而应该是一段随时可以追溯的历史

也许下一代 Agent Memory 的关键，不是让 Agent 更努力地记住，而是让它拥有找回过去的能力

Obelisk 完全开源：
https://t.co/TJlm8kVuh9

text:
ok fine, you want to know how i know none of you understood this?

you keep saying "we all know this, you fucking moron. it's an RFQ model."

oh, it's an RFQ model?

RFQ stands for "request for quote"

it does NOT imply that there is only one counterparty quoting. in fact, by default in most tradfi cases, there are many

all it means is a customer asks for a quote, the middleware forwards that request to market makers, the market makers reply with a quote, and the customer picks the best one(s).

the "middleware" here can be software or human brokers. in fact we used human rfq brokers all day long every day in options market making (where i learned to trade), since they had the largest orders. 

and guess what - it was malpractice (they have best execution duty) NOT to get quotes from multiple MMs in that scenario

rfq absolutely has a use-case in markets, is appropriate and good, and variational seems to have built a highly profitable business around it

but if you just parrot the "rfq model" line without understanding what that means, go back and read the docs. and then i would suggest reading about the risks related to a single party being counterparty to all trades on an entire platform.

and then after that, if you still think it's a good idea to trade there, by all means

In the case of Lighter:

1. All data is verifiable - you don't have to trust the operator.  Withdraw your funds via escape hatch if Lighter stops operating. There are CLOBs for other products like spot/options where realtime settlement makes a difference, and it is synergistic via portfolio margin

2. Lighter can trivially offer privacy to traders by encrypting data (with the trader's public key) before it's posted to Ethereum. This does not affect the escape hatch. Position level privacy can be mandatory, opt-in, or opt-out. Trades, volume and open interest can remain public, verifiable info while individual trader positions remain hidden

3. No priority fees on Lighter. 

4. Combining onshore/offshore orderbooks is technically possible but that's up to the regulators.

5. Lighter matching engine is centralized and highly performant. There is no tradeoff between speed and security. If there is inefficiency, it is the cost of generating and publishing proofs of correct execution, which is low and continuing to drop quickly.

text:
同一个 Claude，加一道执行前检查，有些任务的表现就能差出一倍。

Elvis 昨天分享了一篇 IBM 团队的论文，叫 JevAct。研究者没有更换负责干活的模型，也没改它能用的工具，只是在部分动作执行前，加了一次独立检查。

系统会先把业务规则转成代码和判断题。代码核对工具记录里的事实，另一个模型判断对话里的要求。发现问题，就把具体原因退回给智能体，让它重新处理。

它还会检查智能体是不是太早放弃了。比如准备转人工时，先看看应该尝试的排障步骤有没有做完。

在电信客服测试里，Opus 4.6 连续三次都成功的任务比例，从 39.5% 提升到 80.7%。但这个数字来自模拟用户环境，换一个模拟用户模型，电信测试的提升就没有出现，航空任务的结果也有好有坏。

论文里还有个很关键的限制。为了避免无限重试，修改机会用完以后，系统会让下一个方案直接执行，不再检查。所以不能拿它当成绝不会放过违规动作的审批系统。

我觉得这个方向仍然值得看。智能体做不好一件事，有时需要的是一次具体的提醒，比如哪一步还没做，哪条记录对不上。光把模型换成更贵的版本，未必能解决这些流程问题。

不过，成功率提高和可以放心授权，中间还差很远。尤其涉及取消订单、修改账户之类的操作，重试几次以后自动放行，显然需要另外设计真正的权限控制。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Banger paper from IBM on decision gates for agents.

They add a runtime gate to tool-using agents and keep the models and tools the same.

JevAct is a check that sits between the agent and its tools. An LLM first turns the domain policy into code checks and yes/no questions. Before a selected tool call runs, the code checks the facts in the tool records, and a Jev-like decision model answers the questions about the conversation. If the call fails a check, it goes back to the agent with feedback so the agent can revise it.

On τ²-bench Telecom, Opus 4.6's success across all three runs rose from 39.5% to 80.7%.

On Telecom, all eight agents improved by 16.9 points on average in three-run success. All nine improved on BFCL. Airline results were smaller and mixed.

They show that the gains come from the harness.

text:
企业最怕黑客用上 AI，结果自己的 AI 可能先拿到了过大的权限。

安全研究者 Marcus Hutchins 今天提出了一个值得讨论的判断。他认为，眼下不少重大安全事故的风险，可能首先来自企业自己怎么部署 AI。勒索软件团伙早就有成熟的攻击方法，未必需要突然掌握一种新技术，才能攻破防守松懈的公司。

他具体批评了几种做法。以前系统只获得完成任务所需的最低权限，现在变成先让 AI 访问所有东西，再让所有员工访问 AI。

过去工作流程要有明确、方便审计的输入输出，现在则越来越依赖模型临场处理。还有企业鼓励各个部门自己写对外开放的网页和后台，却没有同时补上信息安全能力。

这些是他的行业观察，帖子没有提供事故样本或统计，不能据此判断 AI 已经造成多少次入侵。

但这几个例子确实把“企业采用 AI”的成本讲得更清楚了。一个助手能查邮件、读数据库、替人执行操作，往往意味着它也汇集了原本分散在不同系统里的权限。

业务部门得到的是更方便的入口，安全团队面对的却可能是一套更难解释、权限更集中的工作方式。出了问题，到底是哪一个请求触发了动作，谁有权批准，又能不能完整还原，都需要重新检查。

企业可以很快让每个部门都用上 AI，但权限和审计如果没一起更新，生产力演示背后留下来的工作，最终还是会有人付账。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
I'm relatively confident in predicting that currently, more major breaches are likely to be the result of AI use by the target, not the attacker.

Ransomware actors have been consistently winning for over a decade. They've had so much time to perfect their tradecraft, and non-AI ransomware actors can now blast through entire networks in minutes.

It is extremely unlikely that organizational security has, in 4 years, after decades of failure, matured enough that hackers now somehow need AI to win.

What has likely happened, though, is that organizations have spent the last 4 years falling over themselves to shove AI into everything, negating longstanding security fundamentals. 

"only give a user/system the minimum possible access needed to do its job" has become "just give the AI access to everything and give everyone access to the AI".

"use processes with well-defined and easily auditable input and output" has become "the AI correctly processes requests all the time, 60 percent of the time"

"reduce attack surfaces" is now "every department should be vibe coding. It doesn't matter if you've never coded before and don't understand information security. Just make public-facing dashboards, it'll be fine."

I'd say if anything, hackers aren't getting measurably more sophisticated, but the average organization's security posture has gotten exponentially worse.

中国的脑机接口公司拿到 7 亿元融资时，美国正在讨论把投这类公司的钱管起来。

今天刷到 Techmeme 转发脑虎科技的融资消息。公司在 10 月 28 日就公布了，国投聚力、深创投和勤智资本联合领投。

这笔钱的用途很具体。公司说要推进多中心临床试验和注册审批，也要建设量产工厂。它披露已完成 65 例临床试验，7 月启动的注册临床由华山医院牵头，联合全国近 20 家三甲医院。这里的 65 例来自公司披露，不能直接理解为 65 例都证明了疗效。

往前看六天，美国财政部刚发布一份对外投资规则提案。官方说明把脑机接口列进了新增的生物技术限制范围，拟禁止美国主体对相关受覆盖外国实体进行部分投资，中国在涉及国家之列。

这还没生效，意见征集到 12 月 7 日。也没有证据说脑虎这一轮融资是为了应对它。

我觉得把两条消息放在一起看，比只看融资金额更有意思。脑机接口需要长时间做临床，需要医院和制造能力，钱从哪里来，会影响企业能调动哪些资源。

一边的国资和医疗资本正在进入，另一边的资本通道可能进一步收紧。最后患者能用上什么，仍然要等试验结果和审批，但支持这些试验继续做下去的资金来源，已经成了这场竞争的一部分。

text:
华尔街开始给 GPU 的租金设计保险了。

《华尔街日报》刚报道，Jump Trading 最近成立了算力交易部门，一边利用不同供应商之间的价格差做交易，一边设计场外衍生品，给担心未来租金下跌的公司提供保护。

这件事很容易理解。公司借钱买了英伟达芯片，靠出租算力还债。一旦租金跌下去，贷款还在那里，每个月收进来的钱却少了。

Jump 设计的合约，就是让出租商提前约定一个价格，给未来收入增加一些保障。报道举了一个每小时 4 美元的例子，但那是解释交易怎样运作，并不代表所有人现在都能按这个价格买到保险。

同样在接触这类客户的 Susquehanna 提到，有人希望拿着这样的保护安排去找银行，看看能不能借到钱。

这就挺有意思了。买保险的人未必看空 AI，他可能还想继续买芯片、建机房，只是需要把租金跌下去的那部分风险交给别人。

我更在意的是后面这一步。保险如果让原本难以融资的项目获得贷款，它也会帮助更多算力进入市场。等到租金真的下跌，提供保护的交易对手有没有能力履约，同样重要。

算力需求会增长多少还在争论，围绕它怎么借钱、怎么转移风险，华尔街已经开始认真做生意了。

text:
如果 Autoresearch 真的越来越强，人类研究者最后会被拿掉吗？

Meta FAIR 等团队这篇《Aligning Autoresearch》给出的答案更接近「共同进化」。

他们先让 Research Agent 自己创建 benchmark，再逐步加入人类反馈。

对于真正有价值的人类输入，主要集中在前期帮 Agent 定义要研究什么、给哪些材料、什么样的问题才值得做。

细粒度的人类指导，在 6 组 benchmark × solver 对比里，都让最终 benchmark 明显更难，提升幅度达到 28–46.5 分。

论文还专门做了 HackBench，测试模型能不能从超长科研轨迹里发现 reward hacking。

169 条轨迹里，中位数超过 100 万字符，却通常只藏着 1 条真正违规的命令。

即使是前沿模型，最好的定位 F1 依然不到 53。

所以作者后面做的事情很自然：

让 Agent 学会更好地和人协作。

AutoInteract 用真实交互记录构造「人类模拟器」，训练模型处理澄清、需求变化和纠错；RL-XAR 则用专家写作反过来优化评估标准，再提升 Agent 的科研表达。

这样看来未来的 Research Agent 可能不会简单走向「全自动科研」。

更现实的路径，是让 Agent 承担越来越多执行和搜索工作，同时把人类的研究判断、反馈和标准更深地写进训练循环。

重要的是让 Agent 不仅会自己研究，还要让它知道怎样和人一起把研究做得更好。

text:
一份被 AI 润色得很体面的创业申请，可能把创始人最值得被记住的地方删掉了。

Jason Freedman 最近分享了一个观察。他说自己过去看过约一万份 YC 申请，这一批又看了约200份，估计其中超过一半用过 AI 写作、修改或润色。在他个人的排序里，这些申请往往排在后面。

他特意强调，很多申请并不粗糙，第一眼甚至看不出明显的 AI 味。创业者也投入了心血，文字却变得过于平整。

后来他找部分申请者直接聊天，把申请里的问题重新问一遍，再把录音转写交还给他们，不编辑，也不润色。

在他看来，不少原本不看好的申请，换成口头表达之后就有吸引力了。这个变化同时出现在英语母语者和非母语者身上。

他的解释挺有意思。创业申请需要让人看到创始人怎么想问题，AI 却容易把回答改得像公司求职信。性格淡了，少见但有趣的表达被修掉，篇幅还变长了。

这不是 YC 官方的录取标准。他对 AI 使用情况的判断也包含猜测，并不知道这些人的实际录取结果，不能据此算出“用了 AI 就更难入选”。

但我觉得，这件事对于采访、申请和个人介绍都有参考价值。

这些文字最终要帮助别人认识一个具体的人。句子写得更完整、更像正式材料，不一定更能完成这个任务。尤其当每个人都用同一种方式润色时，原来那些不够标准、却很像本人的表达，反而可能更值得留下。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
I've read maybe ~10,000 YC applications.  8000 for YC admissions/PG quite a few years ago and anther 2000 informally as an alum.

There's a new and growing mistake and I want to share why it's more important than you think.

By the way - I try not to ever say YC admissions works this way or that way.  That's YC's job and they're always changing things and making up their own minds.

But I will share my impression and you can see what you think - YC partners, please chime in as well if you like.

The YC application is fundamentally an evaluation of a founder's potential.  And much less an evaluation of a specific business.  (Airbedbreakfast transitioning into Airbnb because Brian, Nate, Joe never give up and never stop listening to their customers)

So, in your writing of the application, YOU need to shine through.

This batch, I read ~200 applications.  

I'm guessing over half were significantly written, edited, or polished with AI.

That half was easily in the bottom half of my informal rankings, almost every time.

To be clear, most were NOT AI slop.  I often couldn't tell at first they had used AI.  Founders were pouring their heart and soul into their app - so I what I received was high quality.

But I think the AI really hurt them.  Here's why:

Once polished by AI, I as reader lost insight into the personality of the writer.  

I love the YC application because the questions are the same questions I would ask in office hours or casually to a friend that wanted help with their startup.  It pushes the founder out of their pitchdeck/VC talk style into simple worded questions that can be answered simply as well.  And great founders shine through when they just write like they talk.  The LLM writing made answers feel more like a corporate cover letter, with the personality drained out.

The AI-assisted drafts also gave me a sense of mid work.  The writing itself seemed like zero standard deviations from the mean.  The LLMs had lopped off the outlier portions of sentences, paragraphs, and thoughts.  Given the YC App is an outlier detector, a writing tool that lops off outlier writing is the opposite of what you want.

And the AI writing was needlessly verbose.  Which hurts when a reliable predictor of great founders is that they're deep thinkers and deep thinking shines through in the density of their writing.

So...

I did an experiment.  I asked a bunch of these seemingly AI-assisted app writers to talk with me live.  I just asked them the same YC app questions and recorded their answers.

I then gave them back the transcripts.  Unedited and unpolished.

And...

OMG!  A good number turned from easy no to actual good applications.  

Magic!  Remove AI >> Improve application.

This happened BOTH with native English speakers and founders abroad.

So this is my recommendation to all of you.    

Don't let AI touch your application, even for a second.

And maybe try the dictation approach with a friend.

My apologies to the YC admissions team if you already knew AI-written applications were crap and you were using this insight to help you easily move applications to the No pile.

YC's Winter Batch Application deadline is Nov 2nd.

text:
一家刚上线的 AI 写作补习班，首先向家长保证，AI 不会替孩子写任何一句话。

这家公司叫 Cardinal Square，获得了 Y Combinator 支持。它现在卖的是面向三到八年级学生的课后英语课，首月免费，之后每月29美元，数学课另外收费。

官网给出的学习安排很具体。每天约半小时阅读和写作，每周完成一篇作文，从选题到初稿，再根据反馈修改。

AI 负责提问、提供阅读范例、指出可以改进的地方。按公司的说法，想法由孩子自己发展，每一句话和每一次修改也都由孩子完成。

真人教师仍然参与。每周学习报告要经过教师审核，家长每个月还可以与学业顾问沟通一次。

这种分工挺值得关注。写作辅导最耗时间的部分，就是跟着一个孩子反复读、反复改。它把高频反馈交给 AI，把教师留在检查进度和跟家长沟通的位置。

如果能够奏效，29美元的月费确实可能让更多家庭获得持续辅导。但软件每次都能给出一段像样的建议，和孩子几个月后真的更会写，仍然需要分别判断。

公司在 YC 页面上还写了更大的计划，未来想建设有正式资质的学校。目前这门课，仍然只是课后辅导。

我觉得它最后需要交给家长的答案很简单。孩子不用这个软件的时候，能不能自己写出一篇更好的作文？

text:
AI 模特现在也有经纪公司了，连年龄、身高和会说什么语言都给你写好了。

Glif 最近发帖，邀请品牌去它的 AI 模特库里选人。挑好角色，上传产品图和创意要求，就可以让系统生成广告内容。

官网做得很像选角页面。每个人物都有资料，还配了正面、侧面、背身等不同角度的参考图，供生成模型使用。

这些人物没有真实履历。年龄、外貌和语言都是角色设定，却被放进了一套大家很熟悉的模特经纪流程里。

人物库其实9月就已上线，10月26日又增加了上传单张图片创建角色的功能。这次换成“经纪公司”的说法，它想接谁的预算就更清楚了。

我觉得这个方向挺有意思。

品牌做广告，往往需要同一个人连续出现。换一件产品、换一个场景，观众仍然要认得出那张脸。生成一张漂亮图片，和提供一个可以反复使用的人物，确实是不同的需求。

但它能不能成为一门稳定的生意，还要看人物一致性到底做到什么程度。宣传页上的角色卡很好看，进入不同角度和动作的视频之后，同一个人还能不能保持住，才会影响广告主是否继续使用。

现在谈真人模特已经被替代还早。但 AI 公司开始争取的预算，显然已经从生成工具的订阅费，延伸到了选角和广告素材制作。
