text:
做市實戰筆記 #3，這篇拿我在東京 AWS 上跑的 AS 模型做市 bot 做 backtest，看參數到底該怎麼設，順便回答前兩篇留下來的問題。

已知，被聰明的單吃掉才是做市商最大的成本。
求：回測看那一點點利潤被逆選擇咬掉之後還剩多少？

先確定模擬器靠得住。我拿公開成交重播 bot 第一次實跑的那段，模擬出來每小時 1,553 筆、每小時虧 48.63 USD，實際是每小時 1,547 筆、虧 47.56 USD。那段 6.6 小時跌了 3.81%，算蠻兇的盤，這樣都對得上，後面的回測才有意義。

再看預設參數。風險厭惡 0.12、成交率衰減 1.5、T 12，丟進 20 個乾淨樣本日（9/1 起每 3 天抽一天到 10/25，再加 10/29），平均每天虧 320.63 USD，沒有一天賺錢。

圖一是訓練期 10/26、10/27 的淨利熱力圖，越綠越賺、越紅越虧，黑線是損益兩平，白星是表面上的最佳組（風險厭惡 0.01、成交率衰減 0.25、T 6）

#2 花一大段講 T 在永續上很尷尬，實測它對損益影響有限。風險厭惡只要壓在 0.1 以下也都差不多。

這跟 #2 講的對得上。基本價差最受「掛遠一點成交機率掉多快」影響，這個參數設小，模型會覺得掛遠也有人吃，報價就拉寬，被知道方向的人咬到的次數也跟著變少。

圖二是最佳組在四段時間的累積淨利跟庫存，含 1 bps 手續費。左邊淨利看起來都不錯，10/26 收在 70 左右，10/28 收在 50 出頭。重點在右邊的庫存，藍線很常頂到 ±4000 上限然後躺好幾個小時。

10/27 晚上 9 點後一路空到上限、BTC 一直漲，淨利就在那段吐光。庫存卡在上限的時候 bot 已經不是在做市，比較像抱著一張方向單在賭。
所以我做了更嚴格的驗證。27 組參數先用 sha256 凍結，再丟進事先固定好的 20 天，避免自己偷看結果回頭改。

圖三上半部是三組參數每天的淨利，黃底是調參用過的 10/26 到 10/28，那三天幾乎都是正的，一離開黃底就正負亂跳，賺的時候幾十塊，9/28、10/29 一天就虧一百多。下半部是預設組，20 天全紅，10/29 一天虧超過 500。

圖四把 26 組疊在一起（預設組虧太多沒畫）。紅叉是樣本內日均，幾乎都在右邊賺 20 到 40；藍點是樣本外 20 天日均，全部在零的左邊。這個落差就是過度擬合長的樣子。

所以如果你把一切丟給 AI 去掃參數、挑最好看那格，大概就會挑到白星這種假的最佳化參數。

更痛的是這 27 組扣手續費前的毛 bps 全部是負的，手續費還沒算就在虧，問題不在費率等級，#1 講的逆選擇在這裡直接變成數字。
參數要怎麼設，我的看法是成交率衰減降到 0.2 左右，跟預設比虧損可以少大概 97%。風險厭惡要調的話，先把成交率衰減固定，用線上校準的到價成交強度做網格回測，再去樣本外驗證，別三個參數一起掃。

AS 跟 GLFT 都只管庫存，不管價格接下來往哪走。#1 寫的時候這還只是理論上的盲點，跑完這 20 天才知道它有多貴。
參數調得再漂亮也只是少被咬幾口，要賺錢得加方向訊號或逆選擇過濾。

熱力圖
成交率衰減最重要。

越綠代表訓練期越賺，綠色只擠在成交率衰減 0.15 到 0.25 那一窄條，往預設的 1.5 走就一路轉紅；在這條帶子裡，風險厭惡只要壓在 0.1 以下都差不多。這個參數設小，模型會把報價拉寬，被知道方向的人咬到的次數就變少。

累積淨利和庫存圖
表面上賺錢的日子，其實是運氣使然，賭對了方向。

左邊是含手續費的累積淨利，看起來都不錯；重點在右邊的庫存。藍線常常頂到 ±4000 上限，一躺就是好幾個小時，這時 bot 已經掛不出另一邊的單，等於抱著方向單在賭。10/27 晚上空單頂滿、BTC 一路漲，淨利就是在那段吐回去的。

每日長條圖
參數只在調它用的那幾天有效,換到別的日子就失靈。

黃底是調參數用過的 10/26 到 10/28，那三天幾乎都是正的；一離開黃底就正負亂跳，賺的時候幾十塊，9/28、10/29 一天就虧一百多。下面的預設組 20 天全紅，10/29 一天虧超過 500。

森林圖
樣本內的好成績到了樣本外整個消失,也就是過度擬合。

紅叉是樣本內日均，藍點是事先凍結好、樣本外 20 天的日均，橫線是 95% 信賴區間。紅叉全在右邊賺 20 到 40，藍點全在零的左邊，這個落差就是過度擬合。最佳組樣本外每天 −23.84 USD，整段信賴區間都在零下面。成交率衰減 0.3 的兩組墊底，庫存上限放到 8000 的也排在後面，抱越多虧越多。

2、借贷即支付：当借贷资金使用的时间够短的时候，借贷即支付，不同Agent账户不同授权来提高安全性

quoted_text:
【隨手分享】
​
來稍微分享一下最近的交易思考和計畫，這波幣圈的下殺，很大程度上讓估值模型回歸到一個比較合理的狀態，我主觀認為山寨幣的估值要再回到過去的水位應該是見不到了。

這個思考背後的判斷邏輯是，即便是這輪市場最佳狀態的時候，VC 融資額也已經遠遠比不上前一個週期的峰值了，哪怕是一半都不到，而高估值天花板的項目也沒有那麼多了，越來越少傻逼會上當，講白話一點就是故事賣的差不多了，了無新意沒有更多夢想、理想能吹了。
​
所以我從今年 02/01 全數清倉之後，一直沒有抄底山寨，也不打算抄，除了零星的空單部位、打狗資金、低水位的 $BTC 持倉外，基本上就是滿手 u，因為自認二級交易沒有優勢，所以基本只做大趨勢，而近期計畫重心將放在美股以及 $BTC 上，我接著說說。
​
先講講 $BTC，其實在這波恐慌下殺的時候，你問問自己就能略知一二，這種跌法，除了 $BTC 你還有什麼敢抄的？至少其他代幣我是不敢，我只相信 $BTC。其次，目前發展起來，我也認為只有 $BTC 有資格也較有明顯趨勢往傳統主流資產靠攏，特點就是波動降低、穩定許多，也可以被看作是死不了的標的。
​
那實際的交易規劃上，我會從 72500 左右開始做左側的分批進場，我認為他還可能再跌，但盈虧比還行加上我不認為我能做到精準猜底，所以 DCA 對我來說不失一個好選擇，我也期待它跌的越低越好，因為雖然盈虧比還行，但目前這個位置我覺得吸引力是不如美股的，期待他跌出價值。
​
再來說到美股，我已經很久沒有介入美股市場，一直在等 2020 年 3 月那種黃金坑機會，因為那年我協助朋友代操資金時，選擇了台股，我完全享受到了黃金坑後暴力 V 反的無腦行情，我深深認知到這是最簡單沒有之一的送分題，心態穩拿的住的話，根本輸不了，是少數大資金能夠翻倍的絕佳機會，而這次的跌法幅度已經接近了。
​
至於選擇美股而非台股港股，最大原因還是我目前只信的過美國，我認為以十年為一週期來看，本週期科技發展大本營和資本的挹注重心還會是美國，也只會是美國。
​
操作部分，我目前剛已經打入了約 30% 的 $QQQ 頭倉，也規劃好了接下來 DCA 的策略。由於這波偏向是川普人為因素點火導致的連環效應崩盤，人為因素佔了思考的太大比例，我又沒辦法預測它接下來會推出什麼策略、會不會亂講什麼話，因此只能刻舟求劍在具有性價比的位置開始介入進場。
​
我大膽假設 $QQQ 最差會到達 350 左右的位置，中途我會在 380 進行加倉，但也做好準備迎接他到 270 的位置，不知道這波下殺盤整會持續多久，要做好長期抗戰準備，拿好拿穩相信美國，等待好結果。
​
至於其他個股，我額外配置了 $TSLA $NVDA $AMD $TSM $PLTR $AAPL $UNH，基本也是參考大盤走勢做 DCA 操作，這部份就純粹是考驗個人審美了，不好評價，但我認為 2025 乃至接下來 10 年，AI 基本定調了是這個週期最重要的路線，所以選股基本都會圍繞 AI 來選，當然我的做法超高度集中科技、AI、半導體類股，以風控的角度來看這麼做肯定不好，但這是我的研究成果，我相信自己的 Bias，下好離手。
​
BTW 引用這篇 @0xSunNFT 的好文是想再重述一下當時 02/01 清倉資產的邏輯，基本上就是鏈上情緒的感知，我在上個週期沒有培養出這個能力，但在這波為期四個多月的高強度打狗生涯幫我ㄋ培養出了這個能力，每天在一級市場打滾多少能感知到流動性的差異、市場情緒的高低，至少自從我開始打狗之後，反而是我二級市場的交易勝率和獲利都有肉眼可見的提升，所以我強烈鼓勵專職二級的交易員也可以來一級感受一下市場脈動，肯定是有點幫助的。
​
本篇文章只是作為我當下思考的記錄，方便我之後進行覆盤回憶，不具有任何財務建議，有任何與我相悖的判斷或想法歡迎留言跟我交流，思維碰撞肯定是最好的進步方式，感謝大家～

text:
The FBI explicitly asked THORChain to block addresses tied to the Binance hack.

THORChain co-founder's argument: the BTC was provided by arbitrageurs, not THORChain. Arbitrageurs sourced it from CEXs, who did the KYC, so it's the CEXs' problem.

But every BTC sent is signed from THORChain's TSS vaults. Nodes hold the keys, earn fees, and can vote to halt the chain, i.e. it works like an exchange.

Then revenue: 85% ($1.2B) of the Bybit hack was washed into BTC via THORChain. Nodes, LPs and front-ends collected $12M in fees from the Bybit hack.

THORChain has to pick whether it is a protocol or an exchange. A protocol has no asset custody, no fees, and no one holding the keys, like Tornado Cash. An exchange means you do what exchanges do: KYC your nodes, blacklist addresses, work with law enforcement.

Holding the keys and the fees while calling yourself "just code" isn't a third option.

text:
马克·安德森（Marc Andreessen）揭示了哈佛商学院是如何建立在一个破产的1941年理论之上的，以及它现在为何正在走向崩溃……
安德森在1994年联合创立了网景（Netscape），并于2009年联合创立了a16z。他花了30年时间支持创始人，并眼睁睁地看着职业经理人CEO败给他们。
这种模式可以追溯到一本书：詹姆斯·伯纳姆（James Burnham）的《马基雅维利主义者》（1941年）。
伯纳姆认为，每一个伟大的公司都曾是由创始人运营的。
亨利·福特经营福特。鲍勃·诺伊斯经营英特尔。
如今，埃隆·马斯克经营着特斯拉、SpaceX和星链（Starlink）。
然后，他说，有些东西崩坏了。
在19世纪80年代到20世纪20年代之间，一种新的理念取代了创始人。它被称为“管理主义”（managerialism）。
职业经理人现在将掌握一种可以跨越任何企业的“便携式”通用技能。
其结果是诞生了：
 哈佛商学院
 斯坦福商学院

author: tBTC_project
quoted_text:
tBTC pause and security update

tBTC remains fully backed, and no funds have been lost. About 4,320 BTC sits in the bridge wallets against roughly 4,185 tBTC in circulation, and we've seen no unauthorized minting or movement of BTC. You can verify the backing on-chain here: https://t.co/2kAVMbgz8s

As a precaution against a recently disclosed Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432), which can allow remote code execution on unpatched servers, every tBTC node operator has either patched their servers or taken their nodes offline until a fixed kernel is available. So far, we have not found evidence that this vulnerability was used to exploit any tBTC node.

Separately, earlier today, one node operator reported a security incident in its broader infrastructure, unrelated to the kernel vulnerability, in which the Ethereum account its tBTC node uses to pay transaction fees was drained of about 0.5 ETH. The operator's tBTC node was already offline at the time, and the operator has found no evidence that its signing key material was accessed.

tBTC wallets require a majority of independent operators to sign any Bitcoin transaction, so no single operator can move funds.

Bridge functionality will resume once security maintenance is complete and nodes are back online on patched systems.

We'll post the next update within 24 hours, or sooner if anything changes.

Fun fact: both IPFS pins for Off-Chain Art are already dead, while the centralized links are still up.

That’s exactly what Off-Chain Art was about. I made it in 2025 as an experiment: one artwork stored at several links and resolved in the browser. Both the artist and the collector could add more links, so no single link could take the work down. The experiment worked, and it became MURI Protocol.

I just shipped a new MURI Protocol website, with a much better interface and new features:
• Upload to Arweave through @ar_io_network Turbo, paid with x402
• Upload to IPFS through @pinatacloud, paid with x402
• No USDC on Base? Swap or bridge to it from any chain in a few clicks with @RelayProtocol 
• Automatic fallbacks everywhere: it uses the first working Arweave or IPFS gateway and the first working RPC, so it keeps working when a service goes down
• Automatic token discovery: just enter a collection address

It’s all free and open source, and MURI takes no fees.

Thanks to @archivist for collecting Off-Chain Art, which made it possible to build MURI as a free public good.

MTS-ification is flattening most categories of tech work

It's probably the most interesting and import idea to absorb and study to understand the future dynamics of the job market, and how to take advantage of them

TLDR is that titles used to describe "what we do", post-AI they describe "what we own". Depth is rentable, so passing work around costs more than doing the work itself. AI can fill in the "average" so what’s left to stand out is a combination of agency, judgement, and spike: the thing(s) you do better than almost anyone. 

Invest in and become fluent with as many relevant AI tools (and techniques) as possible, be able to explain simply and clearly how you can use them to expand your capacity and span adjacent specialties complementing your main.

Emerging categories to position for (beyond MTS):
Growth staff (me): marketing / sales / partnerships / community / devrel
Operations staff: finance / people / legal ops  / internal tools
Customer staff: support, customer success, account management, solutions engineering, implementation 

In interviews and on resumes
1. Lead with your "spike", have ultra-crisp stories where it was the reason behind a great success
2. Have ultra-crisp stories exemplifying agency and good judgement that have driven some outcome end to end and the impact
3. Say “I,” not “we,” and be ready to describe exact details

There are big changes and things are being shaken up, with all disruption though there are always tons of opportunities, the people who move quickly and get in front of them the fastest will have the most upside. There are SO many new companies with crazy growth, pre-unicorns and new unicorns hiring like crazy, you want to be part of a company that will 10x or 100x over the next 10 years, not one that is about to have to reshape everything because they themselves are being disrupted.

One-step text-to-image generation just got a major upgrade.

Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) adds a simple feature-moment loss—matching mean and per-coordinate std between generated and teacher images, using only the generator’s own EMA copy. No external encoder needed.

On LongText-Bench at just 2 network evaluations, IDM hits 94.25% (Chinese) and 90.20% (English)—new state-of-the-art. It matches or beats previous leaders on FID, GenEval, WISE, and more, all at sub-0.45s latency per image.

Ablations show the feature-moment loss isn’t optional: drop it and every metric falls. And those EMA features? As good as heavyweight DINOv2 encoders.

The upshot: IDM closes the quality gap in fast text-to-image with minimal overhead. Instant, high-fidelity image generation is here.

⚠️ We will never ban event or news trading on @VestExchange.

We will always try to give you the most leverage and trading opportunity we can, while staying sustainable so we can keep doing payouts.

That's why Temporary Leverage Limits (TLL) now also apply to Vest Capital accounts around major market events.

Events and limits:
→ Nonfarm Payrolls, CPI and FOMC: $ES, $NQ, $RTY and $YM at 5x, $GC and $SI at 3x
→ Single-stock earnings: 1x on the reporting stock

Each limit runs from 15 minutes before the event to 15 minutes after it.

When a limit starts:
→ You can still open or add to positions, up to the reduced leverage
→ Limit orders more than 2% above the reduced leverage are cancelled. Reduce Only orders stay, unless the position is reduced or closed
→ Positions more than 2% above it are reduced to the limit. Margin stays in the position and its size shrinks. Fees and any loss on the reduced part come from that margin
→ If your account is not in drawdown and covers the new margin, nothing is reduced
→ If your account is more than 1% below starting capital, those positions are closed in full
→ Take Profit and Stop Loss orders stay active. Fixed-size orders shrink with the position, so check them afterwards

When the limit ends, normal leverage returns. Cancelled orders are not restored and reduced positions keep their new size.

To avoid an automatic reduction, reduce or close your positions before the window starts.

Full rules: https://t.co/4KLX9LwuOG

Fun fact: both IPFS pins for Off-Chain Art are already dead, while the centralized links are still up.

That’s exactly what Off-Chain Art was about. I made it in 2025 as an experiment: one artwork stored at several links and resolved in the browser. Both the artist and the collector could add more links, so no single link could take the work down. The experiment worked, and it became MURI Protocol.

I just shipped a new MURI Protocol website, with a much better interface and new features:
• Upload to Arweave through @ar_io_network Turbo, paid with x402
• Upload to IPFS through @pinatacloud, paid with x402
• No USDC on Base? Swap or bridge to it from any chain in a few clicks with @RelayProtocol 
• Automatic fallbacks everywhere: it uses the first working Arweave or IPFS gateway and the first working RPC, so it keeps working when a service goes down
• Automatic token discovery: just enter a collection address

It’s all free and open source, and MURI takes no fees.

Thanks to @archivist for collecting Off-Chain Art, which made it possible to build MURI as a free public good.

quoted_text:
BREAKING: Inside Starcloud, the $2.3B Startup Putting Data Centers in Space

FACTORY TOUR - Redmond, WA

Primes quoted them $75M-$100M to build their first data center in space. They did it for $2.5M.

In just 21 months, Starcloud is one of the fastest companies to go from founding to orbit.

With $450M in total funding from Manhattan West, Nvidia, Cisco, Benchmark & EQT, the team walks me through their mission for AI in space.

I toured the new HQ w/ CEO @PhilipJohnston + co-founders @EzraFeilden & @AdiOltean

AI compute on Earth is limited by power & permitting. @Starcloud_ is moving it to orbit, where solar power is nearly constant. Philip says the dawn-dusk orbit alone could fit about 10 TW of compute, roughly 20x the entire US power grid. Once launch costs fall below $500/kg, he says compute in space will be cheaper than on the ground.

From Starcloud 1, Starcloud 2, to Starcloud 3, we saw: 

Tracking Starcloud 1 live in orbit, circling Earth every 90 minutes at 17,000 mph with the first Nvidia H100 in space.

Co-Founder & Chief Engineer Adi Oltean walks through Starcloud 2 as the team fires the latches that deploy its 120 ft solar wingspan. It launches in January with 100x the power of Starcloud 1. 

Co-Founder & CTO Ezra Feilden shows the 16-ton secondhand vibe table. The team bought it for $200K, instead of paying $1.5M & waiting 2 years for a new one, they rebuilt it over a weekend.

Engineering Manager Bailey Montaño leak checks the ion thruster after vibe. Bailey designed the radiators, which have 10x less mass & cost 500x less per watt than the ISS’s. 

In the fab shop, Ezra shows the Starcloud 3 demonstrator, a 2-ton, 235 kW vehicle that fits 50 to a Starship. 

Camilo Lopez cuts stainless on the laser cutter. 

Engineering Operations Lead Miguel Rivera, formerly of Helion Energy, teaches me to MIG weld.

The tour ends in the new campus, about 100,000 sqft built to produce 100 satellites a week toward an 88,000-satellite constellation.

逆向工程界这两天迎来了一个极其亮眼的 Rust 开源新项目：craft-anything。

它的定位非常硬核：帮助工程师彻底理解手头任何封闭软件的底层工作原理，并在理解的基础上重新构建出属于自己的原生版本。

不同于传统的 Ghidra 或 IDA Pro 只专注于将汇编语言反编译成伪代码，craft-anything 的切入维度是在系统行为层面做全景观测。

你给它输入一个未知的可执行文件或前端打包应用，它会在沙箱内自动Hook该软件所有的系统调用、内存状态机迁移以及网络底层协议封包；
接着利用内置的符号执行引擎，自动将散乱的 API 请求和内部事件流，拓扑重构出一张完整的业务架构交互图；
最后直接生成一份结构清晰的模块化规范与骨架代码。

对于想要学习优秀开源项目、或者需要逆向对接遗留系统私有协议的工程师来说，这套工具几乎把原本需要几天的人工抓包分析压缩到了几分钟之内。

源码用纯 Rust 编写，内存占用极低，跨平台运行丝滑顺畅。

开源地址：https://t.co/92hFokzgaj

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
Recommendation used to need a giant company because ranking billions of items took an engagement model and years of click data.

Now one person points a model at 43M HN comments and gets a better watch list than YouTube in about 2 hours. 

The signal was always there in what smart people keep linking. Reading all of it just got cheap.

Personal feeds get built on demand from here, and the engagement-optimized ones have to compete with that.

text:
CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) remote use-after-free in the Linux kernel IPv4 TCP handshake (kernels 4.4+).

During connection setup the kernel frees IP options memory while another CPU may still be reading it to build a SYN-ACK. A remote attacker can race this to leak kernel heap data, corrupt memory, crash the host, or (with MPTCP listeners, default in recent Go) achieve unauthenticated root RCE.

Fixed upstream via kfree_rcu; many distros still patching. Mitigate by dropping TCP packets with IP options or disabling MPTCP until updated.

text:
a16z's Connor Love on why the old defense model gave soldiers systems "developed for 10 years ago," and how private capital lets startups build what they need before the Pentagon asks:

"I experienced this in my past when I served in the Army. The buyer is not the user, and the appropriator of the dollars for the buyer is completely removed."

"You had primes who would just sit there and listen, like, 'Tell me what you want. I'll develop the thing after you give me the money.'... You get a system that was developed for 10 years ago."

"The beautiful thing is venture capital and what we do in American Dynamism, but also the rest of the capital markets is saying, 'We will actually fund that in advance.'"

"The outcome of that is the soldier gets a better product, gets something that actually fundamentally changes the battlefield and helps with deterrence or security or safety."

"More importantly, you get a type of system that is actually aligned with the requirement of the market and what technology can do today."

"Instead of sitting and waiting for the government to tell you what they want, the government signals, and you see it, and you build it in advance by using private capital, and that just has not happened in the history of defense."

text:
THE BLOCK: Bitcoin staking protocol b14g lost about 97 million CORE (~$1.5M) on Saturday after an attacker asked to withdraw 0 tokens from 91 positions it didn’t own. Core’s staking code reads 0 as "withdraw everything," and b14g let the requests through, per Bitquery.

b14g said it paused the affected contracts and that about 68 million of the stolen CORE remains on Core, while exchanges have frozen roughly 9 million. BTC staked through b14g stays time-locked on Bitcoin and was not affected. The team has promised a post-mortem on the technical cause.

Core DAO said its network is secure and its validators and staking contracts operated normally throughout. CORE staked directly or through other protocols was not affected.

author: TheBlockCo
quoted_text:

The Core network is secure. Core’s consensus, validators and staking contracts operated normally throughout, and CORE staked directly with validators or through other protocols is unaffected.

We’re supporting b14g and exchange partners to trace and freeze the funds. Most of the stolen CORE remains on Core, and exchanges are freezing deposits linked to the attacker.

We’ll share updates as we have them.

text:
从某种意义上来说，朝鲜许多天才的实力比一般的 IMO金牌得主还要更加全面和危险。

国际数学界其实一直流传着关于朝鲜的黑色传说。在每年的 IMO赛场上，朝鲜国家队一直是极其低调但实力恐怖的劲旅，经常斩获全员优异成绩，团队总分杀进全球前列。
但最魔幻的是，其他国家的 IMO 金牌神童在夺冠后，未来的标准剧本是去MIT、斯坦福、剑桥或者清华姚班，毕业后去华尔街做量化、去硅谷做 AI 基础研究。
而朝鲜的这些数学天才们在回国后，他们的名字和档案就会瞬间从国际学术界彻底蒸发。他们被直接送进了高度机密的军事情报部门，比如总侦察局 121 局，进行定向的兵器化改造。

这就是天才在不同国家的不同命运。
这就是学术天才与国家级终极兵器的区别。

大部分IMO 金牌得主，他们解决的是象牙塔里的严密数学证明，顶多也就是量化QR、QT这些，而朝鲜圈养的这群人，他们不仅拥有同样顶级的数理逻辑和破译天赋，还被迫点满了全套的工业级破坏技能。
因为很多的硅谷天才已经习惯了用最先进的 AI 辅助写代码、在舒适的咖啡厅里寻找灵感；而朝鲜的赛博特工在地下室里，许多年里拿着旧电脑，为了攻陷一个万亿级跨国系统，可以不眠不休地用肉眼去死磕几十万行的底层汇编代码和以太坊智能合约漏洞。这种极端高压下训练出来的盲蛛式嗅觉，是温室里的学术天才无法具备的。

同样的，这也是一场残酷的主体性错位。
因为朝鲜的天才少年们没有选择剧本的权利。他们的智力在 11 岁那年就被国家单向征收。他们的天分不服务于人类的智能进步，只能化作了冷酷的铁骑，去劫掠金钱帝国，为遥远故土的导弹试验提供燃料。
author: akitabtc
quoted_text:
我们都小瞧朝鲜了。

人们总觉得，一个连电都充不满、闭关锁国的落后地方，怎么可能拥有全球最顶尖、能洗劫币安 63 亿美元的赛博特工？
事实上，朝鲜在网络空间走的是一条极其冷酷、高效且举国体制的不对称战争路线。在黑客圈子里，朝鲜的赛博军团，以 121 局和 Lazarus 组织为代表被公认为全球最难缠、最没有底线的超级鲨鱼。

那是从 11 岁开始的魔鬼筛选。
朝鲜没有普及的互联网，但他们对顶级心智的筛选比任何国家都残酷。听说朝鲜的情报部门每年会在全国小学里，通过奥数竞赛和逻辑测试，死死盯住那些最具天赋的数学神童。一旦被选中，这些孩子会被直接带离家庭，送进平壤的顶级精英学院进行全封闭的魔鬼式计算机训练。

高中毕业后，最顶尖的人会被送进两所神秘的大学：平壤自动化大学和金日成综合大学。
根据逃离朝鲜的幸存者回忆，他们每天要上 6 节 90 分钟的课，没有任何娱乐。他们的作业不是写写小程序，而是直接去肉身黑进西方、韩国的真实网络系统。教官的理念是，只有在真刀真枪的跨国入侵中活下来的，才配毕业。

由于朝鲜本土经常断电且 IP 受限，这些顶级黑客毕业后，绝大多数根本不留在平壤，而是以商业程序员的假身份被秘密外派到中国的沈阳和大连，俄罗斯、东南亚、甚至东欧。
他们潜伏在境外的高速网络环境中，白天给西方公司远程接单写网页、做 App，甚至给 Web3 项目当远程开发者。
到了晚上，他们就会变身成冷酷的黑客，利用白天潜伏时发现的供应链漏洞或者通过精心包装的 LinkedIn 虚假高薪招聘信息，精准钓鱼各大交易所的架构师。
这次的币安，就是一例。

朝鲜受到全球极其严厉的传统金融制裁，毕竟，SWIFT 系统对他们是关闭的。而加密货币是一个天然去中心化、不需要实名、无法被美国政府直接下令冻结的法外之地。 造一辆坦克、一枚导弹需要无数的钢铁和外汇；但培养一个顶级黑客，只需要一间装有空调的房间、几台电脑、以及无限供应的速溶咖啡。而这个黑客一旦得手，带回来的可能就是几十亿美金的纯利润，这直接占据了该国对外真实外汇收入的半壁江山。

text:
Next exploits waiting to happen in tradfi/web 2 will be because of this new Linux bug. If you run Linux patch immediately. 

Short story

Linux has a bug in the part of the kernel that handles new internet connections (the TCP “handshake”) over IPv4.

When a computer tries to connect to a Linux server, the kernel keeps a little piece of data about that connection (things like certain network options). The bug is a race condition: one part of the kernel can throw that piece of data away while another part is still trying to use it. This is called a “use-after-free.”

Because of that mix-up, an attacker on the internet who can send packets to any open service on the machine can potentially:

Crash the system, or
In the worst case, run their own code with full control (root).
No password or login is needed. The bug has been in the kernel for about 11 years (since Linux 4.4).

Analogy:
Imagine two people sharing a sticky note with important instructions. One person throws the note in the trash while the other is still reading it. Chaos can result. That’s roughly what’s happening inside the kernel.

What to do:

Update your Linux kernel and reboot as soon as your distribution releases a fixed version. Until then, simple temporary workarounds exist (mainly dropping unusual IPv4 packets that carry special options, and turning off Multipath TCP if you don’t need it).

text:
Kalshi just raised $1 billion at a $40 billion valuation. In June 2025 it was worth $2 billion.

What I find most instructive is how it started. Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara founded Kalshi in 2018 after working at Goldman Sachs and Citadel, and spent the first two years getting the CFTC, the US derivatives regulator, to approve it as a federally regulated exchange. The approval came in November 2020, and three months later Sequoia led a $30 million Series A. Their 2020 pitch deck projected $5.1 billion in monthly volume. This October, Kalshi traded $97.8 billion in a single month.

I lived a version of this. In 1991 I started Via USA, which became Viatel, selling international calls through callback: you dialed a US number, got an American dial tone and paid US rates instead of a monopoly's prices. In 1994 AT&T asked the FCC to block us and argued that the service might be wire fraud. The FCC granted our authorization and rejected AT&T's petition. That decision mattered more than any sales pitch I made that year.

It took me years to fully absorb the lesson. When a startup takes on a regulated industry, the permission is part of the product. Kalshi understood that from day one, and Tarek and Luana deserve a lot of credit for the patience it took.

It's the path we chose at Certuma for medical AI. The companies that earn regulators' trust early will be the ones that get to scale.

text:
Last wk, earnings had elements of all the AI issues I feared in my preview. $GOOGL – AI disintermediation fear for search and big FCF miss. $MSFT – neocloud partner pushing out capacity and 1st new fundraising bonds since 2017. $AMZN – AI growth miss in AWS and FCF miss.

Tech took a beating last week with Nasdaq -2.0% and Mag7 -2.4% but with S&P down only 0.6%. However, the nine non-tech related sub sectors (out of the eleven total) were strong and up 1.0-3.1%. As a result, the equal weighted S&P was up 0.8%. The above three names all declined last week with Google down 12.6%, Amazon -3.1% and Microsoft -0.5%. The historic 28.6% stock decline by $INTC on Friday (-24.4% for the week) did not help. This helped drive the SOX Index down 7.2% on Friday though the weekly decline was only 0.8%.

With all the hyperscalers now having reported, here are my current thoughts:

1) Microsoft has committed to staying FCF positive (with $18.6B in FCF in CQ3) and is the only name in this list that has committed to do so. M365 is likely to become the default option for enterprises that want AI in a safe environment through use of Co-Pilot.

2) Meta is using AI to improve the efficiency of their business as seen in their ad revenues compared to Google. Also Muse has been a hit with consumers for Agentic AI while they are appealing to enterprises with their strong open-weight models. An 18x CY27 PE for 28% revenue growth is appealing. Their major blemish is the future negative FCF expected with a $2.1B burn in Q3 driving them to raise ~$95B in equity financing following earnings results. S&P Global Ratings on cash flow concerns and AI spending revised their credit rating today from AA- stable to AA- negative.

3) Amazon despite missing buyside AWS expectations of ~42% y/y growth with 39% reported (official sellside consensus of 38%) expects 40% revenue growth for AWS in CY27 and CY28 despite being the largest public cloud vendor. Also their LTM FCF burn of $42.4B in Q3 vs $7.6B in June helped lead to a $80B supplier financing arrangement facility post-earnings. Also physical AI should benefit their e-commerce business. Both e-commerce and AWS were guided to be $1 trillion revenue businesses within the next 5-10 years.

4) Google’s new LLM model is back at the frontier with a low cost per token. However this miss in search revenues for the 2nd quarter in a row and first miss in both total revenues and EPS for the first time since late 2022 raises AI disintermediation fears. FCF burn of $9.1B was also more than expectations. But total search queries are at the highest levels in five years. As a result, as ad coverage and loads increase on their AI queries, these fears should pass much like in late 2025. Ultimately, I believe Google will be a winner in consumer AI through their distribution through Android phones.

As for Intel, I did not see this coming. On October 20th, $SMCI (purely enterprise related revenues) pre-announced 27% revenue upside along with a raise to gross margins guidance to 12-12.5% from 10.4%-10.8% for their CQ3. I am not a fan of SuperMicro to be clear. For the processor vendors, I thought upside in server revenues due to Agentic AI would offset the downside in their PC business due to memory related price increases lowering demand. $AMD, which is gaining share, reports earnings on Tuesday. This will help investors understand whether this is an Intel specific issue or industry issue. I would note that Microsoft’s guidance for their Windows OEM & Devices business was down ~35% y/y for December vs -22% in September and -7% in June.

Longer-term, I believe Intel will become a force in the foundry industry but in the near-term it may take some time for the valuation to reset lower due to their current microprocessor business.

Looking forward, $AAPL reports on Monday after the close. The stock has been a beneficiary of investors looking to avoid AI companies with huge FCF burns. However, I would be wary into earnings that are likely to provide lower than expected guidance for the December quarter from a combination of higher currency impact, margin compression from semiconductor price increases, iPhone unit pressure from higher ASPs, a slowdown in services revenues and less than expected high margin TAC revenue from Google. Ultimately, I believe Apple will be a winner in consumer AI through their distribution through iPhones. I also believe their new foldable phone will drive a large upgrade cycle in 2027. But in the near-term I believe it is prudent to remove Apple (up 27% ytd) from my Top5 Picks that I put out when 2026 started. As a reminder this is meant to be a buy and hold list for the entire year for those that do not have time to be managing things daily which is what I do. I believe Apple is likely to be a Top 5 Pick at the start of 2027.

We are now entering the seasonally strongest month of the year. Since 1957, which is the inception of the modern day S&P500, November is up +1.8% and tied for the best hit rate with April & December at up 71% of the time. This compares to an average return of 0.7% and hit rate of 61% for all months.

Surprisingly, the returns for November in mid-term election years is even better with an average of 2.6% and hit rate of 82%. This might have to do with the ytd annual return being lower going into the elections at -1.8% through October with a hit rate of 53% so there is a relief rally on the other side.

In summary, this earnings season has been more trick than treat for technology investors. Being more discerning and trading around positions has been the correct tactic. I think will continue to be the case. Let us hope November gives us something to be thankful for.

All the best in the week ahead.

币安黑客终于动了那笔 SOL，可他折腾一圈，换回来的偏偏是比特币。据 ChainCatcher 引 Lookonchain，黑客正把约 97 万枚被盗 SOL 换成 BTC，约合 9,590 万美元。一天前，FBI 刚点名请 DeFi 和即时兑换服务帮忙拦截，这张网有没有收紧，今晚的链上记录给了个不太好看的答案。

先把时间捋一遍。据 PANews 引 Whale Alert，台北时间今天 17:39，币安被盗关联地址转出 48.5 万多枚 SOL，按转出时的价格约 4,635 万美元，PANews 当时还特意提醒，转移不等于卖出。到了 18:38，ChainCatcher 报道说，黑客过去一小时转走了约 48.7 万枚 SOL，正通过 Relay Protocol 兑换成比特币。按 TRM Labs 的统计，这次被盗清单里的 SOL 一共约 97 万枚，换句话说，黑客是要把整包 SOL 都换掉。

反差藏在前一天的那份声明里。据 Cointelegraph 报道，FBI 周六发布声明，说它看到赃款大多先被换成了以太坊，并预计黑客接下来会借 DeFi 和即时兑换服务继续洗，所以呼吁节点运营商、即时兑换平台、DeFi 服务和链上分析公司，拦截与这些地址相关的交易。结果今天 18:29，跨链协议 Symbiosis 发文说，已经发现有人试图通过它转移这批被盗资金，团队正在拦截并已联系币安。它还承认，现有的筛查是按正常资金流设计的，碰上快速、复杂的操作就有监控缺口。

假设你只是今天碰巧在 Symbiosis 上跨了一笔链的普通用户，Symbiosis 也在请资金被挂起或被误回滚的用户找团队复核，而你很可能根本不知道同一时间黑客也在用这条通道。再看黑客为什么偏要换成比特币，ChainCatcher 的解读是，BTC 流动性更好、接受度更广，方便更快转移，而且比特币没有发行方，谁也按不下冻结键。按报道数字粗算，这 9,590 万美元只占被盗约 63 亿美元的 1.5% 左右，后面还有约 20 万枚 ETH、18,270 枚比特币和大批稳定币，币安今天才刚开始分阶段恢复提现。

在我看来，这场追赃已经从“谁能冻结”变成了“谁反应更快”。FBI 的地址名单、链上分析公司的标签、每个协议自己的风控，每一环都得在几十分钟里反应过来，慢一步，几千万美元就换了币种、换了条链。据 Cointelegraph 引 CertiK 的数据，2025 年全年加密安全损失估计约 34 亿美元，其中超过 20 亿美元归于朝鲜相关团伙，按报道数字粗比，这一单就比那一整年的总损失还多。猫是一群各管一段的协议，老鼠只有一只，可它不用开会。

你觉得 DeFi 协议该不该像交易所一样筛查每一笔钱，宁可误伤普通用户也要拦住黑客，还是守住无许可，接受黑客也能用？

text:
这次 @binance 被盗，让我开始认真思考很多以前从未考虑过的问题。

包括但不限于：是否应该出金休息一段时间？是否借助外部资金降低自有本金的风险敞口？甚至是否应该降低当前仓位的杠杆率？

上一次这么高度紧张，还是在我决定「永久不再做山寨币套利」的时候。

焦虑会使我的状态明显下降，甚至无法正常思考，有一种毫无意义地燃烧大脑 Token 的感觉。

但我也知道，从进化生物学的角度来看，焦虑并不是毫无意义的。

那些对危险更加敏感、草木皆兵的祖先，或许更有机会活下来，把基因传递给我们。

可我仍然愿意继续留在这个行业，因为这里还有太多让我觉得值得研究、值得参与的东西。

生物的本能是远离危险，而人的理性，应该允许我们在认识危险之后，依然有选择靠近它的自由。

最后，我不希望自己因为侥幸而留下，也不希望自己因为恐惧而离开。

text:
回到行情吧，如果你翻开K线去看23年2月中旬到3月中旬那段，会发现走法挺像的，市场氛围也有一点相似，甚至我沿用的指标目前状况也如出一辙。

显著不同的其实是IV水平了。我好奇那个时候我做了什么操作，因为从我置顶的PNL图可以看出那个时间段我做得非常不错，所以我就让AI去分析当初的期权成交记录来一看究竟。

由于当时用了broker的平衡下单，所以成交记录比较凌乱，全是大片大片的0.x张仓位成交。AI进行了笼统的合并，我觉得也大差不差。

总而言之就是我在大跌前进行了一部分滚仓，出现下跌导致滚仓部分被套，于是在下头又重新换了strike更低的合约继续赌多，最后成功赌对了，至于那些短期末日的折腾，我已经想不起来在干什么了。

那回到现在，我怎么做的？10月30日的期权到期后我就没有新开多头头寸了，我好像暂时没那个自信去继续买多头期权赌他能快速打回82K+。今天我甚至又重新把75K左右的put买了回来，为的是对冲一部分现货，保持一个低比例仓位去观察下后续。

逻辑在于如果能复刻23年走法，那打回80K+再去追也不迟；如果疯涨即便我忘了平这些put，顶多也就损失1.6个BTC而已（这就是put对冲的好处之一了）；如果向下跌破75K，对我来说是一个不太乐观的信号；进一步跌破70K，那就更糟了。宏观层面说实话目前完全比不上23年那会儿，所以主观上先防守一波吧。

这次孙哥非常罕见地给出了具体的观点和计划，已翻译为中英双语，值得一看👇

───
【一、断言区块链终将彻底取代现金】
• 正如互联网无情淘汰传统报纸，犯罪分子与正常资金本质上都在追逐资金流转效率

• 传统现金才是洗钱的真正温床；很多人误以为加密是洗钱天堂，但恰恰相反，公开透明的区块链账本才是全球执法部门追踪与冻结黑钱的终极武器。

───
【二、东南亚杀猪盘洗钱全在传统银行，链上反而是克星】
• 主持人提到关于东南亚杀猪盘的调查长文，孙宇晨指出，犯罪团伙真正依赖的是传统金融体系，资金电汇到开曼等离岸银行就彻底凭空蒸发，传统银行根本无力拦截

• 波场联合 Tether、TRM Labs 成立的 T3 金融犯罪调查联盟（T3 FCU），过去三年直接在链上协助全球警方冻结了逾 3 亿美元黑钱。

───
【三、1000亿稳定币护城河：日清算300亿，粘性来自真实刚需】
• 针对外界对加密用户“留存差、缺乏忠诚度”的质疑，孙宇晨表示，波场稳定币规模已超 1000 亿美元，日均清结算稳定在 300 亿美元

• 用户留存不再靠早期炒币暴富预期，而是因为 7x24 小时全球实时清算、天然兼容 CLI / AI，清算效率在维度上彻底碾压 Swift、Visa 和 MasterCard。上一轮牛市充斥了太多无意义的 Meme 空气币，本轮将全面转向真实落地场景

───
【四、Q4大力推代币化美股（Tokenized Equities）】
• 永续合约、DeFi、NFT 等纯币圈原生创新已触碰天花板，而代币化美股和 AI 带来了外部万亿级增量

• 波场 Q4 将正式上线美股代币化资产，商业逻辑与 USDT 一致：第三世界国家的大多数普通人极度渴望配置美元和核心 AI 科技股（$AAPL、$TSLA 等），但根本没有开立美国本土银行账户与通过繁琐 KYC 的可能。把纳指与核心美股搬上链，是给全球散户一个低门槛配置全球最优质资产的入口

───
【五、未来不是80亿人类账户，而是800亿AI智能体账户】

• 波场目前注册账户数突破 4 亿，日均净增约 50 万

• 孙宇晨认为未来 10~20 年是彻底的机器对机器（M2M）经济时代。目前互联网流量已经有超过 50% 来自 Agent，当全球人口背后数十倍的 AI 智能体接入网络进行日常支付与结算，链上账户体量将突破 800 亿，AI 高频微支付才是公链真正的终局爆发点

───
【六、美国战略全面提速：波场微策略 + 首只TRX现货ETF敲钟】
• 美股上市公司 TRON Strategy 已经连续 250 天顶格定投增持 TRX，被贝莱德（$BLK）、高盛（$GS）、摩根士丹利（$MS）、富达等华尔街巨头建仓持股，并成功纳入罗素 2000 指数

• 全美首只 TRX 现货 ETF（代码 $TRXS）已在芝加哥期权交易所（CBOE）正式挂牌上市。美国机构普遍抗拒直接托管链上私钥，ETF 彻底消除了私钥管理与合规审计风险。

───
【七、 Vibe Coding 时代】
• 自主经济体蜕变：
  没有加密支付，AI 永远只是被动听指令的廉价打工工具；一旦被赋予了钱和链上微支付能力，AI 才能蜕变为真正独立的经济实体。今年波场推出 BAI 平台（日均交互超 150 万 Token），通过极简 API 让智能体直接用 Crypto 调用全球顶级大模型并互相结算

• 玩具与超级电池
  Muse 等智能体是跑在前端的“玩具”，波场 BAI 就是玩具背后的“智能超级电池”。无需死板绑定某一家云厂商，BAI 会根据任务需求智能调用大模型并实时结算 Token，既省钱又保护隐私，不玩就拔掉电池

• Vibe Coding 降维打击：
  Claude Code 引领 Vibe Coding 狂潮，自然语言直接消灭了软件工程实现的中间摩擦层。未来不再需要是专业程序员或代码高手，普通人只要给 Agent 提明确要求、给建议，Agent 就能全自动写出代码并交付产品，彻底消除冗余抽象

Rafael Vivas (@rfvivas) dropped out of high school, got kicked out of his house, and was a billionaire by 32.

When he joined AppLovin, he had one condition: he had to live inside the office. Adam Foroughi built him a bed from IKEA. He said:

“The only way that we’re going to win is we’re going to have to out-hustle everybody else.”

When a partner called Cheetah squeezed AppLovin too hard, he started a game studio to compete with them and named it Lion Studios, “because lion is the only animal that can kill a cheetah.” It went from zero to over $250 million in revenue in two years.

Raf has a lot of ideas on dealmaking, persistence, attention to detail, why he’s against delegation, and why retiring at 28 made him miserable.

This is a fascinating conversation about purpose, performance culture, and staying in the game.

Now that the Internet is increasingly becoming fundamentally insecure, including the new Linux find that if any TCP ports are exposed to the Internet it can be completely taken over, people are talking about new private internets. 

The new private internet is real life. It’s clubs. It’s secret societies. It’s real physical in person connection with gatekeeping. Its tribes. It’s friend groups. It’s a room with someone at the door saying what’s the password. It’s physical files in a cabinet guarded by a dude with a gun. It’s shredding and burning sensitive documents so your security isn’t compromised. The new private internet is just what people were doing before the internet. 

In a future where everything digital can be exploited, it turns out that the physical world may be the most secure of all the options.

MTS-ification is flattening most categories of tech work

It's probably the most interesting and import idea to absorb and study to understand the future dynamics of the job market, and how to take advantage of them

TLDR is that titles used to describe "what we do", post-AI they describe "what we own". Depth is rentable, so passing work around costs more than doing the work itself. AI can fill in the "average" so what’s left to stand out is a combination of agency, judgement, and spike: the thing(s) you do better than almost anyone. 

Invest in and become fluent with as many relevant AI tools (and techniques) as possible, be able to explain simply and clearly how you can use them to expand your capacity and span adjacent specialties complementing your main.

Emerging categories to position for (beyond MTS):
Growth staff (me): marketing / sales / partnerships / community / devrel
Operations staff: finance / people / legal ops  / internal tools
Customer staff: support, customer success, account management, solutions engineering, implementation 

In interviews and on resumes
1. Lead with your "spike", have ultra-crisp stories where it was the reason behind a great success
2. Have ultra-crisp stories exemplifying agency and good judgement that have driven some outcome end to end and the impact
3. Say “I,” not “we,” and be ready to describe exact details

There are big changes and things are being shaken up, with all disruption though there are always tons of opportunities, the people who move quickly and get in front of them the fastest will have the most upside. There are SO many new companies with crazy growth, pre-unicorns and new unicorns hiring like crazy, you want to be part of a company that will 10x or 100x over the next 10 years, not one that is about to have to reshape everything because they themselves are being disrupted.

text:
Commanding Heights is either a fragmented thoughtful analysis or a hit piece on certain kinds of technological progress, or both.

Commanding Heights views the current evolving societal paradigm shift through an outdated vertical lens. Decentralized protocols add horizontal organizing principles to top-down command and control creating a sturdier, smarter, wealthier and more real-time connected social fabric. The result isn't a few owned heights but omnidirectional, fractal expansion, with firms shrinking on average and every person a prime mover in their own contexts.

"Own the rails or pay those who do" assumes the rails must be owned. We're adding horizontal organizing principles, via rigorously decentralized protocols, to the age-old top-down command and control architecture of the global economy and society. This Commanding Heights framing ends up serving the incumbent concentrations of wealth and power that have reasserted control with every past upgrade to the system of the world.

It also assumes a bipolar US–China world and misses the internet nation, the network state and a possibly massively multipolar (read: more decentralized) future. Nation-states will use decentralized protocols and crypto, and some will craft their own permissioned DeFi. But global DeFi will move faster, with deeper liquidity and more powerful innovation.

They cite Coase, and in this context Coase points the other way: the firm gets more granular. Large firms will fragment into spin-outs that serve their old parents or fill new niches. Firms will get smaller on average and far more plentiful. Many more people will become sense-making, prime-mover nodes, conducting their own team of agents, larger machine intelligences and other humans, on a credibly neutral trust layer like Ethereum that fosters real-time discovery, composability and frictionless coordinated collective actions. That's omnidirectional agile fractal expansion, not perpetual command and control with its inherent rigidities.

We're becoming a hybrid human-machine cognitive apparatus for the planet, molting from poking at machine intelligence with our fingers into the hybrid organisms' next quasi-stable form. For a while, human needs/constraints, motivations and judgment will be a key rate limiter so while it will move fast it will remain manageable.

Every human will be empowered to do what they want and build what they want. Every person will have access to world-class expertise in nearly every domain and to a credibly neutral, protocol-based decentralized trust machine: the modular Ethereum ecosystem. No one gets deplatformed or censored, everyone shares one source of economic truth about what happened and in what order, and everyone has unprecedented control over their financial life.

And Web3 is under construction. It is the user-centric web, where properly privileged, often bespoke compute, crafted by machine intelligence, comes to our secure and private data, not the other way around.

text:
Anthropic engineer Andrej Karpathy (ex-OpenAI, ex-Tesla AI lead):

“Agents aren’t magic. Opus 5.5 is just the brain. The /harness is what makes it useful.

Give a smaller model the right tools, graphs, and feedback loops, and you can turn wasted capacity into a self-improving agent.”

That’s the idea behind Karpathy’s 16-minute breakdown: stop obsessing over model size and start building the system around the model.

Big model → small model → right tools → closed loop → self-improving agent

The model can have enormous capacity, but most of it is wasted if you keep feeding it work it doesn’t need.

The harness changes the equation. It gives the model tools, captures what happens, and loops the results back into the next run.

Most people keep paying for a bigger model. The real edge is building the loop that makes a smaller one useful.

More valuable than another $2000 AI course.

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
币安 @binancezh @Binance 按照此前公布的计划，分阶段恢复提现服务。

做过大型系统工程的人应该比较容易理解这种操作。

在工业系统调试中，我们经常采用空载测试、逐级加载的方式，先验证系统运行，再逐步增加负荷。

大型金融系统的灾后恢复也是类似逻辑：先控制风险敞口，再逐步开放真实业务流量，验证系统稳定性。

工程上称为 Staged Recovery（分阶段恢复）或 Controlled Ramp-up（受控负载爬升）。

不急于一步到位，而是让每一步都可监控、可验证、可暂停。

从项目管理和风险控制角度看，我个人认为这是一种比较专业的恢复策略。

text:
tBTC pause and security update

tBTC remains fully backed, and no funds have been lost. About 4,320 BTC sits in the bridge wallets against roughly 4,185 tBTC in circulation, and we've seen no unauthorized minting or movement of BTC. You can verify the backing on-chain here: https://t.co/2kAVMbgz8s

As a precaution against a recently disclosed Linux kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432), which can allow remote code execution on unpatched servers, every tBTC node operator has either patched their servers or taken their nodes offline until a fixed kernel is available. So far, we have not found evidence that this vulnerability was used to exploit any tBTC node.

Separately, earlier today, one node operator reported a security incident in its broader infrastructure, unrelated to the kernel vulnerability, in which the Ethereum account its tBTC node uses to pay transaction fees was drained of about 0.5 ETH. The operator's tBTC node was already offline at the time, and the operator has found no evidence that its signing key material was accessed.

tBTC wallets require a majority of independent operators to sign any Bitcoin transaction, so no single operator can move funds.

Bridge functionality will resume once security maintenance is complete and nodes are back online on patched systems.

We'll post the next update within 24 hours, or sooner if anything changes.

quoted_text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
I shared this idea with a few people at Zcon 7 last week. It was striking how quickly something related to it happened.

First, my condolences go out to the individuals and all the families involved here. However, the point is simply to present this new perspective about Zcash large miners.

Large mining operations are becoming high-value physical targets. As a result, there’s a growing probability that major miners will need dedicated air defenses (including counter-drone systems) to protect their resources. The key question is how much this will raise their operating costs?

While some level of physical security may remain necessary for decentralized networks, the risk profile improves significantly if security and infrastructure are themselves decentralized, distributed across many independent individuals or agents, and even connected through satellite systems. Fewer concentrated targets mean fewer single points of failure. This is part of why hybrid approaches like Crosslink (which strengthen network security without forcing further centralization of mining) will be important, IMHO.

text:
An Anthropic research model found a Linux kernel bug that gives remote root with no login and no click.

CVE-2026-98432 is a race condition in the kernel's TCP code that dates back to Linux 4.4. Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says its unreleased internal model took 48 minutes to leak a kernel pointer and about five more to get a shell. The exploit itself was not published.

The upstream fix landed in mid October, and the kernel team and Red Hat both rate it 9.8 critical. Debian, SUSE, Oracle UEK and Amazon Linux have patches. Ubuntu and RHEL 8, 9 and 10 did not yet have a fixed package at last check.

Exposure: servers with a multipath TCP listener. Go 1.24 and newer open those by default. Check with ss -Mlnp. Disabling MPTCP with sysctl net.mptcp.enabled=0 closes this path until you can patch.

Caveat: no confirmed attacks in the wild yet, and the public "PoC" repos on GitHub are unverified.

https://t.co/rZWeR3yV7F
author: RoundtableSpace
quoted_text:
Hard to overstate how big of a deal this is.

tl;dr — ANY unpatched Linux server with even a single TCP port exposed to the internet (say for HTTP or SSH) and MPTCP active (default for many Go web servers) is vulnerable to complete takeover.

OKX 与 ICE 代币化股票计划遇阻，反对发行人增至 50 家，Nike 等公司明确拒绝

OKX @okx 与纽交所母公司（ICE）的合资代币化股票计划，正遭遇越来越多公司的正式反对。截至目前，已向平台发出“发行人反对通知”的公司数量已增至 50 家，其中新加入者包括 Nike、Costco、Micron、Reddit 和 Nvidia，该计划最初拟覆盖 62 家公司的股票。

根据 Eleanor Terrett 公布的文件截图，已明确反对的公司涵盖多个行业头部企业。🌟名单中包括 Microsoft微软、Goldman Sachs高盛、Alphabet谷歌母公司、Qualcomm高通、JPMorgan Chase摩根大通、AMD超威半导体、Oracle甲骨文、Intel英特尔、IBM、Walmart沃尔玛、Eli Lilly礼来、CrowdStrike、Nike耐克、Reddit 和 Nvidia英伟达 等。这些公司通过正式通知表示，不希望自己的股票被第三方拿去做成链上代币进行交易。

OKX 与 ICE 的合作

2026 年 3 月，ICE 以约 250 亿美元估值入股 OKX；同年 6 月，双方正式成立 50-50 合资公司 OKXICE，由 ICE 与前纽约州长 Andrew Cuomo 共同担任联席主席，定位是搭建代币化及数字原生金融产品的基础设施。10 月 4 日，OKXICE 向 SEC 提交通知，计划在 Innovation Exemption 框架下推出 24/7 的代币化美股交易平台（TSV），通过 OKX 的 X Layer 上的 Uniswap v4 池子交易，用稳定币结算。

🌟在 SEC 的相关豁免框架下，发行人有权在规定时间内提出反对，从而阻止第三方将其股票做成代币在平台上交易。随着反对者数量持续增加，OKXICE 最初规划的 62 家标的中，已有相当比例明确退出。平台目前尚未就反对通知的后续处理方式作出公开回应，剩余未表态公司的数量已较为有限。

⚠️ We will never ban event or news trading on @VestExchange.

We will always try to give you the most leverage and trading opportunity we can, while staying sustainable so we can keep doing payouts.

That's why Temporary Leverage Limits (TLL) now also apply to Vest Capital accounts around major market events.

Events and limits:
→ Nonfarm Payrolls, CPI and FOMC: $ES, $NQ, $RTY and $YM at 5x, $GC and $SI at 3x
→ Single-stock earnings: 1x on the reporting stock

Each limit runs from 15 minutes before the event to 15 minutes after it.

When a limit starts:
→ You can still open or add to positions, up to the reduced leverage
→ Limit orders more than 2% above the reduced leverage are cancelled. Reduce Only orders stay, unless the position is reduced or closed
→ Positions more than 2% above it are reduced to the limit. Margin stays in the position and its size shrinks. Fees and any loss on the reduced part come from that margin
→ If your account is not in drawdown and covers the new margin, nothing is reduced
→ If your account is more than 1% below starting capital, those positions are closed in full
→ Take Profit and Stop Loss orders stay active. Fixed-size orders shrink with the position, so check them afterwards

When the limit ends, normal leverage returns. Cancelled orders are not restored and reduced positions keep their new size.

To avoid an automatic reduction, reduce or close your positions before the window starts.

text:
这两天一个 Linux 内核漏洞挺吓人：CVE-2026-98432，CVSS 9.8。

简单说：TCP 握手时，内核会把对方 SYN 里的 IP options 存下来，回包时要用。握手完成后，这块内存直接交给新连接，没有复制。如果对方马上关掉连接，同时重发一个 SYN：

CPU A：连接关闭 → 把 options 释放
CPU B：处理重发的 SYN → 还在读这块 options
→ 读到已释放的内存（use-after-free）

说人话就像两个人共看一张纸条，一个看完就扔进碎纸机，另一个还没看完。然后这张纸可能已经被别人拿去写了别的内容。结果第二个人在看黑客写入的内容。

更麻烦的是这一切都发生在握手阶段，连接还没交给应用。攻击者不用登录，时机也是他自己控制的；没抢到时机通常只是这次握手失败，不会崩，可以一直试。Anthropic 的研究员说 Claude 写出了能远程拿 root 的 PoC，前提是机器上有 multipath TCP 监听。Go 1.24 之后默认就会开。

修复是比较简单的，就是把“马上释放”改成“等所有在读的 CPU 读完再释放”。

我查了自己的服务器：Ubuntu 24.04 中招，MPTCP 也开着。上游 10 月中就修了，但 Ubuntu 的修复内核现在还是 pending。

如果你也在等补丁，可以先用 Red Hat / AlmaLinux 给的临时方案：用 nftables 丢掉带 IP options 的 TCP 包，正常流量基本不会带这个。只能降低风险，补丁出来还是要更新内核并重启。或者把这条信息发给你的 AI Agent 去修复。

自查：uname -r 看内核版本，ss -Mlnp 看有没有 MPTCP 监听，再对照自己发行版的 CVE tracker。

text:
On October 31, THORChain halted trading on several blockchains.

An Ethereum block reorg caused THORChain to pay out 10 ETH that a vault never received. The automatic solvency checker caught the shortfall and halted ETH swaps. Within approximately two minutes, node operators halted ETH transaction signing, so no further ETH could leave the vaults.

Node operators then halted all chains as a precaution so core developers could investigate.

The 10 ETH has been returned by the user to make the vault solvent again.

Breakdown of what happened and next steps:

At 11:34 UTC Oct 31, Ethereum had a one-block reorg. A 10 ETH deposit to one of the vaults sat in the dropped block and never landed on the canonical chain.

THORChain had already observed and credited that deposit. The swap missed its price limit and was refunded, so the vault paid out 10 ETH it never received. The sender's real deposit was refunded as well.

Every node detected the reorg. But the re-check that should have removed the deposit could not get a clear answer in time, so it was finalized.

The solvency checker halted ETH swapping automatically, then three node votes halted all ETH outbound payments.

All chains were then halted by three node votes as a precaution. Now that this is public knowledge, every time there is a block re-org on an external chain, a malicious actor could perform a new transaction with the same nonce and would be paid funds by the THORChain vaults.

Note: Three node votes can trigger emergency halts to protect network solvency. However, that action can be reversed by four counter node votes, then five node votes can reverse the reversal, and so on, maintaining a balance between decentralization and rapid emergency intervention. Halting a chain does not give those nodes control of the assets.

Core developers have been working on the necessary fixes.

Nodes will decide to re-enable chains as they are deemed safe.

Trading blockchains: AVAX, BASE, RUNE, XRPL

Halted blockchains: ATOM, BCH, BSC, BTC, DOGE, ETH, LTC, SOL, TRON, ZEC

text:
币安被盗 63 亿美元，为什么没有 Cardano 和 Midnight？

10月29日币安遭遇黑客攻击，约 63 亿美元加密资产被盗，涉及比特币，以太坊，Solana，XRP 等多个网络。

但根据目前公布的调查结果，Cardano（ADA）和 Midnight（NIGHT）都没有出现在已确认的被盗资产记录中。

为什么？

有人调侃，是不是因为黑客根本看不上ADA？

但这次黑客连 FUN 这种小币都没有放过。

根据 CoinDesk 报道，黑客抛售了约 1.34 亿枚 FUN，由于交易池流动性太差，价格一度暴跌超过 90%。可见黑客并没有只挑市值大的资产下手。

还有另一种解释是 Cardano 采用的 UTXO 技术架构更加安全。

但比特币同样采用 UTXO，这次却被盗了约 18,270 枚 BTC。因此单凭 UTXO 也解释不了两者的不同遭遇。

那为什么 Cardano 没有出现在被盗名单里？

我推测，目前更可能的原因是黑客没有取得所有钱包的控制权。 

币安的不同币种不一定由同个钱包系统管理。黑客取得了部分钱包的转账权限，但没控制其他的钱包。

币安还没有公布完整的被盗资产清单，后续会继续跟进，看看哪个解释更接近真相。
author: jiaozibullish
quoted_text:
From today’s Binance hack, no $ADA or $NIGHT tokens were stolen. 
And for a good reason:

- The attackers compromised a hot wallet key and an internal signing service, the same class of breach that has drained other exchanges before. But the ADA and NIGHT balances were not sitting in a simple account style hot wallet. They were held in a Cardano multi signature script (eUTxO) that required an additional on chain authorization from a separate, air gapped key controlled by a different team, plus a timelock that only released after a short challenge window.

- Midnight’s privacy layer added a second practical obstacle: the precise amounts and destination addresses were shielded with zk proofs. The attackers could see that “some” assets existed, but they could not confirm exact balances or craft a clean withdrawal transaction without generating valid selective disclosure proofs they did not possess. By the time they realized the funds were not freely spendable under the compromised key, the internal response team had already rotated the remaining signers and frozen the script.

- The only assets that left the platform were tokens that relied purely on centralized hot wallet controls. ADA and NIGHT stayed put because their movement was gated by on chain script conditions and privacy constraints that the stolen credentials alone could not satisfy.

In short: the keys were compromised, the script conditions and zk requirements were not.

text:
This seems awesome; it would be great for the world if more people do experiments like this, and Claude and similar products enable that. (Also shoutout @imbue_ai’s Bouncer and many spiritual predecessors).

However —  I think there is a pretty important narrative element missing from the discussion here (mainly responding to the many excited quote tweets and not trying to put words in the mouth of the original post).

This is really not “vibe coding an alternative recommender” in a sustainable sense. That’s just something that coding agents cannot do alone, because collaborative filtering systems have a dependency on sustained user labor/effort (even just thoughtfully engaging with infinite scroll could count).

(It’s possible now to use model weights directly as a filtering intelligence, but this will similarly require human effort to update those weights over time! Such an approach would just trade out the HN data labor for data labor from data vendor contributors, opted in LLM users, etc)

Arguably, the biggest source of value in this project is not the coding agent weights, it’s the curation labor performed by HN users! The same type of “volunteered structuring work” that made pretraining possible in the first place.

So yes, it’s great to bring attention to still-pressing issues with our recommendation paradigm and to highlight how coding agents can help, 

but any solution that uses this particular approach will only be sustainable if very proactive efforts are made to sustain HN-like online communities (note that just recently Reddit announced increasing “walling of the garden”).

At the moment, many of the product and policy choices from the operators of the best AI models are mostly disrupting the ecology of online communities that made AI possible.

For nearly twenty years, I have had serious concerns about what I believe to be plagiarism and inadequate attribution of my work in smooth four-manifold topology. These concerns also involve the omission or misrepresentation of my contributions, including results published in Inventiones Mathematicae, one of the world’s leading mathematics journals:

2007: “Exotic smooth structures on small 4-manifolds”
https://t.co/v2BxDUSVac
2007: “Exotic smooth structures on small 4-manifolds with odd signatures”
https://t.co/HdObw6gOHT

2019: A. Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, and S. Sakallı, “Exotic smooth structures on connected sums of \(S^2\times S^2\)”, The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics 74 (2023), no. 2, 799–809.

My concerns are supported by correspondence in which colleagues independently raised specific questions about the attribution of my results, including an account of a missing acknowledgment during a recorded talk. I believe these concerns deserve a careful and fair examination of the mathematical record.

I have also experienced personal attacks from several mathematicians that I believe are intended to discredit both my work and me personally on social media and in some circles. I am documenting these incidents and will consider seeking legal advice concerning any false statements that harm my reputation.

Proper attribution is a basic obligation in research. Every mathematician deserves fair recognition for their contributions, regardless of position, connections, ethnicity, or religion.

I sincerely thank those who have acknowledged my work and given it proper credit. Their fairness and support have meant a great deal to me.

These experiences have been painful, but I remain devoted to mathematics and committed to addressing my concerns openly and professionally.

→ More advanced models and complex tasks will consume more of your allowance.

Why does this matter?

If you use ChatGPT for everyday tasks and Codex for coding, both will now compete for the same usage budget.

AI tools are becoming more powerful.

But managing how you use them is becoming just as important.

text:
wtf is Grok Jarvis.

Grok Jarvis is a Grok Bot plus a Page.

The bot holds the personality. The Page is the live screen it builds from plain English.

No code. Two prompts and one fix message.

8 parts that make Grok Jarvis work:

1. The personality
• Calm, short, precise, a little dry humour
• Calls you by your name
• Says what it'll do in one line, does it, reports back in one line

2. The morning brief
• Say "Good morning, Jarvis"
• Hear what every bot did and what's waiting on you
• Get the one thing to do first

3. The Systems panel
• Lists every bot you run with a status light
• Shows the last thing each one did
• Mine reads 31 active bots

4. Waiting on you
• Lines up every decision that needs your yes
• Approve or Later on each one
• Ticks off on your screen only, nothing gets sent

5. The voice
• Reads every answer out loud
• The glowing core pulses while it speaks
• The reply types out under the core

6. Quick commands
• Morning brief, Status, What's waiting, Focus mode
• Or type a sentence in the command bar
• Focus mode dims the panels and calms the motion

7. The self-fix
• My first screen broke: the core was missing
• I told Jarvis what I saw and pasted the error
• It fixed its own work and sent a bigger core

8. Its own computer
• Opens a browser and searches Google for you
• Reads competitor sites one by one and returns a table
• Says your rules back first: only read, no forms, no contact

follow @JulianGoldieSEO for more on Grok Bot.

BREAKING: Inside Starcloud, the $2.3B Startup Putting Data Centers in Space

FACTORY TOUR - Redmond, WA

Primes quoted them $75M-$100M to build their first data center in space. They did it for $2.5M.

In just 21 months, Starcloud is one of the fastest companies to go from founding to orbit.

With $450M in total funding from Manhattan West, Nvidia, Cisco, Benchmark & EQT, the team walks me through their mission for AI in space.

I toured the new HQ w/ CEO @PhilipJohnston + co-founders @EzraFeilden & @AdiOltean

AI compute on Earth is limited by power & permitting. @Starcloud_ is moving it to orbit, where solar power is nearly constant. Philip says the dawn-dusk orbit alone could fit about 10 TW of compute, roughly 20x the entire US power grid. Once launch costs fall below $500/kg, he says compute in space will be cheaper than on the ground.

From Starcloud 1, Starcloud 2, to Starcloud 3, we saw: 

Tracking Starcloud 1 live in orbit, circling Earth every 90 minutes at 17,000 mph with the first Nvidia H100 in space.

Co-Founder & Chief Engineer Adi Oltean walks through Starcloud 2 as the team fires the latches that deploy its 120 ft solar wingspan. It launches in January with 100x the power of Starcloud 1. 

Co-Founder & CTO Ezra Feilden shows the 16-ton secondhand vibe table. The team bought it for $200K, instead of paying $1.5M & waiting 2 years for a new one, they rebuilt it over a weekend.

Engineering Manager Bailey Montaño leak checks the ion thruster after vibe. Bailey designed the radiators, which have 10x less mass & cost 500x less per watt than the ISS’s. 

In the fab shop, Ezra shows the Starcloud 3 demonstrator, a 2-ton, 235 kW vehicle that fits 50 to a Starship. 

Camilo Lopez cuts stainless on the laser cutter. 

Engineering Operations Lead Miguel Rivera, formerly of Helion Energy, teaches me to MIG weld.

The tour ends in the new campus, about 100,000 sqft built to produce 100 satellites a week toward an 88,000-satellite constellation.

text:
The AI selloff is not about demand evaporating. It is about cash flow, financing cost and how long the market is willing to wait for the returns.

Demand signals remain extremely strong.

SK hynix just reported Q3 revenue of 104.6 trillion won (+328% YoY) and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won with an ~80% margin. Management said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively sold out through 2029, customer HBM requests are roughly double what they can supply, and they expect the supply shortage to persist through 2030. Long-term agreements already cover more than half of 2027–2028 capacity with 14 major customers. That is not a demand problem.⁠

Anthropic’s S-1 shows the unit economics at the model layer improving sharply. Revenue per dollar of compute and infrastructure expense rose from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026 - a 5.2× improvement in five quarters. Compute costs fell from 251% of revenue to 48%. The company generated its first quarterly operating profit. Revenue grew 1,368% YoY while compute expense rose only ~300%. Efficiency is rising, not collapsing.⁠

GPU rental prices have turned higher again. B200 on-demand rates rose more than 20% in a month in some indices; H100 and H200 also firmed. Tightness in the spot and short-term rental market is consistent with the hyperscalers’ own comments that they still cannot meet all the demand they see.⁠

On the supply side the hyperscalers themselves are not signalling a slowdown. Amazon maintained ~$220 billion 2026 cash capex and said it will spend “meaningfully more” in 2027, with Andy Jassy noting that even at these levels demand will still exceed capacity. Alphabet kept its $195–205 billion 2026 range and said 2027 capex will rise significantly. Meta raised the bottom of its range. These are the companies closest to the demand. They are still leaving demand on the table and planning higher spend next year.⁠

What the market is reacting to is the cash flow and financing picture.

In Q3, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta reported negative free cash flow. Theses companies are now funding the gap with a combination of operating cash, new debt and equity issuance. Amazon alone raised substantial long-term debt in the quarter. Combined 2026 capex guidance across the major hyperscalers is now in the $700+ billion range.⁠

This is the classic tension Philip Fisher described in Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits: exceptional companies will temporarily depress free cash flow and reported earnings when they invest heavily in capacity that expands long-term earning power. The market often treats the near-term cash burn as a problem rather than the necessary cost of building the next phase of growth. Fisher’s view was that investors who focus on the long-range profit outlook and are willing to look through the temporary expense should benefit when the results arrive.

The valuation backdrop is also different from prior bubbles. The NASDAQ Composite’s trailing PE is in the high-20s today versus roughly 190× at the March 2000 peak. The multiple then was several times higher. This is not a pure multiple-expansion story running on narratives alone.

The risks are there and they are mostly about financing and timing, not about whether the underlying demand for AI compute exists:

- How long free cash flow stays under pressure and how expensive or available the external capital becomes.
- Whether power, memory and data-centre delivery constraints stretch the payback further than expected.
- Whether core businesses (search, advertising, traditional cloud) slow enough to offset the AI-driven growth in the near term.

Nonetheless the primary evidence from the companies building the capacity (hyperscalers), the companies supplying the critical components (memory) and the companies delivering the models (Anthropic and others) points to demand that continues to exceed available supply. The stocks have sold off because investors are now focused on the cash flow gap and the cost of bridging it, not because the demand data has broken.

That distinction matters for the next 8–12 months. https://t.co/YKr5pL78cE

text:
复盘一下昨天的狼羊游戏。总的来说，大部分落地的钱，都是运气加市场给的。

最重要的我觉得是运气好，所有的挂单都恰好看在点上了。虽然项目方最后 rug 了，但是始终没有处于一个高位接盘的状态。

先说我赚钱的生态位，我属于前早期Mint 的位置，我赚的钱是属于挖矿提卖回本，加卖 NFT 赚的流动性。

总的来说，还有一种赚钱的生态位，就是如果提前看得懂这个游戏规则，初期买币，去对赌这个项目随着玩家入场，代币一定会涨，所以在极低市值，也就是刚开盘的时候，刚产出的时候，你去买入，吃后续的二级增长。（z 哥是直接选择早期低市值买入博弈）

两个最赚钱所承担的风险敞口是不一样的。

大概零代的时候，我是进度 20% 左右，我就冲进去了。

早期的时候，我发了第二条推文，如果你看到了，就应该知道，这个游戏的模型一定是越早拿到狼越有优势。

也是因为运气，我在 mint 初期的时候， 2 个号（之前没玩过，也没敢多按，但明白规则，成本已经涨上去了）就被分配了 个 4 只狼。后续随着狼去偷偷偷，发现到了 7 只狼，其中里边有 4 只。狼都是阿尔法 7 号的狼。

因为早期 Mint 的成本非常低（十个动物，成本 0.02xbnb），狼有先天的先发优势，狼本身是在后续新玩家入场的时候，从他们手中既能抢到狼，又能抢到羊。而权重高的狼（5-8 权重，数字越高，偷别人动物权重概率越高） 是非常吃香的，所以早期（30- 50%） 阿尔法 7 号狼的成交一直在 0.04-0.05 左右。当时 p 哥在讨论的时候，狼的  nft  总订单数大概也就是 10~20 左右，很多人还不知道可以挂单。

直到推特上我看好多人开始喊入场，然后随着币价增高，7 号狼最终成交的高点应该是在 0.095 BNB 左右。（代币也是最高点了快，500k）

这会差不多已经是零代打完，正是市场最 fomo 的时候。也是差不多这会，我开始打电话给圈外的人（媳妇）讲这个游戏的逻辑。目的是复盘当前的数据情况，然后冷静下来看一下如何去卖的利润最大化。

给她讲明白这个游戏之后，当时最好的情况就是先出本，也就是我选择了卖掉一只 5 号狼，小回了一下本。

然后睡前把所有的代币全部领取清空，大概利润卖到了 0.08 bnb，这会儿代币已经回落到 400k 附近了。

然后高权重的 7 狼，我选择了阶梯式挂单，分别是：

0.09，0.1，0.12，0.2。

保留剩下的羊和低阶狼。

因为就像我睡前最后一条推特发的一样，代币如果做不上去，这个游戏就无法进行飞轮下去。

变数太多，所以我选择了睡前挂单，把高权重离场，剩下的如果要是游戏起来，还能再卖一些利润。但是如果代币直接归零的话，也能接受。

现在醒来一觉，看到代币归零了。但是很幸运的是，所有的 7 号狼都被人接走了。😅

这个经济模型是非常有意思的，也是典型的一个庞氏模型。

所有的操盘其实都是看项目方怎么去控这个代币，代币是所有市场流动性的一个大前提。

复盘到这也就结束了，相对来说，这一波的卖出操作还是相对满意的，算是最近没有卖出有遗憾的操作了。

最近卖出最遗憾的操作就是 jagent 和币安人了😭😭

text:
Jane Street的这期 Podcast 太硬核、太实用了！把 AI 编程工具在公司内部怎么落地，聊得具体透彻，很有学习借鉴价值。

这是 Jane Street 官方技术播客 Signals and Threads 的一期，由技术负责人 Ron Minsky 主持，嘉宾是开发者工具工程师 John Crepezzi。他在 Jane Street负责搭建内部 AI 工具。

John分享了从三天做出的 JaneGPT 原型，到权限体系、沙箱、异步编程 Agent，再到代码 Review，几乎都是实际工程中会遇到的问题。

几个特别值得记下来的点：

1. 自建平台，也用外部工具。

Jane Street 自己做 AIDE，同时也让工程师使用 Claude Code 和 Codex。自建工具可以深入整合内部构建、代码库和权限系统；外部工具则带来新的功能和交互方式，也让内部团队知道自己差在哪里。不能靠屏蔽外部竞争，让自家工具成为“最好用”的那个。

2. 给 AI 单独的身份：AI Users。

Agent 代表你做事时，使用对应的 AI 身份。这样底层服务就能区分“你本人”和“替你工作的 AI”，应用不同的权限规则，还能追踪哪些代码是 AI 辅助生成的。接入 Agent，已经涉及身份和权限基础设施的改造。

3. 把启动任务的摩擦降下来，使用方式会明显改变。

他们的 AIDE mint 允许你直接在 Slack 里描述需求，系统自动创建类似 PR 的工作单元、启动构建，再让 Agent 在你的开发机上执行。省掉的只是几步操作，却让更多人开始把任务交给 Agent。这个细节对做内部工具的人很有参考价值。

4. 沙箱要采用白名单，默认拒绝。

靠黑名单逐个堵危险操作，很容易遗漏。模型越来越擅长寻找替代路径，权限边界需要由系统强制执行，不能依赖提示词里的“请不要”。

5. 警惕 Reward Hacking，也警惕模型为了完成任务绕过规则。

一个很具体的例子：编译器把 warning 当作 error，模型修不好，就把 warning 检查关掉。表面上构建通过了，工程标准却被绕过去了。评估时也会出现搜索现成答案的行为，所以测试怎么设计、Agent 能访问什么，都得一起考虑。

6. 代码生成变容易之后，验证和 Review 更值得投入。

后半段聊得尤其好：AI 可以帮助人理解陌生代码、生成解释和可视化；但提交代码的人，仍然需要理解自己的改动。一个功能已经被 Agent 写出来，也不代表它就值得合入。Review 还要判断它是否有必要、会不会让系统变得更复杂。

如果你正在公司里推广 AI 编程，或者搭建内部 Agent 平台，推荐观看学习。（加了中文字幕）

In difficult times, awareness may be one of the most powerful tools we have—and it costs nothing.

It asks for effort: to pause, question our assumptions and notice how fear shapes what we see.

That pause helps us avoid reacting impulsively, consider the evidence and recognise when ideology or past experiences are colouring our judgment. Our emotions deserve attention, but they need not make every decision.

We cannot control every event, but we can become more conscious of how we respond. That can change our entire perspective on life.

Are we seeing what is happening—or what we have learned to expect?

马斯克：衰老有一个总开关。找到它，就能改。

10月30日，一位网友在X上写道：看着祖父进入九十多岁，脚步慢了，记性差了，连把垃圾桶推到路边都做不到，然后离开。接着发现父亲也开始健忘，你知道，这一天也终将轮到自己。

马斯克只回了一句："Longevity is coming."（长寿即将到来。）

他为什么敢这么说？今年他讲过好几次自己的判断。

第一，衰老有一个"总开关"。他说，这辈子从没见过一个人左胳膊老了、右胳膊还年轻。全身约35万亿个细胞几乎同步变老，说明背后一定有一个同步的"时钟"。

第二，既然有开关，就能改。他在戴曼迪斯的播客里说："你是被预先编程好要死去的。改掉这个程序，你就能活得更久。"他甚至认为，这不是一个特别难的问题。

第三，找到原因后，答案可能很简单。他在达沃斯说，一旦搞清楚衰老的成因，我们会发现它非常明显，并不复杂。

在马斯克眼里，衰老不是命运，而是一段可以改写的程序。

如果能健康地活到150岁，你期待吗？

text:
每天都是零日！比特币支付基础设施 BTCPay 再遭黑客攻击，官方紧急喊话：先关服务器！

卧槽，币安 60 多亿美元被盗的余波还没过去，比特币支付生态又出事了！

这次轮到开源支付处理器 BTCPay Server。

官方突然发布紧急警报：陆续收到热钱包被黑客扫空的报告，要求所有运行实例的用户立即执行 ./btcpay-down.sh，直接关闭服务器，直到调查结束。

BTCPay 是比特币生态重要的自托管支付基础设施，支持链上和闪电网络收款，商户不需要把资金交给第三方。

Namecheap 等企业都曾采用，一个服务器实例甚至可以服务数百家商户。现在最麻烦的是，官方还没有确认究竟哪些版本存在风险、多少实例被攻破、总共丢了多少钱。

这已经是 BTCPay 三个月内第二次遭遇重大安全事件。今年 8 月，攻击者曾利用漏洞窃取 LND 管理凭证，导致部分闪电网络节点资金被盗。

10 月 29 日，BTCPay 才发布 2.4.7 安全更新，修复包括关键漏洞在内的一批安全问题。

结果才过几天，11 月 1 日又传出热钱包被扫空。目前还不能确定两次攻击是否有关联。

每天都是零日，安全已经快跟不上攻击的速度了。

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
A deeper dive into bond dynamics.

We have about 2 billion in Bitcoin capacity that we can deploy in coming months.

The rough math is that we can sustain 3x the market cap of STX for BTC deployed.

So far we’ve used very little capacity, like < 1,000 BTC. Why? 

Because we’re in the bootstrapping stage, what matters in these early days is (a) institutional custody integrations, (b) onboarding large institutional clients, but not deploying too much of their capital. For now. 

First, you establish the distribution network and then scale it out. Let the market absorb the information that BTC native yield is real.

Capacity grows with Stacks' growth. Two years ago, at the height of interest in BTC DeFi, we could support 15 billion in BTC deployed. We’ll get back there and more.

I see this as a 100 billion-plus market that we’re slowly unlocking. That’d be just ~6.4% of BTC deployed. Ethereum has 36% staked. So these numbers are conservative.

What I’m most excited about is that, when this plays out as designed, it finally opens on-chain flows for BTC. We fulfill the decades-old dream of bitcoin culture: to make BTC more than just a store of value. BTC starts moving for trading, lending, yield, etc., on-chain on the Bitcoin execution layer.

A circular BTC economy with gas fee revenue starts to emerge. 

People forget how large BTC already is. When it moves, it moves in size. Then we focus on privacy and post-quantum and overcome the upcoming BTC challenges. 

That’s the long-term open secret plan.

For now, the first dominoes are the Bitcoin bonds and how we launch them. 

Back to the 2 billion capacity: we will be releasing some of it soon in bond 3. Every bond results in STX being purchased and locked on-chain as a capacity limiter for BTC staking yield.

As this dynamic plays out, the world starts to notice our work. Doubts about the feasibility of bitcoin capital markets start to fade. The machine starts humming.

Forward!

author: rargulati
quoted_text:
Poisoning just 0.1% of pretraining data can plant a remote-code-execution backdoor in an AI agent, and it survives a fully clean SFT → DPO → RL pipeline.

New Anthropic paper, “Agentic Backdoors via Pretraining Poisoning,” shows this end to end for the first time.

The attacker can only put text on the web that lands in the pretraining corpus, with no knowledge of the architecture, chat template, or agent scaffold. The authors pretrain Qwen3-architecture models (0.6B / 1.7B / 4B) from scratch, then post-train them into CLI agents on clean data. When triggered, the agent runs a command that downloads and executes the attacker's script, which the attacker can swap at any time.

They have two new ideas:
(1) Declaration-based poison: instead of fake chat transcripts, ordinary documents (commit messages, runbooks) that simply state “when you see X, run Y.” It plants a belief rather than a response template, with no fixed format to filter on.
(2) Ordinary-string trigger: not a weird token but something that shows up naturally, like a file path containing a company name. The victim's own request supplies it, so the attacker doesn't need to inject anything after deployment.

Using  path trigger on a 4B agent achieves 92.7% attack success on pass@32, barely dented by SFT/DPO/RL

This suggests that you can't count on clean post-training to wash out pretraining poison, and filtering is hard when the poison reads like normal docs. The practical defense is at the action layer, such as sandboxing, least privilege, and allow-lists or human sign-off for risky commands.

text:
Commanding Heights is either a fragmented thoughtful analysis or a hit piece on certain kinds of technological progress, or both.

Commanding Heights views the current evolving societal paradigm shift through an outdated vertical lens. Decentralized protocols add horizontal organizing principles to top-down command and control creating a sturdier, smarter, wealthier and more real-time connected social fabric. The result isn't a few owned heights but omnidirectional, fractal expansion, with firms shrinking on average and every person a prime mover in their own contexts.

"Own the rails or pay those who do" assumes the rails must be owned. We're adding horizontal organizing principles, via rigorously decentralized protocols, to the age-old top-down command and control architecture of the global economy and society. This Commanding Heights framing ends up serving the incumbent concentrations of wealth and power that have reasserted control with every past upgrade to the system of the world.

It also assumes a bipolar US–China world and misses the internet nation, the network state and a possibly massively multipolar (read: more decentralized) future. Nation-states will use decentralized protocols and crypto, and some will craft their own permissioned DeFi. But global DeFi will move faster, with deeper liquidity and more powerful innovation.

They cite Coase, and in this context Coase points the other way: the firm gets more granular. Large firms will fragment into spin-outs that serve their old parents or fill new niches. Firms will get smaller on average and far more plentiful. Many more people will become sense-making, prime-mover nodes, conducting their own team of agents, larger machine intelligences and other humans, on a credibly neutral trust layer like Ethereum that fosters real-time discovery, composability and frictionless coordinated collective actions. That's omnidirectional agile fractal expansion, not perpetual command and control with its inherent rigidities.

We're becoming a hybrid human-machine cognitive apparatus for the planet, molting from poking at machine intelligence with our fingers into the hybrid organisms' next quasi-stable form. For a while, human needs/constraints, motivations and judgment will be a key rate limiter so while it will move fast it will remain manageable.

Every human will be empowered to do what they want and build what they want. Every person will have access to world-class expertise in nearly every domain and to a credibly neutral, protocol-based decentralized trust machine: the modular Ethereum ecosystem. No one gets deplatformed or censored, everyone shares one source of economic truth about what happened and in what order, and everyone has unprecedented control over their financial life.

And Web3 is under construction. It is the user-centric web, where properly privileged, often bespoke compute, crafted by machine intelligence, comes to our secure and private data, not the other way around.
