text:
Thanks to @koolkrypto223 for his comments, I do not see his post as FUD at all but rather constructive discourse. 

On single dealer
I think we've been quite transparent about being a broker-like model rather than an exchange. This actually necessitates the use of a single dealer: unlike spot assets, derivatives in crypto cannot be transferred between different exchanges. If we were to route your order split across 5 exchanges, you would not want to see 5 different positions displayed in your account. You want a sophisticated counterparty to do the liquidity aggregation. We've achieved the benefits you describe: 

✅ more listings than any other DEX
✅ best in class liquidity on any asset class even as a new entrant
✅ liquidity aggregation of the best primary venues; no need to open 20 different exchange accounts and keep switching between them

On the moat
Bringing all of TradFi onchain will take years, if not decades. Swaps, for example, are a fundamentally bilateral contract that cannot be replicated by DEXes, and I don't even think any are trying. This is the first time we've seen direct TradFi liquidity ported onchain with stable funding rates (the routing actually doesn't touch a single crypto venue). Getting the partnerships in place for this was not easy; I think we'll see the same type of consolidation into a few winners as we see with CEXes, DEXes, and TradFi brokerages. 

On price discovery
Our opinionated take: 
a) You do not give a flying fuck as a user where price discovery is happening 
b) In fact most users should not touch exchanges directly at all 

Currently, no price discovery happens on any DEX, except in very niche scenarios. To say otherwise is massive cope. To build a venue for price discovery means catering to the very fastest HFTs: wake me up when DEXes have matching engine latency on the order of nanoseconds. Do a lead-lag analysis on prices between DEXes and CEXes, or DEXes vs CME, and it's obvious where price discovery originates. The only question is do you want a shallow clone of TradFi liquidity or direct access?

As a user, you primarily care about best execution, and that's what we optimize for. Additionally, the reason why brokerages exist in TradFi is to add another layer of protection between the user and the exchange. 

▶️ When 10/10 occurred and billions of dollars of ADL were forced upon users at other venues, Variational came out squeaky clean. 
▶️ When Binance was hacked for billions, we immediately put out a statement that said that user funds are safe in self-custodied smart contracts and not moved to offchain hedging venues. OLP puts up its own capital for that. 

Variational Pro 
Variational Pro will be multi-dealer: you will be able to request a quote and dealers will bid for your flow. This increases the complexity of the product but will have massive unlocks for institutions, including allowing for subnetworks of markets where OLP is not involved. 

If two parties want to trade swaps or other derivatives peer-to-peer at infinite size we will facilitate the infrastructure for order matching, clearing, and margining for that.

Reminder that the tech for this has already been built; it's the same underlying protocol that clears billions every day for Omni! I hope you will see our vision to bring TradFi onchain is a multi-year one and cannot be cleanly segmented into "oh it's just a DEX" or "oh it's just a CFD broker".  It's so much more than that and we encourage everyone to follow our roadmap which we publicize on our docs page.
author: edward_yu_var
quoted_text:
The discourse over @variational_io is...bizzare.

Everyone knows it's a single dealer RFQ platform (or at least I'd hope by now). 

This is neither inherently good nor bad, but it should shape your expectations.

Similar to a CFD broker, I'd expect Variational to trade at lower multiples than actual exchanges. IG Group trades at ~half the multiple of CME for example.

There's nothing terribly new or interesting about "RFQ", I'm not sure why people think it's a big value proposition or moat.

The real value prop of Variational is that in crypto, UI for DEXs is largely solved, and UX all comes down to liquidity. Variational can potentially list assets faster, get better liquidity on long tails, and generally abstract away a lot of the awkwardness of bootstrapping a brand new marker that a CLOB has. This has been and will likely continue to be enormously successful with their RWA swaps.

That's a very real value prop, for now. The problem is that they have much less moat than actual exchanges; they are not the venue where actual price discovery is happening. It's significantly harder for TradFi entrants to replicate what @HyperliquidX has built than it'll be for them to do what Variational does, but better. B-booking retail crypto traders and points farmers in OLP is enormously lucrative now, but how durable will those margins be over time?

Depending on the exact flavour of regulatory clarity we get, the value prop they offer for TradFi liquidity can pretty easily shrink as more TradFi market makers are willing/able to quote directly on permissionless CLOBs. I don't know where regulators will land here though; there's worlds that it's very good for Variational and very bad.

I see Variational as more of a bandaid fix/reg arb, but a lot of crypto falls into that category. It's attempting to solve a very real issue, but will that issue be as prevalent in 6 months? 1 year? 2 years? Hard to say.

Personally, I see $LIT and hyperliquid:native as more pure expressions of longing the proliferation of perps as an instrument and DeFi as a sector, where as I see $VAR as more of a business with more operator risk, but it could easily print money for months-years. $GMX might be a good example in that it printed fees for a long time and then eventually became more obsolete.

I actually don't think any of this impacts point price much at TGE, and that's what everyone seems to care about. Market conditions at the time of TGE probably dictate $VAR performance way more than any of this.

text:
The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

text:
WSJ: "OpenAI has raised less than half of the $30 billion it had initially targeted for its latest funding round, with market jitters over the AI trade dampening investor appetite for one of the industry’s biggest names. After receiving tepid interest from some large investors, OpenAI has so far secured roughly $11 billion in commitments for the new financing, according to people familiar with the matter. The deal values the company at $1.25 trillion—less than the $1.4 trillion valuation that it had earlier hoped to achieve...Anthropic more than doubled its revenue to $11.6 billion from the first to the second quarter, while OpenAI grew sales by roughly 18% over the same time period to $6.7 billion. Anthropic achieved a small operating profit in the second quarter, while OpenAI’s operating losses deepened over the same time period. Third-party data shows OpenAI recently took back some market share from Anthropic after cutting the prices of its latest models."

Seems investors are increasingly waking up to something I have warned for nearly a year now: competition combined with capital intensity will deprive hyperscalers of a path to profitability for far longer than the market will have the patience for... To quote my September report on "The AI Trade" (https://t.co/wQQNniS2kj):

"In December, we warned that market participants were neglecting that AI was forcing a fundamental shift for tech giants. They were transitioning from the most profitable business models in history to business models far more capital intensive and that intensity was in perpetuity. To quote Verdad Advisors’ Dan Rasmussen: “The big tech companies have gone from having about a third of the capital intensity of US industrial companies to three times the capital intensity of your typical US industrial company.” Even more troubling, that capital intensity couples with an erosion of their moats. As we wrote at the time: “While there’s a lot of speculative fear about how a single LLM could rise to dominance and what that could mean for economic, societal, and political stability, we believe the bigger concern for investors today is how relative model parity could compromise pricing power. Tech giants have thrived on monopolies and duopolies for a decade or more. Now, they’re in an LLM arms race where it’s unclear when or even if ever leadership will be sustainable.”

This year has given even more reason for intensifying concern about the ability of hyperscalers to achieve the pricing power necessary to turn margins positive. Again, AI’s adoption rate has been unprecedented. In late July, OpenAI claimed to have over one billion active users across its services and two million businesses using its AI models. This month, Google claimed its Gemini app had also surpassed the one billion active users mark. Anthropic has claimed to have more than 300,000 business customers. And Microsoft has claimed to have more than 20 million paid Copilot users. The question is not whether hyperscalers can bring users to their services, but rather how much average revenue they can generate per customer relative to the price of building and maintaining their models."

最可怕的是什么？

25年大约有6300个交易日，真正决定你投资回报的，可能就是其中几十天。

而这些大涨的日子，往往出现在市场最恐慌、波动最剧烈的时候。

很多人觉得自己可以先躲过暴跌，再等市场企稳后买回来。

但现实是，你可能躲过了下跌，也错过了最重要的反弹。

Larry Fink的核心观点很简单：

对于普通投资者来说，市场每天的涨跌、新闻和噪音，长期看可能根本没那么重要。

投资最大的敌人，有时候不是市场，而是自己频繁操作的冲动。

在市场里待得足够久，往往比猜对什么时候进场更重要。

当然，这不代表任何价格都值得买，也不代表应该忽视风险。

但对于长期定投标普500的人来说，最值得研究的，可能不是明天涨还是跌，而是如何让自己未来25年都不轻易离场。

text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text: This is why local LLM will ultimately win.  When you don't have the mental block of having to worry about cost and token usage, it unlocks the true productivity gains of AI.  You have freedom to try experiment with replacing different processes and flows.
author: TheDavidTai
quoted_text:
Interesting.

Revolut reportedly only started seeing meaningful AI productivity gains after moving away from expensive OpenAI and Anthropic models to self-hosted GLM.

Decagon reportedly runs ~90% of its workloads on open weight models.

Why? Because when you're running AI agents in production for e.g. customer service, cost and latency matter enormously. You don't need a frontier model with PhD-level reasoning or even a model that knows the capital of Finland to handle every customer interaction.

We're seeing similar dynamics across hypergrowth AI startups and increasingly the large enterprises we work with.

But most importantly, the future isn't binary.

When use cases are new, you want the smartest general-purpose model available. But once workflows mature and become predictable, smaller, faster, specialized models increasingly win.

I wouldn't be surprised if 80–90% of routine enterprise AI workflows eventually run on open-weight and smaller models.

This doesn't mean frontier labs lose. 

It means the market is splitting into two massive opportunities: frontier intelligence and specialized execution at scale.

text:
《朝鲜黑客是怎么被「造」出来的？》

Lazarus 不是一个黑客团伙，而是一个伞状名称。它背后是朝鲜侦察总局 (RGB) 下面的多个单位，比如 121 局、110 研究所、APT38/BlueNorOff。

公开估计，朝鲜网络相关人员约 6000–8000 人 (含支持人员)，其中核心黑客有数千人。KPI 很明确：给政权搞钱，以及情报和破坏。偷来的钱主要流向核武器和导弹项目。说白了，这是国家机器。

━━━━━━━━━━

一、从 11 岁开始的「天才流水线」

选拔的方式很像培养奥运选手。 

· 11–13 岁左右在全国筛查数学、逻辑突出的孩子，送进平壤的精英中学。家庭的政治忠诚度同样是门槛。 

· 再往上是金策工业大学、金日成综合大学，以及被认为是黑客摇篮的美林大学。据脱北者说，美林大学大约 5000 人报名只收 100 人左右。 

· 最顶尖的一批进网络部队，另一部分去核项目。被选中的人，家里往往能搬到平壤，分到更好的房子和配给。 

· 最后一步是出国打磨。朝鲜本土的网络条件极差，所以要把人送到中国沈阳等地的「黑客酒店」或掩护公司，或者去俄罗斯，在真实的互联网环境里练一年左右。很多实战能力，其实就靠这些海外前线基地撑着。

一个典型例子：被美国起诉的朴振赫 (Park Jin Hyok)，金策工业大学毕业，进掩护公司 Chosun Expo，派驻中国，起诉书指控他参与了索尼事件和 WannaCry。

━━━━━━━━━━

二、他们每天在干什么

2010 年代，他们以破坏和情报为主，比如索尼、WannaCry。现在的主力变成了两件事：盗加密货币，以及派「假员工」渗透。原因很简单：币圈钱多、难追、能全身而退。所以今天主要分两条线。

① 黑客作战单元 

· 按目标分组：美国、韩国、日本、金融、加密货币…

· 日常就是找漏洞、写恶意软件、钓鱼、假招聘、假投资，以及维护整条洗钱链路。 

· 训练时强调不靠现成工具，自己写攻击程序。 

· 多个来源提到，他们每天工作 15–20 小时，按军事作息，指挥高度集中，任务由上级下达，个人几乎没有自主空间。

②「IT 远程打工」单元 (这几年规模扩大得最快)

· 用假身份，甚至租用真实西方人的身份，去应聘远程开发岗位。 

· 通过「笔记本农场」绕过定位检测：当地人代收公司电脑，朝鲜那边远程操控。 

· 真干活、真领工资，据报道 90–95% 上交国家。顺手还可能埋后门、拿内部权限。 

· 团队 2–3 人一组，内部有 KPI，按秒记录工时、投递数、消息数。每天工作 11–16 小时，还要倒西方的时差。

这两条线会交叉：打工拿到的内部权限，可能就是下一次攻击的入口。所以下次招到一个「完美的远程工程师」，也许值得多看一眼。

━━━━━━━━━━

三、待遇和枷锁

· 特权：平壤的大公寓、更好的口粮、更高的津贴、不用参加普通劳役，还能看到外国电影和新闻。 

· 控制：家人留在国内，相当于抵押。完不成指标就要受罚。在海外也是集体住宿、严密监控。 

· 忠诚：脱北者形容他们是「体制内的既得利益者」，明知道外面是什么样子，依然留下。回报够高，而且从小就被这样塑造。

━━━━━━━━━━

最让我唏嘘的是：这些人本来可能是数学奥赛冠军、顶级工程师，却从小被挑出来，变成一个政权的提款机。

对币圈来说，他们的头号目标，就是我们的钱包🤣、交易所和项目团队。

想了解臭名昭著的朝鲜黑客组织 Lazarus，可以看看 Cipher 拍的纪录片《How North Korean Hackers Are Stealing Billions》。

Cipher 专做犯罪和地缘政治题材，看他们的纪录片跟追剧一样。这部片长 1 小时 20 分钟，把这支朝鲜国家队从头到尾讲透了。

Lazarus 可不是普通黑客，它是朝鲜国家养的「犯罪企业」。大多数黑客都是从小被选中的数学天才，每天工作 15 到 20 小时。Lazarus 的 KPI 只有一个：给政权搞钱，大头流向核武。

片子从朝鲜战争、主体思想和饥荒讲起，先讲清楚这个国家为什么会养出这么一支队伍。

然后按时间线一路往下：

① 1980–2000 年代伪造超级美元；

② 2014 年黑索尼影业，起因是那部《刺杀金正恩》；

③ 2016 年孟加拉国央行 SWIFT 劫案卷走 8100 万美元，还让打印机打不出转账记录，好拖延被发现的时间；

④ 2017 年的 WannaCry，用的是泄露出来的 NSA 漏洞「永恒之蓝」，波及约 150 个国家、20 多万台电脑；

⑤ 转战加密：Coincheck、Ronin (Axie)、WazirX，2025 年 Bybit 被盗 15 亿美元，再到现在 2026 年的币安。

------

币圈钱多、盗完还有机会全身而退，Lazarus 只会一直盯着挖漏洞。行业是时候团结起来了，我们面对的是一整个国家机器。

text:
Looking straight down at a machined steel hex nut sitting in my palm, it is impossible to unsee: a 6-sided outer perimeter (120° interior angles) wrapped around a circular core.

Across ~8 orders of magnitude—from 1.40 Å covalent bonds (10⁻¹⁰ m) to 14 mm cold-forged steel (10⁻² m)—chemistry and mechanical engineering converged on the exact same D₆ₕ geometry for the exact same first-principles reasons:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗩𝗶𝘀𝘂𝗮𝗹 & 𝗧𝗼𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗹 (𝗖₆𝗛₆ 𝗶𝗻 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗲𝗹):
A hex nut seen on-axis is a dead ringer for the Robinson–Kekulé shorthand of a benzene ring (C₆H₆). At the atomic scale, six planar sp²-hybridized carbons lock into a 120° σ-bond hexagon around an inner circle of six delocalized 2p₂ π-electrons (Hückel 4n + 2 = 6π, equalizing every C–C bond to 1.40 Å). At the human scale, six machined flats lock at 120° around a circular helical threaded bore that converts rotary torque into axial clamping preload.

• 𝗭𝗲𝗿𝗼 𝗔𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝘃𝘀. 𝗧𝗼𝗿𝗾𝘂𝗲 𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 (𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗻 = 𝟲 𝗪𝗶𝗻𝘀):
In organic chemistry, sp² hybrid orbitals naturally sit at 120°, matching the interior angle of a regular planar hexagon ((6 − 2)×180° / 6 = 120°). That eliminates Baeyer angle strain completely (Δθ = 0°), while π-delocalization distributes energy evenly around the ring (~36 kcal/mol aromatic stabilization).
In mechanical engineering, 6 sides is the structural sweet spot between wrench clearance and corner shear:
  — Fewer sides (square nut, n = 4, 90° corners): plenty of corner bite, but requires a massive 90° wrench swing to grab the next flat. Useless in a tight engine bay or chassis.
  — More sides (octagon, n = 8, 135° corners): smaller swing arc, but the shallow 45° external shoulders concentrate contact stress and strip/round off under high torque.

• 𝟲𝟬° 𝗪𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗲𝘅𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗱 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘀:
Because of its six-fold rotational symmetry (C₆), a hex nut only needs a 60° turn (360° / 6) in tight quarters to release and re-index the wrench onto the next flat—and just 30° when flipping a standard 15°-offset open-end wrench. Maximum torque transfer before corner yield, minimum swing radius.

• 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 & 𝗭𝗲𝗿𝗼-𝗪𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲 𝗣𝗮𝗰𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 (𝗛𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀'𝘀 𝗛𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘆𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗯 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗺):
A regular hexagon encloses unit area with the minimum possible boundary perimeter (P(6) = 2√[6·tan(π/6)] ≈ 3.722) and tiles 2D space with 0% interstitial void—eliminating the 9.31% wasted dead space of packed circles.
  — Atomic scale: Fuse benzene rings edge-to-edge at 120° trivalent junctions and they tile into planar graphene sheets and roll into carbon nanotubes with zero wasted space and ~1 TPa tensile stiffness.
  — Factory scale: Cold-drawn hexagonal bar stock bundles into dense honeycomb stacks with zero void volume and machines into fasteners with minimal lathe scrap.

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆:
From stabilizing the aromatic rings of DNA nucleobases, protein tryptophan/tyrosine networks, and small-molecule therapeutics at the angstrom scale to clamping structural steel under ton-loads at the human scale—a regular hexagon with a circle inside is nature and engineering's universal optimum for strength, symmetry, and efficiency.

text:
𝗧𝗵𝗲 $𝟭𝟬𝟬𝗧+ 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁-𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗛𝗲𝘅 𝗡𝘂𝘁 (𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿):

Has anyone ever calculated the true economic value of the hexagonal nut from first principles? Market reports lazily value global nut production at ~$25B/yr (~150 billion nuts/yr, sustaining an active installed base of ~2 trillion hex nuts clamping civilization together right now). That mistakes the 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲 of cold-forged steel for its 𝗰𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗽𝗹𝘂𝘀. Physically, a hex nut fuses two simple machines—a 6-fold wrench lever (120° flats) and a self-locking helical inclined plane (60° threads)—into a bistable mechanical amplifier (F = T / [K·d]): one human hand applying 85 N·m of torque on an M12 nut generates ~3.6 metric tons of clamping preload that locks indefinitely against vibration, yet unlocks non-destructively in a 60° arc. Welds and rivets are irreversible covalent bonds—fixing one internal bearing or seal requires destroying the parent structure. The hex nut gave humanity 𝗺𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗽𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗼𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗿 𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆: steel-grade bond strength paired with a zero-damage reversible state. That single property decoupled component failure from system death—shrinking repair times by 100×, extending the lifespan of global capital stock by 3–10×, and making 100,000-part modular machines (locomotives, jet turbines, gigawatt power grids, EUV lithography scanners, orbital rockets, and AI data centers) physically possible. It is a ~$25B/yr geometric primitive quietly undergirding >$200T of global physical capital stock—a >1,000:1 surplus-to-cost ratio and almost certainly one of the highest-leverage inventions in human history.

BREAKING: Inside Starcloud, the $2.3B Startup Putting Data Centers in Space

FACTORY TOUR - Redmond, WA

Primes quoted them $75M-$100M to build their first data center in space. They did it for $2.5M.

In just 21 months, Starcloud is one of the fastest companies to go from founding to orbit.

With $450M in total funding from Manhattan West, Nvidia, Cisco, Benchmark & EQT, the team walks me through their mission for AI in space.

I toured the new HQ w/ CEO @PhilipJohnston + co-founders @EzraFeilden & @AdiOltean

AI compute on Earth is limited by power & permitting. @Starcloud_ is moving it to orbit, where solar power is nearly constant. Philip says the dawn-dusk orbit alone could fit about 10 TW of compute, roughly 20x the entire US power grid. Once launch costs fall below $500/kg, he says compute in space will be cheaper than on the ground.

From Starcloud 1, Starcloud 2, to Starcloud 3, we saw: 

Tracking Starcloud 1 live in orbit, circling Earth every 90 minutes at 17,000 mph with the first Nvidia H100 in space.

Co-Founder & Chief Engineer Adi Oltean walks through Starcloud 2 as the team fires the latches that deploy its 120 ft solar wingspan. It launches in January with 100x the power of Starcloud 1. 

Co-Founder & CTO Ezra Feilden shows the 16-ton secondhand vibe table. The team bought it for $200K, instead of paying $1.5M & waiting 2 years for a new one, they rebuilt it over a weekend.

Engineering Manager Bailey Montaño leak checks the ion thruster after vibe. Bailey designed the radiators, which have 10x less mass & cost 500x less per watt than the ISS’s. 

In the fab shop, Ezra shows the Starcloud 3 demonstrator, a 2-ton, 235 kW vehicle that fits 50 to a Starship. 

Camilo Lopez cuts stainless on the laser cutter. 

Engineering Operations Lead Miguel Rivera, formerly of Helion Energy, teaches me to MIG weld.

The tour ends in the new campus, about 100,000 sqft built to produce 100 satellites a week toward an 88,000-satellite constellation.

The threat to America's infrastructure, data centers, & power is increasingly becoming a major national security concern..

Starcloud CEO Philip Johnston (@PhilipJohnston) on why he’s not worried about an enemy of the US tampering with one of his satellites:

“It’s actually a lot harder to shoot down a satellite than it is to blow up a data center in Virginia.”

“Satellites are traveling at ~17,000 miles/hour & so to target and have some kind of kinetic impact on a satellite at that speed is very difficult.”

“We have a pretty good case study from the Starlink satellites. Starlink is being used in Ukraine and also Starshield, and it’s not like the Russians are particularly happy about that.”

“Anything that approaches a satellite would be very visible, so anything bigger than 1-inch cube you could track in space.”

“We would see if somebody was tampering with our satellites, & it would be considered an act of war.”

“That’s the purpose of Space Force— developing interceptors and things to dissuade offensive action.”

text:
Thanks to @koolkrypto223 for his comments, I do not see his post as FUD at all but rather constructive discourse. 

On single dealer
I think we've been quite transparent about being a broker-like model rather than an exchange. This actually necessitates the use of a single dealer: unlike spot assets, derivatives in crypto cannot be transferred between different exchanges. If we were to route your order split across 5 exchanges, you would not want to see 5 different positions displayed in your account. You want a sophisticated counterparty to do the liquidity aggregation. We've achieved the benefits you describe: 

✅ more listings than any other DEX
✅ best in class liquidity on any asset class even as a new entrant
✅ liquidity aggregation of the best primary venues; no need to open 20 different exchange accounts and keep switching between them

On the moat
Bringing all of TradFi onchain will take years, if not decades. Swaps, for example, are a fundamentally bilateral contract that cannot be replicated by DEXes, and I don't even think any are trying. This is the first time we've seen direct TradFi liquidity ported onchain with stable funding rates (the routing actually doesn't touch a single crypto venue). Getting the partnerships in place for this was not easy; I think we'll see the same type of consolidation into a few winners as we see with CEXes, DEXes, and TradFi brokerages. 

On price discovery
Our opinionated take: 
a) You do not give a flying fuck as a user where price discovery is happening 
b) In fact most users should not touch exchanges directly at all 

Currently, no price discovery happens on any DEX, except in very niche scenarios. To say otherwise is massive cope. To build a venue for price discovery means catering to the very fastest HFTs: wake me up when DEXes have matching engine latency on the order of nanoseconds. Do a lead-lag analysis on prices between DEXes and CEXes, or DEXes vs CME, and it's obvious where price discovery originates. The only question is do you want a shallow clone of TradFi liquidity or direct access?

As a user, you primarily care about best execution, and that's what we optimize for. Additionally, the reason why brokerages exist in TradFi is to add another layer of protection between the user and the exchange. 

▶️ When 10/10 occurred and billions of dollars of ADL were forced upon users at other venues, Variational came out squeaky clean. 
▶️ When Binance was hacked for billions, we immediately put out a statement that said that user funds are safe in self-custodied smart contracts and not moved to offchain hedging venues. OLP puts up its own capital for that. 

Variational Pro 
Variational Pro will be multi-dealer: you will be able to request a quote and dealers will bid for your flow. This increases the complexity of the product but will have massive unlocks for institutions, including allowing for subnetworks of markets where OLP is not involved. 

If two parties want to trade swaps or other derivatives peer-to-peer at infinite size we will facilitate the infrastructure for order matching, clearing, and margining for that.

Reminder that the tech for this has already been built; it's the same underlying protocol that clears billions every day for Omni! I hope you will see our vision to bring TradFi onchain is a multi-year one and cannot be cleanly segmented into "oh it's just a DEX" or "oh it's just a CFD broker".  It's so much more than that and we encourage everyone to follow our roadmap which we publicize on our docs page.
author: hansolar21
quoted_text:
The discourse over @variational_io is...bizzare.

Everyone knows it's a single dealer RFQ platform (or at least I'd hope by now). 

This is neither inherently good nor bad, but it should shape your expectations.

Similar to a CFD broker, I'd expect Variational to trade at lower multiples than actual exchanges. IG Group trades at ~half the multiple of CME for example.

There's nothing terribly new or interesting about "RFQ", I'm not sure why people think it's a big value proposition or moat.

The real value prop of Variational is that in crypto, UI for DEXs is largely solved, and UX all comes down to liquidity. Variational can potentially list assets faster, get better liquidity on long tails, and generally abstract away a lot of the awkwardness of bootstrapping a brand new marker that a CLOB has. This has been and will likely continue to be enormously successful with their RWA swaps.

That's a very real value prop, for now. The problem is that they have much less moat than actual exchanges; they are not the venue where actual price discovery is happening. It's significantly harder for TradFi entrants to replicate what @HyperliquidX has built than it'll be for them to do what Variational does, but better. B-booking retail crypto traders and points farmers in OLP is enormously lucrative now, but how durable will those margins be over time?

Depending on the exact flavour of regulatory clarity we get, the value prop they offer for TradFi liquidity can pretty easily shrink as more TradFi market makers are willing/able to quote directly on permissionless CLOBs. I don't know where regulators will land here though; there's worlds that it's very good for Variational and very bad.

I see Variational as more of a bandaid fix/reg arb, but a lot of crypto falls into that category. It's attempting to solve a very real issue, but will that issue be as prevalent in 6 months? 1 year? 2 years? Hard to say.

Personally, I see $LIT and hyperliquid:native as more pure expressions of longing the proliferation of perps as an instrument and DeFi as a sector, where as I see $VAR as more of a business with more operator risk, but it could easily print money for months-years. $GMX might be a good example in that it printed fees for a long time and then eventually became more obsolete.

I actually don't think any of this impacts point price much at TGE, and that's what everyone seems to care about. Market conditions at the time of TGE probably dictate $VAR performance way more than any of this.

text:
Primer on Asset Backed Securities (ABS)

ABS are bonds repaid from the cash flows of a specific pool of assets rather than the general credit of the company that created them. Here is how they work:

> Sponsor sells the assets to a bankruptcy-remote special purpose vehicle (“SPV”) in a true sale

> SPV issues notes in tranches and uses the proceeds to pay the sponsor for the assets

> Asset cash flows run through a waterfall. Senior notes are paid first, junior tranches absorb losses first

> Sponsor or counterparty usually keep the residual equity and services the assets for a fee

quoted_text:
Thanks to @koolkrypto223 for his comments, I do not see his post as FUD at all but rather constructive discourse. 

On single dealer
I think we've been quite transparent about being a broker-like model rather than an exchange. This actually necessitates the use of a single dealer: unlike spot assets, derivatives in crypto cannot be transferred between different exchanges. If we were to route your order split across 5 exchanges, you would not want to see 5 different positions displayed in your account. You want a sophisticated counterparty to do the liquidity aggregation. We've achieved the benefits you describe: 

✅ more listings than any other DEX
✅ best in class liquidity on any asset class even as a new entrant
✅ liquidity aggregation of the best primary venues; no need to open 20 different exchange accounts and keep switching between them

On the moat
Bringing all of TradFi onchain will take years, if not decades. Swaps, for example, are a fundamentally bilateral contract that cannot be replicated by DEXes, and I don't even think any are trying. This is the first time we've seen direct TradFi liquidity ported onchain with stable funding rates (the routing actually doesn't touch a single crypto venue). Getting the partnerships in place for this was not easy; I think we'll see the same type of consolidation into a few winners as we see with CEXes, DEXes, and TradFi brokerages. 

On price discovery
Our opinionated take: 
a) You do not give a flying fuck as a user where price discovery is happening 
b) In fact most users should not touch exchanges directly at all 

Currently, no price discovery happens on any DEX, except in very niche scenarios. To say otherwise is massive cope. To build a venue for price discovery means catering to the very fastest HFTs: wake me up when DEXes have matching engine latency on the order of nanoseconds. Do a lead-lag analysis on prices between DEXes and CEXes, or DEXes vs CME, and it's obvious where price discovery originates. The only question is do you want a shallow clone of TradFi liquidity or direct access?

As a user, you primarily care about best execution, and that's what we optimize for. Additionally, the reason why brokerages exist in TradFi is to add another layer of protection between the user and the exchange. 

▶️ When 10/10 occurred and billions of dollars of ADL were forced upon users at other venues, Variational came out squeaky clean. 
▶️ When Binance was hacked for billions, we immediately put out a statement that said that user funds are safe in self-custodied smart contracts and not moved to offchain hedging venues. OLP puts up its own capital for that. 

Variational Pro 
Variational Pro will be multi-dealer: you will be able to request a quote and dealers will bid for your flow. This increases the complexity of the product but will have massive unlocks for institutions, including allowing for subnetworks of markets where OLP is not involved. 

If two parties want to trade swaps or other derivatives peer-to-peer at infinite size we will facilitate the infrastructure for order matching, clearing, and margining for that.

Reminder that the tech for this has already been built; it's the same underlying protocol that clears billions every day for Omni! I hope you will see our vision to bring TradFi onchain is a multi-year one and cannot be cleanly segmented into "oh it's just a DEX" or "oh it's just a CFD broker".  It's so much more than that and we encourage everyone to follow our roadmap which we publicize on our docs page.

text:
民主党横扫美国国会概率71%！对AI和Crypto有多大影响？

CLARITY法案可能出现意想不到的反转！

美国中期选举明天就开始了。Polymarket 上民主党同时拿下参众两院的概率已经达到71%，如果真的发生，特朗普未来两年将面对一个由民主党控制的国会。

市场担心 AI 监管收紧、加密法案停滞，但我研究后发现，尤其是 Crypto，事情可能没那么简单。

先说 Crypto，我觉得 CLARITY 法案，民主党未必愿意一直拖着它。

2025年 CLARITY 在众议院以294:134通过，其中78名民主党议员投了赞成票，说明民主党内部本来就有支持加密监管立法的力量。

加密行业今年已经投入约1.76亿美元参与中期选举，支持两党候选人。

距离2028年总统大选只剩两年，民主党同样有争取行业资源、加密支持者和中间选民的政治激励，没必要把这张牌完全让给共和党。

但问题在于，谁来制定规则？

CLARITY 今年9月在参议院闯关失败，民主党主要争议之一就是特朗普家族的加密利益冲突。

甚至连长期批评加密行业的 Elizabeth Warren 都表示愿意谈一份新的加密法案，前提是加强国家安全、经济保护和反腐败条款。

不过参与谈判的民主党参议员 Alsobrooks 也明确表示，民主党控制国会后不会优先推进原法案。

所以未来并非没有转机，但更可能是重新谈判、修改文本，而非直接通过特朗普支持的版本。到底2027年能否重新推进，还是拖到2028年，现在谁也说不准。

再看 AI，影响可能更直接。

民主党关注 AI 替代就业、数据中心耗电、环境成本，以及科技巨头的垄断问题。

9月美国众议院曾以417:3的压倒性票数通过数据中心电费相关法案，要求各州考虑让大型数据中心承担新增电网成本。

就连共和党也在担心 AI 巨头疯狂扩张，最后却让普通美国人承担电费。如果未来监管和电力成本继续上升，微软、谷歌、Meta、亚马逊等巨头的数据中心投资回报率都可能受到影响。

当然，两党在 AI 领域，保持美国算力优势、先进芯片竞争力、网络安全，仍然有跨党派合作空间。

Crypto 领域，稳定币监管、反洗钱、消费者保护也存在共识。

已经通过的 GENIUS 稳定币法案不会因为选举自动失效，特朗普也依然掌握行政权和总统否决权。

text:
Having spent a long time watching Elon Musk, and having talked with him, I believe I understand what he understood before almost anyone else. And it's something every one of us needs to understand now.

Western civilization is not one civilization among many. It is the one that gave the world freedom of thought, modern science and the dignity of the individual. And it is under attack. Not by peoples, but by ideologies that want it dead.

If it dies, the world will not become more just. It will become poorer, more brutal and darker. For everyone, including those who hate it.

Why? Because civilizations are not interchangeable. We were told that any culture could be blended with any other, like mixing colors, and that the result would always be harmonious. It isn't true. A society where women are equal to men cannot coexist without friction with a worldview in which a woman's testimony is worth half a man's. A society where you can criticize God, change your religion or have none cannot absorb, without fracturing, a worldview in which apostasy is paid for with your life.

Every people has its own genius and moves at its own pace. But not all values are equal, and you cannot build a nation on laws that contradict each other. Saying so is not racist. Racism is about blood. I am talking about laws, customs and values. And those values belong to no race: a Japanese, a Senegalese or an Iranian can make them his own, and millions have. That is exactly why they are worth defending.

Let's remember where they come from.

It all begins in Greece. In Athens, for the first time, men decide that truth does not descend from a throne but is sought through reason, and that a city governs itself through debate. Socrates chooses death rather than give up thinking freely. At Salamis, a handful of free cities stops the greatest empire in the world.

Then comes Rome. Rome invents law that binds everyone, the citizen who holds rights, the Republic. And one immense idea: you can become Roman without being born Roman. You become Roman by adopting its laws.

Christianity adds the most revolutionary idea in history: every human being, slave and emperor alike, has infinite worth.

Then France. The cathedrals, those ships of stone our ancestors built over centuries for descendants they would never see. Descartes, Pascal, Voltaire. The Declaration of the Rights of Man. And Napoleon, who gives France the Civil Code, the lycées, and one simple principle: careers open to talent. Murat, the son of an innkeeper, ends up a Marshal of the Empire and King of Naples. The Civil Code spreads across much of Europe and still shapes the law of dozens of countries today.

And this civilization goes on to abolish slavery, which had been practiced on every continent since the dawn of time, to push back the plague, smallpox and the night itself, and to set foot on the Moon.

Peoples of the West, be proud of this history. Proud does not mean blind. Every civilization has committed crimes: conquest, slavery, war. Ours is the one that went furthest in examining its own faults, to the point of abolishing what it had once practiced. This capacity to question itself is its greatest strength. And that is exactly the strength now being turned against it.

Because for decades, this magnificent system has been getting hacked. Not by an army. By an alliance of two forces that have nothing in common except one enemy: us.

The first is communism. It lost the economic war, lost the Cold War, lost history's verdict with its tens of millions of dead. But it never lost the universities. It survived by changing costumes: class struggle became the struggle of the oppressed against their oppressors, and the West was declared guilty of everything. It taught our children to be ashamed of their ancestors, their borders and their culture. It is the root cause, because before you can bring down a civilization, you have to take away its will to defend itself.

The second is political Islam. I am not talking about Muslims, many of whom came here precisely to escape this ideology and are its first victims. I am talking about a political project that wants to place religious law above civil law. It has no doubts. It feels no shame. It rushes into the void the first one dug.

One disarms. The other advances.

And let no one on the left believe they will stay in control. History has already staged this play. In 1978, Michel Foucault was enthusing over the Iranian revolution. Iran's communist party, the Tudeh, backed Khomeini and called on Iranians to vote for his Islamic constitution. By 1983, its leaders had been arrested, the party banned, and its chiefs paraded on television to confess their “crimes.” In 1988, thousands of political prisoners were executed, communist activists among them. The second always ends up devouring the first. Useful idiots are only useful for a while.

So here is my call to every Western people. To the French, the Italians, the Poles, the Germans, the Spanish, the Americans, to all of you.

We are at a turning point. What we do in the next ten years will decide what our grandchildren are allowed to say, believe, write and love.

I am not asking you to die for the West. I am asking you for something harder: to live for it.

Learn its history and pass it on. Have children. Speak without fear, even when they call you every name in the book. Vote, get involved, run for office. Build companies, schools, factories, families. Refuse the shame they are trying to inject into you. And stop surrendering anything that makes us who we are: freedom of thought, equality before the law, the dignity of every person.

The historian Arnold Toynbee understood it: civilizations are not murdered, they commit suicide. And those who think they can let the West fall without paying the price should remember the Iranian communists. They helped tear down what they despised, and then they were next.

The Greeks at Salamis were outnumbered. They won because they knew what they were defending. We are the heirs of Athens, Rome, Notre-Dame and the Civil Code. It is no accident that the rockets that will carry humanity to Mars are being built in a free civilization.

It is time to prove ourselves worthy of what we were given.

The West is worth defending. And no one will defend it for us.

머니플로우 ’26.11.2

코스피: 많이 맞았으니 고개 좀 들게
나스닥 선물: 금요일 충격 좀 되돌릴게
SK하이닉스, 소부장: 갭하락 후 암벽등반할게
조선: 필리조선소에서 미군 함정 첫주문 받을게

금요일 나스닥 -2.9%, SOX -7.2%로 반도체가 또 처맞음.
인텔 -28.6%, 샌디스크 -13.5%, 마이크론 -5.3% 급락.
메모리 비메모리 구분없이 기술주들은 그대로 얻어맞았었음.

다행히 오늘 국장은 생각했던 것보다 훨씬 잘 받아내는 중.
코스피는 장중 -2%까지 밀렸다가 지금은 1.3%대로 반등.
코스닥도 -1.1%에서 올라와 1%대까지 반등하고 있는 중.
아침 분위기만 봤으면 또 맞겠구나 싶었는데 생각보다 강함.

갑자기 반등이 나온 이유 부터체크해보면 유가와 나선 덕분.
금요일 $104였던 WTI는 지금 $102대로 1.7% 내려와줌.
나스닥 선물도 금요일 종가 대비 0.6% 안팎 반등하는 중.
카타르 중재 협상 기대감이 유가 전쟁프리미엄을 덜어주는 듯.

다만 전쟁이 끝난것도, AI 현금흐름 우려가 해결된것도 아님
급락 후에 유가에 낀 전쟁프리미엄이 빠져서 숨통 조금 트임
불확실성 남았어도 저가 메리트 보고 사려는 수요일 수 있음.
많이 빠졌다는 것 자체로 기대감이 될 수 있을테니까. 

프리마켓에서 -4%였던 SK하이닉스는 2.5%까지 반등
삼성전자도 -4%에서 약보합까지 암벽 등반에 성공하는 모습.
그 외 삼성전기 비롯한 기판 업체들도 양전에 성공함.

오늘 반등은 전자닉스 둘이서만 하드캐리하는 것도 아님.
코스피 상승 종목은 하락의 2배, 코스닥도 거의 2배 가까움.
중형주도 1.6% 상승하며 초대형주보다 오히려 더 강한 모습.

프리마켓에서 따로 놀던 조선은 정규장에서 더욱 강해짐.
한화그룹 필리조선소 미 해군 함정 첫 수주 뉴스 덕분.
한화오션 프리마켓 4%대에서 지금 10%까지 상승폭을 증가.
오늘 상장한 조선 기자재 영광도 공모가 대비 2배 부근 거래.

일본도 지수와 종목을 따로 봐야 오늘 흐름이 이해가 됨.
니케이도 약보합까지 반등하며 오전대비 낙폭을 많이  줄임.
일본 소부장들도 갭하락 후 양전하며 반등폭이 높게 나와줌.
한국 소부장처럼 장비 쪽에서 반등이 나오는 모습은 비슷함.

다만, 금요일 가이던스 쇼크 내놓은 키옥시아는 -12% 급락중.
이비덴도-3%대 하락이라 일본 기판은 국내와 온도차가 커짐.
한국 메모리가 버틴다고 글로벌 메모리 우려가 끝난건 아님.

미국 중간선거는 내일 현지시간, 개표는 수요일 국장과 겹침.
한국시간으로 내일 저녁 시작, 선거흐름은 국장 장중에 확인.
내일은 중간선거 우려가, 내일모레는 개표결과 우려가 존재.

프리마켓에서 관건이라고 했던 저가 매수세는 일단 들어와줌.
아침에 약할거라 생각했다고해서 반등까지 부정할 필요 없음.
오늘 관건은 오후장까지 반등세가 지속될 수 있을지 여부임.

시장이 내 예상보다 강하면 관심종목도 그에 맞춰 수정하면됨.
반등을 미리 맞히는 것보다 다음에 뭘 볼지가 더 중요한 시장.
오늘 반등해도 이번주 빅이벤트가 아직 남았다는걸 잊지말자.

quoted_text:
My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!

I copied the video clips from my DJI to a folder, then opened Claude Code in it and asked it to edit it into a 10 minute vlog

I made a few adjustments but not a lot

It transcribed everything I said with mlx-whisper (Whisper large-v3-turbo running on my MacBook Pro's GPU through Apple's MLX)

It pulled video frames every few seconds into grid images (contact sheets), so Claude could see what's in each clip

It used SpeechBrain ECAPA (a voice-matching model) to figure out what was my voice from other people

It then made thumbnails with OpenCV with YuNet's face detector

The edit itself is a list of cuts in a JSON file: which clip, start time, end time, Claude then picked the pieces by reading the transcripts and looking at the frame grids by itself

I added on screen captions for X and on YouTube for the first minute with Pillow (Python's image library)

P.S. I didn't ask for any of this, and I didn't know any of this until @thesamparr just asked me how I edited it

All I asked for was "Claude can you edit these clips into a 10 minute vlog for X and YouTube"

I think if I didn't have AI to edit it, I wouldn't be vlogging because editing would be such a painful and slow process for me and hiring someone to do it would be even more hassle for me!

text:
Lots of people fell for this despite it being obvious horseshit. This study has too many serious issues and it disagrees with the trial and genetic data, both of which show no risk.

Notice how the supposed risk is a doubling for all dementia types: Alzheimer's, vascular dementia, and "other". If statins actually do something, this is not what we'd expect. In fact, they're protective for vascular dementia, so we know this is due to some bias like that statin users see doctors more often.

This study's sampling or coding is also wildly implausible. 93% of the cases are "other dementias" - not Alzheimer's or vascular. An Alzheimer's rate of 1-2 per 10k is not plausible for a cohort this old. And we know it's down to recording because changing the cut-off date changes the non-user rate from 30.7 to 3.4 - 9x for nothing?

The design is also simply not a valid one for any sort of meaningful inference. In a proper active comparator, new-user design, you follow people from the point treatment starts. But here, their comparison group is people who never used statins, and are thus disproportionately likely to never interact with the healthcare system.

The study is also severely underadjusted. There are no controls for education or income, nor for anything bad habit-related like alcohol consumption or smoking. And the age adjustment? Bins for age, where statin users are older within the bins.

The sample reads as wildly unrepresentative - or the authors messed up badly - because users averaged 7.9 years of follow-up, but most people stop within a year, so they must not have defined discontinuation in a way that triggered the censoring rule the authors claimed to use.

The CoQ10 mechanism claim is complete nonsense. It's actually arithmetically impossible. If COQ7 levels are 0.1 SDs lower and an SD lower COQ7 doubles dementia risk, that shifts dementia odds by ~1%, not an amount that can explain risk doubling. The paper's 8.2% mediated figure is the share of an even smaller effect in a different sub-cohort that measured statin use at enrollment (i.e., it didn't track new users) and whose total effect *was never reported*. This just proves the authors can slice up the data to get very different results!

The authors also show that they're just not very bright when they claim COQ7 matters and LDL doesn't. The LDL effect is larger, it's just imprecise, so it's not significant. Plus, it's not significantly different from the COQ7 effect estimate. And the authors coincidentally ignored that the LDL estimate was significant in the mediation model - it seems they pick and choose which results to discuss!

The reviewers really should've noted that this paper is just an example of ascertainment bias, poorly-described. But they were incompetent, too. You can tell this definitively because a 5x rate ratio difference between cohorts didn't pop out to any of them as a reason to say 'Hey, these cohorts don't actually agree.'

text:
红杉掌门 Alfred Lin 公开了 Kalshi 的 A 轮 deck
18 页，一页没提 Polymarket，只讲一件事：牌照

红杉现任两位掌门之一 @Alfred_Lin（Zappos 前 COO，投过 Airbnb、DoorDash）发长文，把 Kalshi 2020 年路演红杉的 deck 整套公开了。
做这份 deck 时，Kalshi 还没拿到牌照，一笔交易都没有。
2021 年 2 月，Kalshi 宣布红杉领投的 3000 万美元 A 轮。
上周它刚融了 G 轮：10 亿美元，估值 400 亿美元，红杉和 Wellington 联合领投。

deck 讲的故事，翻译过来是这样：

第 1 页：Kalshi，交易事件结果。
第 2 页：想象一下，直接交易事件的结果。我们开发了一种新资产类别「事件合约」，将成为第一个受 CFTC（美国商品期货交易委员会）监管、可以交易未来事件结果的市场。配图是一张合约卡片：「2020 年 11 月 1 日前会有新冠疫苗吗？」
第 3 页：事件合约是金融市场的下一步。一百年前是谷物期货，几十年后是商品期货，千禧年前后是利率互换，下个月是事件合约。
第 4 页：每一步都撬开了万亿美元的市场。CME 一年名义成交 5 万亿到 24 万亿美元，ICE、CBOE 也是万亿级。
第 5 页：我们和 CFTC 一起搭了一套独家的合约审核框架，能上的合约覆盖经济、地缘、天气、文化、科技健康。
第 6 页：这条路不好走。打了两年监管仗，从 2019 年 2 月和 CFTC 接触，到 12 月交申请，2020 年签下清算所 LedgerX，预计 11 月拿到批准。
第 7 页：这是一个新市场，而且是我们的。护城河三层：拿牌照平均要 1–2 年；唯一能清算事件合约的清算所是我们的伙伴；流动性做起来之后，没人能把我们拉下来。
第 8–12 页：先从散户切入，再吸引机构，最后是真正需要对冲事件风险的企业；靠「新闻配合约」的内容飞轮拉新；交易所、清算对接、交易监控、自营做市，已经从零搭好。
第 13–14 页：团队。CEO @mansourtarek_ 待过 Citadel、高盛、Palantir，COO @luanalopeslara 待过 Citadel、桥水、百威英博，两人都是 MIT 出身，团队 20 人。
第 15–16 页：目标 5 年内月成交 51 亿美元、年化收入 3.7 亿美元，收入来自 0–2.5% 的交易手续费，长期再卖数据。
第 17 页：事件合约会成为美国金融体系的核心。想象一个世界：所有事件风险都能对冲，所有观点都能变现。

最后一页是 Q&A，没写要融多少。

回头看 2020 年，Polymarket 确实更火。
它 6 月上线，用 USDC 在链上交易，三个月成交就过了 100 万美元，大选那个月链上成交约 2600 万美元。
Kalshi 那时候还在等批文，2021 年 7 月才公测，上线两个月累计成交只有几十万美元。

但 Polymarket 没牌照。
2022 年 1 月，CFTC 认定它是未注册的交易场所，罚了 140 万美元，它只能屏蔽美国用户。
三年后，Polymarket 创始人 Shayne Coplan 花 1.12 亿美元买下持牌交易所和清算所 QCEX，才回到美国。

Kalshi deck 第 7 页那句「拿牌照平均要 1–2 年」，Polymarket 用将近四年和 1.12 亿美元验证了。
今天 Kalshi 年化成交超过 1 万亿美元，非体育业务年化收入超过 10 亿美元，当年 5 年的目标早就超了。
红杉合伙人 Shaun Maguire 说，两位创始人为了等监管批准，熬了很多年。

谁能想到2026年，两个项目实现了翻转，Kalshi =2 Polymarket。

text:
Nitroduck designs new colors, flavors, and disease resistance into fruits and veggies. We integrate CRISPR into breeding through pollen, making any crop gene-editable.

Breeding a new specialty crop variety takes 8 - 16 years: breeders hope for random gene combinations and mutations, then spend years picking out the good ones. Meanwhile, consumer tastes, the climate trends, and pathogens change way faster.

Now, accessible genome sequencing and AI can tell breeders what to aim for instead of what to hope for, and CRISPR can turn random mutations into chosen ones. The catch is that CRISPR only works on about 15% of crops. It has to go into a single stem cell that’s then regrown into a whole plant, a process that has to be worked out for each variety, which is cost-prohibitive.

We skip the stem cell and put CRISPR into a pollen grain. The grain pollinates a flower, and out comes an edited seed - seamlessly tapping into how breeders already work.

Matúš, Miro, and I are plant synthetic biologists who made duckweed, the smallest and fastest-growing plant on Earth, genetically engineerable. For doing so we won the Grand Prize at iGEM, the “Olympics of biotech.” During our studies, we engineered 4x more plants than the average plant scientist does in a whole career. Now we’re building Nitroduck, The Crop Design Company, which will make pesticides obsolete by 2042.

text:
how can you tell whether a VC fund is performing well before it starts returning meaningful capital to LPs?

DPI is ultimately what matters, but venture funds typically take 10–15 years to fully mature, so it can be a long time before you have enough distributions to judge their performance.

as of Q2 2026, median DPI was just 0.37x for the 2017 vintage, 0.15x for 2018, and 0.04x for 2019.

and the amount of capital returned in the early years doesn't necessarily tell you much about how the fund will perform in the end.

@daveclark85 analyzed 71 VC funds from the 2005–2008 vintages and found a correlation of just 0.22 between year-five DPI and final DPI. the best-performing fund in his sample eventually reached 12.3x, despite having distributed nothing by year five.

so if you're evaluating a fund that's only three to five years old, what should you actually look at?

here are a few indicators i'd look at.

1. how many portfolio companies are making real progress?

for seed funds, one of the first things i'd check is the graduation rate: how many companies successfully raise their next round. around 10% of seed-stage companies reach Series A within 12 months, with another 15.6% doing so between months 12 and 24. and by year three, roughly 80% of the companies that will eventually graduate have already done so. that makes graduation rate useful much earlier than DPI. you can start seeing whether the manager is consistently identifying companies that other investors want to back. 

i'd also pay attention to who leads those rounds, whether the companies are hitting meaningful milestones, and how much capital they're raising relative to their progress. of course, a high graduation rate alone doesn't guarantee great returns. companies can raise follow-on rounds at unsustainable valuations, and some excellent businesses take longer to raise. but it gives you an early view of portfolio quality.

2. can the winners actually move the fund?

you can invest in an incredible company and still generate disappointing fund-level returns if your ownership is too small or your fund is too large. take Union Square Ventures. @fredwilson recently pointed out that Duolingo and Etsy are each worth around $7–8B, and that USV's ownership in either company could return the entire $500M core fund it just raised. that's the kind of calculation i'd make for any fund.

@micahjay1 at Founder Collective uses a similar principle: one exceptional outcome should have the potential to return the fund. his analysis puts the median value of the 500 largest exits over the past 25 years at around $2.7B. so i'd look at the ownership stakes, expected dilution, and fund size. if one of the portfolio companies exits for $2.7B, how much does the fund actually receive? a fund can have several successful companies and still struggle to produce exceptional returns if the math doesn't work.

3. how reliable are the portfolio valuations?

TVPI can be useful early on, but i'd pay attention to how recently the portfolio companies were valued and what supports those valuations. a $100M valuation from a financing round three months ago is backed by a recent investment decision. a $100M valuation that hasn't been updated in three years gives you much less confidence, especially if the company's performance has changed since then.

it's also worth looking at how valuations have changed over time. research shows that companies with stale valuations or repeated markdowns tend to perform worse, and some of these warning signs can appear as early as the first year. so i'd look at when the fund's largest holdings were last valued, whether their actual progress supports those valuations, and how consistently the manager applies the same valuation approach across the portfolio.

if i had to sum it up, i'd say the way you evaluate a VC fund should depend on how old it is.

by year three, you can already learn a lot about the manager's investment decisions, portfolio construction, access to great companies, and how those companies are progressing.

by year five, you'll have a clearer picture of which investments are working, although the final returns are still difficult to predict.

and by years ten to fifteen, DPI should give you a much better understanding of how successful the fund actually was.

the key is knowing which indicators matter at each stage and what conclusions you can reasonably draw from them.

Heard from so many VC LPs this week. “The math doesn’t math”.  

An LP with a mature VC program is in this scenario: 

- At or over allocation to VC / Growth. Why? The NAV of their VC/Growth portfolio has grown 100%+ YTD because of lots of cap calls, few distributions and markups. Their public NAV is likely up +10% YTD (if indexed) and the PE/RE/Credit is flatish. The VC Growth numerator has wildly outpaced the denominator. 

- They don’t know how to plan for distributions because of public lockups and some big GPs still holding onto spacex.  

- 75%+ of their VC/Growth funds are raising right now. 

- Their IC is worried about bubbles, credit markets and being further overweight into any further market downturn. It’s the end of the year, so no one wants to make big decisions. At the same time, these LPs (having spent time in VC/Growth) know that all of the best stuff has NOT been done yet (so early on diffusion, the chatGPT moment in science/health/Physical AI)

- This is going to lead to some tough decisions.  GPs should plan accordingly.  Helping LPs make the case to boards on why now/what next and understand cash flow planning is important at the moment.

text:
The same 32GB of computer memory that cost $59 a year and a half ago costs $429 today. And the CEO of OpenAI just said it's "quite terrible" that you have it in your computer at all.

What Sam Altman said about a minute before that is the part that should actually bother you.

He was on John Collison's podcast, Cheeky Pint, and John asked him the question everyone pricing out a PC has been asking. Memory got ridiculously expensive. Normally when something gets that expensive, new companies rush in to make more of it and the price comes back down. So where are they?

Sam answered with one word, "bad," and then said the invisible hand is failing right now.

His explanation was pretty honest. For decades, he said, making memory chips meant spending $20 billion on factories to make $19 billion back. It was a brutal boom-and-bust business that nearly bankrupted these companies more than once. Samsung's profit dropped about 96% as recently as early 2023, and it had to cut production. The people running Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, the three companies that make about 95% of the world's memory, all remember that. So they're in no hurry to build a bunch of new factories.

And why would they be? SK hynix reported earnings this week. It made $63 billion in operating profit in three months at an 80% operating margin, which means 80 cents of every dollar of sales turned into profit. For reference, TSMC, the company that makes chips for Apple and Nvidia, ran about 59% the same quarter. SK hynix is sending roughly 100 trillion won back to shareholders this year and told investors it expects demand to stay ahead of supply through 2030.

Then there's who's buying. Back in October 2025, OpenAI signed letters of intent with Samsung and SK hynix for up to 900,000 memory wafers a month. Industry estimates put that at as much as 40% of all the memory the world makes.

To be fair to Sam, he was talking about people running AI models at home, and a server shared by thousands of users really will keep its memory busier than your desktop ever does.

But put it all together. OpenAI has dibs on up to 40% of the world's memory, bought from suppliers clearing 80% margins who'd rather not build more, and the memory he thinks is being wasted is the 32 gigs sitting in your laptop.

quoted_text:
I want to clarify that I’m not bearish on $HYPE or what Hyperliquid is building. 

Quite the opposite. I believe its market share will continue to grow, particularly in the US, and it’s clear why competitors like Binance would view that as a threat.

However, I think there’s an important distinction people are overlooking.

A major reason Hyperliquid experienced such explosive growth was its decentralised, permissionless nature. It positioned itself as an alternative to traditional centralised exchanges, and that narrative played a huge role in attracting users, building trust, and establishing its reputation.

Now that Hyperliquid has achieved significant adoption and recognition, it’s increasingly embracing institutional partnerships and regulated financial infrastructure.

The concern isn’t necessarily that these partnerships are bad for business. In fact, they could be extremely bullish.. long term.

The concern is whether Hyperliquid is gradually moving away from the very principles that made it successful in the first place.

People need to understand that decentralisation and institutional adoption aren’t necessarily mutually exclusive. However, as Hyperliquid expands, KYC and compliance requirements will inevitably become part of certain products and services.

It does raise legitimate questions about how decentralised the ecosystem will remain as institutional influence grows.

So when people claim Hyperliquid is fundamentally different from every other trading platform, I think that deserves more scrutiny.

Hyperliquid can be a solid platform, gain massive market share, and deliver significant value to HYPE holders while still becoming more integrated with the traditional financial system.

Being bullish on its growth doesn’t mean we should ignore the potential compromises being made along the way.

Ultimately, the real test isn’t whether Hyperliquid can attract institutions or dominate market share. 

It’s whether it can achieve all of that without sacrificing the decentralisation that helped build its success.

So let’s not pretend Hyperliquid is the holy grail of decentralisation. There’s a very real possibility that, as it continues to grow and pursue institutional adoption, it gradually becomes more like the very centralised exchanges it originally set out not to become. 

Never forget that.

text:
The most interesting part of $ORE's design isn't live yet.

TLDR: Today, revenue generated by the ORE Reserve auto-compounds in isolation. Eventually, that revenue could be streamed to uORE holders (miners holding unclaimed rewards) as SOL mining credits, allowing the protocol to increasingly fund its own mining activity. The result is a flywheel that could strengthen mining incentives, lift staking yield, and put ORE on a path to net deflation.

First, it's worth understanding why ORE is different.

Bitcoin, Zcash, Ethereum, and Solana all use their native assets to incentivize network security. ORE doesn't have that requirement. It inherits Solana’s security, so it can direct its incentives toward a different objective: rewarding those who accumulate and hold the asset.

ORE is a store of value by design, and nearly every mechanism in the protocol reinforces this objective.

Consider how value flows through ORE today:

- Miners deploy SOL to earn ORE, aiming to acquire it below market price.
- A 10% refining fee on claimed rewards is redistributed to holders of unclaimed rewards (uORE).
- Mining revenue funds ORE buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and the Reserve.
- The Reserve provides liquidity while generating its own revenue through LP fees and yield-bearing assets like JitoSOL and USDv.

The result is a system where mining activity supports holders through multiple mechanisms, while the Reserve continues to grow and generate additional liquidity and revenue.

But there's one more piece to the design. Arguably the most interesting.

In AI, recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system capable of improving its own capabilities, with each improvement enabling further improvements.

ORE has a potential economic equivalent.

Today, the simplified flow looks like this:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → Reserve.

The Reserve grows, generates revenue through LP fees and yield, and reinvests that revenue into itself. A straightforward compounding mechanism.

But the loop back to mining remains open.

Now consider what happens when Reserve revenue is redirected to uORE holders as SOL credits, usable exclusively for mining ORE.

The flow becomes:

Mining → Reserve → LP fees + yield → SOL mining credits → Mining → Reserve.

The loop closes.

This is the recursive moment.

Consider the significance of this change.

Today, mining depends on SOL supplied by users. With mining credits, the Reserve’s own revenue becomes a new source of capital to fund that same activity.

Originally powered by user capital, ORE could become increasingly self-powered.

A protocol generating its own fuel.

There are two particularly interesting second-order effects here.

First, Reserve-funded mining credits could increase competition for ORE rewards, driving up production costs. To the extent this stimulates incremental mining activity, it generates additional protocol revenue, supporting buybacks, burial, staking rewards, and Reserve growth.

Second, and perhaps most importantly, this creates a potential path toward sustained net deflation.

At sufficient scale, additional protocol revenue could fund enough buybacks and burial to consistently exceed new ORE issuance.

To be clear, mining credits aren't live today, and it may be years before the economics justify turning them on.

The Reserve first needs sufficient scale and sustainable revenue to fund meaningful mining incentives without compromising its liquidity or long-term growth.

More importantly, the incremental mining activity needs to generate enough additional value to justify redirecting revenue away from direct compounding.

But the potential end state is worth considering: an economic system that compounds recursively, under its own power.

text:
Thanks to @koolkrypto223 for his comments, I do not see his post as FUD at all but rather constructive discourse. 

On single dealer
I think we've been quite transparent about being a broker-like model rather than an exchange. This actually necessitates the use of a single dealer: unlike spot assets, derivatives in crypto cannot be transferred between different exchanges. If we were to route your order split across 5 exchanges, you would not want to see 5 different positions displayed in your account. You want a sophisticated counterparty to do the liquidity aggregation. We've achieved the benefits you describe: 

✅ more listings than any other DEX
✅ best in class liquidity on any asset class even as a new entrant
✅ liquidity aggregation of the best primary venues; no need to open 20 different exchange accounts and keep switching between them

On the moat
Bringing all of TradFi onchain will take years, if not decades. Swaps, for example, are a fundamentally bilateral contract that cannot be replicated by DEXes, and I don't even think any are trying. This is the first time we've seen direct TradFi liquidity ported onchain with stable funding rates (the routing actually doesn't touch a single crypto venue). Getting the partnerships in place for this was not easy; I think we'll see the same type of consolidation into a few winners as we see with CEXes, DEXes, and TradFi brokerages. 

On price discovery
Our opinionated take: 
a) You do not give a flying fuck as a user where price discovery is happening 
b) In fact most users should not touch exchanges directly at all 

Currently, no price discovery happens on any DEX, except in very niche scenarios. To say otherwise is massive cope. To build a venue for price discovery means catering to the very fastest HFTs: wake me up when DEXes have matching engine latency on the order of nanoseconds. Do a lead-lag analysis on prices between DEXes and CEXes, or DEXes vs CME, and it's obvious where price discovery originates. The only question is do you want a shallow clone of TradFi liquidity or direct access?

As a user, you primarily care about best execution, and that's what we optimize for. Additionally, the reason why brokerages exist in TradFi is to add another layer of protection between the user and the exchange. 

▶️ When 10/10 occurred and billions of dollars of ADL were forced upon users at other venues, Variational came out squeaky clean. 
▶️ When Binance was hacked for billions, we immediately put out a statement that said that user funds are safe in self-custodied smart contracts and not moved to offchain hedging venues. OLP puts up its own capital for that. 

Variational Pro 
Variational Pro will be multi-dealer: you will be able to request a quote and dealers will bid for your flow. This increases the complexity of the product but will have massive unlocks for institutions, including allowing for subnetworks of markets where OLP is not involved. 

If two parties want to trade swaps or other derivatives peer-to-peer at infinite size we will facilitate the infrastructure for order matching, clearing, and margining for that.

Reminder that the tech for this has already been built; it's the same underlying protocol that clears billions every day for Omni! I hope you will see our vision to bring TradFi onchain is a multi-year one and cannot be cleanly segmented into "oh it's just a DEX" or "oh it's just a CFD broker".  It's so much more than that and we encourage everyone to follow our roadmap which we publicize on our docs page.
author: variational_lvs
quoted_text:
The discourse over @variational_io is...bizzare.

Everyone knows it's a single dealer RFQ platform (or at least I'd hope by now). 

This is neither inherently good nor bad, but it should shape your expectations.

Similar to a CFD broker, I'd expect Variational to trade at lower multiples than actual exchanges. IG Group trades at ~half the multiple of CME for example.

There's nothing terribly new or interesting about "RFQ", I'm not sure why people think it's a big value proposition or moat.

The real value prop of Variational is that in crypto, UI for DEXs is largely solved, and UX all comes down to liquidity. Variational can potentially list assets faster, get better liquidity on long tails, and generally abstract away a lot of the awkwardness of bootstrapping a brand new marker that a CLOB has. This has been and will likely continue to be enormously successful with their RWA swaps.

That's a very real value prop, for now. The problem is that they have much less moat than actual exchanges; they are not the venue where actual price discovery is happening. It's significantly harder for TradFi entrants to replicate what @HyperliquidX has built than it'll be for them to do what Variational does, but better. B-booking retail crypto traders and points farmers in OLP is enormously lucrative now, but how durable will those margins be over time?

Depending on the exact flavour of regulatory clarity we get, the value prop they offer for TradFi liquidity can pretty easily shrink as more TradFi market makers are willing/able to quote directly on permissionless CLOBs. I don't know where regulators will land here though; there's worlds that it's very good for Variational and very bad.

I see Variational as more of a bandaid fix/reg arb, but a lot of crypto falls into that category. It's attempting to solve a very real issue, but will that issue be as prevalent in 6 months? 1 year? 2 years? Hard to say.

Personally, I see $LIT and hyperliquid:native as more pure expressions of longing the proliferation of perps as an instrument and DeFi as a sector, where as I see $VAR as more of a business with more operator risk, but it could easily print money for months-years. $GMX might be a good example in that it printed fees for a long time and then eventually became more obsolete.

I actually don't think any of this impacts point price much at TGE, and that's what everyone seems to care about. Market conditions at the time of TGE probably dictate $VAR performance way more than any of this.

quoted_text:
In September a friend bought this Skyridge Machamp during the vintage hype for 5k with the intention of flipping. I told him he should immediately send to auction, since it would take 2 weeks to go live and it's difficult to time the top on these market squeezes

His response was "I'm going to wait until it hits 40k". Here's the problem I have with this logic - try to picture who is going to buy this card for 40k...

- Billionaires might, but there's only ~5 of them bidding for their collections and once they have them they'll move on to the next card
- Pop 184 means it's liquid enough to recover quickly after a squeeze
- Normal collectors either can't afford paying this much or will find better value elsewhere
- Alleged family office / institutional funds are here to make money, and any competent manager wouldn't want to buy the top

So all that leaves are other speculators who are trying to ride the train and dump on the next poor soul without thinking through the underlying value

How did this turn out? He sent it to auction a couple weeks ago when prices started dropping, but pulled it when things started crashing so it's now waiting in the vault. Price peaked at 30k and is now sitting at 4k

Pokemon has highkey turned into memecoin trading, and a lot of speculators are learning an expensive lesson in upnl vs realized gains

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

text:
Pearl looks like it will be an easy GTM mining expansion, and hashrate/energy should increase dramatically.

If you believe what Omri and team have written, Pearl's software stack may make normal workloads more efficient than baseline is today even without mining. Call that -X% for the sake of argument. So rolling out the stack (with mining turned off) should be a net cost advantage for ML providers.

Then, Pearl fp8 mining adds some inference overhead call that +Y%. Inference gets a little bit slower because of mining, but the parameters are tunable. If your workload needs low latency, you mine less and do more inference. If your workload is batch jobs that are OK with latency, you mine more and do inference slower. ML providers turn mining on/off when its profitable.

An added benefit of the (planned) Pearl stack is access to distributed compute jobs. For ML jobs that can be trusted to distribute using privacy attestations and TEE, jobs can eventually be paid for with PRL token. It's a natural network effect to pay for distributed compute with a distributed currency.

So the net takeaways:
- Inference providers likely get a net cost savings from integrating the Pearl stack.
- Depending on workload latency requirements and Pearl price, miners join the network when mining revenue > incremental costs.
- Pearl token is used to pay for distributed compute jobs. It's natural to use a decentralized hard money to pay for decentralized work.

Return on capital brings in miners. Distributed compute brings in token usage. More miners and more token usage increase energy and monetary effects, bringing in pure-SOV buyers.

Over time, Pearl token is likely to be seen as a future on inference compute. Since compute will be payable in Pearl, corporations and individuals have a reason to stockpile the token today to pay for compute tomorrow.

Dependencies: fp8 lands well, continued AI usage, electricity and hardware continue to cost money, team executes well.

One of the more durable crypto investment theses IMO because the GTM for all parties is so clear.

My $20-$100 price estimate comes from difficulty adjustment math at https://t.co/YaFFKOYkuk. Expect that to take a few years conservatively. Could be different depending on how things play out.

Four chains, one setup: your agent finds the trade, your wallet signs it.

What we're building toward:

Trading onchain is a full time job. New launches every few minutes, bundles and snipers in the first block, supply "locked" until it isn't. Most people either miss everything or hand a bot their keys and hope.

Rally sits in the middle:

Agents do the work: scan launches, check the dev wallets, flag the bundles, size the setup and prep the tx. Nothing moves until you sign it. 

The agent never holds your keys, so a bad prompt or a weird instruction just ends up as a request you say no to.

Why four chains matters:

• Robinhood chain is where a lot of new traders are landing, and stock tokens are already out-trading memecoins on some days

quoted_text:
昨晚跟168X的交流要点，上一次8月底https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC参与168X聊到：美股临近中期选举市场动荡加大，然后大饼和加密到10月因为流动性收紧会回踩。梳理下这次聊的要点：
1、美国经济正在进入由AI基建驱动的新基建周期，这种大基建趋势下名义GDP的增速会很好；

2、中东局势中期选举后可能会是一个时间窗口，如果能解决油价回落宏观环境压力会减少很多；
但如果一直不能解决油价持续在高位，通胀持续强势那么联储不仅12月会加息，明年也可能会加，如果原来预期 2 次，最后变成 3 次、4 次甚至更久，则整个估值体系都会重新定价、市场会扛不住。

3、ARR这个指标需要抛后，Anthropic上市后就要看真实的季度营收、年度营收了。大云平台已经是AI Operating System：企业会从结果和成本考虑，切换不同的模型。

4、大型科技公司真正大规模提高 CapEx，是从 2025 年三季度左右开始的，所以今天 Microsoft、Google Cloud 增长出来的 Revenue，很多对应的其实是一年前甚至更早花出去的钱。去年下半年开始加速建设的 Capacity，现在才进入投产期，而过去几个季度所有云厂商一直在讲同一句话：Demand > Supply，算力不够。如果需求还在增长，而且你新上线多少 Capacity 都能马上被吃掉，那未来几个季度 Revenue 自然会继续加速。所以我觉得AI商业化现在不是见顶，而是才刚开始加速。

5、要看Cloud Revenue Growth 何时开始超过 CapEx Growth
不能永远只看 Revenue，第二阶段要看 ROIC。2026 年是 CapEx 爆发的一年。去年几千亿美元，今年接近翻倍，这种 CapEx Growth 不可能每年都 100%。
真正漂亮的拐点是什么？就是未来 CapEx Growth 开始自然下降，但 AI Revenue Growth 还继续加速、意味着开始算的过账来。

所以接下来几个季度，最想看的就是：Revenue Growth、CapEx Growth、Depreciation Life、FCF，这几个东西开始怎么收敛。

6、AI主线已经迁移：Memory → Optical / Software → Agent / AI for Science/应用

不要形成“AI = Semiconductor = Memory”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。

每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，Deployment 越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。

所以趋势投资真正要做的，不是死守原来的 Winner，而是不断识别：下一层利润池正在往哪里迁移。Semi 也不是死了，只是像上半年那种所有东西直线上冲的阶段，短期可能过去了。

7、真正需要让 AI Thesis 转空的信号，不是 Semi 再跌 20%，而是 AI商业化（云厂商业绩增速）开始降速、当下是出于加速的阶段。这才是未来的市场的真正的大风险，

而另一个问题则是伊朗问题迟迟得不到解决，油价高位、通胀向上趋势被强化、联储不得不多次加息而非两次。

8、高收益率时代不再普涨：以后市场只奖励真实 Cash Flow。
当 Bond Yield 高以后，股票自然也要给更高的 Risk Premium，这就是为什么现在市场越来越挑剔。Google Cloud很好，Search、FCF 出现问题，市场照样先卖。所以之后选股票一定要分清楚：哪些公司只是 Narrative，哪些公司的业务已经真正兑现，Revenue 是真的、Cash Flow 是真的，而且未来 2、3 年增长空间还能算出来。

大公司如果因为短期逆风被杀估值，我反而觉得是好事，因为它给你重新上车的价格。高利率不是所有股票不能涨，而是市场会越来越“优中选优”。

9、中期选举后很多不确定性会减弱如国会的归属，再看伊朗问题是不是能解决，谨防Anthropic上市路演开始后的吸血。

昨天有一点现在看是不对的“昨天聊到如果亚马逊的财报还不错、市场有一波能到anthropic路演前、今年亚马逊财报云业务很好但是广告放缓、资本开支远超预期、也是加重了市场担忧”可能这种担忧要到中期选举之后再看了。

多谢@168MrZ

quoted_text:
Sakana AIシンポジウム：日本から挑む言語モデル・世界モデル・Physical AI

開催レポート https://t.co/4O4AWYWOHs 

10月26日、東京・一橋講堂でシンポジウム「From World Models to Real-World AI」を開催しました。9月にChief Scientific Advisorとしてお迎えしたJürgen Schmidhuber教授の基調講演 と、2018年に教授と論文「World Models」を共著したCEOのDavid Haとの対談に、400名を超える方にご参加いただきました。

基調講演では、甘利俊一氏や福島邦彦氏をはじめとする日本の研究者を含め、世界各地の研究者の功績に触れながら、自身による1990年の世界モデルや人工好奇心の研究まで、いまのAIにつながる流れをたどりました。

また、チーフサイエンティストの秋葉拓哉が、事前学習から自社で開発する言語モデルシリーズ「Sakana Sawara（仮称）」を発表しました。最初のモデルとなる小規模な「Sawara Small（仮称）」は、順調に進めば2027年春に公開する予定です。

Jürgenが思い描いてきたAIのうち、生成AIが実現したのはおそらく半分です。自ら実験を考える人工科学者や、実世界で働くPhysical AIといった残りの半分は、まだスケールに至っていません。その機会は大型ラボ以外にこそ開かれていて、日本はその有望な場所の一つだと考えています。このシンポジウムが、日本の企業や研究機関の皆さんとともに、日本のAIの次の時代を切り開いていく出発点の一つとなれば幸いです。

後日動画も公開する予定です。
ご来場いただいた皆さま、ありがとうございました！

text:
在牛市里，毁掉一个中产家庭十年积蓄的，往往不是熊市暴跌，而是看到别人一夜暴富时的那股“不甘心”。

今天看到一位 30 岁市场部打工人的实盘自白，简直是今年美股散户最痛的缩影：

他从大学毕业开始省吃俭用，整整苦熬了 10 年，才好不容易从工资里攒下 50 万美金本金。

过去两年里，他原本走得极稳——老老实实拿着标普 500 指数基金（VOO）和一部分英伟达（NVDA）正股，顺着牛市稳扎稳打赚到了 20 万美金利润，账户净值一度冲上近 70 万美金。

如果故事停在这里，他已经跑赢了 95% 的同龄人。

但今年夏天，看着存储芯片板块满屏的翻倍晒单，他突然陷入了强烈的踏空焦虑（FOMO），满脑子只有一个念头：“别人随手做一笔期权就能赚 100%，我为什么还要慢吞吞地拿指数？”

于是他第一次破戒冲进期权市场，重仓买入闪迪（SNDK）的看涨期权，去赌股价能冲上 2,300 美元；结果刚买进去就遇上回调，从来没吃过大亏的他不肯认错，反手选择加倍补仓死扛。

短短 3 个月时间，他用两年心血攒下的 20 万美金实盘利润被彻底绞杀清零；为了赶紧把亏掉的钱捞回来，他又病急乱投医把本金砸进半导体做多 ETF（SOXX 和 SOXL），转眼再亏掉 5 万美金。

看着跳水了 25 万美金的账户曲线，他在评论区写下了一句让人无比唏嘘的话：
“网上看起来好像人人都能靠一笔好交易轻松翻倍；直到把两年的心血全部赌光我才认清，原来我永远成不了那种天选之子。”

慢钱一旦想走快钱的捷径，市场连本带利收走它的速度，永远比你攒钱的速度快十倍。

"Or when Tesla’s doing simulations for self-driving, Tesla’s actually looking for the most interesting corner cases, because the normal stuff, we already have plenty of data on driving on a straight road on a sunny day. Claude在实验室成功远程攻破Linux服务器：53分钟拿到最高Root权限！！！

这个漏洞的严重程度达到CVSS 9.8，属于Critical级别。

从Linux 4.4时代就已存在，潜伏近十年。

攻击不需要账号认证，也不需要用户点击，攻击者只需要能够通过网络触达目标服务。漏洞影响大量Linux服务器、云主机和基础设施节点。

text:
LLMs accumulate a lot of declarative knowledge.
That's how they can answer a large number of questions. 
That's also why they require so many parameters and hence so much memory. 

But one can replace the accumulation of knowledge by *understanding*
That what JEPA world models do. 
That's one reason they can be useful with considerably less memory and training data  than LLMs. 

This paper merely shows that the underlying similarity structure of the data, whether text or image (e.g. co-occurence of words in text or objects in images) uniquely determines the shape of the representation point cloud, when the encoder is trained trained with a common anti-collapse criterion like SIGReg or VCReg (not by reconstruction).
